resources.name: 100 Black Men of Sacramento, Inc.
resources.mission: The mission is to enhance educational and economic opportunities for underrepresented youth and to improve the quality of life for all within the community.
resources.services: Mentoring the 100 Way, a holistic group mentoring program for children ages 8-18 addressing social, emotional, and cultural needs, delivered by trained and certified member mentors; Saturday Academy (grades 6-12) with life skills, financial literacy, STEM, and robotics; Youth 100 tutoring in math and English for grades 5-8; school-based mentoring at Sacramento area high schools; scholarships and annual Youth and Parent Conference. Contact chapter by email or phone to enroll.
resources.notes: Mailing address: 1618 Alhambra Blvd #160761, Sacramento, CA 95816. Chapter of 100 Black Men of America, founded 1986. Saturday Academy currently held at Natomas High School and Center of Praise Church about three times monthly during the school year; school-based mentoring includes Natomas Middle and Inderkum High. Programs open to boys and girls. Phone (916) 252-6053 per chapter contact page and Big Day of Giving profile.

resources.name: 211 (211 Connecting Point / 211 Sacramento)
resources.mission: 211 is a free, confidential information and referral line, open 24/7, connecting residents to health and human services in their community, including domestic violence resources.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone for free, confidential, 24/7 referrals to DV shelters, crisis lines, legal aid, counseling, and safety resources. Placer County: 211 Connecting Point, dial 211 or (833) 342-5211 (1-833-DIAL211), searchable database at cde.211connectingpoint.org with translation in 10+ languages. Sacramento County: 211 Sacramento, dial 211 or (916) 498-1000, database at 211sacramento.org. Trained specialists can warm-transfer callers to DV agencies such as Stand Up Placer or WEAVE.
resources.notes: Placer side verified at cde.211connectingpoint.org (open 24/7, free, confidential). Sacramento side operated by Community Link Capital Region at 211sacramento.org, (916) 498-1000; site unreachable during research but service is long-established. 211 is a referral gateway, not a direct DV service; in immediate danger call 911.

resources.name: 211 (211 Connecting Point / 211 Sacramento)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral, connecting people with health and human services in their community.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone, 24/7, free and confidential, for referrals to Native American and tribal services in either county: Indian health clinics, Tribal TANF, ICWA and legal help, Native family services, and cultural programs, plus food, housing, and utility resources. Multilingual assistance available. Placer County: 211 Connecting Point (cde.211connectingpoint.org, also serving nearby foothill counties); Sacramento County: 211 Sacramento operated by Community Link Capital Region. Online searchable directories available on both sites; text options offered.
resources.notes: Placer: cde.211connectingpoint.org; Sacramento: 211sacramento.org or (916) 498-1000. Always current: 211 databases are updated continuously, so use 211 to verify any listing in this category before referring a client. Cross-reference: all categories.

resources.name: 211 (211 Connecting Point for Placer, 211 Sacramento by Community Link Capital Region)
resources.mission: 211 is a free, confidential information and referral service available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, connecting people with health and human services in their community.
resources.services: Dial 211 from any phone, 24/7, for referrals to crisis services, shelter, food, health care, utilities, and more. In Sacramento County, 211 Sacramento (a program of Community Link Capital Region) answers 24/7 with specialists speaking English, Spanish, Hmong, Thai, Lao, and Mien plus 200+ languages by tele-interpretation; press 8 to reach homeless crisis services and emergency shelter intake. Toll-free (844) 546-1464 or (916) 498-1000. In Placer County, 211 Connecting Point answers and also routes homeless callers to the 833-3PLACER helpline. Text and searchable online databases available (211sacramento.org, cde.211connectingpoint.org).
resources.notes: Two operators, one dialing code: Community Link Capital Region runs 211 Sacramento; Connecting Point runs 211 for Placer County. 211 press 8 is the Sacramento coordinated entry access point for people experiencing homelessness; youth 18-24 also use 211 for Wind Youth housing intake. Cross-reference: all categories.
resources.contactPerson: Executive Director, Community Link Capital Region (Sacramento); 211 Connecting Point (Placer)

resources.name: 211 (211 Placer and 211 Sacramento)
resources.mission: To be the best-in-class provider of coordinated information, referral and access to health and human service programs and services, needs data and emergency/disaster volunteer services. (Community Link Capital Region)
resources.services: Free, confidential information and referral line: dial 2-1-1 from either county, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with multilingual assistance. Refers callers to IHSS, caregiver respite, home-delivered meals, friendly visitor and telephone reassurance programs, home repair, and other in-home help resources. Sacramento: dial 2-1-1, (916) 498-1000, or toll-free (844) 546-1464; online database at 211sacramento.org, including a Senior Resource Guide. Placer: dial 2-1-1 or search cde.211connectingpoint.org (211 Placer, operated by Connecting Point).
resources.notes: 2-1-1 Sacramento is a program of Community Link Capital Region; 211 Placer is operated by Connecting Point (211placer.org). Hearing impaired: call 7-1-1 and ask for 2-1-1. Sacramento side verified on 211sacramento.org; Placer line widely published, confirm at 211placer.org.

resources.name: 211 (211 Placer Connecting Point / 211 Sacramento)
resources.mission: 211 is a free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral service connecting residents to health and human services in their community, including the full range of senior services.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone in Placer or Sacramento County, 24 hours a day, for live referrals to senior services: senior centers, meals and nutrition, transportation, caregiver support, elder abuse reporting, the Sacramento Senior Safe House, benefits counseling, in-home help, and more. Multilingual operators and TTY access; searchable online directories at 211placer.org (Connecting Point) and 211sacramento.org. Text and email options available in Sacramento.
resources.notes: 211 Placer operated by Connecting Point (211placer.org); 211 Sacramento operated by Community Link Capital Region (211sacramento.org, also (916) 498-1000). Dialing 2-1-1 routes by county automatically. Referral source for the Senior Safe House.

resources.name: 211 (211 Placer Connecting Point and 211 Sacramento)
resources.mission: 211 connects people with free, confidential information and referrals to health, human, and social services in their community, 24 hours a day.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral, including warm connection to suicide prevention hotlines, crisis services, suicide loss support groups, and county behavioral health intake; multilingual assistance; searchable online databases (211placer.org via Connecting Point for Placer, 211sacramento.org for Sacramento) include a dedicated suicide prevention category; no eligibility requirements.
resources.notes: Dial 2-1-1 in either county. Placer service operated by Connecting Point (cde.211connectingpoint.org, 211placer.org); Sacramento service operated by Community Link Capital Region (211sacramento.org). Not a crisis line: callers in suicidal crisis should call or text 988. Cross-reference: appears in all category tabs.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Connecting Point Placer)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential information and referral, connecting people in Sacramento and Placer counties with community health and human services 24 hours a day.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county 24/7 for free, confidential, multilingual information and referral to trafficking survivor services, emergency shelter, safe housing, legal aid, counseling, and basic needs; 211 Connecting Point maintains a dedicated anti-human trafficking resource list for Placer County; searchable online directories at 211sacramento.org and cde.211connectingpoint.org. Text and web chat options available; no eligibility requirements.
resources.notes: Dial 2-1-1 in both counties. Sacramento: operated by Community Link Capital Region, (916) 498-1000 or (800) 500-4931, confirmed via 211sacramento.org July 2026. Placer: 211 Connecting Point maintains an anti-human trafficking resource page at 211connectingpoint.org with online directory cde.211connectingpoint.org, confirmed July 2026. Cross-reference: appears in all category tabs.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 connects people with community, health, and disaster services through a free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral service.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone, 24/7, free and confidential, multilingual. Maintains current listings for hospice providers, palliative care, bereavement and grief support groups, suicide loss support, caregiver respite, and advance care planning help in both counties. Sacramento database includes a dedicated bereavement support category; Placer service is 211 Connecting Point (cde.211connectingpoint.org, also (833) 342-5211). Use 211 to verify current group schedules, which change frequently.
resources.notes: Dial 211 in either county. Placer: 211 Connecting Point, (833) 342-5211, cde.211connectingpoint.org. Sacramento: 211sacramento.org, operated by Community Link Capital Region. Best first call when grief group schedules or hospice service areas need confirmation.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral, connecting people with community services including job training, employment programs, and workforce resources.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone for free, confidential, multilingual referrals to employment and job training programs in both counties, including America's Job Centers, vocational rehabilitation, pre-apprenticeships, and programs for veterans, youth, people with disabilities, and people experiencing homelessness. Available 24/7 by phone; searchable online databases at 211sacramento.org and cde.211connectingpoint.org.
resources.notes: Sacramento: 211 Sacramento operated by Community Link Capital Region, (916) 498-1000. Placer: 211 Placer Connecting Point, (833) 342-5211, cde.211connectingpoint.org. Always the first call when unsure which employment program fits.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral, connecting callers to health and human services in their community, including mental health and counseling resources.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 (24 hours, multilingual) from anywhere in Sacramento or Placer County for referrals to low-cost and free counseling, county mental health access lines, support groups, and crisis resources. Sacramento: 211sacramento.org (Community Link Capital Region), also (916) 498-1000 or (800) 500-4931. Placer: 211 Connecting Point online directory at cde.211connectingpoint.org, or text your zip code to 898211. No eligibility or documentation requirements.
resources.notes: Not a counseling provider itself; navigation service maintained by Community Link Capital Region (Sacramento) and Connecting Point (Placer). Cross-reference Crisis Help Lines tab for 988 and county crisis numbers.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential information and referral, connecting residents to health and human services in their community 24 hours a day.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 (24/7, free, confidential, multilingual) for referrals to youth mentoring programs, CASA and foster youth mentoring, school-based mentoring, reentry mentoring, and other community services in Sacramento and Placer counties. Placer residents can also search cde.211connectingpoint.org; Sacramento residents can search 211sacramento.org. Text and online chat options available.
resources.notes: Sacramento: 211 Sacramento operated by Community Link Capital Region, (916) 498-1000 if 211 unavailable. Placer: 211 Placer Connecting Point, https://211connectingpoint.org/, (833) 342-5211. Gateway entry for all mentoring referrals in both counties.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential information and referral, connecting residents to health and human services in their community 24 hours a day.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone for free, confidential, multilingual referrals to parenting classes, family resource centers, home visiting, diaper distributions, crisis nurseries, fatherhood programs, and pregnancy support. Available 24/7 by phone, text, and searchable online databases. Sacramento: 211sacramento.org or (916) 498-1000. Placer: 211 Placer at cde.211connectingpoint.org or (833) 342-5211.
resources.notes: Always the fastest way to locate current parenting class schedules and diaper distribution sites in either county. Cross-reference: all tabs.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential information and referral, connecting callers to health and human services in their community 24 hours a day.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for free, confidential, 24/7 referrals to reentry services: transitional housing, employment programs for people with records, record clearance clinics, ID and document help, food, benefits and family reunification resources. Sacramento County: 211 Sacramento (Community Link Capital Region), also (916) 498-1000, online database at 211sacramento.org. Placer County: 211 Placer operated by Connecting Point, database at cde.211connectingpoint.org; texting and online chat available.
resources.notes: Not a direct service provider; gateway to all reentry resources in both counties. Placer database: cde.211connectingpoint.org; Sacramento database: 211sacramento.org. Cross-reference: all category tabs.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 2-1-1 is a free, confidential information and referral service connecting people with local health and human services 24 hours a day, seven days a week, in multiple languages.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 in either county for referrals to detox, treatment, sober living, harm reduction and recovery supports. Sacramento: 211 Sacramento (Community Link Capital Region), database of 1,600+ programs, (916) 498-1000 or toll free (844) 546-1464, 24/7. Placer: 211 Placer operated by Connecting Point, 24/7 phone plus text and live chat Monday to Friday, searchable database at 211connectingpoint.org covering Placer, Nevada County and Tahoe Truckee.
resources.notes: Dial 2-1-1 from within either county. Placer searches: cde.211connectingpoint.org. Relevant to all categories; listed last per database convention.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral, connecting people with health and human services in their community, including transportation programs.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for live, multilingual referral to reduced-fare transit, paratransit, senior ride programs, medical transportation and volunteer driver services. Sacramento County: 211 Sacramento (Community Link Capital Region), also (916) 498-1000 or toll free (844) 546-1464, searchable transportation database at 211sacramento.org. Placer County: 211 Placer operated by Connecting Point, database at cde.211connectingpoint.org. Free, no eligibility requirements, available 24/7.
resources.notes: Two separate operators, one dialing code: Community Link Capital Region runs 211 Sacramento; Connecting Point runs 211 Placer. Both maintain current transportation program listings and can screen for eligibility. Always the referral of last resort when a specific program above cannot serve the caller.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / 211 Placer-Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 connects people with local health and human services, providing free, confidential information and referral 24/7, including housing, shelter, food, healthcare, transportation, and legal assistance.
resources.services: Free 24/7 multilingual information and referral for emergency shelter, homeless services, housing search, rental and utility assistance, and severe weather respite. In Sacramento County, 211 Sacramento maintains the housing and shelter resource database and connects callers to the Coordinated Access System (dial 2-1-1 and press 8 for shelter assessment). In Placer County, 211 Connecting Point is the official access point for Coordinated Entry (Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras): callers complete a standardized assessment and join the centralized housing list from which partner agencies fill openings. Placer also operates the Homeless Resource Helpline (833) 375-2237. Dialing 2-1-1 from either county routes to the correct center.
resources.notes: Placer site: 211connectingpoint.org/placer-county. Sacramento CAS line: (844) 546-1464. Nearly every shelter bed in both counties is filled through these lines rather than by walking in; 211 is the universal first call for housing crisis in both counties.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento / Community Link Capital Region and 211 Placer / Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 2-1-1 provides free, confidential information and referral, connecting callers with health and human services in their community 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, in about 150 languages.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for live referrals to emergency cash aid, utility assistance programs (HEAP, EnergyHELP, REACH), free tax preparation sites during filing season, benefits enrollment help, rent assistance, payee services, and nonprofit credit counseling. 211 Sacramento also maintains the region's VITA tax site list each season. Available by phone, text, and searchable online directories.
resources.notes: Sacramento: dial 2-1-1, (800) 500-4931, or (916) 498-1000 (operated by Community Link Capital Region); from outside the county call (844) 546-1464. Placer: dial 2-1-1 or search cde.211connectingpoint.org (operated by Connecting Point). Always the referral of last resort when a listed program's funding is exhausted.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento and 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 2-1-1 is a free, confidential information and referral service available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, connecting people with local services and resources from a database of more than 1,600 programs.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone in Sacramento or Placer County for free, confidential referrals to furniture banks, thrift vouchers, diaper distributions, medical equipment loans, computer and bike programs, and donation drop-off sites. Sacramento: dial 211, (916) 498-1000, or toll free (844) 546-1464; searchable database at 211sacramento.org. Placer: dial 211, call toll free (833) 342-5211, or search 211connectingpoint.org (211 Connecting Point). Available 24/7 with assistance in multiple languages; hearing impaired callers dial 711 and ask for 211.
resources.notes: Sacramento 211 is a program of Community Link Capital Region; Placer 211 Connecting Point serves Placer, Nevada, and nearby counties. Always current: call 211 to confirm any resource in this tab before referring a client.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento and 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential, 24-hour information and referral, connecting residents to health and human services in their community, including legal aid and self-help resources.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for free, confidential, 24/7 phone referrals to legal aid offices, lawyer referral services, court self-help centers, expungement clinics, senior legal services, disability rights help, and immigration legal providers. Multilingual assistance available. Sacramento: 211sacramento.org (Community Link Capital Region), (916) 498-1000. Placer: 211 Connecting Point, searchable database at cde.211connectingpoint.org, or text your zip code to 898211.
resources.notes: Always available fallback when a specific legal program is full or unreachable. Placer 211 is operated by Connecting Point; Sacramento 211 by Community Link Capital Region. Referral databases are updated regularly but confirm program details directly with providers.

resources.name: 211 (211 Sacramento and 211 Placer Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential, 24-hour information and referral, connecting callers with health and human service resources in their community.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for free confidential referrals to small business assistance programs, microloan providers, entrepreneurship training, employment and financial education resources, plus all other health and human services. Multilingual interpretation available. Sacramento County: dial 211 or (916) 498-1000, searchable database at 211sacramento.org. Placer County: dial 211 or (833) 342-5211, database at 211connectingpoint.org.
resources.notes: Two systems, one dialing code: 211 Sacramento (Community Link Capital Region) serves Sacramento County at (916) 498-1000; 211 Placer Connecting Point serves Placer County at (833) 342-5211. Not a direct provider of business services; use for navigation when other entries do not fit or for wraparound needs.

resources.name: 211 (Connecting Point Placer / Community Link Capital Region Sacramento)
resources.mission: Free, confidential 24/7 information and referral lines connecting residents with community resources for health and human service needs, including free clinics, mental health, dental, prescription discounts, insurance enrollment help, and more.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county, 24/7/365, no eligibility requirements. Placer: 211 Connecting Point, (833) 342-5211, text your ZIP to 898211, searchable database at cde.211connectingpoint.org; also the coordinated entry access point for Placer homeless services, Homeless Resource Helpline (833) 375-2237. Sacramento: 211 Sacramento, program of Community Link Capital Region, (916) 498-1000 or toll-free (844) 546-1464, database at 211sacramento.org, referrals to 1,600+ services including prescription drug discount programs; Spanish, Hmong, Thai, Lao, and Mien in-house plus 200+ languages by tele-interpretation.
resources.notes: Placer contact email: callcenter@connectingpoint.org. Sacramento email not live-monitored, use for non-emergencies only. Hearing-impaired: dial 7-1-1 and ask for 2-1-1. Cross-ref: 211 appears in all category tabs.

resources.name: 211 (Placer 211 Connecting Point / 211 Sacramento)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential information and referral, connecting residents to health and human services in their community 24 hours a day.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for free, confidential, 24/7 information and referral in multiple languages: ILP and foster youth transition programs, TAY shelters and housing (in Sacramento, press option 8 for shelter assessment and Coordinated Access System entry), college support programs, disability transition services, employment programs. Searchable online directories for both counties.
resources.notes: Placer: 211 Connecting Point, cde.211connectingpoint.org, dial 2-1-1 or (833) 342-5211. Sacramento: 211 Sacramento, 211sacramento.org, dial 2-1-1 or (844) 546-1464; option 8 reaches the shelter/Coordinated Access line used for The Grove and other TAY shelters.

resources.name: 211 (Sacramento: 211 Sacramento; Placer: 211 Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 connects people with local health and human services information and referrals, free and confidential, 24 hours a day.
resources.services: Free 24/7 information and referral line covering youth programs, after-school care, summer camps, recreation scholarships, teen centers and youth crisis services. Sacramento County: dial 2-1-1 or (916) 498-1000 or (844) 546-1464 toll-free; database of 1,600+ programs searchable at 211sacramento.org. Placer County: dial 2-1-1 or (833) 342-5211 (1-833-DIAL211); searchable directory at 211connectingpoint.org with live chat Mon-Fri 7 am-6:30 pm.
resources.notes: Dial 2-1-1 in either county. Sacramento 211 operated by Community Link Capital Region; Placer 211 operated by Connecting Point (also serves Nevada County and Tahoe-Truckee). Use as the gateway when a specific youth program is full or unavailable.

resources.name: 211 (Sacramento: Community Link Capital Region; Placer: 211 Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 2-1-1 is a free, confidential information and referral service connecting residents to health and human services in their community 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for referrals to immigration legal services, DOJ accredited representatives, know your rights resources, and immigrant family supports (food, health, housing accessible regardless of status). Sacramento: (916) 498-1000 or (800) 500-4931, searchable immigration/naturalization category online, specialists speak Spanish, Hmong, Thai, Lao, Mien, and English with 200+ languages by tele-interpretation. Placer: dial 211 or (833) 342-5211 (1-833-DIAL211), or search cde.211connectingpoint.org. Free, anonymous, no documentation required.
resources.notes: 211 does not ask about immigration status. Sacramento 211 operated by Community Link Capital Region; Placer 211 by Connecting Point (Auburn). Good first call when unsure which legal provider has capacity. LAST ROW per spec.

resources.name: 211 Sacramento / 211 Placer (Connecting Point)
resources.mission: 211 provides free, confidential information and referral, connecting people with community health and social services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.services: Dial 2-1-1 from either county for free 24/7 multilingual referrals to disability services: independent living centers, IHSS, regional center intake, assistive technology, adaptive recreation, benefits help, accessible housing, and transportation. Placer 211 is operated by Connecting Point (cde.211connectingpoint.org) with a searchable online directory; 211 Sacramento is operated by Community Link Capital Region. Text and online chat options available.
resources.notes: Alternate access: Sacramento (916) 498-1000 or 211sacramento.org chat; Placer via cde.211connectingpoint.org. Landline and mobile 211 dialing works in both counties. Listed last per database convention; relevant to every category.

resources.name: 3Strands Global Foundation (The Table Empowerment Center and Employ + Empower)
resources.mission: 3Strands Global Foundation works to create a world free from human trafficking through prevention education, reintegration programs, and advocacy.
resources.services: Direct services for trafficking survivors and at-risk individuals in the Sacramento region: The Table, a drop-in empowerment center in Sacramento (opened 2024) with service navigation, basic needs (food, clothing, hygiene products, laundry), a technology center for job searches and schoolwork, a wellness room, and client events; Employ + Empower provides trauma-informed intensive case management and wrap-around employment support including career coaching, resume and interview prep, vocational assessments, education navigation, transportation assistance, childcare navigation, professional clothing, and financial literacy coaching for survivors and those at risk of exploitation. Referrals: (916) 338-8879 or referrals@3sgf.org, monitored 9am-5pm PST; also delivers PROTECT prevention education in schools.
resources.notes: Office: 1211 H Street, Sacramento, CA 95814. Referral line (916) 338-8879 and referrals@3sgf.org confirmed on 3sgf.org/help July 2026, monitored 9am-5pm PST; emergencies referred to National Human Trafficking Hotline (888) 373-7888 or 911. Direct services (The Table, Employ + Empower) serve the greater Sacramento region; prevention education is nationwide. Candid Platinum Transparency 2025.
resources.contactPerson: Ashlie Bryant, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: 4-H Youth Development Program (UC Cooperative Extension)
resources.mission: 4-H is the youth development program of the University of California Cooperative Extension, promoting hands-on experiential learning that builds leadership, responsibility, teamwork and positive self-image in youth.
resources.services: Community 4-H clubs for youth roughly ages 5-19: animal science, STEM, gardening, cooking, sewing, civic engagement, camps and county fair projects, led by trained adult volunteers. Placer County: ten clubs, roughly 500 youth; 2026-2027 enrollment fee $72 per youth. Sacramento County served through UCCE Capitol Corridor; contact the county office for current enrollment fees. Program fee waivers or reductions available for families who cannot afford fees; request the fee waiver form from your club leader or county office. Enrollment via the ZSuite system.
resources.notes: Placer 4-H office: 2855 2nd Street, Auburn, CA 95603, (530) 889-7386, placer4h@ucanr.edu. Sacramento County 4-H via UCCE Capitol Corridor: 4145 Branch Center Road, Sacramento, (916) 875-6913, cecapitolcorridor@ucanr.edu. University of California program (government-linked). Fee waivers keep participation accessible to low-income families.

resources.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (answered locally by WellSpace Health, 988 Sacramento)
resources.mission: The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline provides immediate, free, and confidential support 24/7 for people experiencing emotional distress, mental health challenges, substance use concerns, or suicidal thoughts, by call, text, or chat.
resources.services: Call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org, 24/7/365. Calls from the Sacramento region are answered locally by WellSpace Health's accredited crisis center, which serves Sacramento, Placer, and 30+ Northern California counties and answered roughly 62,000 calls and 32,000 chats/texts in 2024. Spanish line available (press 2); interpretation in 240+ languages; veterans press 1. The former LGBTQI+ youth press 3 option was discontinued nationally in July 2025; LGBTQ+ young people can still call 988 or The Trevor Project. Local legacy lines: Sacramento (916) 368-3111, Auburn (530) 885-2300, Roseville (916) 773-3111, Lincoln (916) 645-8866.
resources.notes: WellSpace Health is a Sacramento-based nonprofit FQHC that has operated the regional suicide prevention line for decades. Can dispatch or coordinate with county mobile crisis teams. Cross-reference: Mental Health category.
resources.contactPerson: Dr. Jonathan Porteus, CEO, WellSpace Health

resources.name: A Community For Peace
resources.mission: A Community For Peace is a trauma informed social justice center for victims and survivors of domestic violence, family violence and sexual assault, providing culturally relevant services to victims and their families. All services are free.
resources.services: Trauma-informed DV center serving Citrus Heights and northeastern Sacramento County. 24-hour crisis line at (916) 728-7210. Reported services: individual and group peer counseling, court and social services advocacy, assistance with restraining order paperwork, safety planning, emergency food and clothing, emergency safehouse access for domestic violence and human trafficking survivors, and transitional housing (Soroptimist House). Services free and unlimited.
resources.notes: CAUTION, likely closed but not confirmed: as of July 2026 the website resolves but is completely blank, fundraising profiles on Mightycause and GivingEdge are labeled zz_CLOSED, ProPublica shows no Form 990 filed since fiscal year ending June 2020 (EIN 68-0457704, negative net assets), and no 2025-2026 news, events, or social activity was found. No formal closure announcement located; still listed in 211, People's Guide, and county directories at 6060 Sunrise Vista Drive, Suite 2340, Citrus Heights, CA 95610. Do not refer without first calling the crisis line (916) 728-7210 or office (916) 728-5613 to confirm operation; WEAVE (916) 920-2952 covers this service area.

resources.name: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide
resources.mission: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide is the nation's largest free tax assistance and preparation service, provided free of charge with a special focus on taxpayers who are over 50 and have low-to-moderate income.
resources.services: Free tax preparation by IRS-certified volunteers at sites throughout both counties from early February to mid-April; no AARP membership required and no age requirement, though the focus is taxpayers 50+ with low to moderate income. Options include in-person one-visit preparation, drop-off service, fully remote document upload, and coached self-preparation. Find sites with the online Tax-Aide Site Locator; appointments recommended.
resources.notes: Recent local sites have included Rocklin Library, Auburn, Loomis, Lincoln, Roseville, Kings Beach, and multiple Sacramento locations; sites change yearly, use the locator each season. Service closed between tax seasons.

resources.name: AAUW Roseville-South Placer Branch
resources.mission: The American Association of University Women advances gender equity for women and girls through research, education and advocacy.
resources.services: Scholarships for South Placer high school senior girls and for women students at Sierra College; leadership development; women’s advocacy and public policy education; community programs and speaker events; mentoring.
resources.notes: Listed in the source file as AAUW; the branch serving Lincoln is AAUW Roseville-South Placer, headquartered in Lincoln. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Ability Tools (California Foundation for Independent Living Centers)
resources.mission: Ability Tools is California's Assistive Technology Act program, connecting Californians with disabilities to the assistive technology devices, reuse programs, and funding they need to live independently.
resources.services: Free statewide services: Device Lending Libraries loan assistive technology (portable ramps, AAC communication devices, magnifiers, adapted computer equipment and software) free for up to 30 days, with shipping available anywhere in California; the AT Exchange online marketplace lists gently used devices for free or low cost; financial loan program for AT purchases. The Sacramento lending center is operated by the California Foundation for Independent Living Centers at 1000 G Street, Suite 100, Sacramento; devices ship to borrowers anywhere in California, so Placer County residents can borrow by phone. Browse available devices via NATADS public access on the website.
resources.notes: Program of California Foundation for Independent Living Centers, 1000 G Street, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95814. TTY (800) 900-0706. Devices ship statewide; 30 day free loans. Cross-reference: Disability tab.
resources.contactPerson: Ability Tools Information and Assistance Line

resources.name: ACC Senior Services
resources.mission: Our mission is to promote the general welfare and enhance the quality of life for our community by identifying, developing, and providing culturally sensitive health and social services for older adults.
resources.services: Community programs that help Sacramento area older adults age at home: Bridge to Healthy Families (care assessment and management for family caregivers, connecting them to support services and resources), Friendly Visitor/In-Home Respite Program (enrichment activities and care assistance for frail seniors that give family caregivers a break), PEARLS depression self-management coaching, ACC Rides door-to-door transportation, Senior Escort Program, utilities assistance, and classes and lifelong learning programs. Founded in 1972 by Sacramento Asian American community leaders; serves older adults of all backgrounds with culturally and linguistically sensitive services.
resources.notes: 7334 Park City Drive, Sacramento CA 95831. Verified on accsv.org July 2026; main phone on current site is (916) 394-6399 (older listings show 393-9026). Also operates ACC Care Center, Greenhaven Terrace, and Maple Tree Village residential communities. Affiliated nonprofit runs Meals on Wheels Sacramento County (separate row). Cross-references: Transportation, Food tabs.

resources.name: ACC Senior Services (ACC Rides)
resources.mission: ACC Rides provides door-to-door transportation service so seniors can get to medical and dental appointments, grocery shopping, senior centers, and other errands.
resources.services: Door-to-door rides for adults 60 and over living in Sacramento zip codes 95811, 95814, 95816, 95817, 95818, 95820, 95822, 95823, 95824, 95828, 95831, 95832 and 95758 (Elk Grove), plus the Delta communities of Locke, Courtland, Hood/Franklin and Walnut Grove. Destinations include medical and dental appointments, Meals on Wheels cafe sites, ACC and other senior centers, Triple R adult day program, grocery shopping, field trips and errands. Call the ACC Rides team at (916) 393-RIDE (7433) or email rides@accsv.org to register and schedule rides in advance.
resources.notes: ACC Senior Services: 7334 Park City Drive, Sacramento, CA 95831. ACC Rides line is (916) 393-RIDE (7433); Agency on Aging Area 4 also lists (916) 393-9026 ext 333. Zip code restricted; riders outside the area should call 211 or Agency on Aging Area 4 for alternatives. Cross-reference: Eldercare category for ACC's senior center, classes and care services.
resources.contactPerson: Darrick Lam, President and CEO, ACC Senior Services

resources.name: ACC Senior Services (Asian Community Center of Sacramento Valley)
resources.mission: ACC Senior Services' mission is to promote the general welfare and enhance the quality of life for our community by identifying, developing, and providing culturally sensitive health and social services for older adults.
resources.services: Major multi-service senior provider founded 1972: Lifelong Learning and Wellness program with 50-75 weekly classes (computers, tai chi, yoga, line dancing, fitness, arts); ACC Rides door-to-door transportation for Sacramento area seniors; care management, Friendly Visitor in-home respite, and Bridge to Healthy Families caregiver support; Senior Community Service Employment Program job training for low income seniors 55+; utilities education and assistance; and the nonprofit ACC Care Center skilled nursing facility. Culturally and linguistically responsive services, open to all older adults.
resources.notes: Main campus: 7334 Park City Drive, Sacramento, CA 95831; office hours Mon-Fri 8:30-5:00 per directory listings. Website accsv.org confirmed active July 2026; main phone on site is (916) 394-6399 (older listings show (916) 393-9026). Current services include ACC Rides, ADRC, caregiver support and Bridge to Healthy Families, Friendly Visitor respite, PEARLS, senior job training (SCSEP), CHAT program, senior escort, and utilities assistance. Cross-reference: Transportation tab (ACC Rides), Employment tab (SCSEP), In-home Help tab (care management).

resources.name: Accion Opportunity Fund
resources.mission: Accion Opportunity Fund is committed to advancing economic mobility for underserved small businesses and low-income communities through affordable capital, knowledge resources, networks, and policy.
resources.services: Nonprofit small business lender (CDFI): affordable small business loans generally from about $5,000 to $250,000 with transparent terms, free one-on-one business coaching, free online educational resources in English and Spanish, and specialty financing such as food truck loans for California operators. Over 90 percent of clients are women, people of color or low-to-moderate income entrepreneurs. Apply online at aofund.org; no fee to apply.
resources.notes: National nonprofit headquartered at 111 W. St. John Street, Suite 800, San Jose, CA 95113; lends statewide in California including Sacramento and Placer counties, all services delivered online and by phone. Phone hours Mon-Fri 10am-7pm Eastern; Spanish line (888) 209-7637, Punjabi/Hindi line (888) 706-8030. Loan amounts and terms vary by state and applicant; check current products on aofund.org.

resources.name: Acres of Hope
resources.mission: Acres of Hope is a spiritually-based renewal center that provides a safe family environment and a healthy living program for women with children. Our balanced approach sets the foundation of change and breaks the cycle of homelessness.
resources.services: Residential program on a rural campus in Applegate where homeless women with children live on-site for up to two years. Capacity 13 families. Structured phased programming: life skills and job skills training, mentoring, spiritual direction, education completion, record clearing, family reunification, and permanent housing placement. Apply through the online inquiry form at acresofhopeonline.org/get-help/. Also operates ReNew thrift boutique in Roseville (1725 Santa Clara Dr., (916) 782-5777).
resources.notes: Campus: 17855 Lake Arthur Rd., Applegate, CA 95703; mail: P.O. Box 238, Auburn, CA 95604. Spiritually-based program; residents should expect faith-oriented programming. Women with children only; no single men or couples.

resources.name: Acres of Hope (Placer Family Housing)
resources.mission: Acres of Hope is a spiritually-based renewal center that provides a safe family environment and a healthy living program for women with children. Our balanced approach sets the foundation of change and breaks the cycle of homelessness.
resources.services: Residential program on a rural campus in Applegate where homeless women with children live on-site for up to two years. Capacity 13 families. Structured phased programming: life skills and job skills training, mentoring, spiritual direction, education completion, record clearing, family reunification, and permanent housing placement. Apply through the online inquiry form at acresofhopeonline.org/get-help/. Also operates ReNew thrift boutique in Roseville (1725 Santa Clara Dr., (916) 782-5777).
resources.notes: Campus: 17855 Lake Arthur Rd., Applegate, CA 95703; mail: P.O. Box 238, Auburn, CA 95604. Spiritually-based program; residents should expect faith-oriented programming. Women with children only; no single men or couples.

resources.name: Agency on Aging Area 4
resources.address: 1401 El Camino Avenue, 4th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95815
resources.mission: Agency on Aging Area 4 plans and coordinates programs, services and advocacy for older adults across a seven county region including Placer and Sacramento counties, helping seniors live with independence and dignity.
resources.services: Regional Area Agency on Aging and primary senior services gateway for both counties: Information and Assistance line connecting seniors 60+, caregivers, and families to services; funds and coordinates contracted providers for congregate and home delivered meals, transportation, legal services, caregiver respite and support, residential repair, disease prevention, and grandparent support; operates the Long-Term Care Ombudsman program and coordinates the Aging and Disability Resource Connection (ADRC); HICAP Medicare counseling is provided through its funded partner HICAP Services of Northern California. Call the toll free line for intake and referral.
resources.notes: Office: 1401 El Camino Avenue, 4th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95815; Mon-Fri 8:30am-4:30pm. Serves Nevada, Placer, Sacramento, Sierra, Sutter, Yolo and Yuba counties. County-specific resource pages on website. Cross-reference: Food, Legal, Transportation, Employment tabs.

resources.name: Agency on Aging Area 4 (Health Insurance Counseling and Advocacy Program, HICAP)
resources.mission: HICAP provides free, unbiased counseling and advocacy on Medicare, Medigap, Medicare Advantage, prescription drug plans, and long-term care insurance for Medicare beneficiaries of any age.
resources.services: Free one-hour appointments with registered HICAP Medicare counselors: help comparing and enrolling in Medicare plans during open enrollment, Medigap and Part D guidance, appeals assistance, long-term care insurance review, and Medicare Savings Program screening for help paying premiums. Serves Medicare beneficiaries and those approaching 65 in Placer and Sacramento counties; counseling by phone, video, or at community sites including senior centers. Delivered by AAA4 funded partner HICAP Services of Northern California (hicapservices.net). Not affiliated with any insurance company; no sales.
resources.notes: Statewide referral line (800) 434-0222 routes to local counselors. AAA4 lists HICAP Services of Northern California at (916) 376-8915 for Placer County and (530) 258-6827 for the wider Northern California region (both confirmed on agencyonaging4.org July 2026). Registered with the California Department of Aging.

resources.name: Agency on Aging Area 4 (Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program)
resources.mission: The Long-Term Care Ombudsman investigates and endeavors to resolve complaints made by, or on behalf of, individual residents in long-term care facilities, including nursing homes, residential care facilities for the elderly, and assisted living facilities.
resources.services: Advocacy for residents of skilled nursing facilities, assisted living, and residential care facilities for the elderly in Placer and Sacramento counties: investigates complaints about care quality, rights violations, and elder abuse in facilities; makes unannounced facility visits; witnesses advance health care directives in nursing homes; and educates residents and families. Free and confidential; anyone may file a complaint on a resident's behalf during office hours at (916) 376-8910; after hours emergencies via the state CRISISline (800) 231-4024, answered 24/7.
resources.notes: Designated local representative of the California Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman for PSA 4 (includes Placer and Sacramento). Fax (916) 376-8914. For abuse in private homes, use county APS instead (see county entries).

resources.name: Agency on Aging Area 4 (Transportation Information and Assistance)
resources.address: 1401 El Camino Avenue, 4th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95815
resources.mission: Agency on Aging Area 4 plans, coordinates and funds services that help older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers live with independence and dignity in Planning and Service Area 4.
resources.services: Information and assistance line that connects adults 60 and over, caregivers and adults with disabilities to funded senior transportation providers and other aging services across its seven-county area, including Sacramento and Placer counties. Staff refer callers to programs such as Seniors First Placer Rides (Placer), ACC Rides and Stanford Settlement (Sacramento), plus paratransit and volunteer driver options. No wrong door: call for a warm referral; no fee.
resources.notes: Office: 1401 El Camino Avenue, 4th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95815. Toll free (800) 211-4545. Serves Nevada, Placer, Sacramento, Sierra, Sutter, Yolo and Yuba counties. Funds senior transportation contracts rather than driving clients directly (current funded transportation partners include Seniors First in Placer and ACC Rides and Stanford Settlement in Sacramento); referral gateway for senior rides. Cross-reference: Eldercare category.
resources.contactPerson: Information and Assistance Staff, Agency on Aging Area 4

resources.name: Alchemist Community Development Corporation (Alchemist Kitchen and Microenterprise Academy)
resources.mission: Alchemist CDC connects Sacramento area communities to land, food, and opportunity, toward a vision in which all neighborhoods are vibrant, equitable, healthy and diverse.
resources.services: Food business incubation for aspiring entrepreneurs from low-income Sacramento communities: Alchemist Microenterprise Academy, a 12-week business training course covering financial literacy, legal business structures, recipe development and safe food handling; Alchemist Kitchen Incubator Program for select academy graduates with technical assistance, mentorship and low-cost commercial kitchen access at the shared-use kitchen in North Sacramento; kitchen rental also open to other food businesses. Apply through the website.
resources.notes: Main office 2901 K Street, Suite 302, Sacramento, CA 95816; shared-use kitchen at 882 El Camino Ave, Sacramento. Org email info@alchemistcdc.org; kitchen program email AlchemistKitchen@alchemistcdc.org. Alchemist Public Market project in development, check website for status. Cross-reference: Food category (CalFresh Market Match at farmers markets is run by the same org).

resources.name: Alcoholics Anonymous, Placer County District 21
resources.mission: Alcoholics Anonymous is a fellowship of people who share their experience, strength and hope with each other that they may solve their common problem and help others to recover from alcoholism. The only requirement for membership is a desire to stop drinking.
resources.services: Nonprofit AA service body for Placer County: about 60 groups and more than 200 meetings per month in Auburn, Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln, Colfax and foothill communities; online meeting finder at aaplacer.org; 24 hour hotline answered through the Sacramento central office at (916) 454-1100. Free, no registration or documentation; open meetings welcome anyone, closed meetings for those with a desire to stop drinking.
resources.notes: District meets fourth Tuesday, 6 pm, 244 Palm Ave, Auburn 95603. Mailing: CNIA District 21, PO Box 591, Auburn CA 95603. Roseville Alano Club provides meeting space for 12 step groups.

resources.name: Alta California Regional Center (ACRC)
resources.address: 4151 E Commerce Way, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95834
resources.mission: Alta California Regional Center creates partnerships to support all eligible individuals with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities, children at risk, and their families in choosing services and supports through individual lifelong planning as a means to achieve healthy and productive lives in their own communities.
resources.services: State funded regional center and the entry point for developmental disability services in both counties: intake and eligibility assessment, diagnosis and evaluation, lifelong individual program planning and service coordination, Early Start for infants and toddlers 0-3 with delays, purchase of services (respite, day programs, supported living, transportation), genetic counseling, and client advocacy. Free eligibility assessment; call intake to apply. Serves people with intellectual disability, cerebral palsy, epilepsy, autism, and related conditions.
resources.notes: Sacramento HQ: 4151 E Commerce Way, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95834. Serves ten counties: Alpine, Colusa, El Dorado, Nevada, Placer, Sacramento, Sierra, Sutter, Yolo, and Yuba (36,000+ clients). Confirmed from altaregional.org July 2026. Most nonprofit DD day programs in this tab are accessed via ACRC referral.
resources.contactPerson: Jennifer Bloom, Director of Client Services

resources.name: Alta California Regional Center (Transition and Adult Services)
resources.address: 4151 E Commerce Way, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95834
resources.mission: Alta California Regional Center creates partnerships to support all eligible individuals with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities.
resources.services: For regional center clients leaving school (typically ages 16-22): transition planning through the Individualized Program Plan (IPP), guidance on adult services including day programs, supported and competitive integrated employment, independent living services, supported living, and transportation. Publishes A Family Guide to Transition Planning and an adult services guide in multiple languages. WarmLine FRC's DDS-funded Community Navigator Program can pair families and adult clients with peer navigators. Eligibility: qualifying developmental disability under the Lanterman Act; services coordinated by assigned service coordinator.
resources.notes: Main office: 4151 E Commerce Way, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95834; serves a 10-county area including Sacramento and Placer. Youth in special education should start transition planning at the IEP by age 16. Cross-reference: Disability tab (regional center intake and family supports).

resources.name: Alyn W. Butler American Legion Post 169 (Roseville)
resources.mission: Long-established Roseville American Legion post providing community service and support to veterans and their families in south Placer County.
resources.services: Veteran fellowship and peer support; referrals to VA benefits and the Placer County Veterans Service Office; participation in the Roseville Veterans Memorial Hall Board; honor guard and memorial ceremonies; community and youth activities; American Legion Auxiliary Unit 169 support for military families.
resources.notes: Meets at Roseville Veterans Memorial Hall, 110 Park Dr., Roseville, CA 95678. No standalone website found; the number listed is the Roseville Veterans Memorial Hall contact - confirm a direct post contact.

resources.name: Alzheimer's Association (Northern California and Northern Nevada Chapter)
resources.address: 2710 S Gateway Oaks Drive, Suite 200, Sacramento, CA 95833
resources.mission: The Alzheimer's Association leads the way to end Alzheimer's and all other dementia by accelerating global research, driving risk reduction and early detection, and maximizing quality care and support.
resources.services: Free dementia services for both counties: 24/7 Helpline (800) 272-3900 with confidential support and crisis assistance in over 200 languages; peer and professionally led support groups (in-person and virtual) for caregivers and people with early-stage dementia; family care consultations to build care plans; education workshops and annual conferences; safety services; and online Community Resource Finder. Open to anyone affected by Alzheimer's or related dementias at no cost; call the Helpline any time to be connected.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 2710 S Gateway Oaks Drive, Suite 200, Sacramento, CA 95833; office phone (916) 930-9080. Chapter serves Northern California and Northern Nevada, including Placer and Sacramento counties. Cross-reference: In-home Help tab (dementia caregiving) and Crisis tab (24/7 helpline).

resources.name: American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (Greater Sacramento Chapter)
resources.mission: The grassroots work we do focuses on eliminating the loss of life from suicide by delivering innovative prevention programs, educating the public about risk factors and warning signs, raising funds for suicide research and programs, and reaching out to those individuals who have lost someone to suicide.
resources.services: Free community suicide prevention education: Talk Saves Lives (including Spanish and Latinx, and Black/African American L.E.T.S. Save Lives editions), More Than Sad for parents and school staff, It's Real: Teens and Mental Health, Finding Hope for those supporting someone at risk; suicide bereavement facilitator trainings (adult and children/teens tracks); International Survivors of Suicide Loss Day sites each November; Healing Conversations peer outreach for loss survivors; annual Out of the Darkness Walks including the Sacramento Walk (September 12, 2026) and Placer County Walk (October 10, 2026). Programs are free; request a program or register via website; many sessions offered virtually.
resources.notes: Chapter covers 19 counties from the Oregon border through the Sacramento Valley, including Placer and Sacramento. Contact email is published behind a protection script on the chapter page; use the website contact and program request forms. National 501(c)(3). In crisis: call or text 988 or text TALK to 741741.
resources.contactPerson: Lauren Pulido, Area Director, Greater Sacramento and Central Valley

resources.name: American River Area Narcotics Anonymous (ARANA)
resources.mission: Narcotics Anonymous is a nonprofit fellowship of men and women for whom drugs had become a major problem; members meet regularly to help each other stay clean. The only requirement for membership is a desire to stop using.
resources.services: NA area service body with meetings throughout Sacramento, Placer and Yolo counties: in person and online meetings daily, meeting finder at sacramentona.org, 24 hour helpline (call or text a zip code to (877) 623-6363 for current schedules). Free, anonymous, no registration or documentation. Sierra Foothills Area NA (sfana.org) covers Auburn and foothill communities.
resources.notes: No fixed public office; all access via helpline and website. Northern California Region of NA (norcalna.org) provides additional meeting listings.

resources.name: AMI Housing, Inc. (Advocates for Mentally Ill Housing)
resources.mission: AMI Housing is a California 501(c)(3) nonprofit that provides housing, employment, and life skills programs to residents of Placer and Nevada Counties who otherwise might be homeless, housing over 400 people every night.
resources.services: Broadest supportive housing portfolio in Placer: Sun Rose Apartments (82-unit Homekey permanent supportive housing, Roseville, tenants pay 30% of income); permanent supportive housing (62 beds, no time limit, max 40% of income); transitional housing (24 beds in shared homes in Roseville, Rocklin, Auburn, up to 2 years); peer supported housing (11 beds); TAY housing for ages ~16-25 (with Turning Point); Monarch House 2-week emergency respite (5 beds); CalWORKs and Bringing Families Home rapid rehousing; City of Roseville rapid rehousing and homeless prevention (short-term rent, utility, deposit help, ~125 households/year); ESG and HHAP rapid rehousing; housing coordination with landlord recruitment; 15-bed adult residential facility. Referrals via Housing Coordination Team.
resources.notes: Office: 3123 Professional Drive, Suite 210, Auburn, CA 95603. Hours M-F 9am-4pm (closed 12-1). Legal name Advocates for Mentally Ill Housing, Inc. Serves Placer and Nevada counties. Merged operations with Nevada County Housing Development Corp.

resources.name: AMI Housing, Inc. (Transition Age Youth Housing)
resources.mission: AMI Housing's mission is to house and support the most vulnerable residents of the Sierra Region. AMIH is a California 501(c)(3) nonprofit providing housing, employment, and life skills programs to residents of Placer and Nevada counties who otherwise might be homeless.
resources.services: TAY house: an 18-month residential program run in collaboration with Turning Point Community Programs that teaches young adults the independent living skills required to live in the community. Groceries, transportation, rent, utilities, and supportive services included; residents attend weekly check-in meetings and weekly life skills classes. Eligibility: young adults eligible for TAY services (generally 16-25, mental health system involvement). Office hours Monday-Friday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
resources.notes: Office: 3123 Professional Drive, Suite 210, Auburn, CA 95603; mail P.O. Box 5216, Auburn, CA 95604. Office closed for lunch noon to 1 p.m. Housing referrals: HCTeam@amihousing.org. TAY house (5 beds, since 2014) referrals typically flow through Placer County Adult System of Care/Turning Point; call to confirm current openings. Also partners with Whole Person Learning and Golden Sierra on youth housing (ages 16-24 in school or job training). Cross-reference: Housing tab and Mental Health category.

resources.name: Another Choice, Another Chance
resources.mission: Another Choice, Another Chance was founded in 1987 to improve the quality of life for youth and families, providing substance use, mental health, dual diagnosis and trauma informed care.
resources.services: Nonprofit outpatient SUD and behavioral health provider: individual and group counseling for substance use, mental health and trauma for youth, adults and families; intensive outpatient, recovery coaching, clean and sober living linkage, anger management, cognitive behavioral therapy, motivational interviewing, relapse prevention. Culturally responsive services rooted in South Sacramento. Referral form, email or phone intake; accepts Medi-Cal, government funding and self pay.
resources.notes: 7000 Franklin Blvd, Suite 200, Sacramento 95823. Longstanding county contracted provider serving predominantly African American and underserved communities.

resources.name: Anti-Recidivism Coalition (Sacramento office)
resources.mission: ARC's mission is to empower formerly and currently incarcerated people to thrive by providing a support network, comprehensive reentry services, and opportunities to advocate for policy change.
resources.services: Membership based reentry support for formerly and currently incarcerated people: intensive case management, support attaining education and stable housing, workforce development, clinical therapy and support groups, and opportunities for systems change advocacy. Sacramento office opened in 2016 and serves over 500 members in the region. Contact the office to become a member; services are free.
resources.notes: ARC's contact page lists (916) 942-9080 for the Sacramento office; the site footer lists (916) 850-3158 as an alternate. 501(c)(3), Tax ID 46-2140915. Cross-reference: Mentorship tab (peer mentoring and lifer support network).

resources.name: Anti-Recidivism Coalition (Sacramento Office)
resources.mission: The Anti-Recidivism Coalition (ARC) works to end mass incarceration in California. To ensure our communities are safe, healthy, and whole, ARC empowers formerly and currently incarcerated people to thrive by providing a support network, comprehensive reentry services, and opportunities to advocate for policy change.
resources.services: Reentry mentoring and peer support network for formerly incarcerated people (adult mentoring): membership includes life coaching by mentors with lived experience, intensive case management, trauma-informed counseling, housing assistance, workforce and education programs, and expungement help. Over 500 members in the Sacramento region. Prospective members complete an intake questionnaire on the website or visit the office.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 2830 G St Suite 210, Sacramento, CA 95816; Mon-Fri 9am-5pm. Main Sacramento number (916) 942-9080 per ARC contact page; (916) 850-3158 also appears on some ARC pages. Statewide 501(c)(3) headquartered in Los Angeles; Sacramento office open since 2016. Cross-reference: Employment (workforce programs) and Housing tabs. Recovery peers cross-ref: members access support groups and CBT skills training.

resources.name: Asian Pacific Community Counseling (Transcultural Wellness Center)
resources.mission: APCC, a community-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit incorporated in 1977, provides culturally and linguistically relevant outreach, prevention, education, therapy, counseling, and recovery support services to Asian and Pacific Islander communities in Sacramento.
resources.services: Outpatient mental health program funded by Sacramento County Behavioral Health serving all ages (children, transitional age youth, adults, older adults) with emphasis on Asian and Pacific Islander language and cultural groups: mental health assessment and treatment, individual, group and family therapy, medication support, psychoeducation and life skills training, socialization activities, and linkage to community supports. Multilingual staff; interpreters available through partner agencies. Access directly or through the county Access Team (888) 881-4881.
resources.notes: Note: this is the independent Sacramento nonprofit Asian Pacific Community Counseling, not the Los Angeles SSG division of similar name.

resources.name: Asian Resources, Inc. (Employment and Job Center Services)
resources.mission: Asian Resources, Inc. is committed to providing a wide spectrum of social services to low-income and limited-English-speaking youth, immigrant, and refugee communities in Sacramento, empowering the community through employment and training programs.
resources.services: Operates a SETA-funded Sacramento Works job center serving about 2,000 clients a year: personalized career coaching, resume development, interview preparation, job placement with subsidized on-the-job training (employers reimbursed 50 percent of wages up to 240 hours), Individual Training Account scholarships, paid work experience for out-of-school youth ages 18-24, Prison to Employment reentry services, one-on-one computer classes, typing tests, and refugee support services. Multilingual staff. Free; open weekdays during business hours.
resources.notes: ARI Job Center: 2411 Alhambra Blvd., Suite 110, Sacramento, CA 95817, (916) 324-6202. Headquarters: 6270 Elder Creek Rd., Sacramento, CA 95824, (916) 454-1892. Citrus Heights office: 5750 Sunrise Blvd., Suite 100, (916) 745-4313. Partner in SETA/Sacramento Works network. Serves all job seekers; specialty is immigrant, refugee, and limited-English populations.

resources.name: Assistance League of Greater Placer
resources.mission: Assistance League of Greater Placer is a nonprofit, all volunteer, charitable community service organization whose member volunteers are dedicated to improving lives of children and adults in Greater Placer communities through philanthropic programs.
resources.services: All volunteer thrift shop selling low cost clothing, baby clothes and accessories, housewares, linens, home decor, sporting goods, antiques, and jewelry; open to everyone, no eligibility requirements. Shop revenue funds 13 philanthropic programs including Operation School Bell (new school clothes for K-12 students referred by schools). Donors may drop off gently used clothing and household goods Tuesday, Wednesday, and Saturday, 11:00 am to 3:00 pm (donation area at the back left corner of the same shopping center); furniture and large donations preferred on Wednesdays and require management approval, call first. The shop no longer accepts men's shoes, books, CDs, DVDs, children's toys, or vinyl records. Shop hours Tuesday through Saturday, 11:00 am to 4:00 pm.
resources.notes: Thrift Shop at 1263 Grass Valley Highway, Auburn, CA 95603. Open Tue-Sat 11:00 am-4:00 pm; donations Tue, Wed, Sat 11:00 am-3:00 pm. Open to the public. Chapter office (530) 885-4397. Program services (school clothing) require school or agency referral. Cross-reference: Clothing tab (Operation School Bell).

resources.name: Assistance League of Greater Placer (Thrift Shop)
resources.mission: Assistance League of Greater Placer is a nonprofit, all volunteer, charitable community service organization whose member volunteers are dedicated to improving lives of children and adults in Greater Placer communities through philanthropic programs.
resources.services: All volunteer thrift shop selling low cost clothing, baby clothes and accessories, housewares, linens, home decor, sporting goods, antiques, and jewelry; open to everyone, no eligibility requirements. Shop revenue funds 13 philanthropic programs including Operation School Bell (new school clothes for K-12 students referred by schools). Donors may drop off gently used clothing and household goods Tuesday, Wednesday, and Saturday, 11:00 am to 3:00 pm (donation area at the back left corner of the same shopping center); furniture and large donations preferred on Wednesdays and require management approval, call first. The shop no longer accepts men's shoes, books, CDs, DVDs, children's toys, or vinyl records. Shop hours Tuesday through Saturday, 11:00 am to 4:00 pm.
resources.notes: Thrift Shop at 1263 Grass Valley Highway, Auburn, CA 95603. Open Tue-Sat 11:00 am-4:00 pm; donations Tue, Wed, Sat 11:00 am-3:00 pm. Open to the public. Chapter office (530) 885-4397. Program services (school clothing) require school or agency referral. Cross-reference: Clothing tab (Operation School Bell).

resources.name: Auburn Area Recreation and Park District (Youth Assistance Fund)
resources.mission: The Auburn Area Recreation and Park District established the Youth Assistance Fund to help ensure every child in the district can participate in recreational programs, providing program scholarships to lower income individuals and families.
resources.services: Program scholarships so lower income youth can participate in ARD recreation classes, camps, sports and aquatics. Open to individuals living in and out of the district boundaries as funding is available. Income eligibility guidelines apply; application available from the Customer Service Office ((530) 885-8461, option 6) or the Forms page at auburnrec.com. Fund is supported by donations through Friends of the Auburn Area Recreation and Parks, Inc.
resources.notes: ARD office: 123 Recreation Drive, Auburn, CA 95603; office hours Mon-Fri 9 am-5 pm. Serves the greater Auburn area; out-of-district youth may qualify as funding allows. Government program (independent special district).

resources.name: Auburn Senior Center
resources.address: 11960 Heritage Oak Place, Suite 15, Auburn, CA 95603
resources.mission: Our mission is to honor the dignity of seniors by enriching their quality of life while supporting their independence and vitality. We promote their participation in all aspects of community life by providing opportunities for socialization, recreation, education, information, health and fitness.
resources.services: Membership-based senior center serving adults 50+ since 1980: recreation (games, clubs, social events), education classes, exercise and fitness programs, AARP Tax-Aide free tax preparation (over 1,500 appointments yearly), resource information, room rentals, and annual community events. Membership $30/year single, $50/year couple; free membership for members 90+; scholarships available. Over 750 members.
resources.notes: Location: 11960 Heritage Oak Place, Suite 15, Auburn, CA 95603. Website active July 2026 with 2025 annual report posted. Tax assistance line (530) 830-2232 (seasonal, through mid-April).

resources.name: Bayanihan Clinic (UC Davis student-run free clinic)
resources.mission: Bayanihan Clinic provides accessible primary and preventative healthcare to Filipino immigrants and all diverse, underserved communities of the Greater Sacramento area, while honoring the legacy of Filipino veterans through advocacy and community engagement.
resources.services: Free primary and preventive care, prioritizing uninsured patients, Saturdays 8am-12pm (call ahead, walk-ins not guaranteed): specialty services include cardiovascular care, dental, dermatology, diabetes empowerment, mental wellness and psychiatry, ophthalmology, pediatrics, social services, and women's health; outreach to Filipino war veterans. Telehealth follow-ups offered; new patients seen in person. Languages: English, Tagalog, Spanish. No cost.
resources.notes: 3030 Explorer Drive, Sacramento, CA 95827 (clinic relocated; do not use older addresses). Clinic dates posted through July 2026 on the website; some Saturdays are telehealth-only. Cross-ref Veterans tab for veteran outreach.

resources.name: BenefitsCal (State of California online benefits portal)
resources.mission: BenefitsCal is the easiest way to apply for and manage California benefits online: food, health coverage, and cash assistance for the people of California.
resources.services: Statewide online portal to apply for and manage CalWORKs cash aid, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, and county General Assistance programs, available 24/7 in multiple languages. Users can apply, upload verification documents, report changes, review notices, check application status, and complete renewals. Applications route automatically to the applicant's county welfare department (Placer HHSA or Sacramento DHA), which completes the required interview by phone or in person.
resources.notes: No direct phone; for application help call Placer County Human Services (888) 385-5160 or Sacramento County DHA (800) 560-0976. Replaced the older C4Yourself and MyBenefits CalWIN portals. Cross-reference: Food tab (CalFresh applications).
resources.contactPerson: County Eligibility Staff (via county welfare department)

resources.name: Bereavement Network Resources of Sacramento (BNRS)
resources.mission: The Bereavement Network Resources of Sacramento offers supportive resources to help you process the feelings that come with grief, and maintains a directory of local resources that aid in the grief process.
resources.services: Volunteer nonprofit network operating since 1984. Publishes the free Community Bereavement Resource Directory (online at griefhelpsacramento.com/directory or mailed on request) listing grief support groups by loss type (spouse, child, suicide, overdose, pet loss), hospice bereavement programs, and 24-hour crisis lines for Sacramento and surrounding counties. Operates a phone and email referral line connecting grieving individuals to appropriate local support. Free, no eligibility requirements. Also hosts quarterly networking and education meetings for bereavement professionals and volunteers.
resources.notes: Mailing address: P.O. Box 660365, Sacramento, CA 95866. Referral and directory service, not a counseling provider; use as the gateway to find the right grief group. Phone (916) 557-5882 confirmed on the org's own website July 2026; 2026 edition of the directory is posted online. 501(c)(3), EIN 68-0027863 (GuideStar). Directory covers surrounding counties including Placer.

resources.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Northern Sierra
resources.address: 3461 Robin Lane Suite 2, Cameron Park, CA 95682
resources.mission: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Northern Sierra is a nonprofit organization dedicated to creating transformative, one-to-one mentoring relationships that ignite the potential of young people throughout El Dorado, Nevada, and eastern Placer counties.
resources.services: Community-based and school-based one-to-one mentoring matching adult and older peer volunteer Bigs with youth Littles for at least one year; matches meet weekly at school sites or several times monthly in the community. Free to families. Serves El Dorado, Nevada, and eastern Placer counties, including Truckee and North Lake Tahoe areas. Offices in Cameron Park (main), Placerville, and Grass Valley. Enrollment and volunteer applications via website or phone.
resources.notes: Main office: 3461 Robin Lane Suite 2, Cameron Park, CA 95682; Grass Valley office: 516 Brunswick Rd, Grass Valley, CA 95945, (530) 556-5771, Mon-Thu 10am-4pm; Truckee mailing: PO Box 393, Truckee, CA 96160. Florence Parks became CEO in 2025. GuideStar EIN 94-2523254. Old site bigsofnc.wordpress.com (Peggy Martin era, Pal Program) is outdated; confirm current Placer school sites and eligibility for specific Placer addresses by phone before referral. Serves north and east Placer communities not covered by BBBS Greater Sacramento (which serves South Placer).

resources.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters of the Greater Sacramento Area, Inc.
resources.mission: Our mission is to create and support one-to-one mentoring relationships with trusted adults which ignite the independence and creativity of youth.
resources.services: One-to-one community-based mentoring for children ages 8-18, primarily youth raised by single parents, relatives, or foster families: volunteer Bigs commit to at least one year and are professionally matched and supported; school and site-based mentoring programs also offered. Parents/guardians enroll a child via the website; volunteers apply online and complete screening and training. Free to families.
resources.notes: Office: 1750 Howe Ave Ste 250, Sacramento, CA 95825. Serving the region since 1964; stated service area includes Sacramento, Placer, Yolo, Yuba, San Joaquin, and other counties, with child enrollment historically focused on Sacramento, Yolo, and South Placer (Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln area). Confirm eligibility for specific Placer addresses at intake. General email info@bbbs-sac.org.
resources.contactPerson: Jacob Peterson, President and Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: Birth & Beyond Family Resource Centers
resources.mission: Birth & Beyond Family Resource Centers help build strong families, meet the needs of growing children, and ensure families receive the resources they need.
resources.services: Network of neighborhood family resource centers across Sacramento County offering Nurturing Parenting home visitation for pregnant women and families with children 0-5, parenting workshops and classes, crisis intervention, school readiness and Play & Learn groups, baby bonding and nutrition classes, support groups (including Spanish-language moms groups), community referrals, car seats after class completion, and family activities. Free; call the central line or contact the nearest center. Centers are operated by partner nonprofits: Sacramento Children's Home, La Familia Counseling Center, River Oak Center for Children, Mutual Assistance Network, Folsom Cordova Community Partnership, and WellSpace Health.
resources.notes: Central line (916) 244-1906 (Child Abuse Prevention Information and Referral) confirmed on birth-beyondfrc.com July 2026. Nine current sites: Meadowview and Valley Hi (Sacramento Children's Home, 4343 Williamsbourgh Dr), North Sacramento (1565 River Park Dr), WellSpace North Highlands (6015 Watt Ave), La Familia (5523 34th St), River Oak FRC (4625 44th St), Folsom Cordova Community Partnership (10665 Coloma Rd), and Robertson (3525 Norwood Ave) and Arcade (2427 Marconi Ave) centers run by Mutual Assistance Network. Referral by zip code via online forms on the Locations page. Funded by First 5 Sacramento. Serves CPS-involved and prevention-focused families.
resources.contactPerson: Program Director (via The Child Abuse Prevention Center, network coordinator)

resources.name: Bishop Gallegos Maternity Home
resources.mission: The home answers the call of Sacramento's homeless pregnant women and their infants in providing the fundamental human needs of food, clothing, shelter and emotional support, while respecting each individual's personal journey and preserving their dignity.
resources.services: Free residential maternity shelter for homeless pregnant women: shelter, food, safety, comfort, and support during pregnancy and for a short time after birth. Two 6-bedroom houses in South Sacramento. Non-denominational; serving the Sacramento area since 1992; 2,000+ women and babies helped. Access by phone inquiry and intake.
resources.notes: South Sacramento locations (addresses semi-confidential for resident safety). Length of stay: through pregnancy plus a short postpartum period. Also at bgmhsacramento.org.

resources.name: Boys & Girls Club of Placer County
