resources.mission: To inspire and empower all young people who pass through our doors to realize their full potential as productive, responsible and caring citizens.
resources.services: After-school care during the school year plus holiday and summer camp programs (including Level Up All Sports Camp) for school-age youth: homework help, education, character development, career exploration, sports and recreation, arts and community service. Operating since 1994 at four sites: Mullin & McAdams Clubhouse & Teen Center (679 Lincoln Way, Auburn, TK-12th), E.V. Cain Extension (150 Palm Ave, Auburn), Auburn Elementary Extension (11400 Lariat Ranch Rd) and Union Pacific Railroad Clubhouse (313 High St, Roseville, 1st-8th). Registration for 2026-2027 after-school care opens July 13, 2026 via the website.
resources.notes: Headquarters: 679 Lincoln Way, Auburn, CA 95603 (fax (530) 889-2532). Roseville clubhouse: (916) 789-7884. Low-cost membership; confirm current fees when referring. 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

resources.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Sacramento
resources.mission: Our mission is to inspire and enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, caring, and responsible citizens.
resources.services: After-school and summer programs at neighborhood clubhouses and school-based sites, including the Thomas P. Raley Teen Center (1117 G Street): homework help, academic support, character and leadership development, arts, sports and healthy lifestyles programming for school-age youth and teens. Low-cost annual membership; targeted to youth who need the club most. Contact the administrative office for club locations and registration.
resources.notes: Administrative office: 5212 Lemon Hill Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95824 (also the Teichert Branch). Sacramento County sites include Raley Teen Center (1117 G Street), North Laguna Branch (7400 Imagination Parkway), Rancho Cordova Youth Center (10455 Investment Cir) and elementary school clubs (Fairbanks, Hillsdale, Navigator); council also operates clubs in Woodland and Stockton. 501(c)(3) nonprofit (EIN 68-0338324).

resources.name: Bridges Professional Treatment Services, Inc.
resources.mission: Bridges provides a wide variety of exceptional alcohol and drug treatment services for the Greater Sacramento area, helping individuals and families build lasting recovery.
resources.services: Nonprofit outpatient and intensive outpatient SUD treatment for adults: assessment, individual, group and family counseling, case management, court mandated services including Sacramento County DUI Treatment Court and drug diversion, CPS referral programs, Celebrating Families, STARS and ROOMS for Dads parenting programs, and Promise House sober living environment for women and women with children in downtown Sacramento. Intake (916) 453-2704; Medi-Cal and sliding fees.
resources.notes: Main office: 3600 Power Inn Rd, Suite C, Sacramento 95826. 501(c)(3) confirmed via GuideStar (EIN 52-2129001). DUI program is nonprofit run, within category scope.

resources.name: CalFresh (administered by Placer County HHSA and Sacramento County DHA)
resources.mission: CalFresh, federally known as SNAP, provides monthly food benefits to assist low-income households in purchasing the food they need.
resources.services: Monthly food benefits on an EBT card for income-eligible households; benefits can be used at grocery stores, farmers markets, some restaurants, and online retailers. Listed in this Financial tab as a core income support for household budgets: applying for CalFresh alongside cash aid often frees cash for rent and utilities. Apply at BenefitsCal.com, by phone, or in person at the county welfare office; interview by phone available; expedited 3-day service for households with very low income or resources.
resources.notes: Placer intake: (888) 385-5160; Sacramento intake: (800) 560-0976. Primary listing with full detail is in the Food tab; cross-referenced here as an income-stabilizing benefit.

resources.name: California Capital Financial Development Corporation (Lending Center and Women's Business Center)
resources.mission: California Capital's mission is to provide capital and capacity to serve communities, offering fair financing options to entrepreneurs and small business owners who cannot access traditional financing, with the goal of creating asset and wealth development in low-to-moderate-income and historically underinvested communities.
resources.services: Nonprofit financial development corporation founded in 1982, certified CDFI: small business loans, state loan guarantees, the SBA-funded California Capital Women's Business Center (free one-on-one counseling, DreamBuilder online business plan course in English and Spanish, Licensed to Care childcare business training, classes and workshops open to all genders at low or no cost), and the California Capital APEX Accelerator for government contracting help. Also hosts the Sacramento Valley SBDC. Register through the online calendar or call.
resources.notes: WBC hours Mon-Fri 8:30am-5pm, evening and weekend appointments by request, in person, online or by phone. Lending serves a broad Northern and Central California footprint including the Sacramento region; WBC training open regardless of gender. Cross-reference: hosts Sacramento Valley SBDC (separate row).
resources.contactPerson: Sophia Kanaan, Director, Women's Business Center

resources.name: California Department of Health Care Services (CalAIM Community Supports, in-home services)
resources.mission: CalAIM (California Advancing and Innovating Medi-Cal) is a long-term commitment to transform and strengthen Medi-Cal, offering Californians a more equitable, coordinated, and person-centered approach to maximizing their health and life trajectory.
resources.services: Medi-Cal managed care plans in both counties may offer Community Supports relevant to in-home help: personal care and homemaker services, respite services for caregivers, home modifications (environmental accessibility adaptations), medically tailored home-delivered meals, and nursing facility transition services. Plans differ by county: in Placer County most Medi-Cal members are in Partnership HealthPlan of California (Kaiser serves some eligible members); in Sacramento County members choose among Anthem Blue Cross, Health Net, Kaiser, and Molina. Which Community Supports are offered varies by plan, so members should request services through their plan's member services line or care manager; Enhanced Care Management is also available for members with complex needs.
resources.notes: Summary row: not a direct provider; services are requested through each member's Medi-Cal managed care plan and offerings differ by plan and county. Phone listed is the DHCS Medi-Cal Managed Care Ombudsman. Placer County transitioned to Partnership HealthPlan of California (partnershiphp.org, member services (800) 863-4155) on January 1, 2024. Verify current Community Supports menus with each plan.

resources.name: California Department of Rehabilitation (Sacramento District)
resources.mission: The Department of Rehabilitation works in partnership with consumers and other stakeholders to provide services and advocacy resulting in employment, independent living, and equality for individuals with disabilities.
resources.services: Vocational rehabilitation for adults and transition-age youth with physical, intellectual, or mental health disabilities that create barriers to employment: career counseling, individualized plans for employment, funded vocational training and education, assistive technology, job placement assistance, on-the-job supports, and student services for youth with disabilities. Apply at any office or online; eligibility based on documented disability affecting employment. Offices open weekdays 8am-5pm.
resources.notes: Local offices: Sacramento District (main), Auburn branch (530) 823-4040, Roseville branch (916) 774-4400. TTY (916) 558-5673. Referrals to partner vendors such as PRIDE Industries for job coaching and supported employment.

resources.name: California Department of Rehabilitation (Student Services / Youth Services)
resources.mission: The Department of Rehabilitation works in partnership with consumers and other stakeholders to provide services and advocacy resulting in employment, independent living, and equality for individuals with disabilities.
resources.services: Pre-employment transition services for students with disabilities ages 16-21 who have an IEP or 504 plan: job exploration counseling, work-based learning and paid work experiences, counseling on post-secondary options, workplace readiness training, self-advocacy instruction. No DOR case required for student services; students, parents, or schools can contact the local office or email the Youth Services inbox. Adult vocational rehabilitation services available after application.
resources.notes: The Sacramento Northern Sierra district serves Sacramento and Placer counties through Sacramento area branch offices; district youth services inbox YouthServices_SacramentoNorthernSierra@dor.ca.gov (DOR site, checked July 2026). DOR no longer publishes named student services coordinators; email the statewide or district inbox to be routed. DOR's online application was temporarily unavailable in July 2026; contact the local office to apply. Cross-reference: Employment and Disability categories.
resources.contactPerson: Youth Services, Sacramento Northern Sierra District

resources.name: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (Taxpayers' Rights Advocate and Small Business Liaison)
resources.mission: The Taxpayers' Rights Advocate Office helps taxpayers who are unable to resolve a problem through normal channels, and serves as the small business liaison for the CDTFA to help small business owners understand and comply with sales and use tax and fee requirements.
resources.services: Free government help for small business owners on state sales and use tax and special fees: seller's permit questions, help resolving disputes, collections issues and audit concerns when normal channels fail, free tax education classes and webinars for new businesses. Available to any California business owner; call the advocate line or use online services at cdtfa.ca.gov.
resources.notes: Physical address 651 Bannon St, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95811; mailing address PO Box 942879, MIC 70, Sacramento, CA 94279-0070. Statewide, serves both counties. For state income tax issues, the Franchise Tax Board has a separate Taxpayers' Rights Advocate reachable through ftb.ca.gov, (800) 852-5711 general line. Government information and dispute resolution service, not financial assistance.

resources.name: California Employment Development Department (Workforce Services)
resources.mission: The EDD connects millions of job seekers and employers in an effort to build the economy of the Golden State, providing workforce services, job search tools, and labor market information for California.
resources.services: State workforce services delivered through America's Job Centers in both counties: CalJOBS online job matching system (caljobs.ca.gov), job search workshops, resume assistance, referrals to training and education providers, veteran employment representatives (Jobs for Veterans State Grant), and unemployment insurance claimant reemployment services. Free to all California job seekers. CalJOBS help line 1-800-758-0398; workforce services line open weekdays 8am-5pm.
resources.notes: EDD workforce staff are co-located in America's Job Centers operated by Golden Sierra (Placer) and SETA/Sacramento Works (Sacramento). Sacramento office at 2901 50th St., Sacramento, (916) 227-0301. Unemployment insurance claims: 1-800-300-5616 (separate from workforce services).

resources.name: California Franchise Tax Board (Free Tax Help, CalFile, and CalEITC)
resources.mission: The Franchise Tax Board provides free tax help through Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) locations and the free CalFile application, and administers the California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC) which may provide cash back or reduce tax owed.
resources.services: State EITC outreach and free filing: CalEITC for workers earning up to $32,900 (2025 tax year) with a valid SSN or ITIN, plus the Young Child Tax Credit; CalFile for free direct e-filing of state returns; referrals to VITA sites statewide (FTB directs users to the IRS VITA Site Locator). Phone assistance for state tax questions Monday-Friday. Filing a return is required to claim CalEITC even when no tax is owed.
resources.notes: State government agency; services delivered online and by phone, with a Sacramento field office at 3321 Power Inn Road (check website for hours). ITIN filers qualify for CalEITC even though they are excluded from the federal EITC.

resources.name: California Indian Heritage Center Foundation (State Indian Museum)
resources.mission: The mission of the California Indian Heritage Center Foundation is to procure funding in support of the interpretive and educational programs and projects of the State Indian Museum, and to support development of the future California Indian Heritage Center.
resources.services: Nonprofit foundation (est. 2009) supporting Native cultural and educational programming at the State Indian Museum State Historic Park in midtown Sacramento: Native-oriented special events, the Native Education for All lecture series, cultural demonstrations, and exhibits of California Indian cultural items. Museum open to the public (admission fee; children low-cost). The Foundation also supports the California Indian Heritage Center in West Sacramento, which broke ground in April 2026; phase one (outdoor welcome area and amphitheater seating) is expected to open in fall 2026.
resources.notes: State Indian Museum: 2618 K St, Sacramento, CA 95816 (adjacent to Sutter's Fort). Cultural enrichment rather than social services; useful for families seeking cultural connection, school programs, and community events. Future CIHC site is in West Sacramento (Yolo County). Phone listed is the State Indian Museum; the Foundation museum store is (916) 324-8112.
resources.contactPerson: Board of Directors, California Indian Heritage Center Foundation

resources.name: California Indian Legal Services (Sacramento Office)
resources.mission: California Indian Legal Services is committed to securing justice for California's Tribal peoples by protecting and advancing Indian rights, self-determination, and tribal nation-building, offering free or low-cost representation to Native individuals and tribes in matters of federal Indian law.
resources.services: Nonprofit statewide Indian law firm; the Sacramento office (the CILS principal office) serves the Sacramento and Placer region. Legal help in all areas of federal Indian law: Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA) cases for parents, Indian custodians, and tribes; tribal enrollment issues; Indian estate planning and probate (wills for trust or restricted property); Public Law 280 and jurisdiction issues; tribal governance; and individual Indian rights. Free brief counsel and representation for income-eligible Native Americans; flexible fee structure otherwise. Call or use the website intake to request help; statewide toll-free line available.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 106 K St, Suite 300, Sacramento, CA 95814 (mail and donations: PO Box 1167, Sacramento, CA 95812); toll free (800) 829-0284; fax (916) 400-4891. Serves clients across Northern California including Placer County residents. Income eligibility applies for free services. Cross-reference: Legal category.

resources.name: California Office of the Small Business Advocate (CalOSBA, GO-Biz)
resources.mission: CalOSBA supports economic growth by providing resources and support to the state's 4.3 million small businesses, helping small business owners find and navigate resources, programs and regulations so they can start, manage, grow, become more resilient, and thrive.
resources.services: State government hub within the Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development: free navigation help to the statewide network of small business technical assistance centers (SBDCs, Women's Business Centers, VBOC and other centers searchable by zip code at calosba.ca.gov), information on state grants, loans and loan guarantees, disaster preparedness and recovery resources, and permit and regulation guidance. Open to all California small businesses and nonprofits at no cost.
resources.notes: Statewide program serving both counties. Use the Centers Search page to find free advising nearby. Information and navigation service, not a direct lender; contact via website form if phone line is busy.
resources.contactPerson: Office of the Small Business Advocate staff

resources.name: California Poison Control System (Poison Help Line)
resources.mission: The California Poison Control System provides fast, free, expert help for poison emergencies and questions 24 hours a day, every day, with calls kept confidential.
resources.services: Call (800) 222-1222 any time, 24/7/365, for poison exposures or questions: medicines, household chemicals, plants, bites and stings, food poisoning, drug interactions. Answered by pharmacists, nurses, and poison specialists. Interpreter services in 200+ languages. Free and confidential; serves all California residents. Text and online resources at calpoison.org.
resources.notes: Administered by the UCSF School of Pharmacy. Call 911 if the person is unconscious, not breathing, or seizing.
resources.contactPerson: Public Information Office, California Poison Control System (UCSF School of Pharmacy)

resources.name: California Rural Legal Assistance Foundation (Sacramento Office)
resources.mission: CRLAF is a statewide nonprofit providing legal services and policy advocacy for California's rural poor, focusing on marginalized communities including the unrepresented, the unorganized, and the undocumented.
resources.services: Immigration legal assistance through its Citizenship and Immigrant Integration Project and removal defense program: naturalization application help, DACA, VAWA, T visas, U visas, family-based relief, asylum and SIJS for unaccompanied minors, removal defense in Northern California and the Central Valley, plus know your rights, family emergency planning, and immigration fraud protection education. Also farmworker employment and housing rights work. Access by phone or website intake; free for low-income rural and immigrant clients.
resources.notes: 2210 K Street, Suite 201, Sacramento, CA 95816 (confirmed July 2026); main (916) 446-7904; Citizenship and Immigrant Integration Project voicemail intake line (916) 446-7901; info@crlaf.org. EIN 94-2800442. Statewide rural focus headquartered in Sacramento; prioritizes farmworker and rural immigrant communities, which includes rural Placer and south Sacramento County. Distinct from California Rural Legal Assistance Inc (CRLA); the Foundation handles immigration.

resources.name: California State University, Sacramento (Center for Counseling & Diagnostic Services)
resources.mission: The Center's mission is to offer free and low-cost, accessible services to the Sacramento community, provided by trained graduate students supervised by experienced faculty in the Counselor Education program at Sacramento State.
resources.services: University training clinic operating for more than 50 years: individual, partner, couples, and family counseling plus career counseling, groups, workshops, and low-cost educational/diagnostic testing of K-12 students for learning disabilities. Most services free or low-cost; open to the general public. Services offered during the academic year (September-December and February-May). Call or book an appointment online; no insurance required.
resources.notes: Eureka Hall, Room 421, Sacramento State campus, 6000 J Street, Sacramento. Hours 8 am-noon and 1-5 pm (summer 7:30 am-noon, 12:30-4 pm). Closed between academic terms; plan around semester calendar.

resources.name: California State University, Sacramento (Guardian Scholars Program)
resources.mission: The Sacramento State Guardian Scholars Program is committed to improving educational outcomes for students with lived experience in foster care by providing holistic wraparound support and a comprehensive range of services.
resources.services: Wraparound support for university students with lived experience in foster care: academic advising, priority on-campus housing, priority registration, textbook assistance, scholarships, and community. The Guardian Scholars Promise guarantees admission to Sacramento State and the program for youth who experienced foster care (and homelessness under McKinney-Vento) who meet CSU eligibility requirements. Contact the office to apply.
resources.notes: Sacramento Hall, Room 118, 6000 J Street, Sacramento, CA 95819. Largest Guardian Scholars enrollment in Northern California (approximately 195 students). Launched 2006; Guardian Scholars Promise guaranteed-admission pathway announced November 2024.

resources.name: California State University, Sacramento (Project Rebound)
resources.mission: Project Rebound assists formerly incarcerated students to prepare, apply, enroll, and graduate with a degree from Sacramento State, transforming formerly incarcerated individuals into scholars through counseling, mentoring, academic resources, and career development.
resources.services: Support program for formerly incarcerated and system-impacted students at Sac State: admissions application help, academic and financial counseling, peer mentoring and tutoring, career placement, a dedicated student center, and transitional housing in university-owned homes near campus (first such housing program in Northern California). Serves 50 to 60 students per year; fewer than 1 percent of participants return to prison. Contact the office to apply, including from inside prison by mail.
resources.notes: Office: Sacramento Hall, Room 161, 6000 J Street, Sacramento, CA 95819; hours Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Staff offices in Sacramento Hall 152-154. Housing coordinator: Harold Jordan, (916) 278-1145, haroldjordan2@csus.edu. Part of the multi-campus CSU Project Rebound consortium. Cross-reference: Mentorship tab.

resources.name: California Victim Compensation Board (CalVCB)
resources.mission: The California Victim Compensation Board is a state program that helps victims of violent crime, including domestic violence, by reimbursing eligible crime-related expenses.
resources.services: State compensation for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking: can reimburse medical and dental care, mental health treatment, income loss, funeral expenses, home security improvements, and relocation costs (relocation is frequently used by DV survivors). Apply online at victims.ca.gov, by mail, or with free help from county victim advocates: Placer County DA Victim/Witness (916) 543-8000 or Sacramento County DA Victim/Witness (916) 874-6218. Filing deadlines and cooperation requirements apply, with exceptions for DV; no cost to apply.
resources.notes: Verified at victims.ca.gov July 2026: phone (800) 777-9229 and email info@victims.ca.gov confirmed on the CalVCB contact page. Mailing address: CalVCB, P.O. Box 3036, Sacramento, CA 95812-3036. Apply online at online.victims.ca.gov. DV survivors do not need a police report in all cases (restraining orders and other records can support claims); ask a county victim advocate for filing help.

resources.name: CalWORKs Homeless Assistance (Placer County HHS / Sacramento County DHA)
resources.mission: CalWORKs Homeless Assistance is an entitlement program in all 58 California counties that helps families in or apparently eligible for CalWORKs meet the costs of temporary shelter and securing or maintaining permanent housing.
resources.services: Two components: Temporary HA pays up to 16 days of temporary shelter (hotel or motel), issued 3 days at a time initially then up to 7 days at a time. Permanent HA pays security deposit and last month's rent, legal move-in fees (application fees, credit check, pet deposit), OR up to 2 months of rent arrearages to prevent eviction (housing cost generally must not exceed 80% of family income). Available once every 12 months, with exceptions for domestic violence, medically verified illness, or uninhabitability. Family must be homeless or at risk and CalWORKs-eligible. Same-day issuance rules apply for temporary HA.
resources.notes: Apply at Placer County Human Services (Rocklin/Auburn) or Sacramento County DHA bureaus (e.g., 2700 Fulton Ave), or via BenefitsCal.com. State fact sheet at cdss.ca.gov. Sacramento DHA also administers General Assistance for indigent adults.

resources.name: CalWORKs Housing Support Program (Placer County HHS / Sacramento County DHA)
resources.mission: The CalWORKs Housing Support Program fosters housing stability for CalWORKs families experiencing or at risk of homelessness, offering financial assistance and wraparound supportive services so families can secure and keep permanent housing.
resources.services: Housing-related financial assistance for CalWORKs families: rental assistance and subsidies, security deposits, utility payments, moving costs, hotel and motel vouchers, housing navigation, landlord mediation, and case management. Placer County operates HSP through HHS with nonprofit partners (VOA, Stand Up Placer, AMI Housing); Housing First principles, up to 12 months of subsidy within a 36-month period. Sacramento County operates HSP through the Department of Human Assistance; voluntary, does not reduce the CalWORKs grant. Must be a current CalWORKs recipient (or apparently eligible) who is homeless or at risk. Ask the CalWORKs worker for an HSP referral.
resources.notes: Placer intake: Placer County Human Services, 1000 Sunset Blvd Suite 220, Rocklin, and Auburn Government Center, (888) 385-5160. Sacramento intake: DHA bureaus, (916) 874-3100. Apply via BenefitsCal.com. NOTE: Sacramento HSP state funding has been reduced in recent budget cycles; confirm current availability. Distinct from CalWORKs Homeless Assistance (next entry); families may use both.

resources.name: CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work Employment Services (Placer County HHS / Sacramento County DHA)
resources.mission: County welfare departments provide CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work services that offer education, employment, and training programs to support families moving toward self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Mandatory and voluntary employment services for CalWORKs cash aid recipients: work activities, community work experience, job search and job readiness training, education and training (high school completion, community college, ESL, GED), subsidized employment placements, plus supportive services paid in advance including Stage One child care, transportation (bus passes, mileage), school or work expenses, diaper assistance for children under 36 months, and mental health, substance use, and domestic violence services. Placer delivers Employment Services (formerly Welfare to Work) through its Business Advantage Network; Sacramento through DHA and SETA partners. Apply at BenefitsCal.com or county offices; must have eligible children and meet income limits.
resources.notes: Sacramento DHA service center: 1-800-560-0976 (case information and reasonable accommodations). Placer CalWORKs application and intake: 1-888-385-5160, (916) 784-6000, or (530) 889-7610; offices in Auburn (Placer County Government Center), Rocklin (1000 Sunset Blvd., Suite 220), and Carnelian Bay. State program administered by both county welfare departments; details at placer.ca.gov/2111 and ha.saccounty.gov.

resources.name: CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work Transportation Assistance (Sacramento DHA / Placer HHS)
resources.mission: Counties must provide CalWORKs participants with supportive services, including transportation, that are necessary to participate in assigned Welfare-to-Work activities or to obtain or retain employment.
resources.services: Government benefit inside CalWORKs: participants in approved Welfare-to-Work activities (job search, training, education, work) are entitled to transportation supportive services, typically monthly bus passes or per-mile reimbursement, paid by the county welfare department. Request through your CalWORKs employment case manager. Sacramento County: Department of Human Assistance Service Center, (800) 560-0976, apply at BenefitsCal.com. Placer County: Health and Human Services, Human Services Division, (888) 385-5160.
resources.notes: Not a standalone program: bus passes and gas/mileage reimbursement flow through each county's CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work plan. Placer info: placer.ca.gov/2111/CalWORKs-Employment-Services. Sacramento community college CalWORKs offices also issue transportation help for student participants. Cross-reference: gateway rows in Financial Assistance category (DHA, Placer HHS).
resources.contactPerson: CalWORKs Employment Services Case Manager (assigned at intake)

resources.name: Capital Pro Bono, Inc. (formerly Voluntary Legal Services Program of Northern California)
resources.mission: Capital Pro Bono's mission is to secure access to justice for low income people through the use of volunteers donating pro bono assistance, and by educating clients about the law to increase their knowledge and self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Free civil legal help for low income residents of Northern California through volunteer attorneys in four areas: Debt Collection Defense and Bankruptcy (Debt Clinic), Employment Law and Misdemeanor Expungement Projects, Guardianship and Conservatorship, and the Family Law Assistance Project (priority to Sacramento County cases; direct line (916) 551-2166). Services in person, by phone, and online; eligibility screening required before any appointment. Call intake at (916) 551-2102. Cannot assist with criminal cases, anyone in jail or prison, minors, or anyone seeking to sue.
resources.notes: Office at 1860 Howe Avenue, Suite 130, Sacramento, CA 95825. Renamed from Voluntary Legal Services Program (VLSP) in 2020 (confirmed on capitalprobono.org); founded 1981, created with LSNC and the Sacramento County Bar Association. Current site says Northern California and Sacramento region; Placer County is not named, so Placer residents should call to confirm coverage before relying on it. Placer County's Clean Slate page refers Sacramento residents here for expungement help. Cross-reference: Sacramento County Public Defender row for felony record relief.

resources.name: CASA of Placer, Yuba and Sutter (formerly Child Advocates of Placer County)
resources.mission: CASA Connects envisions a world where every child feels safe, valued, and supported, and where families are strengthened, cycles of abuse are broken, and communities are transformed through compassion and connection.
resources.services: Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) who advocate for and mentor abused, neglected, and at-risk children in the juvenile dependency system; Be Bold one-to-one mentorship matching youth with trained adult mentors; K9s 4 Kids; Family Services volunteer mentors for parents with children in or at risk of entering foster care. Volunteers must be 21 or older, pass background checks, and complete about 30 hours of training. Referrals accepted from families, schools, and county agencies via website.
resources.notes: Auburn based; EIN 77-0620948 (same legal entity as Child Advocates of Placer County, rebranded and expanded to Placer, Yuba, and Sutter counties). Website active July 2026 with 2025 impact report. Be Bold is their dedicated non-court youth mentoring program. Cross-reference: Foster tab (CASA and Family Services programs).

resources.name: Center for Employment Opportunities (CEO Sacramento)
resources.mission: The Center for Employment Opportunities Sacramento provides immediate, effective, and comprehensive employment services exclusively to people recently released from incarceration, supporting successful transitions to stable, productive lives.
resources.services: Transitional jobs program exclusively for people recently released from incarceration, most on probation or parole. After a one week job readiness orientation, participants get up to four days a week of paid transitional crew work (maintenance and neighborhood beautification) with daily pay, plus job coaching on non-work days, full-time job placement, and 12 months of retention support after placement. Free; serves Sacramento County residents. Enroll by emailing referralssacramento@ceoworks.org or through probation/parole referral. Office hours 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Opened in Sacramento in 2019.
resources.notes: Office: 444 North 3rd Street, Suite 230, Sacramento, CA 95811. Participant referrals: referralssacramento@ceoworks.org; partnerships: cathomas@ceoworks.org. National nonprofit (501c3) with Sacramento office. Cross-reference: Employment tab.

resources.name: Center for Fathers and Families
resources.mission: The Center for Fathers and Families is committed to strengthening and empowering families by promoting responsible fatherhood and family involvement.
resources.services: Father engagement and parent education nonprofit. Parenting classes cover parenting styles, boundaries, anger management, child development stages, discipline, self-esteem, family conflict, and communication. Current schedule: Practical Parenting Tuesdays 4-5 pm; Co-Parenting Tuesdays 5 pm; Taming Your Temper (anger management) Tuesdays 4 pm; Daddy's Here father support group Thursdays 7 pm; one-on-one sessions and virtual classes available. Classes carry fees (register or pay via website; call to confirm court-ordered certificate requirements). Also offers Dealing with Teenagers and Being a Mom support groups, drug testing by appointment (including court ordered), M.A.S.T.E.R.S expanded learning youth programs, and family events.
resources.notes: 920 Del Paso Boulevard, Sacramento, CA 95815; office (916) 568-DADS (3237); general email info@cffsacramento.org. Operating status, address, phone, Terry Moore x210 contact, and class schedule confirmed on cffsacramento.org July 2026 (agency is actively hiring). Court approval of co-parenting classes could not be confirmed on the org's site; verify with Sacramento Superior Court family court services before advising court-ordered clients. Other father resources: Native Dads Network, United and Guided Fatherhood Support Services.

resources.name: Central California Fellowship of Alcoholics Anonymous (CCFAA)
resources.mission: Alcoholics Anonymous is a fellowship of people who share their experience, strength and hope with each other that they may solve their common problem and help others to recover from alcoholism. CCFAA is the intergroup serving the greater Sacramento area since 1954.
resources.services: Nonprofit AA intergroup/central office: 24 hour hotline (916) 454-1100 staffed by volunteers, online and printed meeting schedules for hundreds of weekly meetings across the greater Sacramento area, literature sales, 12 step call coordination, outreach to institutions. Free; no registration, insurance or documentation; the only requirement for membership is a desire to stop drinking.
resources.notes: Office: 9960 Business Park Dr, Suite 110, Sacramento 95827. Mailing: 3643 Bradshaw Rd, Ste G PMB 176, Sacramento 95827. Hotline also serves Placer County callers.

resources.name: CEPS (Community Engaged Payee Support)
resources.address: 3111 Fulton Avenue (Suite 101 for client mail), Sacramento, CA 95821
resources.mission: CEPS provides assistance for individuals who have difficulty managing their day-to-day financial affairs, with services designed to meet each client's individual money management needs while serving as representative payee.
resources.services: Social Security representative payee and money management services for people who have difficulty managing their day-to-day finances, including elderly and disabled recipients of SSI/SSA benefits: monthly budgeting, bill payment, financial record keeping, and protection from financial fraud, abuse, or exploitation; funds disbursed by check, direct deposit, or prepaid Rapid! card. Organizational payee fees are capped by the Social Security Administration, which sets the maximum monthly fee each year. To enroll, download intake forms from the website or request them by mail, email, or fax; after CEPS submits the application, allow 15 to 45 days for SSA to redirect benefits.
resources.notes: 3111 Fulton Avenue (Suite 101 for client mail), Sacramento, CA 95821; fax (916) 348-1894. 501(c)(3) serving Sacramento and Stanislaus Counties (Modesto office (209) 544-8591). Operating status, phone, and address confirmed on the org's own site (July 2026). SSA must approve payee assignment. Placer County residents needing payee services should call 211 for the current Placer provider.

resources.name: Chapa-De Indian Health (Auburn Health Center)
resources.mission: The mission of Chapa-De Indian Health is to advance the health and well-being of American Indians and low income individuals living in our communities by providing convenient access to high-quality, compassionate care.
resources.services: Nonprofit tribal health program and safety-net clinic: adult and pediatric primary medical care, comprehensive dental (exams through dentures and orthodontics), optometry (eye exams age 4 and up at Auburn), behavioral health (psychiatry and therapy), in-house pharmacy with reduced-cost medications, prenatal care (Baby Luv), diabetes prevention, substance use disorder treatment, and telehealth. Open to everyone: priority is American Indians, Alaska Natives, and low-income patients, but care is provided regardless of ethnicity or financial situation. Accepts Medi-Cal and Medicare; sliding fee scale based on income for the uninsured. After-hours nurse and dentist advice via main number.
resources.notes: Auburn Health Center: 11670 Atwood Road, Auburn, CA 95603; hours 8am-5pm, closed 12-1pm. Second clinic in Grass Valley (Nevada County), (530) 477-8545. A new South Placer Health Center at 1451 W. Stanford Ranch Road, Rocklin (medical, dental, behavioral health) is scheduled to open early 2027. Serves non-Native patients: confirmed on chapa-de.org.

resources.name: Chapa-De Indian Health (Auburn Health Center)
resources.mission: Chapa-De's mission is to advance the health and well-being of American Indians and low income individuals living in our communities by providing convenient access to high-quality, compassionate care.
resources.services: Nonprofit tribal FQHC founded under the United Auburn Indian Community. Adult and pediatric primary medical care, dental and orthodontia, behavioral health counseling and psychiatry, substance use disorder treatment (all addictive disorders), optometry, pharmacy, nutrition and health education, women's health, prenatal Baby Luv program, telehealth. Verified American Indian / Alaska Native patients (federally recognized and California tribes) receive services at no cost through Indian Health Service funding; low-income non-Native community members also served on Medi-Cal, Medicare, private insurance, or sliding scale. Call to enroll as a new patient; bring tribal enrollment documentation for IHS eligibility. Auburn clinic open weekdays 8:00am to 5:00pm (closed 12:00pm to 1:00pm).
resources.notes: Auburn Health Center: 11670 Atwood Rd, Auburn, CA 95603. Second clinic at 1350 E Main St, Grass Valley (Nevada County), (530) 477-8545, serves Placer residents near the county line; a new South Placer Health Center is in development (see chapa-de.org). Serves Native and non-Native patients. Native patients with verified AI/AN status receive no-cost services and medications. Cross-reference: Health category.

resources.name: Chapa-De Indian Health (Behavioral Health and Medication Assisted Treatment)
resources.mission: Chapa-De Indian Health provides medical, dental, optometry, behavioral health and substance use disorder services, advancing the health and well-being of American Indian people and other community members with high quality, compassionate care.
resources.services: Outpatient substance use disorder services integrated with primary care: medication assisted treatment (buprenorphine/naloxone) for opioid use disorder in a three phase program with addiction trained doctors, nurses and behavioral health specialists; weekly MAT support groups (Auburn); individual counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, relapse prevention, adolescent behavioral health. Auburn clinic: 11670 Atwood Rd, weekdays 7:30 am to 5:30 pm. Serves American Indian/Alaska Native patients and accepts Medi-Cal and other patients per clinic policy. SUD line (530) 887-2804.
resources.notes: Auburn: 11670 Atwood Rd, Auburn 95603. Also a Grass Valley clinic (Nevada County). Cross-reference: Health/Tribal category. Nonprofit tribal health program (Indian Health Service contracted).

resources.name: Children's Receiving Home of Sacramento (Supporting Community Connections TAY Program)
resources.mission: Supporting Community Connections is a suicide prevention outreach program for transition-age youth in the foster, homeless, and LGBTQ communities that seeks to prevent suicide by offering connections and links to housing opportunities, mental health services, and other social services.
resources.services: Prevention and early intervention for transition-age youth ages 12-25: individual case management, peer support, educational groups on the CRH campus and in the community, links to housing, mental health services, women's health providers, and LGBTQ+ resources. Serves TAY in the community and on campus; grant-funded through Sacramento County MHSA prevention and early intervention. Contact by phone or email.
resources.notes: CRH campus: 3555 Auburn Blvd, Sacramento, CA 95821; main line (916) 482-2370. Program listed as active on CRH site as of July 2026; grant-funded, so confirm funding cycle if referring long-term. Outreach at Pride events, suicide prevention walks, and wellness fairs. CRH residential programs for minors are covered in the Foster tab. Cross-reference: Foster and Mental Health categories.

resources.name: City of Auburn, Auburn Transit (Auburn OnDemand)
resources.mission: Auburn Transit, operated by City of Auburn Public Works, provides public ride-share transit service within the City of Auburn and portions of unincorporated Placer County.
resources.services: Auburn OnDemand curb-to-curb rideshare service: request a pickup anywhere within the service area and the bus takes you to your requested destination. Fares $3.50 per ride for adults, $1.75 for seniors (60 and over), persons with disabilities, and youth ages 6 to 18. Schedule through the GO South Placer Spare app or by calling the Transit Dispatcher at (530) 906-3171; pay by credit or debit card in the app, through dispatch, or on the vehicle.
resources.notes: Service area: City of Auburn and portions of adjacent unincorporated Placer County. General transit questions also handled by the South Placer Transit Information call center, (916) 745-7560. Connects with Placer County Transit routes at Auburn for regional travel.
resources.contactPerson: Transit Dispatcher, City of Auburn Public Works

resources.name: City of Refuge Sacramento
resources.address: 3216 Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard, Sacramento, CA 95817
resources.mission: City of Refuge Sacramento is a community-based organization that exists to empower individuals to make personal changes that lead to a strong and thriving community, offering support and services for individuals experiencing homelessness, formerly incarcerated, and women who have been victimized by sexual exploitation, trafficking, or abuse.
resources.services: Refuge Housing (Phase 1) and Restorative Housing (Phase 2): emergency and restorative housing for women, often with their children, who have been exploited, trafficked, abused, or are facing homelessness, including 24-hour beds and longer stays with mentorship and leadership development supporting movement toward self-sufficiency; Legacy Kids arts-based youth program; MLK Resource Center in Oak Park with community cafe (9am-5pm), diaper distribution in partnership with Sacramento Food Bank, and Resource Hotline (866) 733-8438 for housing support and client advocacy. Hours Monday-Friday 9am-5pm; weekends by appointment.
resources.notes: 3216 Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard, Sacramento, CA 95817 (MLK Resource Center). Hours M-F 9am-5pm, Sat-Sun by appointment (confirmed on contact page July 2026). 501(c)(3) confirmed, EIN 46-2676243 (ProPublica). Participates in HMIS. Cross-reference: Housing tab (housing programs).

resources.name: City of Refuge Sacramento (Refuge Housing)
resources.address: 3216 Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard, Sacramento, CA 95817
resources.mission: City of Refuge Sacramento is a community-based organization that exists to empower individuals to make personal changes that lead to a strong and thriving community, offering support and services for individuals experiencing homelessness, formerly incarcerated, and women who have been victimized by sexual exploitation, trafficking, or abuse.
resources.services: Refuge Housing (Phase 1) and Restorative Housing (Phase 2): emergency and restorative housing for women, often with their children, who have been exploited, trafficked, abused, or are facing homelessness, including 24-hour beds and longer stays with mentorship and leadership development supporting movement toward self-sufficiency; Legacy Kids arts-based youth program; MLK Resource Center in Oak Park with community cafe (9am-5pm), diaper distribution in partnership with Sacramento Food Bank, and Resource Hotline (866) 733-8438 for housing support and client advocacy. Hours Monday-Friday 9am-5pm; weekends by appointment.
resources.notes: 3216 Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard, Sacramento, CA 95817 (MLK Resource Center). Hours M-F 9am-5pm, Sat-Sun by appointment (confirmed on contact page July 2026). 501(c)(3) confirmed, EIN 46-2676243 (ProPublica). Participates in HMIS. Cross-reference: Housing tab (housing programs).

resources.name: City of Roseville (Maidu Community Center Senior Programs and FAB Club)
resources.mission: The Maidu Community Center Senior Wing offers a wide variety of classes, activities, special events and services to anyone 50 and better.
resources.services: Municipal senior programming for adults 50+: Fifty and Better (FAB) Club at Maidu Community Center and Mahany Fitness Center with bingo, bunco, mahjong, cribbage, dominoes, Stitch and Chat, organized day trips, fitness classes, enrichment classes, and special events. FAB membership approximately $40/year for Roseville residents (nonresident rate higher); open to anyone over age 50. Register through Roseville Parks, Recreation and Libraries.
resources.notes: Maidu Community Center: 1550 Maidu Drive, Roseville, CA 95661; open Mon-Fri 8am-5pm. City of Roseville government program; annual membership fee applies but many drop-in activities are low cost.
resources.contactPerson: Parks, Recreation and Libraries Department staff

resources.name: City of Roseville Parks, Recreation & Libraries (Scholarship Program)
resources.mission: The Parks, Recreation & Libraries Scholarship Program provides fee assistance so that income-eligible Roseville residents can participate in PRL camps, classes and recreation programs.
resources.services: Recreation fee assistance of $200 per individual per household per calendar year toward City of Roseville camps, classes, sports and programs. Eligibility: Roseville residency plus household income at or below the program income scale (proof of income and residency required). Paper application signed and submitted with supporting documents to 316 Vernon Street, Suite 400, Roseville; electronic submissions not accepted. Must reapply each calendar year.
resources.notes: Apply at 316 Vernon Street, Suite 400, Roseville, CA 95678. Roseville residents only. Award is $200 per person per calendar year; income verified annually. Government program (city department).

resources.name: City of Roseville, Roseville Transit (local routes, Arrow on-demand, Commuter)
resources.mission: Arrow combines the convenience and flexibility of ride-hailing services with the capacity and affordability of traditional transit; Roseville Transit provides local, commuter and on-demand public transportation for the Roseville community.
resources.services: City-operated transit: local fixed routes within Roseville, weekday commuter service to downtown Sacramento, and Arrow, the on-demand successor to Dial-A-Ride, open to riders of any age. Arrow fares: $3.75 general public, $2.50 discount or ADA (discount or ADA ID required when boarding), children 4 and under free (up to two per paying adult). Arrow operates Mon-Fri 5:45am-10pm and Sat-Sun 8am-5pm; book through the GO South Placer app, online, or by calling (916) or (530) 745-7560 (agents 7 days a week, 8am-5pm); rides bookable same day up to 14 days ahead. Exact cash fare required on board; drivers carry no change.
resources.notes: City website moved to roseville.ca.gov (old roseville.ca.us pages are stale). Arrow replaced traditional Dial-A-Ride with app-based on-demand service bookable through GO South Placer; regional connections via transfer points. Serves City of Roseville city limits; commuter routes serve downtown Sacramento. ADA paratransit operates using Arrow vehicles: call (916) 774-5293 or email transportation@roseville.ca.us for eligibility; pass sales (916) 774-5293. Alternate phone (279) 745-7560.
resources.contactPerson: Alternative Transportation Division, City of Roseville Public Works

resources.name: City of Sacramento (Ethel MacLeod Hart Senior Center, Older Adult Services)
resources.mission: The Hart Senior Center is a gathering place for people who come together to stretch their horizons, have fun, learn new things, make friends and discover the joys of life after age 50.
resources.services: Hub of the City of Sacramento's Older Adult Services for adults 50+: enrichment and art classes, writing groups, fitness programs including yoga and a walking program, special events, All Seasons Cafe congregate meal program, and periodic on-site services such as HICAP Medicare counseling appointments (call the center to confirm the current schedule). Older Adult Services also runs the Triple R Adult Day Program providing respite care for people with dementia at city sites. Most activities free or low cost.
resources.notes: Location: 915 27th Street (Marshall Park), Sacramento, CA 95816; open Mon-Fri 8am-5pm. Cross-reference: Food tab (All Seasons Cafe meals) and In-home Help tab (Triple R respite for caregivers).

resources.name: City of Sacramento Access Leisure (Youth, Parks, and Community Enrichment)
resources.mission: Access Leisure provides enhanced life experiences to people with disabilities through accessible recreation programs and inclusive services.
resources.services: Government adaptive recreation program serving the disability community for over 50 years: adaptive and Paralympic sports, adaptive cycling, adaptive swim, adult social programs for people with developmental disabilities, day camps, youth and teen programs, and inclusion support so people with disabilities can join general city recreation programs. Open to youth and adults with disabilities; register through the city; some programs have fees with scholarship options.
resources.notes: Program of the City of Sacramento Department of Youth, Parks, and Community Enrichment. Primarily serves City of Sacramento residents but regional participants welcome in many programs.

resources.name: City of Sacramento Department of Community Response (DCR)
resources.mission: DCR deploys outreach specialists trained to resolve crises such as behavioral health, homelessness, youth and family disturbances, school response, and substance abuse.
resources.services: City homeless outreach and engagement teams; coordinates the Incident Management Team responding to 311 reports regarding encampments (outreach, connection to behavioral health services, shelter referral, camp cleanups); oversees city-funded shelter and respite sites. Residents and people experiencing homelessness within Sacramento city limits access via 311.
resources.notes: City of Sacramento only, not countywide. Homelessness services page: cityofsacramento.gov/community-response/homelessness-services. Not a shelter operator itself; connects people to city-funded sites.

resources.name: City of Sacramento Youth, Parks, & Community Enrichment (Access Leisure)
resources.mission: The mission of Access Leisure is to provide enhanced life experiences to people with disabilities through accessible recreation programs and inclusive services.
resources.services: Adaptive recreation for children, teens and adults with disabilities for over 50 years: youth art and dance series, fall teen day camp, kids night out, youth holiday hang, The Hangout teen socials, sensory swim (ages 3-12), adaptive sports (power soccer, goalball, adaptive cycling, aquatics, baseball, beep ball) and residential camping/outdoor education. Low or no cost; open houses held to introduce families to programs. Contact by email for registration help.
resources.notes: Programs run at city community centers. Cross-reference Disability tab. Serves city and nearby county residents; veterans programs also offered. Direct program phone not published; email is primary contact.

resources.name: City of Sacramento Youth, Parks, & Community Enrichment (Youth Programs and Camp Scholarships)
resources.mission: The Youth, Parks, & Community Enrichment Department operates the city's parks, community centers, pools and recreation programs, providing enrichment services for residents of all ages, including free and low-cost youth camps.
resources.services: Free and low-cost youth programming across 16 community centers, 16 pools and city parks: free Kids Camp, free Teen Scene Camp and free Hot Spots Remix summer programs, plus the licensed 4th R before/after-school program (TK-6th grade) at school sites. Participants 18 and under receive free meals at many summer sites. Youth Program Scholarship Fund (YPSF) scholarships available for fee-based sessions; call or email for scholarship information. Register via the YPCE online portal.
resources.notes: City of Sacramento residents prioritized; programs at community centers citywide. 4th R is fee-based licensed child care (cross-reference Childcare tab). Free camps fill quickly; register early through the ActiveCommunities portal.
resources.contactPerson: YPCE Recreation Staff (scholarship inquiries: J. Brunetti)

resources.name: Coalition for Compassionate Care of California (Advance Care Planning and POLST Resources)
resources.address: 2530 River Plaza Drive, Suite 200, Sacramento, CA 95833
resources.mission: The Coalition for Compassionate Care of California promotes high-quality, compassionate care for everyone who is seriously ill or nearing the end of life, working to ensure communities have the information, resources, and tools to expand palliative care.
resources.services: Statewide 501(c)(3) headquartered in Sacramento, founded 1998; home of California POLST (Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment). For individuals and families: free consumer-friendly advance care planning tools, guides for goals-of-care conversations with loved ones, POLST forms and explanations in multiple languages (capolst.org), and community education events. Materials available in print and digital formats. Primarily an education and resource organization rather than a counseling provider; use its tools to complete advance directives and POLST with your own physician.
resources.notes: Not a direct care provider: included for its free consumer advance directive and POLST resources. GuideStar EIN 27-0419836. For hands-on help completing documents, local hospices above and hospital social workers assist patients directly.

resources.name: Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) Immigrant Assistance Line
resources.mission: CHIRLA is a California leader with national impact made of diverse immigrant families and individuals who act as agents of social change to achieve a world with freedom of mobility, full human rights, and true participatory democracy.
resources.services: Statewide toll-free Immigrant Assistance Line, (888) 624-4752 (888-6-CHIRLA), Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm: information about immigration options, referrals to trusted low-cost legal service providers anywhere in California including the Sacramento region, help reporting ICE detentions (CHIRLA leads a raids rapid response network), and know your rights information. Free, confidential, Spanish and English, regardless of status.
resources.notes: Headquartered in Los Angeles; included for its statewide phone line only, useful as backup when local providers are at capacity. Hotline number (888) 624-4752 and Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm hours re-confirmed July 2026 via California State Senate and City of Los Angeles resource pages (chirla.org itself blocks automated readers but is live); callers after hours can leave a message. Direct in-person legal services are LA-based. For local representation use Opening Doors, SFBFS, World Relief, IRC, McGeorge, or UC Davis clinic rows.

resources.name: Community Against Sexual Harm (CASH)
resources.mission: Our mission is to assist commercially sexually exploited women through survivor-led peer support and harm reduction and health services, while providing education about the harm inflicted on women and the community.
resources.services: Survivor-led services for commercially sexually exploited women and youth: Drop-In Center (Monday-Friday 12:30pm-4:30pm) offering hot meals, food pantry, clothing boutique, hygiene products, diapers and formula, children's room, safe sex and HIV prevention education, assessment for case management, peer mentoring, and housing assistance, and support groups; Comprehensive Services for Survivors (emergency housing, case management, recovery assistance, health care connections); Dignity Health Medical Safe Haven clinic providing trauma-informed medical care; RESET 25-hour court diversion course meeting prostitution diversion requirements; peer mentoring with street-level and online outreach; housing support; ReCon job readiness class. All are welcome; nonjudgmental and free.
resources.notes: Located in Oak Park, Sacramento (call for address). Drop-in hours M-F 12:30pm-4:30pm (updated July 2026; previously listed as 1pm-5pm). Capital campaign underway with Sierra Health Foundation for a larger permanent center. Executive Director reachable at svaden@cashsac.org per website.

resources.name: Community HealthWorks (formerly Sacramento Covered)
resources.mission: Advancing community, social and economic health one person at a time. Our diverse team of Community Health Workers provides personalized and culturally responsive support to help individuals overcome barriers to care, connect to needed services and navigate complex systems.
resources.services: Free health navigation and enrollment: Medi-Cal and Covered California enrollment assistance, CalAIM Enhanced Care Management and Community Supports, coordination of behavioral health and substance use treatment, hospital and ER patient navigation, street outreach and case management for people experiencing homelessness, CalFresh application help, transportation facilitation, and housing supports. Walk-ins accepted at service locations; online Request for Services form. Languages include Spanish, Russian, Ukrainian, Farsi, Dari, Pashto, Urdu, Vietnamese, and Hmong. All services free.
resources.notes: Admin office 2029 H Street, Sacramento, CA 95811 (no services on site). Service sites: Community Cafe, 724 7th St; 1545 River Park Dr, Suite 450 (Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30); outstations at SNAHC Florin Rd, Sacramento County Health Center (Thursdays), Elica Resource Center, Galt, Elk Grove, and Loaves and Fishes. Rebranded from Sacramento Covered around 2023-2024; use the new name.

resources.name: Community Resource Project, Inc. (HEAP Utility Assistance)
resources.mission: Community Resource Project's utility assistance department utilizes government and utility grants to provide payments towards energy bills to those who are income-qualified in Sacramento, Yuba and Sutter County.
resources.services: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP): one credit of typically $300 to $600 every 12 months toward energy bills for income-eligible Sacramento County residents; available to PG&E and SMUD customers and households heating with wood, propane, or oil. Priority for high energy burden and households with seniors 60+, disabled persons, or children under 5. Also free weatherization services. Apply online or by phone; requires Social Security card, photo ID, prior 6 weeks income verification, and copies of all current utility bills. Office hours Monday-Friday 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Processing takes 8-12 weeks; keep paying bills while the credit processes.
resources.notes: Founded 1972; the current LIHEAP/HEAP provider for Sacramento County (also serves Sutter and Yuba counties, Yuba/Sutter line (530) 671-7590). Income limits published on website (2026 table: $3,331.66/month for 1 person up to $6,407.16 for 4). Sacramento offices: 250 Harris Avenue and 3821 41st Avenue. All program details confirmed on the org's own site (July 2026).

resources.name: Computers 4 Kids, Inc.
resources.address: 2455 West Capitol Ave., Suite 106, West Sacramento, CA 95691
resources.mission: Computers 4 Kids seeks to greatly improve the educational outcome of low income students in the community by providing free and low cost computers to those who meet program qualifications, and to provide computers and Internet access for youth and adults in the greater Sacramento Region.
resources.services: Nonprofit that recycles and refurbishes donated computers: free desktop computers for low income K-12 students enrolled in the Washington Unified School District (referral form from the school's Computers 4 Kids representative); free and low cost computers for Los Rios Community College District students (referral through RISE or EOPS, proof of public assistance required). Adults and families can receive equipment through the United Way Digital Equity Program collaboration. Recipients attend a 30 to 60 minute orientation. Also helps households find affordable internet plans. Donors and businesses can donate used computers and e-waste for refurbishment.
resources.notes: 2455 West Capitol Ave., Suite 106, West Sacramento, CA 95691 (located in Yolo County; serves the greater Sacramento region including the Los Rios Community College District). Office hours Mon-Fri 10:00 am-6:00 pm. Call ahead for eligibility screening.

resources.name: Consulate General of Mexico in Sacramento
resources.mission: The Consulate General of Mexico in Sacramento protects the rights and interests of Mexican nationals in its Northern California district and connects community members with legal orientation, documentation, and protection services.
resources.services: Government of Mexico services, free of charge: legal orientation through the Legal Assistance Program (PALE) with partner immigration attorneys, protection department help for detained nationals and families separated by enforcement, emergency planning documents (passports, consular IDs, dual citizenship registration for US-born children), and general legal consultations that have been open to the public (Monday, Wednesday, Friday mornings per directory listings, non-Mexican nationals accepted for general consultations). Ventanillas (community windows) refer to health and education services regardless of status.
resources.notes: Foreign government provider, included because it delivers free direct legal orientation locally and is a critical first stop for detained Mexican nationals; consular district covers both counties. Phone conflict in directories resolved toward (916) 536-6599, listed as the main line by 211 Connecting Point (database current June 2026); (916) 329-3500 appears in older listings and may still work. Official consulmex.sre.gob.mx site was unreachable during July 2026 verification, so PALE consultation days and phone could not be confirmed from the source: call before referring. Appointments via MEXITEL/Citas SRE.

resources.name: Consulate General of Mexico in Sacramento (Legal Assistance and Protection Department)
resources.mission: The Consulate General of Mexico in Sacramento protects the rights and interests of Mexican nationals in its Northern California district and connects community members with legal orientation, documentation, and protection services.
resources.services: Government of Mexico services, free of charge: legal orientation through the Legal Assistance Program (PALE) with partner immigration attorneys, protection department help for detained nationals and families separated by enforcement, emergency planning documents (passports, consular IDs, dual citizenship registration for US-born children), and general legal consultations that have been open to the public (Monday, Wednesday, Friday mornings per directory listings, non-Mexican nationals accepted for general consultations). Ventanillas (community windows) refer to health and education services regardless of status.
resources.notes: Foreign government provider, included because it delivers free direct legal orientation locally and is a critical first stop for detained Mexican nationals; consular district covers both counties. Phone conflict in directories resolved toward (916) 536-6599, listed as the main line by 211 Connecting Point (database current June 2026); (916) 329-3500 appears in older listings and may still work. Official consulmex.sre.gob.mx site was unreachable during July 2026 verification, so PALE consultation days and phone could not be confirmed from the source: call before referring. Appointments via MEXITEL/Citas SRE.

resources.name: Cottage Housing, Inc. (Serna Village)
resources.mission: Cottage Housing provides housing and services to homeless individuals and families, offering communities of transformation where families rebuild their lives.
resources.services: Serna Village: supportive housing community for formerly homeless families at McClellan Park; 83 one-to-four-bedroom apartments, community center, kitchen, and SKYLAB youth program; serves roughly 100 adults and 200 children. Operated in partnership with Mercy Housing California (property) with Cottage Housing providing supportive services (case management, sobriety-supportive community, employment and life skills programming). Application via sacwaitlist.com when waitlist is open.
resources.notes: Serna Village: 5836 Dudley Blvd, McClellan Park, CA 95652. Waitlist reported CLOSED as of late 2025; applicants directed to monitor sacwaitlist.com. Confirm phone before referral.

resources.name: Court Appointed Special Advocates of Sacramento County (CASA Sacramento)
resources.mission: CASA Sacramento trains and supports volunteer advocates who speak up for abused and neglected children in Sacramento County's dependency system, providing consistent adult relationships that help foster youth thrive.
resources.services: Volunteer Court Appointed Special Advocates matched one-to-one with foster youth; advocates mentor the youth, gather information, and advocate for their best interests in juvenile court, school, and placement settings. Volunteers must be 21 or older, pass screening, and complete pre-service training. Youth are referred through the Juvenile Court; volunteers apply via website.
resources.notes: Office: 301 Bicentennial Cir Ste 220, Sacramento, CA 95826; mailing PO Box 278383, Sacramento, CA 95827-8383. Website confirmed active July 2026; CEO Tiffany Sickler, PhD, confirmed on org site. Founded 1991 with support of the Junior League of Sacramento and Sacramento Superior Court; has sworn in over 1,985 volunteers serving over 4,729 foster youth. Mission statement is a close paraphrase, not verbatim. Cross-reference: Foster tab.

resources.name: Covered California
resources.mission: Covered California is the state's official health insurance marketplace where individuals and families can compare and buy brand-name health plans and receive financial assistance to lower the cost of coverage.
resources.services: Subsidized private health insurance for California residents without affordable employer coverage; income-based subsidies for households above Medi-Cal limits. The single application also screens for Medi-Cal. Apply online at coveredca.com, by phone at (800) 300-1506 (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm, extended during open enrollment Nov-Jan), or through free local Certified Enrollment Counselors and agents found via the Find an Enroller tool. Free enrollment help available throughout Placer and Sacramento counties, including at Community HealthWorks, SNAHC, and Peach Tree (see those rows).
resources.notes: TTY (888) 889-4500. Open enrollment generally November through January; special enrollment year-round after qualifying life events. Medi-Cal enrollment through the same application is year-round.

resources.name: Crisis Text Line
resources.mission: Crisis Text Line provides free, 24/7, confidential crisis support in English and Spanish; a live, trained volunteer Crisis Counselor responds with care, helping texters move from a hot moment to a cool calm.
resources.services: Text HOME to 741741 any time, 24/7, from anywhere in the US. Spanish speakers text AYUDA to 741741 or WhatsApp 442-AYUDAME. Trained volunteer counselors support people through suicidal thoughts, self-harm, anxiety, depression, loneliness, bullying, abuse, and substance use. Free (standard message rates may apply on some carriers), anonymous, all ages. Chat also available via web and WhatsApp.
resources.notes: Text-first alternative for people who cannot or prefer not to call. Not a replacement for 911 in life-threatening emergencies.

resources.name: Crocker Art Museum (Free and Reduced Admission Programs)
resources.mission: The Crocker Art Museum promotes awareness of and enthusiasm for human experience through art, serving as the leading art institution of the Sacramento region.
resources.services: Low-cost arts access for families: Museums for All free general admission for up to four people with a SNAP EBT card and photo ID, Pay What You Wish Sundays on the third Sunday of each month, Art Access free group admission for qualifying community organizations, free family festivals with hands-on art activities for kids, plus youth art classes and camps. Children 5 and under always free; youth admission (6-17) $8, adults $15. Open Wed-Sun 10 am-5 pm (Thu until 9 pm); closed Mon-Tue.
resources.notes: Bring EBT card and photo ID for Museums for All free admission (no reservation required). Third Sunday of each month is Pay What You Wish; check the events calendar for free family festival dates. 501(c)(3) nonprofit in partnership with the City of Sacramento.

resources.name: Del Oro Caregiver Resource Center
resources.mission: Del Oro's mission is to improve the well-being of family caregivers and provide support throughout the caregiving process.
resources.services: Free support for unpaid family caregivers of adults with chronic or disabling conditions (including dementia, stroke, Parkinson's, and frail aging): family consultation and care planning, funded respite care (in-home or in adult day/assisted living settings), counseling and emotional support, support groups, legal and financial consultation, education and training, and information and assistance. Serves caregivers in 13 Gold Country counties including Placer and Sacramento; call to complete an intake. All programs and services free of charge.
resources.notes: One of California's 11 Caregiver Resource Centers, partly funded through Agency on Aging Area 4. Serves Alpine, Amador, Calaveras, Colusa, El Dorado, Nevada, Placer, Sacramento, San Joaquin, Sierra, Sutter, Yolo and Yuba counties. Cross-reference: In-home Help tab (respite).

resources.name: Del Oro Caregiver Resource Center
resources.mission: Del Oro's mission is to improve the well-being of family caregivers and provide support throughout the caregiving process. Founded in 1987, Del Oro is part of a statewide system of caregiver resource centers.
resources.services: No-cost support for unpaid family caregivers: family consultation/case management and care planning, funded respite care (in-home respite, adult day care, or short-term out-of-home placement through contracted professional agencies so caregivers can rest), support groups, short-term counseling (up to six sessions), education and training, legal/financial consultation with an attorney, and the GUIDE dementia support program with Tembo Health. Eligibility: caring for an adult with a cognitive impairing condition that began after age 18 (dementia, stroke, brain injury, Parkinson's) or for someone 60 and over who needs help with two or more activities of daily living. Serves a 13-county area including Placer and Sacramento. Call (916) 728-9333 for intake.
resources.notes: 8421 Auburn Blvd, Suite 265, Citrus Heights CA 95610. Fax (916) 728-9313. Serves caregivers, not care receivers directly; respite is funded through contracted agencies and subject to funding availability. Primary nonprofit respite gateway for both counties.

resources.name: Developmental Disabilities Service Organization (DDSO, Short Center North and South)
resources.mission: DDSO enriches the quality of life for persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities while fostering individual growth, creativity, and community involvement through innovative and artistic strategies.
resources.services: Arts based day programs for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Short Center North (est. 1978) and Short Center South remain separate program sites offering visual and performing arts instruction (painting, ceramics, mosaic, sculpture, collage, woodwork, textiles), life skills and community classes, and gallery shows; student art has been exhibited at the Crocker Art Museum, California State Fair, and State Capitol. Other DDSO programs include Employment Plus (employment training) and Achievement Development and Care (for adults with severe and profound disabilities). Access is typically through Alta California Regional Center referral.
resources.notes: Administrative office: 5051 47th Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95824. Short Center North: 2331 St. Marks Way, Sacramento, CA 95864, director John Berger, (916) 973-1951, scn@ddso.org. All contact details confirmed from ddso.org July 2026; no consolidation of the two Short Centers found.
resources.contactPerson: John Berger, Program Director, Short Center North

resources.name: Dignity Health (Mercy Hospice)
resources.mission: Mercy Hospice is a comprehensive program for individuals and families facing serious and life-limiting illness, providing care that focuses on comfort, dignity, and quality of life.
resources.services: Hospice program of Dignity Health (CommonSpirit Health, nonprofit Catholic health system) serving the greater Sacramento region since 1979. Interdisciplinary team provides medical care, pain and symptom management, emotional and spiritual support in the patient's home or facility; medications, equipment, and supplies related to the hospice diagnosis covered under the Medicare/Medi-Cal hospice benefit. Bereavement follow-up for families for 13 months after a death, plus grief support resources. Referral by physician, family, or self: call (916) 281-3900. Open to all faiths.
resources.notes: Parent Dignity Health/CommonSpirit is nonprofit (do not confuse with for-profit hospices using similar Mercy branding elsewhere). Service area is greater Sacramento; some coverage into neighboring counties, confirm at intake. Program website also at seriousillness.org/sacramento.

resources.name: Disability Rights California
resources.mission: Disability Rights California is the agency designated under federal law to protect and advocate for the rights of Californians with disabilities.
resources.services: Free legal advice, advocacy, and in select cases representation for Californians with disabilities: civil rights, special education, employment discrimination, healthcare and home and community-based services, housing discrimination and reasonable accommodations, and voting rights. Office of Clients' Rights Advocacy serves regional center clients; California Office of Patients' Rights serves state hospital patients. Statewide intake line (800) 776-5746, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 9:00 am to 3:00 pm; TTY (800) 719-5798.
resources.notes: Headquarters at 1831 K Street, Sacramento, CA 95811. Statewide nonprofit; serves residents of both counties through the toll-free intake line. Capacity limited: cases are accepted under annual priorities, others get advice and referral. Cross-reference: Housing tab for disability-related housing discrimination.

resources.name: Disability Rights California (Sacramento Office)
resources.mission: Disability Rights California is the agency designated under federal law to protect and advocate for the rights of Californians with disabilities.
resources.services: Free legal advocacy with direct client services: statewide intake line for legal advice on civil rights, special education, benefits (SSI, IHSS, Medi-Cal appeals), healthcare, housing discrimination, and voting; Office of Clients' Rights Advocacy (OCRA) for regional center clients including Alta California Regional Center consumers; Client Assistance Program for vocational rehabilitation disputes; investigation of abuse and neglect. Intake hours Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 9:00-3:00.
resources.notes: Headquartered in Sacramento; TTY (800) 719-5798. Included because it provides direct legal services to individual clients, not advocacy only. Cross-reference: Legal tab. OCRA advocates serve Alta California Regional Center clients in both counties.

resources.name: Dress for Success Sacramento
resources.mission: Dress for Success Sacramento empowers women to achieve economic independence by providing a network of support, professional attire, and the development tools to help women thrive in work and in life.
resources.services: Workforce readiness services for disadvantaged women: professional attire for interviews and employment (by referral from partner agencies), interview preparation, resume review, mock interviews, job search support, career center access, mentoring and networking programs, and post-employment support for retention and advancement. Referral from a partner agency (job center, shelter, DV program, county office) is required for suiting services.
resources.notes: Serves the greater Sacramento region including surrounding counties; clients come by agency referral once they have an interview scheduled, and returning employed clients receive a week of work attire. Some services offered remotely; call ahead. Cross-reference Clothing (interview and work attire).

resources.name: Easterseals Superior California
resources.address: 9812 Old Winery Place, Suite 21, Sacramento, CA 95827
resources.mission: Easterseals provides services to support, inspire and empower people with disabilities and their families so they can live, learn, work and play in their communities.
