resources.services: Community based adult day programs in the greater Sacramento area for adults with developmental disabilities: ACE IT I (community based, volunteer opportunities and community connections), ACE IT II (Citrus Heights; life skills through cooking, crafting, woodworking, art, and a Fair Oaks Farmers Market booth), and the Functional Integrated Living Skills (FILS) program in Sacramento (cooking, advocacy, life skills, wellness). Person-centered plans include self-advocacy, community safety, health and wellness, time and money management, vocational training, and creative arts. Also runs Easter Seals Enterprises (paid employment and vocational training) and pediatric services (physical, occupational, and speech-language therapy plus child development). Adult day program access is typically through Alta California Regional Center referral.
resources.notes: Contact office: 9812 Old Winery Place, Suite 21, Sacramento, CA 95827. FILS: 2617 Alta Arden Expressway, Suite A, Sacramento 95825. ACE IT II: 8089 Madison Avenue, Suite 4, Citrus Heights 95610. Pediatric clinic: 2033 Howe Avenue, Suite 160, Sacramento 95825. ACE IT III fine and performing arts program is located in Yuba City, outside the two county area. Program lineup confirmed from easterseals.com/superior-ca July 2026; service region includes Placer and Sacramento counties.

resources.name: Elica Health Centers
resources.mission: Elica Health Centers offers quality comprehensive healthcare, health outreach, and links to social services to tens of thousands of low-income people in the Greater Sacramento region, regardless of their ability to pay, embodying the mission of Healing with Heart.
resources.services: Nonprofit FQHC with about 11 sites plus mobile units: primary and preventive care, pediatrics, immunizations, dental with emergency walk-in hours at select clinics, optometry, integrated behavioral health, substance use services, podiatry, chiropractic, lab, and pharmacy. Mobile Medicine and Street Medicine teams serve schools, shelters, and people living on the streets. Elica Resource Center in North Highlands is a multilingual social services hub. Immigration status never asked. Uninsured accepted; appointments at (916) 454-2345, which also reaches after-hours on-call providers. Multilingual: English, Spanish, Russian, Dari and more.
resources.notes: Sites include Arden Arcade campus, Franklin Blvd, Mack Rd, Marysville Blvd, Midtown J Street, North Highlands, V Street, and West Sacramento (Halyard Dr). Served 66,807 patients in 2025. Housing navigation and Enhanced Care Management also offered (cross-ref Housing tab).

resources.name: Fairytale Town (Access Programs)
resources.mission: Fairytale Town is a nonprofit children's park and educational center in William Land Park dedicated to promoting the imagination, creativity and education of children.
resources.services: Low-cost family access to a children's play park and literacy-based programs: general admission $10 (children 1 and under and members free), Blue Star Museums free admission for active duty military families, plus theater shows, Toddler Time and seasonal FunCamps. Open daily 9 am-4 pm March-October and Thu-Sun 10 am-4 pm November-February, weather permitting (guests inside by 4 pm may stay until 5 pm); closed July 4. Reduced-admission access programs (Museums for All/EBT, library Discover & Go passes) have been offered; call to confirm current discounts.
resources.notes: Weather line and membership: (916) 808-7462. If skies are gray, call or check social media to confirm hours. 501(c)(3) nonprofit operating on city park land.

resources.name: Family Promise of Sacramento
resources.mission: Family Promise of Sacramento's mission is to help homeless and low-income families achieve sustainable independence through a community-based response.
resources.services: 24/7 emergency shelter program for homeless and low-income families with children through a network of congregation and community sites: Day Center, emergency shelter, meals, shower facilities, job search assistance, housing search help, and homelessness prevention services. Serves intact families including fathers with children (rare among family shelters). Intake conducted by phone. Office hours Mon-Fri 8am-5pm.
resources.notes: Capacity limited; phone intake screening required. Prevention program: familypromisesacramentoca.org/prevention.

resources.name: FieldHaven Feline Center
resources.mission: FieldHaven Feline Center works toward a solution for every cat in need, providing rescue, medical care, adoption and community cat programs in Placer County and the greater Sacramento region.
resources.services: Cat and kitten adoption; Trap-Neuter-Return (TNR) for community cats; Spay/Neuter Assistance Program (SNAP); vaccination and basic veterinary care; kitten foster and kitten-sitter programs; community and owner cat assistance; FieldHaven Marketplace thrift store.
resources.notes: Shelter at 2754 Ironwood Lane, Lincoln (daily 11 AM-4 PM adoptions); FieldHaven Marketplace at 454 F Street, Lincoln. The source file listed an email address in the website field; corrected here. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: First 5 Placer Children and Families Commission
resources.mission: First 5 Placer supports the healthy brain development of children prenatal through age 5 in Placer County by advocating for family-friendly policies, facilitating collaborative systems, developing education and outreach, and funding direct services.
resources.services: Government commission (Prop 10 tobacco tax) that funds and coordinates the Placer network of family resource centers and parenting programs, including KidsFirst, Lighthouse Counseling and FRC, Latino Leadership Council, Parenting Time, Community Recovery Resources, and Placer County Office of Education programs. Direct program: Road to Resilience, in which navigators from community based organizations partner with pregnant mothers who have current or past substance use to plan for a healthy pregnancy and baby. Website lists funded parenting resources and referral pathways for families with children 0-5.
resources.notes: Public agency created under Proposition 10; also listed at placer.ca.gov/2344. Office: 1400 W Stanford Ranch Road, Rocklin, CA 95765; staffed through Placer County Office of Education. Phone, executive director name, and email confirmed on first5placer.org July 2026. Primarily a funder and system coordinator: families are typically referred to funded partners (KidsFirst, Lighthouse, Latino Leadership Council) for direct services.

resources.name: First 5 Sacramento Commission
resources.mission: First 5 Sacramento uses Proposition 10 tobacco tax funds to support the healthy development of children ages zero through five and their families in Sacramento County.
resources.services: County commission that funds the Birth & Beyond Family Resource Center network, home visiting, developmental screening, oral health, safe sleep (Black Child Legacy Campaign partners), and parent education programs across Sacramento County. Families are connected to funded direct service partners; the website lists programs and locations. Primary parent-facing entry point for First 5 funded services is the Birth & Beyond network line, (916) 244-1906.
resources.notes: Government agency, 2750 Gateway Oaks Drive, Suite 330, Sacramento. Primarily a funder; direct services delivered through contracted nonprofits (see Birth & Beyond row). Cross-reference: Childcare tab.

resources.name: First Step Communities
resources.mission: First Step Communities will create interim housing and emergency shelter for people experiencing homelessness. Here they will live in safety and dignity, receive the services they require, and take a first step away from homelessness toward self-sufficiency and permanent housing.
resources.services: Operates multiple shelter campuses: North A Street Campus (80-bed adult shelter, River District); The Grove (50-cabin shelter for transitional-age youth 18-24); Roseville Road Campus (60 cabins plus 40 trailers, dog-friendly, North Highlands); Stockton Blvd Safe Stay (175-bed pet-friendly shelter, South Sacramento); seasonal Weather Respites during extreme weather; CAN street outreach team. Access: call 2-1-1 and press 8 for shelter assessment; no walk-in placement.
resources.notes: Office: 1455 Response Rd, Suite 190, Sacramento, CA 95815. First Step Housing dba First Step Communities, Tax ID 35-2537631. All placements via 211/Coordinated Access System.

resources.name: First Step Communities (The Grove Transition Age Youth Community)
resources.mission: First Step Communities serves people experiencing homelessness by building and operating safe, service-rich shelter communities. The Grove is a 50-unit tiny cabin community for transitional-age youth ages 18-24, operated in partnership with the City of Sacramento, designed to empower and uplift young people.
resources.services: Emergency bridge housing for TAY ages 18-24 experiencing homelessness: private tiny cabin, meals, case management, housing navigation, employment support with on-site partners like Goodwill, Ready to Rent eviction prevention class, weekly mental health assessments and on-site therapy, and a rapid re-housing component supporting youth for up to a year after move-out. Access is through Sacramento's Coordinated Access System: call 2-1-1 and press 8 (or 844-546-1464) and complete a shelter assessment; no walk-in intake.
resources.notes: No direct intake line; referral only via 211 Sacramento Coordinated Access System shelter assessment. Phone listed is the 211 Sacramento access line. Cross-reference: Housing tab.

resources.name: Folsom Cordova Community Partnership (Community Support and EnergyHELP)
resources.address: 10665 Coloma Road, Suite 200, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670
resources.mission: The mission of the Partnership is to enhance the education, health and well being of children, youth, and families in our communities, building strong families and increasing self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Community Support Services at the Family Resource Center address basic needs and serve as a gateway to additional services: Safety Net services during designated hours each week with immediate tangible resources during hardship (diapers, food, bus passes), one of four charities distributing SMUD EnergyHELP funds (up to $200/year toward unpaid SMUD balances), plus referrals to food, clothing, childcare, employment, housing help, and other local partners. Serves Folsom, Rancho Cordova, and eastern Sacramento County; walk in, call, or email CS@theFCCP.org.
resources.notes: 501(c)(3) founded 1992 in collaboration with Folsom Cordova Unified School District. Phone, address, and contacts confirmed on the org's own site (July 2026); EnergyHELP partner role confirmed via SMUD. Cross-reference: Childcare tab (family resource center services).

resources.name: Folsom Cordova Community Partnership (Family Resource Center)
resources.address: 10665 Coloma Road, Suite 200, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670
resources.mission: The Folsom Cordova Community Partnership provides family support, workforce, and community services that empower individuals and families in the Folsom and Rancho Cordova area to thrive.
resources.services: Family Resource Center hub with parenting workshops, kids activities, support groups, exercise classes, and community events. Birth & Beyond In-Home Visitation delivers weekly case management and Nurturing Parenting lessons at home for pregnant women and families with children 0-5 (more than 2,000 home visits yearly). Parent education classes and workshops, plus basic needs assistance and referrals. Free; serves Rancho Cordova, Folsom, and eastern Sacramento County.
resources.notes: Part of the Birth & Beyond network funded by First 5 Sacramento. Cross-reference: Employment tab (workforce programs).

resources.name: Folsom Cordova Community Partnership (Folsom Cordova Job Center)
resources.mission: The Folsom Cordova Community Partnership builds hope and opportunity by connecting families in Folsom and Rancho Cordova to resources, with a community-based job center located in a high-need area of Rancho Cordova.
resources.services: Free one-stop job center services: resume building assistance, interviewing skills training, professional skill building workshops, online job search and application assistance, local job openings and career fair information, vocational training information and scholarship assistance, typing and data entry testing and certification, specialized youth career services (ages 16-24), and refugee and asylee employment services. Serves adults and youth in the Folsom, Rancho Cordova, and eastern Sacramento County area. Open Monday-Thursday 9:00am-3:00pm, Friday by appointment.
resources.notes: Job Center: 10826 Gadsten Way, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670, (916) 294-9107. Main office: 10665 Coloma Rd., Suite 200, Rancho Cordova, (916) 361-8684. Part of the America's Job Center network with WIOA funding through SETA. Also offers family resource center services (cross-reference Childcare/Family Support).

resources.name: Foothills Compassionate Care (Hospice of the Foothills)
resources.address: 11270 Rough and Ready Hwy, Grass Valley, CA 95945
resources.mission: With expertise, quality, and compassion we empower and guide individuals and families to prepare for and navigate life's challenging chapters.
resources.services: Nonprofit hospice founded 1979, Joint Commission accredited with deemed status. Full interdisciplinary hospice team (physician medical director, nurses, social workers, spiritual counselors, hospice aides, therapists, volunteers) serving patients wherever they call home; Sierra Community Palliative Care program; bereavement support open to the community; caregiver support and education; thrift stores fund care. Eligibility: prognosis of six months or less certified by physician; covered by Medicare, Medi-Cal, and private insurance; services provided at no cost to patient or family regardless of ability to pay. Referrals by self, family, physician, or clergy: call (530) 272-5739 or fax (530) 272-0618. Supports patients exploring the California End-of-Life Option Act.
resources.notes: Serves all of western Nevada County and Placer County (strongest coverage in north and east Placer: Auburn, Colfax, foothill communities). Nonprofit, only community-based hospice headquartered adjacent to north Placer. Grief support groups open to community members, not only hospice families. Thrift stores in Grass Valley area support the mission.
resources.contactPerson: Emily Turcios, Director of Patient Care Services

resources.name: Foothills Habitat for Humanity
resources.mission: Foothills Habitat for Humanity is an independent affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International providing affordable housing in Placer County, bringing people together to build homes, communities, and hope.
resources.services: Affordable homeownership program: partner families purchase homes with affordable mortgages and contribute sweat-equity hours. Home repair programs as capacity allows. ReStore discount home-improvement outlet (8292 Industrial Ave, Roseville, (916) 797-8674) open to the public. Homeownership applicants must live or work in Placer County, meet income limits, demonstrate need, and be willing to partner (sweat equity, homebuyer education). Application cycles open periodically.
resources.notes: Independent affiliate serving Placer County; separate from Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento (whose paper territory overlaps Placer). Not an emergency or rental resource.

resources.name: Foothills Habitat for Humanity (ReStore)
resources.mission: Seeking to put God's love into action, Habitat for Humanity brings people together to build homes, communities and hope, with a vision of a world where everyone has a decent place to live.
resources.services: Nonprofit home improvement store and donation center open to the public: gently used and surplus furniture, appliances, cabinets, doors, windows, building materials, and home goods sold at deep discounts. No income eligibility, anyone may shop. Donors can drop off usable furniture, appliances, and building materials Wednesday through Saturday, 10:00 am to 4:30 pm; proceeds fund affordable homebuilding in Placer County. Shopping hours Wednesday through Saturday, 10:00 am to 4:30 pm. Purchases by debit or credit card only, cash not accepted.
resources.notes: ReStore at 8292 Industrial Ave., Roseville, CA 95678. Open Wed-Sat 10:00 am-4:30 pm. Open to all shoppers, no referral needed. Donations of large items: call ahead to confirm acceptance. Cross-reference: Housing tab (Foothills Habitat homeownership and home repair programs).

resources.name: Friends for Survival, Inc.
resources.mission: Friends for Survival is dedicated to providing a variety of peer support services that comfort those in grief after a suicide death, encourage healing and growth, foster the development of skills to cope with a loss, and educate the community regarding the impact of suicide.
resources.services: National 501(c)(3) headquartered in Sacramento, founded 1983 by survivor mothers; all staff and volunteers have been directly impacted by a suicide death. Free peer support for anyone grieving a suicide loss: monthly support meetings in the Sacramento region, telephone support line, monthly newsletter, mailings of grief materials, and referrals. No cost, no membership requirement; call (916) 392-0664 or toll free (800) 646-7322 to be connected. Also trains community members and professionals on suicide loss.
resources.notes: Mailing: P.O. Box 214463, Sacramento, CA 95821. Meetings in the Sacramento area; phone and mail support available anywhere, including all of Placer County. Cross-reference: Suicide Prevention tab. GuideStar EIN 68-0006749 confirms 501(c)(3) (31-1640393 is the separate Sacramento chapter profile).

resources.name: Friends for Survival, Inc.
resources.mission: We are a non-profit bereavement outreach organization available to those who are grieving a suicide death of family or friends. Since 1983, Friends for Survival has provided compassionate peer support services to those grieving a suicide loss, organized by survivors for survivors.
resources.services: Free suicide bereavement peer support: monthly drop-in grief support meetings at locations throughout Northern California and online (no RSVP required, open-ended, attend as long as needed); free monthly Comforting Friends eNewsletter; phone support; webinars available anytime; resources for children and teens grieving a suicide death; support for first responders and professionals who work with the suicide-bereaved; speaking engagements. All staff and volunteers are themselves suicide loss survivors. Meetings are peer support, not therapy.
resources.notes: Headquartered in Sacramento with national reach; 211 listings show coverage of Sacramento, Placer, El Dorado, Yolo, and surrounding counties. Founded 1983. Meeting schedule at friendsforsurvival.org/meetings. Not a crisis service: in crisis, call or text 988. Cross-reference: Grief/Mental Health tabs if present.

resources.name: Friends of the Lincoln Library
resources.mission: A nonprofit, charitable organization that supports and promotes the Lincoln Public Library and the reading life of the Lincoln community.
resources.services: Fundraising for library programs and materials; used book sales; sponsorship of children’s, teen and family programming; summer reading and literacy support; volunteer opportunities.
resources.notes: Mailing address P.O. Box 1177, Lincoln, CA 95648; supports the Lincoln Public Library at 485 Twelve Bridges Drive. The source file listed a Kiwanis website on this row; corrected here. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Friends Outside (Family Liaison Services, CSP Sacramento region)
resources.mission: Friends Outside has provided services to incarcerated and reentering people, their families, and communities since 1955.
resources.services: Family Liaison Services (FLS) Specialists located within 30 California state prisons, including California State Prison Sacramento (Represa/Folsom area), provide pre-release planning, act as liaisons between incarcerated people and their families, facilitate communication with support systems, teach parenting and conflict resolution classes, and refer families to community resources. Contact through the statewide office in Stockton or the FLS office at the prison where a loved one is housed (ask the institution for the Family Liaison Services Specialist).
resources.notes: No Sacramento County community chapter: local chapters/affiliates exist only in Los Angeles, Santa Cruz and Sonoma counties. Listed here for FLS delivered inside Sacramento County prisons (CSP Sacramento; CDCR facility pages confirm an on-site Family Liaison Services Specialist). Statewide office: 1148 W. Fremont Street, Stockton, CA 95203; mailing P.O. Box 4085, Stockton, CA 95204. Cross-reference: Mentorship tab (family support).

resources.name: Full Circle Treatment Center
resources.mission: Full Circle Treatment Center changes lives through early intervention and treatment of substance abuse, focusing on teens and families.
resources.services: Nonprofit outpatient and intensive outpatient substance abuse treatment for adolescents and their families: assessment and intervention counseling, IOP with group sessions about 4 days per week, individual and family therapy, chemical dependency and parenting education, 12 step support, aftercare. Referrals accepted from schools (works with area school districts), parents and providers. Accepts private insurance and self pay.
resources.notes: 730 Sunrise Ave, Suite 250, Roseville 95661. 501(c)(3) per GuideStar (EIN 20-8680425), but GuideStar notes the organization has recently dropped off the IRS Business Master File (possible merger or closure) and its website was unresponsive when checked in July 2026. Call to confirm the center is still operating before referral.

resources.name: Girl Scouts Heart of Central California
resources.mission: Girl Scouting builds girls of courage, confidence, and character, who make the world a better place.
resources.services: Girl Scout troops and programs for girls K-12 across 18 counties including Placer and Sacramento: leadership, outdoor adventure, camp, civic engagement and STEM programming including a girl-led STEM Center + Makerspace in Sacramento. Financial assistance available for membership fees, uniforms and activity/program fees; apply through the council's online financial assistance forms (Forms and Documents page). Customer care available Mon-Fri 8 am-5 pm by phone, email or live chat.
resources.notes: Sacramento program center: 6601 Elvas Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95819. Financial assistance ensures cost is not a barrier to membership, uniforms or activities. Serves girls in both counties through local troops. 501(c)(3), Tax ID 94-1582429.

resources.name: Girls on the Run of Greater Sacramento
resources.mission: Girls on the Run inspires girls to be joyful, healthy and confident using a fun, experience-based curriculum which creatively integrates running, improving the health and well-being of girls ages 8 to 13.
resources.services: After-school physical activity and positive youth development program for girls in grades 3-8 at school sites in Sacramento and Yolo counties and the western slopes of Placer and El Dorado counties: trained volunteer coaches deliver a social-emotional curriculum combined with 5K training over 8 weeks (two 90-minute practices weekly), ending in a celebratory community 5K. Serves nearly 800 girls per year. Registration $215 with honor-system sliding scale financial aid ($105 or $30 options) plus payment plans; more than $40,000 in program scholarships provided so no girl is turned away, and running shoes can be provided if needed.
resources.notes: Mailing address: PO Box 19602, Sacramento, CA 95819. Fall and spring seasons; sliding scale fee selected during online registration. 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

resources.name: Glen Edwards VFW Post 3010 (Lincoln/Sheridan)
resources.mission: Veterans of Foreign Wars post supporting combat veterans and their families in the Lincoln and Sheridan communities.
resources.services: Comradeship and peer support for overseas and combat veterans; assistance understanding and pursuing VA claims and benefits; support programs for service members and their families; military funeral honors; scholarship and youth programs; hall rental for community events.
resources.notes: 541 5th St., Lincoln, CA 95648 - shares the Lincoln veterans hall with American Legion Post 264. Business meetings the second Wednesday of each month at 6 p.m.

resources.name: Golden Empire Council, Scouting America
resources.address: 3851 N Freeway Blvd, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95834
resources.mission: The Golden Empire Council prepares young people to make ethical and moral choices over their lifetimes by instilling the values of the Scout Oath and Scout Law through outdoor adventure, leadership and service.
resources.services: Scouting programs across 16 Northern California counties including Placer and Sacramento: Cub Scout packs (ages 5-11), Scouts BSA troops (11-18) and Venturing crews (14-21), with more than 250 units serving roughly 6,000 youth. Camps, outdoor education and leadership training. Scholarships (camperships) and financial assistance available so every child can participate regardless of financial means; ask the council service center about assistance when registering.
resources.notes: Council service center: 3851 N Freeway Blvd, Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95834; open Mon-Fri 8:30 am-5 pm. Units meet throughout both counties; use the BeAScout finder on the website to locate a local pack or troop.

resources.name: Golden Sierra Job Training Agency (America's Job Center of California)
resources.mission: Golden Sierra offers free resources to job seekers and businesses in Placer, El Dorado, and Alpine counties, assisting individuals in career transition through its network of job centers.
resources.services: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) operator and America's Job Center of California for Placer County. Free services: job search assistance, resume and interview workshops, career counseling, skills assessments, funded occupational training scholarships (ITAs), on-the-job training subsidies, youth programs (ages 16-24), and employer hiring services. Open to all job seekers; enrollment in WIOA training requires eligibility documentation (ID, work authorization, income for some programs). Roseville Career Center open Monday-Thursday 8:00am-4:30pm; walk-ins welcome.
resources.notes: America's Job Center: 115 Ascot Dr., Suite 100, Roseville, CA 95661, (916) 746-7722, open Monday-Thursday 8:00am-4:30pm. Administrative office: 115 Ascot Dr., Suite 140, (916) 773-8540. Serves Placer, El Dorado, and Alpine counties. Gateway agency for all federally funded job training in Placer County; Roseville is the only full-service job center listed on the agency site.

resources.name: Goodwill Industries of Sacramento Valley & Northern Nevada (Workforce Development / GoodU)
resources.mission: Goodwill Industries of Sacramento Valley & Northern Nevada is an employment social enterprise driven by its commitment to helping individuals overcome barriers to employment and achieve self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Free workforce services with a person-centered model: employment specialists provide skills assessment and career guidance, job readiness training, customer service and soft-skills courses, GoodU certifications, out-of-school youth programs, work experience and on-the-job training placements, and advocacy/referral services (22,722 services delivered in 2024). Serves people with disabilities and other barriers to employment. Sacramento Job Connection office walk-in hours: Tuesday 11am-1pm, Wednesday 1pm-3pm, Thursday 11am-1pm; Monday and Friday by appointment.
resources.notes: Sacramento Job Connection: 8001 Folsom Blvd., Sacramento, CA 95826. Territory spans the Sacramento Valley including Placer County retail locations, but workforce offices are in Sacramento, Chico, and Redding. Cross-reference Clothing (thrift stores and vouchers).

resources.name: Goodwill Industries Sacramento Valley & Northern Nevada
resources.mission: By shopping and donating, you help Goodwill change lives by empowering individuals with barriers to achieve self-sufficiency in your local community; every purchase supports life-changing job training programs.
resources.services: Regional 501(c)(3) operating 38 retail stores and 16 Donation Xpress sites selling low cost clothing, furniture, home goods, small appliances, and electronics; open to everyone, no eligibility requirements. Stores throughout Sacramento County (Sacramento, Elk Grove, Citrus Heights, Rancho Cordova) and Placer County (Roseville: 312 N Sunrise Ave and 5110 Foothills Blvd; Auburn: 2460 Grass Valley Hwy). Most stores open daily 9:00 am to 9:00 pm. Donation drop-offs accepted at all stores and Xpress sites; revenue funds free job training and placement services.
resources.notes: Store locator at goodwillsacto.org/locations. Main phone is administrative; individual store phones on website (Roseville Sunrise store (916) 462-3546). Cross-reference: Clothing tab and Employment tab (Goodwill job training).

resources.name: Granite Wellness Centers (formerly Community Recovery Resources, CoRR)
resources.mission: The mission of Granite Wellness Centers is to promote wellness and quality of life. Sustainable recovery requires a personalized and culturally responsive strategy so each individual can navigate recovery with dignity, connection, and purpose.
resources.services: Nonprofit (founded 1974) offering the full SUD continuum: medically supervised withdrawal management, residential treatment (Grass Valley campus), partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient and outpatient counseling, medication assisted treatment, DUI programs, perinatal and family services, adolescent services, and recovery residences (sober living for men, women, and women with young children, stays up to six months). Placer County campuses in Auburn (12183 Locksley Ln, (530) 885-1961), Roseville ((916) 782-3737) and Lincoln ((916) 434-8927); Grass Valley campus (530) 273-9541. Accepts Medi-Cal via county contracts, insurance, sliding scale.
resources.notes: Main Placer intake: Auburn campus, 12183 Locksley Ln, Auburn 95603. Primary contracted SUD provider for Placer County. CASTLE transitional/sober living program name could not be confirmed on the current website; recovery residences are confirmed. Also serves Nevada County (HQ Grass Valley).

resources.name: Greater Sacramento Urban League (Entrepreneurship and Business Development)
resources.mission: The Greater Sacramento Urban League's mission is to empower Black and other historically marginalized people throughout the region in securing economic self-reliance, educational fulfillment, social justice and civil rights while living well, being well and thriving.
resources.services: Economic empowerment programs supporting entrepreneurship and wealth building for underserved residents: financial wellness workshops at the Empowerment Center (offered with Golden 1 Credit Union), wealth building education, and small business incubation planned through the Hub in the Heights and Grand Gathering commercial kitchen and maker space projects in Del Paso Heights (in development). Also offers job training, career services, housing counseling and homeownership education. No standalone entrepreneurship class schedule is posted on the website; call or email for current small business offerings.
resources.notes: Empowerment Center, 3725 Marysville Blvd, Sacramento, CA 95838, open Mon-Fri 8:30am-5pm. Org, address, phone and hours confirmed on gsul.org July 2026, but no current entrepreneurship or business class schedule is published there; the Grand Gathering incubator space was still in development, confirm current offerings before referral. Cross-reference: Employment category (job training and career services).
resources.contactPerson: Executive staff, Greater Sacramento Urban League

resources.name: Greater Sacramento Urban League (Sacramento Works Job Center)
resources.mission: The Greater Sacramento Urban League empowers African Americans and other underserved communities to achieve economic self-reliance, parity, power, and civil rights; its job center helps individuals find rewarding employment with the tools and training to secure the job best tailored to their needs.
resources.services: Operates a Sacramento Works America's Job Center open to the general public, serving over 3,000 clients annually. Free services: resume building, job search and interview technique training, dress for success guidance, computer/copier/phone access for applications and assessments, one-on-one computer assistance, job coach services, career counseling, employment plan development, on-the-job training enrollment, youth workforce programs, and Job Talk employer recruitment workshops every fourth Thursday 1:00pm-3:00pm. Job Center hours: Monday-Thursday 9:00am-4:00pm, Friday 9:00am-2:00pm.
resources.notes: Empowerment Center: 3725 Marysville Blvd., Sacramento, CA 95838 (Del Paso Heights), building open Monday-Friday 8:30am-5:00pm; Job Center direct line (916) 286-8623, main line (916) 286-8600. Partner site in the SETA/Sacramento Works network. Also offers housing counseling, wealth building, health, and youth programs.

resources.name: Green Technical Education and Employment (Green Tech)
resources.mission: Green Technical Education and Employment is a Sacramento nonprofit that offers innovative workforce skills to youth and young adults of frontline communities, with an emphasis on environmental protection, justice, and economic development, connecting young adults to jobs in the clean green market sector.
resources.services: No-cost green jobs training for youth and young adults of frontline communities: urban farming, urban forestry, aquaponics, solar technology, weatherization and energy efficiency, computer programming, 3-D printing and Arduino, construction trades, landscaping, and general labor. Weekly workshops with stipends based on performance, plus case management including resume writing, business communication, financial literacy, interview techniques, and proper attire. Call to enroll.
resources.notes: Mailing address: P.O. Box 188976, Sacramento; Green Tech Urban Farm training site at 4309 38th St., Sacramento. Confirmed active as of early 2026 (Sacramento Audubon partnership at the urban farm; NetZero Mobility Hubs youth green jobs initiative). Phone confirmed on the org's own site. Main website is script-based and hard to browse; call to confirm current cohort schedule and enrollment.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento
resources.mission: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento brings people together to build homes, communities, and hope, seeking a world where everyone has a decent place to live.
resources.services: Affordable homeownership: new construction with affordable mortgage and 500 sweat-equity hours. Critical home repair program for existing low-income homeowners (roofing, accessibility, health and safety repairs). ReStore retail outlets. Applicants must meet income guidelines (generally 30-80% AMI), demonstrate housing need, and live in the service area (Sacramento County primary; affiliate territory also covers El Dorado, Yolo, and parts of Placer). Application periods announced on website.
resources.notes: 819 North 10th Street, Sacramento, CA 95811; office Mon-Fri 10am-4pm. Separate affiliate from Foothills Habitat (Placer); territory overlap with Placer on paper only.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento (ReStore)
resources.mission: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento brings people together to build homes, communities and hope, driven by the vision that everyone needs a decent place to live.
resources.services: Nonprofit discount home improvement outlet open to the public: new and used donated building materials, fixtures, appliances, furniture, and home furnishings at prices significantly below retail. No eligibility requirements. Donation drop-offs accepted Wednesday through Saturday, 10:00 am to 3:00 pm; donation pickup can be scheduled through the ReStore donation pages. Proceeds fund Habitat home construction and repair in the Sacramento region. Open Tuesday through Saturday, 10:00 am to 4:00 pm. Cash and credit cards accepted, no checks.
resources.notes: Open Tue-Sat 10:00 am-4:00 pm; closed Sun-Mon. Open to all shoppers. Cross-reference: Housing tab (Habitat Greater Sacramento homeownership and repair programs).

resources.name: Harm Reduction Services (HRS)
resources.mission: Hope without limits for all people through Harm Reduction. Founded in 1993, HRS offers a non judgmental, non threatening delivery of public health centered services and resources.
resources.services: Free, confidential harm reduction services for people who use drugs: state authorized syringe services program with sterile supplies and safe disposal, mobile SSP routes across Sacramento County Monday to Friday, naloxone (Narcan) distribution and overdose recognition and response training, HIV, hepatitis C and STD testing (arrive by 4 pm), medical case management for low income HIV positive individuals, linkage to treatment. Main site hours Monday to Friday noon to 6 pm; no appointment or documentation required.
resources.notes: 2800 Stockton Blvd, Sacramento 95817. Saturday free clinic at 3647 40th St, Sacramento 95817, starting noon. All services free and confidential.

resources.name: Her Health First (Black Mothers United)
resources.mission: Her Health First improves the health and well-being of at-risk women, children, and families; its Black Mothers United program supports pregnant Black women in Sacramento County to ensure a safe pregnancy and a healthy baby.
resources.services: Non-directive, community-based pregnancy and early parenting support. Pregnant African American women in Sacramento County (enroll at 32 weeks gestation or less) are paired with a Personal Advocate for individualized support through pregnancy and up to four months postpartum: one-on-one case management, prenatal care navigation, doula services, lactation support, health education, prenatal yoga and wellness activities, Mommy Mingles support groups, parenting skills, and referrals to WIC, mental health, and other resources. Free; enroll by calling (916) 558-4809.
resources.notes: Medical and social-service oriented pregnancy support (not a crisis pregnancy center). Program also has its own site, blackmothersunited.org. Org reports zero maternal deaths among participants since inception. Intake number (916) 558-4809 confirmed in current 211 records July 2026. Part of the Black Child Legacy Campaign network reducing Black infant deaths. Cross-reference: Health tab.

resources.name: Home Safe Program (Adult Protective Services - Placer HHS / Sacramento DCFAS)
resources.mission: Home Safe is a homelessness prevention program serving Adult Protective Services clients who have been victims of elder and dependent adult abuse or neglect, helping keep vulnerable older adults safely housed.
resources.services: Homelessness prevention for APS-involved older and dependent adults: case managers identify housing risks (late payments, hoarding, arrearages) and work with landlords and utility companies on solutions, including settling arrearages, short-term rent subsidies, utility back payments, deep cleaning, and relocation assistance. Placer County operates Home Safe through HHS. In Sacramento County, Home Safe funds also support shelter for adults 60+ (Nottoli Place safe house for elders who are homeless or abuse/neglect victims). Access in both counties is through an APS referral, not direct application.
resources.notes: Entry point is an APS report or case; not walk-in. Placer APS: (888) 886-5401. Sacramento APS Hotline: (916) 874-9377 (confirmed on dcfas.saccounty.gov, July 2026). Home Safe grant funding is cyclical; confirm current capacity with the county. Cross-reference: Eldercare category.

resources.name: Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras (Placer Homeless Resource Helpline, 833-3PLACER)
resources.mission: The Homeless Resource Helpline lets people experiencing homelessness in Placer County call one number, answer a few questions, and be connected to emergency shelter, rapid re-housing, and permanent supportive housing programs.
resources.services: Coordinated entry phone line for people who are homeless or at risk of homelessness in Placer County. Callers are screened for eligibility, referred to emergency shelter, and can be added to the centralized housing assistance list shared with participating providers. Spanish assistance available. Also reachable by dialing 211 in Placer County. Walk-in access remains available at local emergency shelters for people without phones.
resources.notes: Operated by the Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras (Placer and Nevada counties Continuum of Care) in partnership with Placer County and 211 Connecting Point. Not a 24/7 crisis line; after hours callers can use 211. Cross-reference: Housing tab.
resources.contactPerson: Executive Director, Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras

resources.name: Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras (Placer-Nevada Continuum of Care)
resources.mission: To lead, collaborate, coordinate, develop, and implement strategies and resources to end homelessness in Nevada and Placer Counties.
resources.services: Administers the Placer-Nevada Counties Continuum of Care: HUD CoC funding, the Homeless Management Information System, and the Coordinated Entry System, the centralized access point through which shelter and housing placements in Placer County flow. Individuals call 211 or (833) 342-5211 to be assessed and placed on the By Name List, prioritized for shelter, rapid rehousing, and permanent supportive housing. Planning and gateway body, not a direct shelter operator.
resources.notes: Mail: P.O. Box 130, Auburn, CA 95604. 501(c)(3) coalition of shelter providers, consumers, advocates, and government representatives. Front door to nearly every shelter bed in the county: 211 Connecting Point (211connectingpoint.org/coordinated-entry).

resources.name: Hope Cooperative (TLCS, Inc.)
resources.mission: Hope Cooperative moves people from a life of instability by providing permanent supportive housing, mental health services, substance-use rehabilitation, and life skills, serving Sacramento County for over 45 years.
resources.services: Interim, transitional, permanent supportive housing, and sober living at properties around Sacramento County with on-site services; homeless outreach; crisis intervention; intensive case management; psychiatric services and therapy; co-occurring substance use treatment; residential support services; life skills education. Serves 12,000+ people annually, primarily adults with behavioral health challenges experiencing homelessness. Most housing entry via county behavioral health referral or Coordinated Access System.
resources.notes: Administrative office: 650 Howe Ave, Bldg 400-A, Sacramento, CA 95825. Most programs referral-based (county mental health plan or CAS), not walk-in. Get Help page: hopecoop.org/get-help/.

resources.name: Hope Cooperative (TLCS, Inc.)
resources.mission: Hope Cooperative moves people from a life of instability to connection and self sufficiency through a combination of permanent supportive housing, mental health services, substance use rehabilitation and life skills, serving Sacramento and Yolo counties for over 45 years.
resources.services: Nonprofit psychosocial rehabilitation agency for adults experiencing homelessness, mental illness and co-occurring substance use disorders: co-occurring substance use treatment integrated with intensive case management, psychiatric services, therapy, homeless outreach, crisis intervention, supportive housing and residential support services, life skills education. Serves more than 12,000 people per year; referrals through county behavioral health, outreach teams or directly.
resources.notes: Administrative office: 650 Howe Ave, Bldg 400-A, Sacramento 95825. Also serves Yolo County. Cross-reference: Housing category (permanent supportive housing programs).

resources.name: Housing Is Key (California Tenant & Landlord Protections, State of California)
resources.mission: Housing Is Key is the State of California's hub of resources for renters, landlords, and homeowners, providing tenant eviction protection resources and forms under California's tenant protection laws.
resources.services: Free online information and self-help forms: tenant eviction protection resources, tenant eviction protection forms, and landlord protection guidelines, available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, and Tagalog. The California COVID-19 Rent Relief program is CLOSED (existing applicants can still access their application portal via the site). The site now functions as an information and self-help resource on state tenant protections, applying equally to Placer and Sacramento County residents.
resources.notes: No financial assistance currently available through this program; rent relief closed. Pair with Legal Services of Northern California (above) for actual legal help. Web-only resource; former call center (833) 430-2122 may be discontinued.

resources.name: iFoster, Inc.
resources.mission: iFoster's mission is to ensure that every child growing up outside of their biological home has the resources and opportunities they need to become successful, independent adults.
resources.services: Statewide (Truckee-based) resource hub for current and former foster youth: free online member portal with daily living expense support, discounts, education and employment aids, and self-directed life skills training; Jobs Program with trauma-informed training, paid peer support internships in colleges and child welfare agencies (Community Service Pathway), and employer placement; Peers Paving the Path, free one-on-one Medi-Cal certified peer support for youth ages 16-26 preparing for or transitioning out of care. Register online at ifoster.org; TAY, caregivers, and agencies can all create accounts. Call or text the support line.
resources.notes: Headquartered in Truckee, CA; national 501(c)(3) (EIN 80-0627614) serving statewide including both counties. Most services accessed online through the iFoster portal. Jobs Program intake: meredith@ifoster.org. Cross-reference: Foster and Employment tabs.

resources.name: Imani Clinic (UC Davis student-run free clinic)
resources.mission: Imani Clinic provides culturally informed and community-based care in partnership with UC Davis Health, offering holistic, preventive, episodic, and culturally competent care targeted towards the African Diaspora of current and historic Oak Park.
resources.services: Free primary care regardless of insurance, ethnicity, address, immigration status, language, religion, gender identity, or financial means. Specialty clinics include neurology, musculoskeletal health, optometry, and a legal clinic, plus outreach programs (health fairs, youth programs). Open Saturdays 9am-1pm; walk-ins accepted until 11am based on availability; appointment request form online. No cost, no documentation required.
resources.notes: 2425 Alhambra Blvd, Sacramento, CA 95817 (clinic relocated from Oak Park proper; still serves the Oak Park African American community). Hours listed as 9am-1pm on the clinic's own site (UC Davis directory says 8am start); call to confirm.

resources.name: Immigration Legal Services Providers (summary row: see Undocumented Resources tab)
resources.mission: Multiple nonprofit providers offer free or low-cost immigration legal services to residents of Sacramento and Placer counties; full entries are maintained on the Undocumented Resources tab.
resources.services: Immigration legal help in the region includes: McGeorge School of Law Immigration Law Clinic (916) 340-6080; NorCal Resist pro se asylum and work permit clinics (916) 382-0256; California Rural Legal Assistance Foundation Sacramento office (immigration and citizenship); Opening Doors Inc.; and World Relief Sacramento. Services span asylum applications, work permits, naturalization, DACA renewals, and removal defense referrals. Verify each provider's intake process on the Undocumented Resources tab before referring.
resources.notes: This is a pointer row only; do not treat it as a single provider. Detailed, verified entries for each immigration legal services organization live on the Undocumented Resources tab. immigrationlawhelp.org is a national directory for locating accredited low-cost immigration help by zip code.

resources.name: Improve Your Tomorrow (IYT)
resources.mission: Improve Your Tomorrow's mission is to increase the number of young men of color who attend and graduate from colleges and universities.
resources.services: College and career programs for young men of color from 6th grade through college (open to youth of all backgrounds): school-based College Academy mentoring (grades 6-12) at Sacramento-area campuses, College Completion persistence support, a Mentor Fellowship career program, and a College Success Center providing career development pathways, paid internships, workshops, and employer connections. Free; enrollment through partner schools or directly with IYT.
resources.notes: National headquarters: 1901 Royal Oaks Dr., Sacramento, CA 95815, (916) 299-3432. 501(c)(3), EIN 46-2981774. Now operates in multiple states; Sacramento region is home base. Employment angle: internships and career pathway programs; primary focus is education. Contact via website form.
resources.contactPerson: Michael Lynch, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: Improve Your Tomorrow, Inc. (IYT)
resources.mission: Improve Your Tomorrow (IYT) is a nonprofit dedicated to increasing the number of young men of color who graduate from college and university, with a vision of a nation in which young men of color are overrepresented in higher education and underrepresented in the criminal justice system.
resources.services: College Academy for grades 6-12 delivered on school campuses via near-peer mentor fellows: mentorship sessions, academic support, college tours, parent engagement, and college advising; College Completion supports IYT Brothers through college; Mentor Fellowship trains college students and recent grads as paid near-peer mentors (20-40 hrs/week, AmeriCorps supported). Enrollment through partner middle and high schools across Sacramento County; open to all races per Title VI.
resources.notes: HQ and College Success Center: 1901 Royal Oaks Dr, Sacramento, CA 95815. 99% high school graduation rate among members since 2015. No public phone on website; use website contact form. Cross-reference: Employment tab (career pathways and Mentor Fellowship paid positions).
resources.contactPerson: Michael Lynch, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS, Placer and Sacramento Counties)
resources.mission: IHSS is a Medi-Cal based program whose goal is to allow low income aged, blind, and disabled persons, including children, who are at risk for out-of-home placement, to remain safely at home by providing payment for care provider services.
resources.services: State program administered by each county: pays for a care provider to help with housecleaning, meal preparation, laundry, grocery shopping, personal care (bathing, grooming, paramedical), accompaniment to medical appointments, and protective supervision. Eligibility: Medi-Cal recipients who are 65+, blind, or disabled and unable to live safely at home without help. Apply by phone: Sacramento County (916) 874-9471 (application processed by telephone); Placer County (530) 889-7115. County social worker completes an in-home needs assessment.
resources.notes: Sacramento: DCFAS Senior and Adult Services, PO Box 269131, Sacramento, CA 95826, (916) 874-9471 (confirmed July 2026). Placer: (530) 889-7115 confirmed; applications also taken through Placer Adult Intake (916) 787-8860 or toll free (888) 886-5401 with forms faxed to (916) 787-8922. Recipients may hire family members as providers; each county has an IHSS Public Authority provider registry. Cross-reference: In-home Help tab for full detail; summary row here for disability audience.

resources.name: Indian Health Service, California Area Office
resources.mission: The Indian Health Service, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, is responsible for providing federal health services to American Indians and Alaska Natives; the California Area Office supports tribal and urban Indian health programs throughout California.
resources.services: Federal administrative office (information and referral, not a clinic). Helps American Indians and Alaska Natives locate IHS-funded tribal health programs and urban Indian health programs, including Chapa-De Indian Health (Placer/Nevada Counties) and Sacramento Native American Health Center (Sacramento). Information on IHS eligibility, Purchased/Referred Care, scholarships, and public health programs. Office hours weekdays, business hours; use the website program directory to find the correct clinic before calling.
resources.notes: Office: 650 Capitol Mall, Ste 7-100, Sacramento, CA 95814. This is an administrative office, not a care site: no walk-in medical services. Included as an information row for locating IHS-funded care and benefits. Direct care providers: Chapa-De (Auburn), SNAHC (Sacramento), Shingle Springs Health and Wellness Center (El Dorado).

resources.name: Institute on Aging (Friendship Line)
resources.mission: Institute on Aging's Friendship Line is the nation's only accredited 24-hour toll-free emotional support line for older adults, seniors, caregivers, and adults living with disabilities.
resources.services: Free, confidential 24/7 warmline and crisis line for adults 60+ and adults with disabilities anywhere in California: emotional support for loneliness, grief, and depression; suicide intervention and prevention; elder abuse reporting; well-being checks; grief support; and information and referrals. Also offers scheduled outbound friendship calls to isolated seniors. No appointment or enrollment needed; simply call any time, day or night. Responds to more than 11,000 calls monthly in eight languages.
resources.notes: Operated by Institute on Aging (San Francisco based nonprofit); serves seniors statewide including Placer and Sacramento counties by phone. Cross-reference: Crisis tab (crisis and warmlines) and Suicide Prevention tab.

resources.name: Institute on Aging (Friendship Line)
resources.mission: The Friendship Line is the nation's only accredited 24-hour toll-free emotional support and crisis line for people aged 60 and older and adults living with disabilities.
resources.services: 24/7 warmline and crisis line for older adults (60+), adults with disabilities, and their caregivers: emotional support, grief support, suicide intervention, elder abuse reporting, well-being checks, and information and referrals. Callers can also sign up for ongoing outreach calls from trained volunteers. Free and confidential; serves lonely, isolated, anxious, or depressed older adults nationwide.
resources.notes: Operated by Institute on Aging, a San Francisco nonprofit; serves callers nationwide including both counties. (888) 670-1360 and 24/7 availability re-confirmed on ioaging.org July 2026. Cross-reference: Seniors category if built; Placer and Sacramento APS rows for abuse reports.
resources.contactPerson: Friendship Line Program Team, Institute on Aging

resources.name: International Rescue Committee (Sacramento, Immigration Program)
resources.mission: The International Rescue Committee helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives; the IRC in Sacramento offers high-quality, low-cost immigration legal services and citizenship assistance to all populations.
resources.services: DOJ recognized immigration legal services open to all low-income immigrants (refugees, asylees, undocumented persons, and citizens): consultations, adjustment of status (green cards), DACA renewals, employment authorization, family-based petitions, travel documents, and naturalization through the Pathway to Citizenship program. Most consultations are virtual (Zoom, Teams, or phone), booked online at immigration.as.me or via the NorCal legal services line (510) 452-8222; the Sacramento office also has in-person walk-in consultation hours every Wednesday 11am to 4pm. Free in-person citizenship workshop at the Sacramento office every 3rd Tuesday of the month, 10am to 5pm (registration required). Also refugee resettlement, case management, and employment services.
resources.notes: 2020 Hurley Way, Suite 420, Sacramento, CA 95825 (confirmed July 2026). Wednesday walk-in hours 11am to 4pm per IRC's own Citizenship and Immigration Program page; consultation fees not published on IRC's site (older third-party postings mentioned a small fee around $25), so ask when booking. IRC announced a new Sacramento/Turlock leadership structure in June 2026. Does not focus on removal defense; refers court cases out. Sacramento DOJ accredited rep (Farsi/Dari/Pashto): Assadullah Hanif (916) 413-6859. Cross-reference: employment and refugee services.
resources.contactPerson: Ketaki Srivastava, Immigration Manager for Northern California

resources.name: International Rescue Committee in Sacramento (HOPE Anti-Trafficking Program)
resources.mission: The IRC walks alongside refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, survivors of torture, and other immigrants, helping them rebuild their lives and become self-reliant; the Anti-Trafficking program supports survivors with housing, legal aid, and counseling and advocates for survivor rights and anti-trafficking awareness.
resources.services: Human-trafficking Outreach, Prevention and Education (HOPE) Program: comprehensive trauma-informed case management for survivors of both labor and sex trafficking, foreign-born and U.S.-born; long-term case management, housing assistance, food and clothing, immigration and legal assistance referrals, interpretation services, and counseling connections; outreach to vulnerable communities and training for law enforcement and service providers to improve survivor identification. Serves the greater Sacramento region and 30 Northern California counties including Placer. Call office to be connected to anti-trafficking staff.
resources.notes: Office: 2020 Hurley Way, Suite 420, Sacramento, CA 95825. HOPE serves 30 Northern California counties including both Placer and Sacramento. Immigration legal consults: (510) 452-8222. Email listed is the office's public contact; ask to be routed to anti-trafficking staff.

resources.name: James E. Fowler American Legion Post 264 (Lincoln)
resources.mission: Veteran-led American Legion post serving Lincoln-area veterans, service members and their families through camaraderie, advocacy and community service.
resources.services: Peer support and fellowship for veterans of all eras; help connecting to VA benefits and the Placer County Veterans Service Office; military funeral honors and honor guard; flag education and youth programs; scholarships; hall available for veteran and community events; American Legion Auxiliary support for military families.
resources.notes: Post and Auxiliary meet the first Wednesday of each month at 7 p.m.

resources.name: Joan Viteri Memorial Clinic (UC Davis student-run free clinic)
resources.mission: JVMC offers unbiased health care to individuals who use intravenous drugs, work in the sex trade, or identify as transgender, as well as their families, providing basic medical care and health education in a non-judgmental and easily accessible manner.
resources.services: Free primary care for uninsured people in the Oak Park area with a harm reduction focus: hypertension and diabetes management, substance use support, HIV and infectious disease prevention, testing, education, and referrals in partnership with Harm Reduction Services. Hosts Gender Health Clinic hours (first and third Fridays 6-9pm, by appointment). Open every Saturday 1-4pm; walk in during clinic or arrange a phone screening. Everyone welcome; no one turned away for life history. Free.
resources.notes: 3647 40th Street, Sacramento, CA 95817 (Oak Park). Own site lists Saturdays 1-4pm (UC Davis directory says 1-5pm); call to confirm. Phone number is from the UC Davis School of Medicine clinics directory.

resources.name: Joshua's House Hospice (a YoloCares program)
resources.mission: Joshua's House offers comfort, care, and dignity to terminally ill people experiencing homelessness in the Sacramento area, providing a safe, home-like place to spend their final days.
resources.services: First hospice house on the West Coast dedicated to people experiencing homelessness, opened summer 2025 in South Natomas and operated by nonprofit YoloCares. Hosts up to 15 residents at a time in a home-like setting; room, board, personal care, and end-of-life doula companionship provided free to eligible terminally ill homeless individuals, with hospice care delivered by YoloCares or licensed health system partners. On-site staff 24/7 including caregivers, CNAs, and end-of-life doulas. Referrals typically come from hospitals, street medicine teams, shelters, and hospice agencies; most patients come from Sacramento County, with referrals also accepted from Solano, Sutter, Placer, Yolo, Colusa, and Napa counties. Contact the YoloCares patient access team at (530) 758-5566 or patientaccess@yolocares.org.
resources.notes: South Natomas, Sacramento (residential address not broadly published). Cross-reference: Housing/Homeless Services tab. Eligibility: terminally ill and experiencing (or at risk of) homelessness; all services free. Operated by YoloCares (see Both Counties row); YoloCares site confirms open and accepting patients, and CapRadio profiled it as operational May 2026. The old standalone site joshuashousehospice.org shows outdated pre-opening fundraising content; use the YoloCares page.

resources.name: JustServe
resources.mission: JustServe is a free volunteer-matching service that connects community organizations needing help with volunteers who want to serve, strengthening neighborhoods through service.
resources.services: Free online listing of local volunteer projects; organization registration and project posting; volunteer matching for individuals, families and groups; support for nonprofits, schools and faith-based groups recruiting volunteers.
resources.notes: Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Kaiser Permanente Northern California Hospice (Sacramento and Roseville)
resources.mission: Kaiser Permanente Hospice provides comfort, dignity, and quality of life for patients with a life-limiting illness, supporting patients and families with an interdisciplinary team wherever the patient calls home.
resources.services: Hospice program of nonprofit Kaiser Foundation Hospitals, with Sacramento and Roseville branches sharing intake at (916) 486-5300. Interdisciplinary team (physician, nurses, social worker, chaplain, hospice aides, volunteers) provides home hospice, 24/7 on-call support, medications and equipment related to the terminal diagnosis, plus bereavement follow-up for families. Eligibility: generally Kaiser Permanente members (and Medicare beneficiaries per hospice benefit rules) with a prognosis of six months or less; ask your Kaiser care team for a referral. Palliative care departments at Sacramento and Roseville medical centers serve patients earlier in illness.
resources.notes: Branches serve Sacramento and Roseville/Placer areas. Primarily for Kaiser Permanente members; non-members should use Snowline, YoloCares, Sutter, Mercy, or Foothills rows. Kaiser contracts some overflow to for-profit agencies (e.g., Bristol); families can request a nonprofit provider.
resources.contactPerson: Hospice Intake, Kaiser Permanente Northern California

resources.name: KidsFirst (Counseling and Family Resource Centers)
resources.mission: KidsFirst's mission is to treat and prevent child abuse and neglect through education, advocacy, and counseling, to empower and strengthen children and families.
resources.services: No-cost child, adult, and family therapy, postpartum depression therapy, parenting classes, in-home parent education, support groups, community workshops, and referrals to low and no-cost resources. All services free, in English and Spanish. Request services via referral form on website or by calling the Roseville office (916) 774-6802 or Auburn office (530) 887-3536. Serves families throughout Placer County.
resources.notes: Roseville: 516 Gibson Dr., Ste. 100, Roseville, CA 95678. Auburn: 200 Auburn Folsom Rd., Ste. 101, Auburn, CA 95603. KidsFirst is the Child Abuse Prevention Council of Placer County (Tax ID 68-0195225). Cross-reference Trafficking and Foster tabs.

resources.name: KidsFirst (Counseling and Family Resource Centers)
resources.mission: KidsFirst strengthens families and supports children in Placer County through counseling, resources, and advocacy for thriving communities.
resources.services: Placer County's primary child abuse prevention agency and family resource centers in Roseville and Auburn. Free services in English and Spanish: parenting classes (Active Parenting Now, Incredible Years for ages 2-12, Co-Operative Parenting, early childhood support for new parents), child and family counseling including Parent-Child Interactive Therapy, support groups, Dinosaur School social skills groups, health and wellness programs, financial literacy classes, rental and financial assistance (grant dependent), case management, and concrete supports (resource closet items such as diapers and basic needs vary by site). Serves parents, children, and young adults countywide, including CPS-involved and court-referred parents. Access via online referral form (English and Spanish) or by calling either office.
resources.notes: Roseville office: 516 Gibson Drive, Suite 100, (916) 774-6802; Auburn office: 200 Auburn Folsom Road, Suite 101, (530) 887-3536. Office hours Monday-Thursday 9 am to 6 pm, Friday 9 am to 5 pm. Gateway agency for Placer parenting support; funded in part by First 5 Placer. Cross-reference: Mental Health (counseling) and Childcare tabs. Tax ID 68-0195225.

resources.name: KidsFirst (CSEC Program, Counseling and Family Resource Centers)
resources.mission: KidsFirst works to treat and prevent child abuse and neglect through education, advocacy, and counseling, empowering and strengthening children and families in Placer County.
resources.services: Placer County's designated community program for Commercially Sexually Exploited Children (CSEC): community-based support meeting immediate and long-term needs of youth who are being exploited or at risk, including linkages, safety planning, system navigation, crisis intervention, assessments, short-term mental health services, and harm-reduction education; CSEC team co-located with the Placer County DA, law enforcement, mental health agencies, Probation, and Children's System of Care; also no-cost counseling, support groups, and family resource center services at Roseville and Auburn offices. Access by phone or through Placer County Child Welfare (24-hour hotline for suspected child exploitation). Free of charge.
resources.notes: Roseville office (916) 774-6802 and Auburn office (530) 887-3536. Placer County's Human Trafficking Resource Portal identifies KidsFirst as the county's CSEC community program; suspected child victims should also be reported to the 24-hour Placer County Child Welfare hotline. Cross-reference: Foster and Childcare tabs (KidsFirst family support programs).

resources.name: KidsFirst Counseling and Family Resource Centers (LEAP Youth Mentoring)
resources.mission: KidsFirst strengthens families and supports children in Placer County through counseling, resources, and advocacy for thriving communities. Award-winning services are available at no cost in English and Spanish.
resources.services: LEAP Jr. mentoring for grades 1-6 and LEAP for youth through grade 12, run with the Roseville Police Activities League at the Roseville Police Department and with the Placer Sheriff's Activities League at Rock Creek Elementary in Auburn; also a mentorship program for fathers (Forever Fathers) with clinical groups, therapy, and case management. All services free; request services via referral form on website, offered in English and Spanish.
resources.notes: Roseville office: 516 Gibson Dr Ste 100, Roseville, CA 95678, (916) 774-6802; Auburn office phone (530) 887-3536. Org operation confirmed on own website July 2026; LEAP runs three days per week, October through May, at Roseville Police Department (with RPAL) and Rock Creek Elementary in Auburn (with PSAL); confirm current LEAP sites before referral. Cross-reference: Childcare/parenting education services in other tabs.

resources.name: Koinonia Family Services (Homes for Teens)
resources.mission: Koinonia Homes for Teens began in 1985 as an extension of Koinonia's vision to provide for the needs of abused and at risk children in a structured and nurturing setting.
resources.services: Nonprofit Short Term Residential Therapeutic Programs (STRTP) in Loomis for teens, including youth struggling with substance abuse, addiction, trauma and behavioral health diagnoses: six bed licensed homes, mental health treatment certified by DHCS, therapy, education support, life skills, crisis resolution. Access is typically by county placement (child welfare, probation) or managed care referral; accepts Medi-Cal.
resources.notes: 5980 Webb St, Loomis 95650 (mailing PO Box 1403). STRTP program line (916) 652-0171 per kfh.org locations page; corporate office (800) 927-9900 or (916) 652-5802, 3731 Magnolia St, Loomis. Primarily a youth residential/foster care agency; SUD treatment is one component. Cross-reference: Foster category (Koinonia Family Services).

resources.name: La Familia Counseling Center (Employment and Education Programs)
resources.mission: La Familia Counseling Center improves the quality of life for at-risk youth and families of diverse backgrounds by offering multicultural counseling, support, outreach, training, and services to help them succeed.
resources.services: Operates a Sacramento Works America's Job Center at its Maple Neighborhood Center: computer access, resume workshops, interview preparation, GED support, adult on-the-job training placements, and an Out of School Youth program offering paid work experience and advanced training for youth ages 17-24. Bilingual Spanish/English services. Free; call for orientation schedule.
resources.notes: America's Job Center site: 5523 34th St., Sacramento, CA 95820 (Maple Neighborhood Center), (916) 452-3601; public access hours Monday/Wednesday/Friday 8:30am-6:00pm, Tuesday/Thursday 8:30am-7:00pm per SETA listing. Employment and training programs also listed at 3301 37th Ave. with line (916) 210-8773. Partner in SETA/Sacramento Works network. Also provides counseling and immigration services (cross-reference other categories).

resources.name: La Familia Counseling Center (Youth Programs, Maple Neighborhood Center)
resources.mission: La Familia's mission is to improve the quality of life for at-risk youth and families of diverse backgrounds by offering multicultural counseling, support and outreach services and programs to help families overcome adversity, become empowered and succeed in their lives.
resources.services: Free youth programming at the Maple Neighborhood Center and other sites: after-school programs, Kids Club, Girl Scout group, Club Excel, karate classes, a free summer lunch program with activities for ages 6-17, and the Sacramento Adventure Playground on the Maple campus (free outdoor play, run in partnership with Fairytale Town), alongside free counseling for children and youth. Bilingual (Spanish/English) staff; all services free.
resources.notes: Main office: 5523 34th Street, Sacramento, CA 95820; Maple Neighborhood Center: 3301 37th Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95824. Org confirmed operating (2026) but lafcc.org requires JavaScript and program lineup could not be re-checked on the org's own site; confirm current youth program schedule by phone. Cross-reference Mentorship and Mental Health tabs.

resources.name: La Familia Counseling Center, Inc.
resources.mission: La Familia Counseling Center provides multicultural counseling, outreach and support services to low income, at-risk youth and families in Sacramento County.
resources.services: Free bilingual (English/Spanish) mental health counseling for children, youth, and families, available at the main center, via home visitation, at school sites, and at the Maple Neighborhood Center. Also offers behavioral health services for children and youth, youth career and employment programs, and family support services. All services free; bilingual staff available. Hours Mon/Wed/Fri 8:30 am-6:00 pm, Tue/Thu 8:30 am-7:00 pm.
resources.notes: 5523 34th St, Sacramento, CA 95820; Maple Neighborhood Center at 3301 37th Ave. Phone (916) 452-3601 and hours re-confirmed July 2026 via multiple directories, but lafcc.org blocks automated verification (JavaScript wall); confirm current counseling intake process directly with the center.

resources.name: Latino Leadership Council
resources.mission: The Latino Leadership Council is a non-profit organization dedicated to connecting Latino families to bilingual and bicultural services and advocating for wellness in the Latino community; it has advanced well-being in the Sacramento-Placer Latino community since 2007.
resources.services: Bilingual, bicultural family navigation and referral for Latino and immigrant families regardless of immigration status: health access and navigation (medical, dental, vision, nutrition, mental health, prenatal referrals and support), education navigation (school system help for parents, college preparation for youth), youth development and mentorship programs, support groups, and basic needs assistance. Access by phone referral line (530) 320-5353 or online referral form on website; no documentation of status required.
resources.notes: Mailing address 2945 Bell Road Suite 274, Auburn, CA 95603 (confirmed on site July 2026). Referrals by phone (530) 320-5353 or online form; client follow-ups: Deputy Director Celina Salas, CelinaS@LatinoLeadershipCouncil.org. Only Latino-focused nonprofit based in Placer County; does not provide in-house immigration legal representation, refers out to regional legal providers. Placer County has very thin nonprofit immigration legal coverage; residents are mainly served by Sacramento based Both Counties providers below. Cross-reference: Health tab (clinic access regardless of status).

resources.name: Latino Leadership Council
resources.mission: The Latino Leadership Council is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit supporting Latino families in the Placer and northern Sacramento region by connecting them to vital health, education, and youth development services.
resources.services: Bilingual, bicultural promotores (community health workers) conduct home visits, assess family needs, and connect Latino families to health, parenting, and youth services. Parenting and family strengthening programs include Parent Project parenting classes and culturally specific support groups: Rincon de las Comadres, Superacion Personal, Mami y Yo, Personas de Sabiduria, Mis Cuates, Entre Amigos, Entre Chiquillos, and Youth Ambassadors. Apply for services by phone or via the online promotor referral form at latinoleadershipcouncil.org/referral. Promotores provide advocacy, system navigation, transportation connections, and culturally responsive support. Services offered in Auburn, Roseville, Lincoln, and surrounding communities, generally free.
resources.notes: Current directory listings (Roseville Area Chamber, California Local, July 2026) give 2945 Bell Road, Suite 274, Auburn, CA 95603 and (530) 320-5353; the older DeWitt Center address (11434 B Avenue) and (530) 889-7247 no longer appear. Org site is live and programs confirmed, but phone and address could not be confirmed on the org's own contact page, so verify by calling before publication. GuideStar EIN 27-0970476. Funded in part by First 5 Placer. Cross-reference: Health and Immigration-related tabs if present.

resources.name: Legal Services of Northern California (Housing / Eviction Defense)
resources.mission: Legal Services of Northern California is a federal, state, and locally funded legal services program providing free civil legal representation to low-income clients in 23 Northern California counties.
resources.services: Free civil legal help for low-income tenants: eviction (unlawful detainer) defense, response to 3-day and other eviction notices, Section 8 and Housing Choice Voucher terminations and denials, habitability, lockouts, housing discrimination, and disability accommodations; also public benefits disputes (including CalWORKs HA/HSP denials). Sacramento office serves Sacramento County: unlawful detainer intake by phone, first-come first-served, Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri starting 8:30am sharp; slots fill immediately. Auburn office serves Placer County. Senior Legal Services offers free legal help to adults 60+ regardless of income in some matters. Income eligibility applies; does not represent landlords.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 515 12th Street, Sacramento, CA 95814, Mon-Fri 8:30-12 and 1-5. Auburn office: 190 Reamer Street, Auburn, CA 95603, (530) 823-7560 or (800) 660-6107. Call at exactly 8:30am for eviction help. Cross-reference: Legal category.

resources.name: Legal Services of Northern California (Mother Lode Regional Office, Auburn)
resources.mission: LSNC's mission is to provide quality legal services to empower the poor to identify and defeat the causes and effects of poverty within their community, efficiently utilizing all available resources.
resources.services: Free civil legal aid for low-income Placer County residents: eviction defense and other housing problems, public benefits (CalWORKs, CalFresh, General Assistance, Medi-Cal, Social Security), health access, consumer issues, and senior legal services. Intake Monday through Thursday 9:00 am to 12:00 pm and 1:15 pm to 4:00 pm by phone or walk-in; income eligibility generally at or below 125 percent of the federal poverty level with some exceptions for seniors. Self-help materials in multiple languages at lsnc.net.
resources.notes: 190 Reamer Street, Auburn, CA 95603; also (800) 660-6107. Serves Placer, Amador, Calaveras, El Dorado, Nevada, and Sierra counties. Gateway legal aid provider for Placer County. Cross-reference: Housing tab (eviction defense); see also Clean Slate Clinic row and Senior Legal Hotline row. Evening intake message line (866) 815-5990.
resources.contactPerson: Managing Attorney, Mother Lode Regional Office

resources.name: Legal Services of Northern California (Sacramento County Office)
resources.mission: LSNC's mission is to provide quality legal services to empower the poor to identify and defeat the causes and effects of poverty within their community, efficiently utilizing all available resources.
