resources.services: Free civil legal aid for low-income Sacramento County residents: eviction defense and tenant rights, subsidized housing terminations, public benefits appeals (CalWORKs, CalFresh, General Assistance, unemployment insurance), Medi-Cal and health access, and consumer protection. General intake Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 8:30 am to 12:00 pm and 1:00 pm to 5:00 pm or until full, by phone or in person. Income eligibility generally at or below 125 percent of the federal poverty level. Extensive self-help library online in six languages.
resources.notes: 515 12th Street, Sacramento, CA 95814 (executive office at 517 12th Street, (916) 551-2150). Gateway legal aid provider for Sacramento County. Evening intake message line (866) 815-5990. Cross-reference: Housing tab (eviction defense), Senior Legal Hotline row for residents 60 and over.

resources.name: Legal Services of Northern California (Senior Legal Hotline)
resources.mission: The Senior Legal Hotline is a special program within LSNC whose mission is to provide legal help to protect the dignity, independence, safety, and economic stability of the seniors and dependents they serve.
resources.services: Free legal advice and assistance by phone for Sacramento County residents age 60 and over (and grandparent caregivers age 55 and over) on almost any civil issue: estate planning, grandparent rights, landlord-tenant disputes, elder abuse, consumer problems, and public benefits. No income limit for basic hotline advice. Call (800) 222-1753 weekdays during business hours; after-hours message line (866) 815-5990.
resources.notes: LSNC program based in Sacramento. Hotline advice is for Sacramento County seniors 60 and over; extended representation subject to program guidelines. Placer seniors: request senior legal services through LSNC Auburn, (530) 823-7560. Cross-reference: Housing tab for tenant issues.

resources.name: Lighthouse Counseling & Family Resource Center
resources.mission: Lighthouse provides no-to-low cost counseling, educational classes and programs, and assists clients in obtaining needed resources that help them through a challenging time.
resources.services: No-to-low cost individual counseling for all ages, couples and family therapy, adolescent and teen therapy, grief and bereavement counseling, postpartum anxiety and depression counseling, trauma therapy, group classes (anger management, DBT, parenting, grief support), Medi-Cal counseling, and family resource services (Medi-Cal and CalFresh enrollment, diaper bank, new mom home visits). In-person and telehealth in English and Spanish. Hours M-F 8:00-4:30, closed for lunch noon-1:00. Referral form online or call.
resources.notes: Offices in Lincoln, Roseville, Auburn, and Rocklin; mailing address 110 Gateway Drive, Suite 210, Lincoln, CA 95648. Tax ID 35-2252834. Serves 5,000+ Placer residents yearly. For hospice-based grief support see Hospice tab.

resources.name: Lighthouse Counseling and Family Resource Center
resources.mission: Lighthouse provides no-to-low cost counseling and educational services in English and Spanish to help individuals and families in western Placer County thrive.
resources.services: Counseling and family resource center with offices in Lincoln, Roseville, Auburn, and Rocklin serving more than 5,000 Placer County residents a year. Group classes include parenting (Love and Logic), parenting children with trauma, Spanish-language parent group (Juntos por Nuestros Hijos), anger management and DBT emotion management, grief support, and self-care. Also offers individual, couples, and family counseling (including postpartum anxiety and depression), a diaper bank, New Mom home visitation program, car seat safety, Medi-Cal and CalFresh enrollment help, resource navigation, and referrals. Services are no-to-low cost, in English and Spanish, in person and telehealth. Office hours Monday-Friday 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, closed 12:00 to 1:00 pm.
resources.notes: Mailing and Lincoln office: 110 Gateway Drive, Suite 210, Lincoln, CA 95648; additional offices in Roseville, Auburn, and Rocklin. Tax ID 35-2252834. Funded in part by First 5 Placer. Diaper bank and New Mom home visitation confirmed on site July 2026. Cross-reference: Mental Health category for counseling services.

resources.name: Lincoln 4th of July Foundation
resources.mission: An all-volunteer nonprofit that raises funds for and produces the annual Lincoln 4th of July Celebration, building community pride through a free, family-friendly civic event.
resources.services: Annual Independence Day celebration and fireworks show; free community event programming; volunteer opportunities; local fundraising and sponsorship.
resources.notes: 501(c)(3) public charity; mailing address 150 Lincoln Blvd #104-133, Lincoln, CA 95648. Event held at McBean Park. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Lincoln Area Chamber of Commerce
resources.mission: The Lincoln Area Chamber of Commerce serves as a resource and advocate for local businesses and the wider Lincoln community, promoting economic vitality and community leadership.
resources.services: Business directory and referrals; business advocacy, networking and member support; community leadership programs; production of community events including the Lincoln 4th of July parade.
resources.notes: Listed in the source file as LincolnChamber. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Lincoln Lions Club
resources.mission: The Lincoln Lions Club is a volunteer service club affiliated with Lions Clubs International, focused on vision care, youth support and seasonal assistance for Lincoln-area residents.
resources.services: Vision screening and help with eye exams and eyeglasses for low-income residents of any age (income verification required); seasonal food and gift assistance; community service projects; youth programs and scholarships.
resources.notes: Meets at the Veterans Memorial Hall, 541 Fifth Street, Lincoln. No direct phone published; contact through the club website. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Lincoln Serves DLA
resources.mission: Lincoln Serves is a collaborative network convened by the Lincoln Community Foundation that brings Lincoln-area nonprofits, service clubs, schools, faith communities and government agencies together to coordinate local support for residents in need.
resources.services: Cross-agency referral meetings; coordination of local nonprofit and service club efforts; identification of unmet community needs; connection to Lincoln-area food, housing, youth and senior resources.
resources.notes: Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster. The DLA abbreviation in the source name is unconfirmed and may refer to Downtown Lincoln Association; confirm the correct legal name and add a direct phone number.

resources.name: Lions Eye Foundation of California-Nevada
resources.address: 711 Van Ness Ave, Suite 250, San Francisco, CA 94102
resources.mission: To preserve and restore the gift of sight by providing free ophthalmic examinations, operations, and medication to the less fortunate members of our community.
resources.services: Free eye exams, eye surgery (cataract, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy and more), and medications for uninsured, low-income Northern California residents, performed at Sutter California Pacific Medical Center in San Francisco. Eligibility: at least 1 year residency in served communities, completely uninsured (no government or private coverage, no share-of-cost), income within guidelines with proof. Access requires a doctor referral AND sponsorship by a local Lions Club; Placer and Sacramento residents qualify through their local clubs. Referral forms downloadable in English, Spanish, and Chinese.
resources.notes: Caveat: treatment requires travel to San Francisco. For local low-vision rehabilitation see Society for the Blind row; for free optometry consults and glasses via referral see SPIRIT row. Local Lions Clubs also collect and provide eyeglasses.

resources.name: Loaves & Fishes (incl. Maryhouse & Sister Nora's Place)
resources.mission: Loaves & Fishes feeds the hungry and shelters the homeless, providing survival services to homeless men, women and children with dignity and compassion, and advocating for decent affordable housing.
resources.services: Daily noon meal 7 days/week, 364 days/year (600-1,000 guests/day); Friendship Park safe day space; Maryhouse daytime shelter for homeless women and children ((916) 446-4961); Sister Nora's Place long-term overnight shelter with case management for 13 chronically homeless, mentally ill women ((916) 669-7000); Wash House showers and laundry; Mustard Seed School for homeless children 3-15; library; mental health counseling; kennel for guests' pets. No documentation required for survival services; walk-in.
resources.notes: 1351 North C Street, Sacramento, CA 95811 (P.O. Box 13495, Sacramento, CA 95813). Privately funded; weekday services roughly 7am-3pm. CAUTION: their website still lists Sacramento Self-Help Housing as an affiliate; that organization closed in bankruptcy May 2023. Cross-reference: Food category.

resources.name: Los Rios Community College District (NextUp/Guardian Scholars Foster Youth Services)
resources.mission: NextUp is a supplemental support service program for eligible students who are current and former foster youth, aiming to assist, encourage, and support participants in achieving their academic, enrollment, retention, transfer, and career goals.
resources.services: Enhanced support for current and former foster youth at all four Los Rios colleges (American River, Sacramento City, Cosumnes River, Folsom Lake): books and supplies, counseling and career guidance, educational planning, emergency housing assistance, food assistance, child care help, life skills and financial literacy, mental health services, transportation assistance, tutoring. Eligibility: dependency established or continued on or after age 13, and no older than 25 at the start of the academic year. As of fall 2025, NextUp participants are no longer automatically enrolled in EOPS/CARE; ask the campus NextUp office about qualifying for both. Each campus has a foster youth liaison; apply through the campus NextUp office.
resources.notes: Per-campus intake: American River College (916) 484-8627, arcnextup@arc.losrios.edu; Sacramento City College (916) 558-2403, Rodda Hall North RHN 155; Cosumnes River College (916) 691-7075, Library building L 125C; Folsom Lake College (916) 608-6560 (EOPS/CARE/NextUp office). All four campuses are in Sacramento County (FLC in Folsom also draws El Dorado students). Many Placer residents attend ARC; Placer-resident foster youth may also use Sierra College programs.

resources.name: Los Rios Community Colleges (Native American Student Centers at Sacramento City College and American River College)
resources.mission: The Native American Student Success Center at Sacramento City College is dedicated to fostering a supportive and culturally affirming environment that empowers American Indian and Alaska Native students to achieve academic success, personal growth, and community engagement.
resources.services: Public community college centers serving Native students in the Sacramento region, free to enrolled students. SCC Native American Student Success Center (South Gym SOG 119): student support and mentorship, academic advocacy, safe gathering space, AI/AN focused library, community programming, and NASSSP grant-funded counseling and wraparound services; open in person Monday and Wednesday 12:00pm to 4:00pm, Tuesday and Thursday 10:00am to 2:00pm, online Friday 11:00am to 12:00pm. ARC Native American Resource Center (UNITE Center): sanctuary space, resource referrals specific to AI/AN students, peer connection, and leadership development for a learning community of about 150 Native students; open Monday to Friday 8:30am to 5:00pm during fall and spring semesters (closed summer). Enroll at either college to use services.
resources.notes: SCC center: South Gym SOG 119, 3835 Freeport Blvd, Sacramento, CA 95822. ARC center: UNITE Center, 4700 College Oak Dr, Sacramento, CA 95841; coordinator Jesus Valle, (916) 484-8253, vallej@arc.losrios.edu. The Sacramento Native American Higher Education Collaborative (SNAHEC, snahec.org, chair@snahec.org) is an unincorporated workgroup of Native educators that hosts occasional events but provides no staffed direct services; students should contact the campus centers directly. Cross-reference: Education category.
resources.contactPerson: Dr. Vanessa Esquivido-Hernandez, Director, Native American Student Support and Success Programs (SCC)

resources.name: Louis A. Conter VA Clinic (VA Northern California Health Care System)
resources.mission: VA outpatient clinic in Auburn that brings VA health care close to home for enrolled veterans living in Placer County and the surrounding foothills.
resources.services: Primary care; mental health counseling and psychiatry; laboratory services; pharmacy; nutrition and wellness counseling; telehealth visits; VA enrollment and eligibility assistance; referrals to the Sacramento VA Medical Center for specialty and surgical care.
resources.notes: Formerly the Auburn VA Clinic; renamed in honor of Pearl Harbor survivor and WWII veteran Louis A. Conter.

resources.name: Lutheran Social Services of Northern California
resources.mission: LSS of Northern California's mission is to promote stability and honor the dignity of those we serve by providing supportive housing services that lead to self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Sacramento-based supportive housing and services: Step Up Sacramento (supportive services tied to housing for formerly homeless adults), Achieving Change Together, Anthem Housing Navigation Partnership, Housing with Dignity, on-site services at Lavender Courtyard (LGBTQ-welcoming senior housing), Mutual Housing at the Highlands, Saybrook and Mosaica Family Apartments; Connections program for transition-age and former foster youth; Medi-Cal Transformation (CalAIM) housing services; Zak's Closet household goods for people moving into housing.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 2450 Alhambra Blvd, Suite 101, Sacramento, CA 95817. Programs mostly referral-based through CAS, county, or health plans; people in a housing emergency should call 211.

resources.name: Lutheran Social Services of Northern California (Sacramento Housing Programs)
resources.mission: LSS of Northern California's mission is to promote stability and honor the dignity of those we serve by providing supportive housing services that lead to self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Sacramento-based supportive housing and services: Step Up Sacramento (supportive services tied to housing for formerly homeless adults), Achieving Change Together, Anthem Housing Navigation Partnership, Housing with Dignity, on-site services at Lavender Courtyard (LGBTQ-welcoming senior housing), Mutual Housing at the Highlands, Saybrook and Mosaica Family Apartments; Connections program for transition-age and former foster youth; Medi-Cal Transformation (CalAIM) housing services; Zak's Closet household goods for people moving into housing.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 2450 Alhambra Blvd, Suite 101, Sacramento, CA 95817. Programs mostly referral-based through CAS, county, or health plans; people in a housing emergency should call 211.

resources.name: McGeorge School of Law (Community Legal Services Clinics)
resources.mission: McGeorge School of Law's Community Legal Services is a student led clinic program offering pro bono legal assistance, under the supervision of experienced faculty, to community members facing legal challenges who are unable to afford private attorneys.
resources.services: Free legal assistance by supervised law students in three areas only: Bankruptcy (Chapter 7 cases only, with a Pro Se Bankruptcy Clinic), Elder and Health Law (clients age 60 and over), and Immigration. Eligibility: low to modest income and Sacramento County residence. By appointment only, no walk-ins: call (916) 340-6080 and leave a detailed voicemail with your name, callback number, and the type of legal help needed, or submit the online CLS inquiry form. CLS cannot assist with legal issues outside these three areas.
resources.notes: Street address 2925 34th Street, Sacramento, CA 95817 (mailing: 3200 Fifth Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95817). Details confirmed on pacific.edu July 2026; the older mcgeorgelegalclinics.com blog is stale. The Homeless Advocacy and Federal Defender clinics are student programs not part of public CLS intake. Immigration clinic: cross-reference Undocumented Resources tab. UC Davis law clinics were excluded as primarily serving Yolo County.

resources.name: McGeorge School of Law Community Legal Services (Immigration Law Clinic)
resources.mission: In the McGeorge Immigration Law Clinic, students provide in-depth legal assistance to low-income clients on immigration matters under supervising attorneys, including representation before the Immigration Court in removal proceedings; McGeorge legal clinics deliver quality pro bono representation to underserved Sacramento community members.
resources.services: Free immigration legal services for low-income non-citizens: family-based immigration, naturalization, DACA, asylum, SIJS petitions for immigrant youth, U visas, T visas, VAWA petitions for immigrant survivors of domestic violence, post-conviction relief for immigration consequences of criminal convictions, and removal defense in immigration court. Law students interview clients and prepare cases under supervising attorneys. Call (916) 340-6080 or email clsmcg@pacific.edu for an intake screening.
resources.notes: 3455 Fifth Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95817 (mailing: 3200 Fifth Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95817). Strict low-income eligibility. Capacity limited by academic calendar; intake may pause between semesters; call to confirm current office hours. University of the Pacific is a private nonprofit university. Clinic blog at mcgeorgelegalclinics.com is not regularly updated; use the mcgeorge.edu clinic page.
resources.contactPerson: Blake Nordahl, Supervising Attorney, Immigration Law Clinic

resources.name: Meals on Wheels Sacramento County (a program of ACC Senior Services)
resources.mission: Meals on Wheels Sacramento County connects seniors to food, care and compassion, combining nutritious meals with friendly personal visits, wellness checks and links to vital community resources.
resources.services: Senior nutrition provider (formerly Meals on Wheels by ACC): home delivered meals for homebound Sacramento County seniors age 60+, with delivery drivers providing wellness checks; Community Cafes offering congregate lunches and friendship for adults 60+; Restaurant Program vouchers giving eligible seniors additional healthy meal options; and AniMEALS pet food delivered alongside meals so seniors and pets both eat. No charge; donations requested. Call or apply online; brief intake assessment required for home delivery.
resources.notes: Office: 7375 Park City Drive, Sacramento, CA 95831; phones answered Mon-Fri 8:00am-3:30pm. Supported by Agency on Aging Area 4, SHRA, and the cities of Citrus Heights, Elk Grove, Folsom, Galt, and Rancho Cordova. Website active July 2026 (June 2026 menu posted). Cross-reference: Food tab.

resources.name: Meals on Wheels Sacramento County (formerly Meals on Wheels by ACC)
resources.mission: Connecting Seniors to Food, Care and Compassion. The mission of Meals on Wheels is to enhance the dignity and quality of life of Sacramento area older adults through nutritional programs that include assessment of needs, education, supportive services and assistance to families and caregivers.
resources.services: Home-delivered meals for Sacramento County seniors aged 60 or better who are homebound, plus Community Cafes (congregate lunch sites), a restaurant meal program, and AniMEALS pet food delivered with meals. Deliveries include wellness checks and a friendly connection for isolated seniors; programs serve about 2,000 Sacramento County seniors each week. Call (916) 444-9533 to request meals; appeal and grievance forms available on the website.
resources.notes: 7375 Park City Drive, Sacramento CA 95831. 501(c)(3), Tax ID 30-0610870. Rebranded from Meals on Wheels by ACC to Meals on Wheels Sacramento County; supported by Agency on Aging Area 4, SHRA, and the cities of Citrus Heights, Elk Grove, Folsom, Galt, and Rancho Cordova. Cross-reference: Food tab.

resources.name: Medi-Cal Enrollment (Placer County HHS and Sacramento County DHA)
resources.mission: Medi-Cal is California's Medicaid program, paying for medical, dental, vision, and mental health care at little or no cost for children and adults with limited income, administered locally by county human services departments.
resources.services: Free or low-cost health coverage for low-income residents (adults 19-64 up to 138 percent FPL under ACA expansion; higher limits for children and pregnant women). Apply online at BenefitsCal.com (24/7, with document upload and renewals), by phone, by mail, or in person. Placer: (888) 385-5160, (916) 784-6000, or (530) 889-7610; offices in Auburn (11519 B Avenue), Rocklin (1000 Sunset Blvd), and Carnelian Bay. Sacramento: DHA Medi-Cal service center (800) 560-0976 or general line (916) 874-3100; offices include 2700 Fulton Ave, 1725 28th St, 2450 Florin Rd, North Highlands, and Galt, Mon-Fri 8am-4pm. Bring photo ID and proof of income and residency if available; anyone has the right to apply.
resources.notes: Placer page: placer.ca.gov/2125/Medi-Cal-Program; Sacramento page: ha.saccounty.gov/benefits/medi-cal. 2026 note: asset limits reinstated for some populations; confirm current rules with an eligibility worker. Medi-Cal covers dental (Medi-Cal Dental), vision, and prescriptions (see Medi-Cal Rx row).

resources.name: Medi-Cal for Kids and Teens (former CHDP program, DHCS)
resources.mission: Medi-Cal for Kids and Teens provides free preventive services for Medi-Cal members from birth to age 21: checkups, immunizations, screenings, and treatment for physical, mental, and dental health problems.
resources.services: Successor to the Child Health and Disability Prevention (CHDP) program, which ended statewide June 30, 2024. Parents of children with Medi-Cal should schedule well-child checkups through the child's Medi-Cal managed care plan (number on the member ID card) or call the Medi-Cal Member Help Line (800) 541-5555 for help finding a provider, scheduling, and free transportation. Uninsured children should apply for Medi-Cal at BenefitsCal.com; income limits for children reach 266 percent FPL. EPSDT preventive and treatment services continue unchanged.
resources.notes: TDD (800) 430-7077. Old CHDP county pages are historical: Sacramento County's CHDP page redirects families to DHCS, and Placer's remaining CHDP references are outdated. Do not direct families to county CHDP units; use the child's managed care plan or the Member Help Line.

resources.name: Medi-Cal Rx (DHCS Pharmacy Benefit)
resources.mission: Medi-Cal Rx is the statewide pharmacy benefit for all Medi-Cal members: prescriptions are billed through Medi-Cal Rx at little or no cost at enrolled pharmacies.
resources.services: Automatic prescription coverage for anyone with Medi-Cal in either county; no separate enrollment. Use the online pharmacy directory to find participating pharmacies; call the Customer Service Center at (800) 977-2273 (24/7/365) for coverage questions or problems at the pharmacy counter. For uninsured residents needing medication help: nonprofit resources include NeedyMeds (needymeds.org, (800) 503-6897, free database of patient assistance programs) and Rx Outreach (rxoutreach.org, nonprofit mail-order pharmacy for low-cost generics); FQHC pharmacies (Chapa-De, WellSpace, Elica) offer reduced-cost medications to their patients; dial 211 for current local discount programs.
resources.notes: TTY 711, available 24/7. No dedicated local nonprofit prescription assistance program was found in either county as of July 2026; the old Partnership for Prescription Assistance is defunct. Medicare-eligible clients should also ask about the federal Extra Help low-income subsidy.

resources.name: Medi-Cal Transportation Benefit: NEMT and NMT (California DHCS)
resources.mission: Medi-Cal offers transportation to and from appointments for services covered by Medi-Cal: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT) for members who cannot travel by car, bus or taxi due to their condition, and Non-Medical Transportation (NMT) for rides to covered services.
resources.services: Free rides to medical, dental, mental health and substance use appointments and to pick up prescriptions and medical supplies for Medi-Cal members. NEMT (ambulance, wheelchair van or litter van) requires a prescription from a licensed provider; NMT (private or public vehicle) is available to full-scope members and pregnant members through the end of the month of the 365th day postpartum. Access: members in managed care plans (as of 2026 in Sacramento: Anthem Blue Cross, Health Net, Kaiser, Molina; in Placer: Anthem Blue Cross, California Health and Wellness, Kaiser) call their plan's member services line to request rides; fee-for-service members use the DHCS online NMT/NEMT Scheduling Form (on the DHCS transportation page) or contact enrolled transportation providers directly. Request rides as far ahead as possible; plans may require several business days.
resources.notes: Government benefit row: rides are delivered through plan-contracted brokers and providers; for-profit brokers intentionally not listed individually per database policy. Members should call the member services number on their Medi-Cal plan card. (800) 541-5555 is the Medi-Cal Telephone Service Center; FFS NMT eligibility questions also via DHCSNMT@dhcs.ca.gov. County Medi-Cal eligibility: Sacramento DHA (800) 560-0976; Placer HHS (888) 385-5160. DHCS page confirmed current (last modified March 2026). Cross-reference: Healthcare category.
resources.contactPerson: Medi-Cal Member Help Line / your managed care plan member services

resources.name: Mental Health Association of San Francisco (California Peer-Run Warm Line)
resources.mission: The California Peer-Run Warm Line is a confidential, non-emergency emotional support phone and chat line serving residents of California, staffed by counselors who are peers with their own lived experience of mental health challenges.
resources.services: Free, non-crisis emotional support by phone and web chat for any California resident: loneliness, anxiety, depression, stress, early signs of crisis. Peer counselors listen without judgment and help with coping and referrals. No longer 24/7: current hours are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday 7:00 am to 11:00 pm, Thursday 8:00 am to 10:00 pm, closed weekends and MHASF holidays. Hours have fluctuated with state funding, so confirm when calling.
resources.notes: Number changed from the older (855) 845-7415, which still appears in many directories; (855) 600-9276 and the reduced weekday-only schedule re-confirmed July 2026. Hours remain subject to state budget changes; re-check before each reprint. For crisis-level needs or when the line is closed use 988.
resources.contactPerson: Program Director, Mental Health Association of San Francisco

resources.name: Mercy Housing California (Placer County Properties)
resources.mission: Mercy Housing creates stable, vibrant and healthy communities by developing, financing and operating affordable, program-enriched housing for families, seniors and people with special needs who lack the economic resources to access quality, safe housing.
resources.services: Income-restricted affordable rental apartments in Placer County: Mercy North Auburn at Rock Creek (79 units, 1-3BR, Placer County Government Center campus, Auburn, includes 20 No Place Like Home supportive units referred through Placer County Adult System of Care); McAuley Meadows (59 one-bedroom senior 55+ apartments, Auburn); Pleasant Grove Apartments (Roseville, households at 30-60% AMI); The Lohse Apartments (Roseville). Each property runs its own application and waitlist; apply via the find-housing search on the website.
resources.notes: No central application line; contact each property through mercyhousing.org/find-housing. Waitlists commonly long or closed. Supportive units are referral-only via Placer County Adult System of Care. Not an emergency resource.

resources.name: Mercy Housing California (Sacramento Affordable & Supportive Housing Properties)
resources.mission: Mercy Housing California develops and operates affordable, service-enriched housing that changes the lives of families, seniors, and people who have been homeless, working with public and private partners to keep the most vulnerable stably housed and prevent homelessness.
resources.services: Nonprofit affordable housing developer and operator with a Sacramento regional office: 49 properties serving about 3,500 households in the Greater Sacramento region (27 family, 10 senior, 12 permanent supportive), including Serna Village supportive housing operated with Cottage Housing. Free on-site resident services: health and wellness, after-school enrichment, financial stability programs. Apply via the property-search tool on the website; supportive units typically referral-only through the Coordinated Access System or sacwaitlist.com.
resources.notes: Property-level applications only; no central waitlist. Use the Find a Property search (filter Accepting Applications vs Referral Only). Placer properties listed separately under Placer.

resources.name: Mission Oaks Recreation and Park District (Adult and Senior Programs)
resources.mission: Mission Oaks Recreation and Park District provides recreation programs and park facilities that enhance the quality of life for the Carmichael area community, including a full slate of adult and senior programs.
resources.services: Government recreation district senior programming at Mission Oaks Community Center: fitness, yoga, pilates, mobility and balance classes, dance, art and craft classes, pickleball and tennis, senior clubs and dances, and tours and trips; the district's Gibbons Community Center hosts a weekday Meals on Wheels senior lunch site (Mon-Fri 11:45am, age 60+, by appointment) and a free simple will, power of attorney, and health care directive service for adults 55+ (donation suggested). Open to older adults in Carmichael and surrounding Sacramento County communities; register online or at the district office; modest class fees, some free activities.
resources.notes: Mission Oaks Community Center: 4701 Gibbons Drive, Carmichael, CA 95608. District office: 3344 Mission Avenue, Carmichael, CA 95608, Mon-Fri 8am-5pm. Similar senior programming also offered by Carmichael Recreation and Park District. Cross-reference: Food tab (lunch cafe) and Legal tab (simple will service).

resources.name: Money Management International (nonprofit credit counseling)
resources.mission: Money Management International is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that helps consumers create, restore, and maintain a life of financial wellness through empowered choices.
resources.services: Free confidential credit counseling by phone and online 24/7: budget review, debt repayment options, and action plans. Debt management plans (consolidated payments with reduced interest, modest monthly fee), housing counseling, bankruptcy counseling and education, and student loan counseling. Member of the National Foundation for Credit Counseling; the successor organization to the region's Consumer Credit Counseling Service (CCCS of the Sacramento Valley, later ByDesign/ClearPoint, which merged into MMI).
resources.notes: No local walk-in office; all counseling by phone/online, available to residents of both counties. Included as the vetted nonprofit credit counseling option; avoid for-profit debt settlement companies. Initial counseling is always free; only voluntary debt management plans carry fees.

resources.name: Mutual Assistance Network
resources.address: 811 Grand Avenue, Suite A3, Sacramento, CA 95838
resources.mission: Mutual Assistance Network works to foster healthy families, promote health, and expand economic opportunity in the Del Paso Heights community of Sacramento.
resources.services: Operates two Birth & Beyond Family Resource Centers (Robertson Community Center, 3525 Norwood Ave, (916) 696-6689, and Arcade Community Center, 2427 Marconi Ave Suite 103, (916) 514-8096) in North Sacramento and Arden Arcade offering Nurturing Parenting home visitation, parenting classes, crisis intervention, school readiness, and family activities. Also runs community diaper distribution, food resources, youth programs, and economic opportunity services. Free; walk in or call.
resources.notes: Main office: 811 Grand Avenue, Suite A3, Sacramento, CA 95838. FRC referral email: Referrals@MutualAssistance.org. Current B&B sites (Robertson and Arcade) confirmed on birth-beyondfrc.com July 2026; the former Firehouse Community Center is no longer listed as a B&B FRC. Community diaper distribution confirmed in 211 records. Cross-reference: Food tab.

resources.name: Mutual Assistance Network (Youth Programs)
resources.mission: Mutual Assistance Network's mission is to advance social and economic opportunities so families can thrive, engaging and empowering families, preparing youth for adulthood and promoting a web of neighborhood support in Del Paso Heights and surrounding North Sacramento neighborhoods.
resources.services: Free neighborhood-based youth development in Del Paso Heights and Arden Arcade: Passport to Adulthood, a cohort program preparing high school youth for life after graduation (mental health, career development, financial literacy, life skills workshops and real-world work experience), plus recreational activities, organized sports and youth work experience. Also operates Firehouse Community Center (810 Grand Ave) and Arcade Community Center (2427 Marconi Ave).
resources.notes: Main office: 811 Grand Avenue #A3, Sacramento, CA 95838. Firehouse Community Center (916) 567-9567; Arcade Community Center (916) 514-8096. Cross-reference Childcare tab (Birth & Beyond Family Resource Centers).

resources.name: Mutual Housing California
resources.address: 3321 Power Inn Road, Suite 320, Sacramento, CA 95826
resources.mission: Mutual Housing California develops, operates and advocates for sustainable housing that builds strong communities through resident participation and leadership development.
resources.services: Nonprofit affordable housing developer and operator with communities across Sacramento and Yolo counties (Mutual Housing on the Boulevard, Cornerstone, Wong Center, Lavender Courtyard LGBTQ-welcoming senior housing, Mutual Housing at the Highlands, the last two with on-site LSS supportive services). Income-restricted family, senior, and special-needs apartments; resident leadership development; some units for formerly homeless households via referral. Apply directly to properties through website listings (RentCafe portal); TTY (800) 735-2929.
resources.notes: Corporate office: 3321 Power Inn Road, Suite 320, Sacramento, CA 95826. Incorporated 1988. Waitlists vary by property; check individual community listings.

resources.name: My Sister's House
resources.mission: My Sister's House serves Asian and Pacific Islander and other underserved women and children impacted by domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking by providing a culturally appropriate and responsive safe haven, job training, and community services.
resources.services: Culturally responsive DV services centered on Asian and Pacific Islander survivors but open to all underserved women and children. 24-hour Multilingual Helpline at (916) 428-3271, available 365 days a year with Spanish, Vietnamese, Hmong, Russian and many other language interpreters. Services: confidential emergency shelter, safety planning, case management, counseling, peer support, legal services (including restraining order help), employment advocacy and job training through the My Sister's Cafe social enterprise, and community education. Free and confidential; access via the helpline.
resources.notes: Shelter address confidential; administrative office in Sacramento (office phone 916-930-0626). Serves the greater Sacramento region including surrounding counties; culturally specific programming for AAPI and immigrant survivors including limited-English speakers. Website has a Leave Now quick-exit button and a Resources page with local DV referral information.

resources.name: My Sister's House (24-Hour Multilingual Helpline)
resources.mission: My Sister's House serves Asian and Pacific Islander and other underserved women and children impacted by domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking by providing a culturally appropriate and responsive safe haven, job training, and community services.
resources.services: 24-hour confidential helpline with multilingual capacity (Asian and Pacific Islander languages among others) for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking. Gateway to a 6-bed emergency shelter, case management, counseling, peer support, legal services, and job training. Free; serves underserved and immigrant communities; all survivors welcome.
resources.notes: Confidential shelter location; office at 3053 Freeport Blvd #120, Sacramento. Culturally specific alternative to WEAVE for API and immigrant survivors. Cross-reference: Housing tab.

resources.name: My Sister's House (Anti-Trafficking and Safe Haven Services)
resources.mission: Our mission is to serve Asian and Pacific Islander and other underserved women and children impacted by domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking by providing a culturally appropriate and responsive safe haven, job training, and community services.
resources.services: Culturally responsive services for trafficking survivors: 24/7 multilingual helpline (916) 428-3271; confidential emergency Safe Haven shelter (stays up to 90 days with food, supplies, and case management), the only shelter in the Central Valley specifically serving Asian and Pacific Islander women and children; legal advocacy (restraining orders, court accompaniment); trauma-informed counseling; Women to Work career development and job training through the My Sister's Cafe social enterprise. All services free, confidential, and open to underserved survivors of all backgrounds.
resources.notes: Office phone (916) 930-0626; shelter location confidential. Serves the greater Sacramento region. Multilingual services address language barriers and cultural stigma. Cross-reference: Domestic Violence tab (same org, DV and sexual assault services).

resources.name: MyFreeTaxes (United Way Worldwide)
resources.mission: MyFreeTaxes is the only free, national online tax filing program offered by a nonprofit, helping people file their state and federal taxes for free while getting the assistance they need.
resources.services: Free online federal and state tax filing: self-file option for households earning under $89,000 (takes most filers an hour or less), or a Have My Taxes Prepared for Me option (VITA) for households earning under $69,000, online or in person, including 2023-2025 prior-year returns. Guided software screens for the Earned Income Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit. Email, chat, and phone helpline support from IRS-certified VITA specialists.
resources.notes: Fully online/phone service, no local office; good option for residents who cannot reach a VITA site or file outside tax season. United Way does not have access to personal tax information.

resources.name: NAMI Placer County
resources.mission: NAMI Placer County is an organization of families, friends and individuals whose lives have been affected by mental illness. Together, we advocate for better lives for those individuals who have a mental illness, serving residents with free mental health support, online groups, resources and education.
resources.services: All services free with no eligibility requirements: NAMI Connection peer support groups for adults living with mental illness; NAMI Family Support Groups in person in Roseville and Rocklin and via Zoom; education classes including Family-to-Family, Peer-to-Peer, Basics, and Homefront; and community presentations (Ending the Silence, In Our Own Voice, Compartiendo Esperanza in Spanish). Register through the Program Interest Form on the website. No cost, no documentation required.
resources.notes: Mailing: PO Box 81, Roseville, CA 95661; no walk-in office, contact by email or web form. Volunteer-run 501(c)(3). Not a crisis line: for crisis use Placer access line (888) 886-5401 or call/text 988 (cross-ref Crisis Help Lines tab). NAMI National HelpLine (800) 950-6264, Mon-Fri 10am-10pm ET.

resources.name: NAMI Placer County
resources.mission: NAMI Placer County is an organization of families, friends and individuals whose lives have been affected by mental illness, serving residents with free mental health support, online groups, resources and education.
resources.services: Free peer and family support (not clinical therapy): NAMI Family Support Groups in Roseville, Rocklin, and via Zoom (typically evenings, 6:00-7:30 pm), NAMI Connection recovery groups, and free education courses including Family-to-Family (8 sessions), NAMI Basics, Peer-to-Peer, and Homefront for military families. Open to anyone affected by mental illness at no cost; no diagnosis or documentation required. Register via website calendar or program interest form.
resources.notes: Mailing: PO Box 81, Roseville, CA 95661. Contact via website form; no public phone. Groups meet at rotating Placer locations and online. Refers crises to Placer line (888) 886-5401: cross-reference Crisis Help Lines and Suicide tabs.

resources.name: NAMI Placer County
resources.mission: NAMI Placer County is an organization of families, friends and individuals whose lives have been affected by mental illness; together they advocate for better lives for those individuals who have a mental illness.
resources.services: Free peer-led NAMI Family Support Groups for family members, caregivers, and friends of people living with mental illness (including loved ones of people with suicidal thoughts), currently meeting monthly in Roseville and Rocklin and on Zoom, 6:00 to 7:30 pm (see calendar at namipc.org); NAMI education classes (Family-to-Family, Peer-to-Peer, Basics, Homefront) offered periodically, request via the Program Interest Form; community presentations; referral help navigating Placer County crisis and mental health services. Note: the NAMI Connection peer support group for adults living with mental illness is not currently offered by this affiliate. No diagnosis, referral, or fee required.
resources.notes: Volunteer-run NAMI affiliate. Mailing address: PO Box 81, Roseville, CA 95661. No office phone is published on namipc.org; contact by email or the website contact form. The number (916) 554-0554 appears only on the Placer County HHS Crisis Resources page and could not be confirmed on the affiliate's own site, so it is not listed here. Groups are mental health support, not suicide-specific, but serve people with suicidal ideation and their families. Verified against namipc.org July 2026. Cross-reference: Mental Health tab. In crisis, call (916) 787-8860 or (888) 886-5401, or call or text 988.

resources.name: NAMI Sacramento
resources.address: 7230 S. Land Park Dr., Suite 115, Sacramento, CA 95831
resources.mission: NAMI Sacramento provides peer-led education programs, support groups, outreach and a welcoming community for people living with mental illness and their families or caregivers. Our goal is to promote anyone seeking help into an improved state of wellness; to thrive, not just survive.
resources.services: All free: Information and Resource Helpline Mon-Fri 9am-5pm at (916) 890-5467; NAMI Connection Recovery Support Groups for adults living with mental illness (online); NAMI Family Support Groups (in person and online); education classes including Peer-to-Peer, Family-to-Family, NAMI Basics, and Homefront; community presentations (Ending the Silence, In Our Own Voice, Compartiendo Esperanza); and a searchable local resource directory. Register for groups through the website calendar. No cost or documentation.
resources.notes: Not a crisis line: call or text 988 for crisis (cross-ref Crisis Help Lines tab). Groups require registration via the website calendar.

resources.name: NAMI Sacramento
resources.address: 7230 S. Land Park Dr., Ste. 115, Sacramento, CA 95831
resources.mission: NAMI Sacramento provides support, education, and advocacy for individuals and families affected by mental illness in Sacramento County.
resources.services: Free peer and family support (not clinical therapy): NAMI Family Support Group for adults with a loved one experiencing mental health symptoms, NAMI Connection peer recovery groups, and free education courses (Family-to-Family, Peer-to-Peer, Basics). Groups held in person and online; all support groups free with no documentation required. Also maintains local resource lists including LGBTQ mental health resources.
resources.notes: Support and education only; refers clinical needs to county Access Team (888) 881-4881. Cross-reference Suicide tab.

resources.name: NAMI Sacramento
resources.address: 7230 S. Land Park Dr., Suite 115, Sacramento, CA 95831
resources.mission: NAMI Sacramento offers support groups, educational classes, information, and outreach for people living with mental illness and their family members, at no charge.
resources.services: Free peer-led NAMI Connection recovery support groups for adults living with mental health conditions (including suicidal ideation and attempt survivors), currently held online (2nd Thursdays and 2nd Sundays), and NAMI Family Support Groups for family members, significant others, and friends, held in person and online; Peer-to-Peer and Family-to-Family classes and community presentations. No diagnosis, referral, insurance, or fee required; schedules and registration on website. Local non-crisis Information and Resource Helpline (916) 890-5467, Monday to Friday 9 am to 5 pm; NAMI national HelpLine (800) 950-6264 or text NAMI to 62640.
resources.notes: Office: 7230 S. Land Park Dr., Suite 115, Sacramento, CA 95831; office phone for appointments (916) 364-1642. Helpline is non-crisis. Groups are mental health support rather than suicide-specific but regularly serve people with suicidal thoughts and their families. Verified against namisacramento.org July 2026. Cross-reference: Mental Health tab. In crisis, call or text 988.

resources.name: Nation’s Finest (formerly Veterans Resource Centers of America)
resources.mission: Nation’s Finest gives every veteran the support and respect needed to live their best life, providing housing, health and employment services to veterans and their families.
resources.services: Transitional and permanent supportive housing including Mather Veterans Village; homeless veteran outreach and case management; employment readiness, training and job placement; behavioral health and substance use treatment; benefits navigation.
resources.notes: Formerly known as Sacramento Veterans Resource Center and Veterans Resource Centers of America.

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
resources.mission: The National Domestic Violence Hotline provides essential tools and support to help survivors of domestic violence so they can live their lives free of abuse, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
resources.services: Call (800) 799-SAFE (7233), text START to 88788, or chat at thehotline.org, 24/7. Trained advocates provide crisis intervention, safety planning, education, and referrals to local programs (including WEAVE and Stand Up Placer). Interpretation in 200+ languages; deaf/hard of hearing services via videophone (855) 812-1001. Free and confidential.
resources.notes: National line; routes callers to local resources. For local 24/7 DV lines see WEAVE (Sacramento) and Stand Up Placer (Placer) rows.
resources.contactPerson: Support Team, National Domestic Violence Hotline

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
resources.mission: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year, the National Domestic Violence Hotline provides essential tools and support to help survivors of domestic violence so they can live their lives free of abuse.
resources.services: Free, confidential, 24/7/365 national support: call (800) 799-SAFE (7233), text START to 88788, or chat live at thehotline.org. Advocates provide crisis support, safety planning, education about abuse, and referrals to local providers (including WEAVE and Stand Up Placer). Specialized lines: love is respect teen dating abuse helpline (866) 311-9474, StrongHearts Native Helpline (844) 762-8483, Deaf Hotline videophone (855) 812-1001. Interpretation available in 200+ languages. No documentation required; does not provide direct financial assistance.
resources.notes: National backup to local lines; for local shelter access use Stand Up Placer (800) 575-5352 in Placer County or WEAVE (916) 920-2952 in Sacramento County first. Website includes safety alert and quick-exit features; internet use can be monitored, so survivors may prefer calling. Administrative line (737) 225-3150, Austin TX.

resources.name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
resources.mission: The National Human Trafficking Hotline connects victims and survivors of sex and labor trafficking with services and supports to get help and stay safe.
resources.services: 24/7 confidential national hotline: call (888) 373-7888 (TTY 711), text 233733, or live chat at humantraffickinghotline.org; crisis intervention, safety planning, tip reporting, and connection to the National Human Trafficking Referral Directory of local service providers (including Sacramento and Placer County programs); assistance in over 200 languages; anonymous callers accepted; no documentation or immigration status requirements. Federally funded through HHS Administration for Children and Families.
resources.notes: 24/7/365. Text 233733 (BEFREE); live chat on website; Spanish site available. Operated by Compass Connections with HHS funding. Referral directory lists local providers in both counties. In emergencies call 911.

resources.name: National Runaway Safeline (1-800-RUNAWAY)
resources.mission: The National Runaway Safeline is the federally designated national communications system for runaway and homeless youth, keeping them safe and off the streets through free, confidential, 24/7 support.
resources.services: Call 1-800-RUNAWAY, text 66008, chat or email via 1800runaway.org, 24/7/365. Serves youth thinking about running away, youth who have run away or are homeless, and their parents and families. Services include crisis intervention, local referrals, three-way calls with family or agencies, message relay, and the Home Free program (free Greyhound bus ticket home in partnership with Greyhound). Free, confidential, anonymous, non-judgmental.
resources.notes: National nonprofit based in Chicago. For local youth shelter see Wind Youth Services row (Sacramento) and county CPS lines for minors in danger.

resources.name: Next Move Homeless Services
resources.mission: Next Move offers programs to support housing stability and access to social services for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, serving an average of 600 people every day.
resources.services: Emergency Family Shelter (20 private units for families with minor children); Mather Single Adult Interim Housing (shelter and meals up to 90 days with case management, life skills, mental health services, financial literacy); 3 federally funded permanent supportive housing programs providing rental assistance to 125+ households countywide; Francis House Center day services (bus passes, hygiene kits, clothing, resource coaching, ID vouchers). Shelter access via 211/Coordinated Access System.
resources.notes: Main office 2925 34th Street, Sacramento, CA 95817. IMPORTANT: Francis House Center (1422 C St) paused operations June 24, 2026 while transitioning to a new operator; call 211 for current day-service alternatives. Re-check this entry in 60-90 days.

resources.name: NorCal GO and 511 Traveler Information (Sacramento Area Council of Governments)
resources.mission: NorCal GO helps travelers find options like carpool, vanpool, transit, walking and biking throughout the Northern California region, with rewards for commuting sustainably; it is free and easy to use.
resources.services: Free trip planning and traveler information for the SACOG region including Sacramento and Placer counties: NorCal GO (launched February 2025, replacing the Sacramento Region 511 website) is a free web and app platform for finding transit, carpool, vanpool, biking and walking options and earning commuter rewards. Dialing 511 from within the region still reaches SACOG's traveler information and motorist aid phone line. No eligibility requirements.
resources.notes: Government service of SACOG (Sacramento Area Council of Governments), 1415 L Street, Suite 300, Sacramento, CA 95814, main line (916) 321-9000. sacregion511.org now redirects to norcalgo.org. SACOG is modernizing the 511 phone system as an interactive voice response line; the old STARNET data hub was retired August 2025. Information service only, does not operate vehicles.

resources.name: NorCal Resist
resources.mission: NorCal Resist is community members organizing for a better world, building infrastructure against oppression and empowering communities through shared resources and support.
resources.services: Volunteer-run immigrant defense and mutual aid regardless of status: accompaniment to ICE check-ins, court appearances, and other essential appointments; Migra Watch legal observer trainings and Court Watch; ICE bond fund (member of the National Bail Fund Network) to free people from detention; deportation defense campaigns and material support; pro se asylum clinics (I-589 preparation with volunteer support); day laborer outreach; Know Your Rights trainings; monthly food and diaper distributions open to all. Access via website forms, event calendar, and social media; no fees, no documentation required.
resources.notes: 501(c)(3), EIN 83-1003248 (confirmed on org site). No public office; mailing address PO Box 188331, Sacramento, CA 95818. Phone (916) 382-0256 doubles as the Sacramento Rapid Response Hotline, which NorCal Resist operates (see Sacramento FUEL Network row). Serves Sacramento and surrounding region including Placer residents at Sacramento clinics. Given July 2026 ICE activity surge, clinic dates change often; check calendar on site. Cross-reference: Food tab (distributions).

resources.name: NorCal Services for Deaf and Hard of Hearing
resources.mission: NorCal's mission is to empower Deaf individuals to live independently and productively, advocate for equal access and opportunities, and educate family members, service providers, employers and the general public about the unique communication needs, abilities and accomplishments of Deaf children and adults.
resources.services: Services for Deaf, hard of hearing, and DeafBlind people: advocacy (education, employment, public services, ADA), counseling and independent living skills, community education, specialized employment services, sign language interpreting (requests (916) 349-7525), the EXCEL day program for Alta Regional Center consumers who are deaf or hard of hearing, DeafSAFE support for survivors of sexual violence, Camp Grizzly youth summer camp, and DeafPlus family support. Contact by voice phone, videophone, or email.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 4044 N Freeway Blvd, Sacramento, CA 95834; videophone (916) 993-3048; email info@norcalcenter.org. Open Mon-Fri 8:30-5:00. Serves a 24 county region of northeastern California including Sacramento and Placer counties. Confirmed from norcalcenter.org July 2026.

resources.name: Northern California Construction Training (NCCT)
resources.address: 10411 Old Placerville Rd., Suite 205, Sacramento, CA 95827
resources.mission: Since 1993, NCCT has provided free pre-apprenticeship training designed to launch careers in the building trades, preparing and placing motivated individuals into apprenticeship programs and meaningful construction careers.
resources.services: Free pre-apprenticeship construction training: hands-on job-site experience building real projects, classroom instruction in construction math, reading, and blueprint basics, industry certifications (OSHA 10, HAZWOPER, welding, traffic flagging, traffic control, CPR and first aid), exposure to more than 22 trades, remedial education and GED preparation at some sites, employment barrier assistance, life-skills development, and placement assistance into union apprenticeships (over 80 percent of graduates enter apprenticeships or construction career pathways). No cost to participants. Enroll online at ncct.ws or call.
resources.notes: Training sites vary with active construction projects around the Sacramento region. Also listed with 211 Connecting Point for Placer-area referrals.

resources.name: Northern California Construction Training (NCCT)
resources.mission: Since 1993, NCCT has provided free pre-apprenticeship training designed to launch careers in the building trades for people experiencing barriers to employment.
resources.services: Free construction pre-apprenticeship for adults with barriers to employment, including justice-involved individuals; enrollment tracks exist through Sacramento County Probation and parole partnerships. Classroom instruction plus hands-on building experience under a journeyman carpenter, exposure to more than 22 trades; graduates are connected to union apprenticeship programs (over 80 percent placement into apprenticeships or construction careers). Apply online via the enrollment form at ncct.ws/enrollment or through a probation officer or case manager. Hours Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 3 p.m.
resources.notes: 10411 Old Placerville Rd #205, Sacramento, CA 95827; mailing PO Box 293585, Sacramento, CA 95829. Additional training sites listed at ncct.ws/enrollment. Placer PREP and Sacramento County Probation ADRCs refer clients here. Cross-reference: Employment tab.

resources.name: One Community Health
resources.mission: As one community, we empower all people through equitable, quality, patient-centered care. We envision a healthy community that compassionately cares for all.
resources.services: Nonprofit FQHC providing care for everyone regardless of background or ability to pay: primary care from pediatrics through geriatrics, walk-in clinic, dental, comprehensive mental health and psychiatry, optometry and vision services, HIV care and prevention (over 30 years), street medicine, perinatal care, lab, and on-site pharmacy. Accepts Medicare, Medi-Cal, Covered California plans, and uninsured patients. Appointments at (916) 443-3299 or online; MyChart portal. Four locations: Midtown (main campus), Arden-Arcade, Carmichael, and the Wind Youth Clinic for youth experiencing homelessness.
resources.notes: Main campus: 1500 21st Street, Sacramento, CA 95811. Founded 1989 as CARES (Center for AIDS Research, Education and Services); rebranded One Community Health. Serves greater Sacramento.

resources.name: Opening Doors Inc (Immigration Legal Services)
resources.mission: Opening Doors empowers refugees, immigrants, human trafficking survivors, and underserved Sacramento area residents to achieve self-sufficiency by accessing opportunities to mainstream economic and social systems.
resources.services: Pro bono (free) immigration legal representation by licensed attorneys and DOJ accredited representatives for the greater Sacramento region including Placer, Sacramento, El Dorado, and Yolo counties: individualized consultations, free representation in removal proceedings for low-income individuals including unaccompanied minors (one of few regional providers doing pro bono immigration court work, mostly asylum), application help for U visas, T visas, VAWA, SIJS, adjustment of status, asylum, DACA, and naturalization, plus community education workshops and seminars. Services provided by licensed attorneys and DOJ accredited representatives. Call or use website contact form for intake.
resources.notes: GATEWAY entry for this category: broadest free representation in the region, including immigration court. Also runs 24-hour human trafficking crisis line (916) 504-1118. Serves both counties from Sacramento office. Cross-reference: refugee resettlement, anti-trafficking, health navigation (Uplifting Health), economic programs.

resources.name: Opening Doors, Inc. (Economic Prosperity Programs)
resources.mission: Opening Doors enriches communities by supporting immigrants, refugees, and survivors of trafficking on their path to stability, self-sufficiency, and belonging.
resources.services: Microenterprise development and small business support for immigrants, refugees, survivors of trafficking and other underserved Sacramento-area entrepreneurs: microloans through its certified CDFI (Sacramento's CDFI specializing in newcomer communities), business counseling and technical assistance, financial education classes and asset-building programs for clients with limited or no credit history. Also provides career pathway support (college and certification enrollment help including tuition support) in partnership with Los Rios Community College District. Multilingual staff. Call or use the online contact form and select Economic Prosperity Programs; microloan application starts on the program page.
resources.notes: No public program email on current site; intake is by phone or the website contact form, call to confirm current office hours. Serves the Sacramento region regardless of immigration status for most programs. Cross-reference: Undocumented/Immigration category (legal services, resettlement) and Human Trafficking services.

resources.name: Opening Doors, Inc. (Supporting Survivors of Human Trafficking)
resources.mission: Opening Doors is a Sacramento nonprofit dedicated to welcoming refugees, defending immigrants, and supporting survivors of human trafficking, empowering them to achieve self-sufficiency by accessing mainstream economic and social systems.
resources.services: Comprehensive trafficking survivor services for both U.S.-born and foreign-born survivors of sex and labor trafficking: 24-hour human trafficking crisis hotline (916) 504-1118; emergency, temporary, and permanent housing support; case management providing food, clothing, medical and mental health connections, and transportation; immigration legal services including T-visas and other relief for trafficking victims; mental health and counseling services; employment and life skills support; economic empowerment programs. Serves Sacramento and surrounding counties; no fees for survivor services.
resources.notes: Office: 1111 Howe Avenue, Suite 125, Sacramento, CA 95825. Human Trafficking 24-Hour Crisis Hotline (916) 504-1118 and main line (916) 492-2591 confirmed on site July 2026. Trafficking program (Supporting Survivors) and immigration legal services both active per current website; Defending Immigrants program provides immigration legal aid. Tax ID 37-1417129. One of the few local providers of immigration legal relief (T-visas) for trafficking survivors.

resources.name: Operation HOPE, Inc. (Credit and Money Management coaching)
resources.mission: Operation HOPE is the leading provider of financial dignity education and economic empowerment programs for low- and moderate-income youth, individuals and families in underserved communities.
resources.services: Free one-on-one financial wellbeing coaching and group workshops covering credit and money management, credit score improvement, budgeting, savings, debt reduction, homeownership readiness, and small business basics; all programs free of charge. Sacramento HOPE Inside office (credit and money management plus homeownership coaching) is hosted inside the Bank of America branch at 5744 Stockton Blvd, Sacramento. Placer County residents and anyone without a nearby office can enroll through the virtual coaching portal at operationhope.org.
resources.notes: National 501(c)(3); HOPE Inside offices are hosted in partner bank branches. Sacramento location (HOPE Inside Bank of America, 5744 Stockton Blvd) confirmed on the org's own locations page (July 2026); coach assignments change, so call the national line to confirm before an in-person referral. No Placer County office; use virtual enrollment.

resources.name: Pacific Clinics (Sacramento, formerly Uplift Family Services)
resources.mission: Pacific Clinics, California's largest community-based nonprofit behavioral health provider (formed by the merger of Pacific Clinics and Uplift Family Services), provides behavioral health and social services to advance health equity.
resources.services: Children's outpatient mental health in the Capital Region including Flexible Integrated Treatment (FIT): therapy, behavioral support, medication management, therapy groups, and family support for youth up to age 21 with Medi-Cal; no referral necessary and walk-in options available. Contact sacfit@pacificclinics.org or call (916) 388-6400 or (916) 921-0828 to schedule an intake. Walk-in hours: Tech Center office Tue 3-5 pm and Wed 10 am-noon; Rosin Court office Thu 9 am-5 pm.
resources.notes: Sacramento locations: 9343 Tech Center Dr. 2nd Fl. (95826) at (916) 388-6400, 3840 Rosin Ct. Ste. 100 (95834) and 7248 South Land Park Dr. Ste. 103 (95831) both at (916) 921-0828. 501(c)(3), Tax ID 94-2295953. Statewide client services line 877-722-2737.

resources.name: Pacific Northwest Regional VBOC (formerly NorCal VBOC, Veterans Business Outreach Center)
resources.mission: The Pacific Northwest Regional VBOC is a no-cost, go-to resource for transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses looking to start, purchase or grow a business, providing business development assistance, training, counseling, mentoring, and resource referrals at no cost to clients.
resources.services: Free confidential business advising and mentorship for veterans, transitioning service members, Guard and Reserve members, military spouses and military-connected family members: Boots to Business workshops, Military Spouse Pathway to Business, government contracting training series, business plan development, help navigating SBA programs and lenders, and a Sierra College veterans entrepreneurship course. Serves Northern California, Oregon and Washington; Sacramento is one of four California hub offices. New clients sign up online; existing clients call or email for appointments.
resources.notes: Rebranded from NorCal VBOC to Pacific Northwest Regional VBOC; website still norcalvboc.org. Funded by SBA, affiliated with the NorCal SBDC network (Cal Poly Humboldt Sponsored Programs Foundation). Sacramento office relocating as of mid 2026 (site says new location coming soon, previously 1792 Tribute Rd); other CA offices in Redding, Clovis and Fairfield, virtual appointments regionwide. Confirm office address by phone before any in-person visit. Cross-reference: Veterans category.
resources.contactPerson: Center staff, Pacific Northwest Regional VBOC

resources.name: Paratransit, Inc.
resources.mission: Paratransit, Inc. is dedicated to creating independence through smart transit, providing transportation for the elderly, persons with disabilities, and underserved youth in the Sacramento metropolitan area and support services to other agencies.
resources.services: Nonprofit mobility agency: one-on-one Mobility Training (travel training) that teaches seniors and people with disabilities to ride buses and light rail independently, at no cost to qualified individuals; community shuttles including Home to Healthcare (rides to medical care) and People to Produce (rides to fresh food); Consolidated Transportation Services Agency (CTSA) partnerships and contract transportation for human service agencies; vehicle maintenance shop serving nonprofit fleets. Call to enroll or inquire.
resources.notes: Address: 2501 Florin Road, Sacramento, CA 95822. 501(c)(3) nonprofit, EIN 94-2519965. Distinct from SacRT GO: SacRT operates ADA paratransit rides; Paratransit, Inc. focuses on training, contracted agency transportation and mobility management across the Sacramento region.

resources.name: Peach Tree Health (North Sacramento Health Center)
resources.mission: We seek to improve lives within the communities we serve by providing compassionate, high-quality healthcare regardless of a person's background or ability to pay.
resources.services: Nonprofit FQHC serving uninsured and underserved families: family medicine, pediatrics, immediate care, women's health, behavioral health and psychiatry, substance use disorder services including medication-assisted treatment, dental and mobile dental clinic, optometry with low-cost eyeglasses, pharmacy, telehealth, and Medi-Cal application and enrollment assistance. Sliding fee discount scale offered to all eligible patients; accepts Medicare and Medi-Cal. Sacramento site: North Sacramento Health Center, 3810 Rosin Court, Suite 100 (Natomas area), with behavioral health suite at 3840 Rosin Court, Suite 150. Hours Mon 8-5, Tue-Fri 8-6:30, closed 12-1.
resources.notes: Sacramento appointments (916) 779-7656; administration in Marysville, (530) 749-3242. Other sites in Yuba, Sutter, and Butte counties. Historical note: Peach Tree managed the former Mercy Clinic Norwood (Dignity Health) from 2014 and replaced it with the North Sacramento center in 2016; the Norwood Ave clinic is now closed.

resources.name: Placer County Adult Protective Services (24-Hour Abuse Hotline)
resources.mission: Adult Protective Services is a 24-hour service program that receives and investigates reports of abuse and neglect of elders age 60 and older and dependent adults age 18 to 59 living in their homes in Placer County.
resources.services: 24/7 hotline to report physical abuse, sexual abuse, financial abuse, isolation, neglect, or self-neglect of elders (60+) and dependent adults (18-59 with physical or mental impairment) in Placer County. Any concerned person may report, anonymously if preferred. Alternate 24-hour confidential line (916) 787-8860. Social workers investigate and connect victims to services.
resources.notes: General information line (530) 886-2900 (business hours). Shares the (888) 886-5401 number with the county mental health crisis line. Call 911 for emergencies. Cross-reference: Seniors category if built.
resources.contactPerson: Adult System of Care Director, Placer County HHS

resources.name: Placer County Children's System of Care (Independent Living Program)
resources.mission: The Children's System of Care provides every eligible foster youth with Independent Living skills training opportunities to assist in the transition to a successful, independent adulthood, delivering services in the community where foster youth are living and learning.
resources.services: County ILP for current and former foster and probation youth: independent living skills training, education and employment support, help applying for financial aid, housing resource navigation, transition planning to age 21. Eligible: youth 14-15 with an open dependency case attending school or living in Placer County, and youth in out-of-home placement at least one day after their 16th birthday; serves ages 16-21 preparing to exit or already aged out of care. Referral through social worker, probation officer, or self-referral. Staff use a trauma-informed approach.
resources.notes: Coordinated by Placer County Health and Human Services, Children's System of Care; ILP services delivered in partnership with the Placer County Office of Education (Michelle Graf contact confirmed on county site July 2026). Other county-listed transition partners: Whole Person Learning THP-Plus (530) 823-6903 and Youth Empowerment Support YES! Program (530) 886-5461. Cross-reference: Foster tab (child welfare services) and Housing tab (THP-Plus transitional housing for former foster youth).
resources.contactPerson: Michelle Graf, Independent Living Program Coordinator

resources.name: Placer County Clean Slate Clinic (Business Advantage Network with Legal Services of Northern California)
resources.mission: Placer County's Business Advantage Network, in association with Legal Services of Northern California, offers a monthly Clean Slate Clinic to assist participants in removing or dismissing past convictions from their records.
resources.services: Free criminal record relief clinic held the first Wednesday of every month: conviction dismissal and reduction, arrest record relief, and related remedies. Limited to residents of Placer, El Dorado, Sierra, Amador, and Calaveras counties. Eligibility: no pending charges, not on parole (or at least half of probation completed), and all fines, fees, and restitution paid. Pre-registration required, no walk-ins; participants must be Live Scanned and provide a copy of their RAP sheet (Record of Arrests and Prosecutions) before one-on-one attorney review, and must be US citizens or legal residents (green card copy required). Register through Legal Services of Northern California at (530) 823-7560. Improves eligibility for employment and housing.
resources.notes: Run jointly by Placer County's Business Advantage Network (employment program) and LSNC's Auburn office. Confirmed active on placer.ca.gov July 2026. Dismissal does not erase the record; it updates it to show the conviction is dismissed. RAP sheet required prior to registration. Sacramento residents should use the Sacramento County Public Defender expungement program or Capital Pro Bono instead (the county page refers them to Capital Pro Bono).

resources.name: Placer County Clean Slate Clinic (with Legal Services of Northern California)
resources.mission: The Clean Slate Clinic, offered by Placer County's Business Advantage Network in association with Legal Services of Northern California, assists participants in removing or dismissing past convictions from their records.
resources.services: Free monthly record clearance clinic, first Wednesday of every month. Attorneys review records for eligibility, help with court forms, advise on fines, fees and restitution, and explain remedies including conviction dismissal or reduction, probation reduction, arrest record sealing and certificates of rehabilitation. Participants must provide a copy of their RAP sheet before registration; pre-registration required, no walk-ins. Register through Legal Services of Northern California, Auburn office. Serves residents of Placer, El Dorado, Amador, Calaveras and Sierra counties. Federal convictions, most prison-sentence convictions, and certain violent or sex offenses do not qualify.
resources.notes: Clinic held monthly (first Wednesday); pre-registration through LSNC Auburn office required, no walk-ins. RAP sheet copy (obtained via Live Scan fingerprinting) required before one-on-one attorney review. Participants must be U.S. citizens or legal residents. California convictions only. Sacramento residents are referred to Capital Pro Bono instead. Cross-reference: Legal tab (Legal Services of Northern California).
resources.contactPerson: Intake staff, Legal Services of Northern California Auburn office

resources.name: Placer County District Attorney (Victim/Witness Assistance Program)
resources.mission: The Victim/Witness program provides advocacy, information, and support services to victims and witnesses of crime in Placer County. Program services are free and available regardless of citizenship status.
resources.services: County government victim advocacy for domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking victims whose cases enter the criminal justice system. Victim advocates available by appointment Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-5 p.m.: crisis intervention, court accompaniment and orientation, case status updates, help preparing victim impact statements, assistance completing California Victim Compensation Board applications, restraining order information, and referrals to emergency shelter, food, and counseling. The DA's Family Protection Unit prosecutes domestic violence, stalking, and restraining order violations. Free regardless of immigration status.
resources.notes: Location per county site (July 2026): 10810 Justice Center Drive, Suite 240, Roseville, CA 95678; fax (916) 543-2594. By appointment, Monday-Friday 8-5, excluding county holidays. Program includes a Joint Powers Unit that processes CalVCB crime victim compensation applications (funeral/burial, home security, medical/dental, mental health, relocation, income loss).

resources.name: Placer County District Attorney's Office (Victim Services and Human Trafficking Resource Portal)
resources.address: 10810 Justice Center Drive, Suite 240, Roseville, CA 95678
resources.mission: The Placer County District Attorney's Office has a dedicated Special Prosecutions Unit that works to hold traffickers accountable, find victims justice, help survivors connect to resources, and find legal options to help keep them safe moving forward.
resources.services: County gateway for trafficking victims: Victim Advocates trained in the criminal justice process and community resources, available by appointment Monday-Friday 8am-5pm; Special Prosecutions Unit prosecutes trafficking cases and connects survivors to services; online Human Trafficking Resource Portal with reporting guidance; California Victim Compensation Board claim assistance. Free; no documentation required to speak with an advocate. Referrals to Stand Up Placer 24-hour helpline (800) 575-5352 and KidsFirst CSEC program.
resources.notes: Victim Services Center: 10810 Justice Center Drive, Suite 240, Roseville, CA 95678. Advocates by appointment M-F 8am-5pm. Serves all of Placer County. Portal directs emergencies to 911 and crisis needs to Stand Up Placer. Cross-reference: Domestic Violence tab (DA victim services also serve DV and sexual assault victims).

resources.name: Placer County Family and Children's Services (24-Hour Child Abuse Reporting Hotline)
resources.mission: Placer County Children's System of Care intake staff are available 24 hours a day to take reports from anyone who has knowledge of, or suspects, that a child is being abused or neglected.
resources.services: 24/7 child abuse and neglect reporting hotline for children in Placer County, answered by county intake staff. Anyone may report; reports can be anonymous. Mandated reporters must call and then submit written report SS8572 within 36 hours. Local number (916) 872-6549. Have child and family names, ages, and addresses ready if known.
resources.notes: Operated by Placer County Children's System of Care, Auburn. Call 911 if a child is in immediate danger. Cross-reference: Foster tab (Placer child welfare services).
resources.contactPerson: Children's System of Care Director, Placer County HHS

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (24/7 Mental Health Crisis Line and Mobile Crisis Team)
resources.mission: Placer County's crisis teams use a whatever it takes approach to make sure that children, adolescents, adults, and older adults receive the care, support, and treatment they need when experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis.
resources.services: 24/7 county mental health crisis and access line answered by county behavioral health staff.
