Callers can request phone crisis intervention, psychiatric emergency screening, and dispatch of the Mobile Crisis Team (mental health clinician, psychiatric nurse, and/or peer advocate) which responds in the field 24/7. Serves all ages regardless of insurance. Local number (916) 787-8860. TTY 711 or (800) 735-2929. Interpreter services available.
resources.notes: Adult System of Care, 101 Cirby Hills Dr, Roseville, CA 95678; Children's System of Care in Auburn. Same number (888) 886-5401 also takes Adult Protective Services reports. Mobile Crisis Team expanded to 24/7 countywide. For life threatening emergencies call 911 or 988. Cross-reference: Mental Health category.
resources.contactPerson: Behavioral Health Director, Placer County HHS

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Adult System of Care, Behavioral Health)
resources.mission: Placer County Adult System of Care provides an array of mental health and supportive services for those who live with mental illness, with services individually designed to help each person achieve their personal recovery goals.
resources.services: County gateway for adult outpatient mental health: screening and eligibility assessment, outpatient therapy, medication support, case management, crisis triage, and linkage to contracted community providers. Adults 18 and older experiencing mental health challenges can call the 24-hour line at (888) 886-5401 or (916) 787-8860 to request a screening or attend an in-person screening clinic. Medi-Cal specialty mental health services; uninsured and low-income residents served. Substance use services line (530) 889-7240, M-F 8-5.
resources.notes: 11512 B Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603, with Roseville area clinics. 24/7 line (888) 886-5401 doubles as Placer mental health crisis line: cross-reference Crisis Help Lines tab. Gateway to contracted providers including Sierra Mental Wellness Group.
resources.contactPerson: Behavioral Health Director (Adult System of Care Administration)

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Adult System of Care, Crisis Services and Suicide Prevention Resources)
resources.mission: Placer County Health and Human Services provides crisis resources for residents, including suicide prevention resources, a 24-hour mental health crisis line, mobile crisis services, and the Lotus Crisis Center.
resources.services: 24-hour Adult Crisis and Intake phone line at (916) 787-8860 or (888) 886-5401 for any Placer County resident experiencing a mental health emergency or suicidal crisis; Child and Family Crisis and Intake at (866) 293-1940 or (916) 872-6549; mobile crisis response teams; Lotus Crisis Center (crisis stabilization); maintains countywide suicide prevention hotline referrals (English, Spanish, Veterans, Trevor Lifeline) and text line (text HOPE to 916-688-4226). No cost to call, available to all residents regardless of insurance.
resources.notes: Auburn Administrative Office: 11434 B Ave, Auburn, CA 95603, (530) 886-1870; Tahoe office: 5225 N Lake Blvd, Carnelian Bay, CA 96140. Crisis line is 24/7. Gateway entry for Placer County suicide-related crisis services. Cross-reference: Crisis Help Lines and Mental Health tabs. County crisis page also lists Know the Signs (suicideispreventable.org) campaign materials.
resources.contactPerson: Adult System of Care Crisis and Intake staff

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Adult System of Care, Mental Health Access)
resources.mission: The Adult System of Care helps adults and seniors by offering mental health care, substance abuse treatment and in-home support. We also help protect older and dependent adults.
resources.services: 24-hour mental health crisis and intake line at (888) 886-5401 or (916) 787-8860: screening and access point for county specialty mental health services, counseling, crisis support, and substance use treatment, primarily for Medi-Cal beneficiaries and uninsured residents with serious mental illness. Also operates the Cirby Wellness Center drop-in recovery programs and Family Support Services for family and caregivers of adults with mental illness or substance use disorder, (916) 787-8915. Free or low cost through Medi-Cal; access line screens eligibility.
resources.notes: Main behavioral health campus: 101 Cirby Hills Drive, Roseville, CA 95678. Auburn office hours Mon-Thu 8-5:30, Fri 8-5. TTY 711. Cross-ref Crisis Help Lines tab: 24/7 access line (888) 886-5401 or (916) 787-8860; call or text 988 for suicidal crisis. Serves Placer County residents of all regions including Tahoe.
resources.contactPerson: Amy Ellis, MFT, Adult System of Care Division Director

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Adult System of Care, Substance Use Services)
resources.mission: Placer County's Adult System of Care provides a wide array of substance use services depending on individual needs, supporting residents on the path to recovery and wellness.
resources.services: County gateway for publicly funded SUD treatment (Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System): screening, assessment, referral to residential treatment, outpatient and intensive outpatient, residential withdrawal management (detox), case management, recovery services, physician consultation and medication assisted treatment. 24/7 access line (916) 787-8860 or toll free (888) 886-5401. Free walk-in screening clinics on a weekly rotating schedule: Mon 10-11 am at 101 Cirby Hills Dr, Roseville; Tue 1-2 pm at 11434 B Ave, Auburn; Wed 1-2 pm at 10810 Justice Center Dr, Roseville; Thu 3-4 pm at 101 Cirby Hills Dr, Roseville; Fri 10-11 am at 11434 B Ave, Auburn. Medi-Cal and sliding scale; no one turned away for inability to pay.
resources.notes: Screening clinic sites: 101 Cirby Hills Dr, Roseville and 11434 B Ave, Auburn. 24/7 access line. Serves all of Placer County including Tahoe area (telehealth options for North Lake Tahoe). Entry point for county funded treatment network including Granite Wellness Centers. Cross-reference: Mental Health (same Adult System of Care).
resources.contactPerson: Behavioral Health Director, Placer County HHS

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Adult System of Care)
resources.mission: Placer County Adult System of Care offers comprehensive services for adults, including mental health, substance use, older adult, and disability related supports, helping residents live safely and independently in the community.
resources.services: County gateway for adults with disabilities: IHSS enrollment (call (530) 889-7115), Adult Protective Services, mental health and crisis services (24 hour crisis and intake line (888) 886-5401 or (916) 787-8860), older and dependent adult services, and referrals to community providers. Serves Placer County adults; Medi-Cal linkage required for IHSS. Offices open Mon-Thu 8:00-5:30, Fri 8:00-5:00.
resources.notes: Main office: 101 Cirby Hills Drive, Roseville, CA 95678. Auburn office: 11434 B Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603, (530) 889-7247. TTY: 711 or (800) 735-2929. Cross-reference: In-home Help tab (IHSS detail) and Health tab (mental health).
resources.contactPerson: Amy Ellis, MFT, Adult System of Care Division Director

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Children's System of Care, Children's Behavioral Health)
resources.mission: Children's System of Care provides integrated behavioral health, child welfare, and juvenile justice services to help Placer County children and families be safe, healthy, and successful.
resources.services: County gateway for children's outpatient mental health: assessments for non-crisis intensive mental health services provided by masters-level clinicians in all geographic areas of Placer County, individual and family therapy, medication support, wraparound, and school-linked services. Serves children and youth up to age 21, primarily Medi-Cal eligible; uninsured low-income families screened for coverage. Call (530) 889-6700 weekdays; 24-hour line (916) 872-6549 or toll free (866) 293-1940.
resources.notes: 24-hour numbers also serve as crisis contact for minors: cross-reference Crisis Help Lines tab. Foster youth services: cross-reference Foster tab.

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Homeless Services & Housing Programs)
resources.mission: Placer County Health and Human Services offers services for individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including prevention, outreach and engagement, emergency shelter, interim and transitional housing, permanent supportive housing, and supportive services.
resources.services: County gateway for housing crisis. Prevention: CalWORKs Homeless Assistance, CalFresh, General Relief, Medi-Cal; CalWORKs Housing Support Program (rapid rehousing delivered via Stand Up Placer, Kids First, VOA, and AMI Housing); Home Safe (APS clients); HDAP (disability advocacy plus interim housing); Bringing Families Home. Housing: permanent supportive housing units in 19 locations; 7 transitional houses (Auburn, Rocklin, Newcastle, Roseville) with AMI Housing; housing coordinators. Outreach: Homeless Liaison Team. Manages Coordinated Entry contract (211, By Name List). First step for any resident in housing crisis: call the Homeless Resource Helpline (833) 375-2237.
resources.notes: Auburn Administrative Office: 11434 B Ave., Auburn, CA 95603. Tahoe office: 5225 N. Lake Blvd., Carnelian Bay, CA 96140, (530) 546-1912. Homeless Resource Helpline (833) 375-2237 (833-3PLACER) feeds the By Name List and Coordinated Entry. 2026 Point-in-Time count showed a roughly 10% one-year decrease in homelessness.

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Human Services Division: CalWORKs, General Relief, CAPI)
resources.mission: Human Services provides a variety of programs to help Placer County families and individuals have a better future through access to healthy nutrition, healthcare, affordable housing, and training and temporary assistance when times are difficult.
resources.services: County gateway for cash aid and benefits enrollment: CalWORKs (time-limited cash aid and employment services for families with children), General Relief (time-limited cash aid for adults without dependent children, apply in person), Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI, state-funded cash for aged, blind, disabled non-citizens ineligible for SSI), plus CalFresh and Medi-Cal. Apply online at BenefitsCal.com, by mail, or in person; call center staffed by Eligibility Specialists for applications, case questions, EBT card replacement, and status updates. In-person help Monday-Friday.
resources.notes: Main benefits office: 11434 B Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603; mail applications to P.O. Box 20400, Auburn, CA 95604. General Relief requires in-person application at a Human Services office. Document drop boxes available 24/7 at office entrances. Cross-reference: Food tab (CalFresh, WIC) and Housing tab (Housing Choice Voucher program).

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (In-Home Supportive Services, IHSS)
resources.mission: The In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) program will help pay for services provided to you so that you can remain safely in your own home. IHSS is considered an alternative to out-of-home care, such as nursing homes or board and care facilities.
resources.services: Medi-Cal funded program that pays a caregiver (often a family member or friend) to provide in-home services: housecleaning, laundry, meal preparation, grocery shopping, personal care (bathing, grooming, bowel and bladder care, paramedical services), accompaniment to medical appointments, and protective supervision for the mentally impaired. Eligibility: over 65, blind, or disabled (disabled children also eligible) and eligible for Medi-Cal. Apply by completing the county application plus Health Care Certification (completed by a licensed health care professional) and calling Placer County Adult Intake at (916) 787-8860 or toll free (888) 886-5401. Offices open Monday to Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
resources.notes: Offices: 11434 B Ave, Auburn CA 95603 and 101 Cirby Hills Dr, Roseville CA 95678. Fax paperwork to (916) 787-8922 ATTN: IHSS Intake. Requires Medi-Cal eligibility; recipient hires and supervises the provider. Payroll unit: (530) 889-7135. Cross-reference: Placer County IHSS Public Authority row for provider registry.

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Older Adult Services and Adult Protective Services)
resources.mission: Placer County Adult System of Care offers comprehensive services for adults, including mental health, substance use, older adult, and disability related supports, helping residents live safely and independently in the community.
resources.services: County gateway for seniors: Adult Protective Services (APS) investigates reports of physical abuse, sexual abuse, financial abuse, neglect, self-neglect, isolation, and abandonment involving Placer residents age 60+ and dependent adults 18-59; reports accepted 24/7 at (916) 787-8860 or toll free (888) 886-5401, anonymous reports allowed. Social workers link elders to community resources, involve family, and alert law enforcement when a crime is suspected. Also operates Home Safe (housing stabilization for APS-involved seniors) and serves as the county entry point for IHSS.
resources.notes: Office: 101 Cirby Hills Drive, Roseville, CA 95678; Auburn office at 11434 B Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603. Office hours Mon-Fri 8:00-5:00; abuse reports taken 24 hours a day. Cross-reference: In-home Help tab (IHSS) and Housing tab (Home Safe).
resources.contactPerson: Adult System of Care staff (see county staff directory)

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Public Health Division)
resources.mission: Public Health works to keep communities safe and healthy, focusing on stopping problems before they start and making sure everyone has a fair chance to get care and stay healthy.
resources.services: County public health services: childhood and adult immunizations including no-cost vaccines for uninsured or Medi-Cal-eligible children through the Vaccines for Children Program (Shots for Students clinics are by appointment only, call (530) 886-1883 or email placeriz@placer.ca.gov), travel health, flu and mpox vaccines, communicable disease control, California Children's Services, childhood lead poisoning prevention, public health nursing, and vital records. Note: Placer County no longer operates county medical clinics (closed 2016-2017); the county refers patients to Western Sierra Medical Clinic, Chapa-De, and other community clinics.
resources.notes: 11434 B Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603; Mon-Fri 8am-5pm. Tahoe office: 5225 N. Lake Blvd., Carnelian Bay, CA 96140, (530) 546-1912. Immunization line (530) 886-1883, toll-free (888) 822-7274. Placer WIC (cross-ref Food tab): Rocklin (916) 784-6447, Auburn (530) 889-7187, Kings Beach (530) 546-1982. County medical clinics are closed; see Western Sierra and Chapa-De rows for safety-net primary care.
resources.contactPerson: Michael Romero, MPH, Deputy Director of Public Health

resources.name: Placer County Health and Human Services (Public Health Nursing Home Visiting)
resources.mission: Placer County Public Health Nurses work to meet the preventive health needs of families and individuals and promote positive health behavior in the community.
resources.services: In-home visits by registered Public Health Nurses for new parents, pregnant women, infants, and children in Placer County. A nurse performs a comprehensive in-home needs assessment (about one hour) covering newborn care, breastfeeding, child development, safety, and maternal health, then provides education, follow-up visits, and linkage to community resources. Access by submitting the Public Health Nursing Referral Form (self-referrals accepted) by email, fax, or mail, or by calling. Services are free.
resources.notes: Auburn Administrative Office: 11434 B Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603, (530) 886-1870; Tahoe Administrative Office: 5225 N Lake Blvd, Carnelian Bay, CA 96140, (530) 546-1912. Countywide including Tahoe area. Placer County does not brand its program as Nurse-Family Partnership; nurse home visiting is provided through Public Health Nursing with referral form intake. Cross-reference: Health category.

resources.name: Placer County Housing Authority (Housing Choice Voucher / Section 8)
resources.mission: The Housing Choice Voucher Program (formerly Section 8) is a rental assistance program to help low and very low-income families, persons with disabilities and seniors live in affordable, safe, and decent housing.
resources.services: Tenant-based Housing Choice Vouchers covering all of Placer County except the City of Roseville (which has its own housing authority). Also HUD-VASH vouchers for homeless veterans, Family Unification Program, mainstream vouchers for non-elderly persons with disabilities, project-based vouchers, and Family Self-Sufficiency Program. 2026 income limits: $45,050 (1 person) to $84,900 (8 persons). Pre-applications taken online only during open waitlist periods; status checks at waitlistcheck.com.
resources.notes: Mail: P.O. Box 5346, Auburn, CA 95604. Waiting list CLOSED as of mid-2026; do not refer clients expecting immediate applications. Emergency Housing Voucher program winding down (funding estimated to end around June 2026). Roseville residents apply to Roseville Housing Authority instead.

resources.name: Placer County IHSS Public Authority (Provider Registry)
resources.mission: Placer County In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) Public Authority provides information and support to IHSS Consumers who need help choosing a home care provider, and works with the IHSS program to help older adults and people with disabilities remain safely in their homes.
resources.services: Serves as employer of record for over 5,000 IHSS providers in Placer County. Recruits and screens IHSS providers, maintains a registry of screened and trained providers, matches IHSS consumers with qualified providers, and offers provider education. For consumers: call the main line (530) 889-7115 to request registry referrals. For prospective providers: enrollment (orientation videos, Live Scan fingerprinting) is completed online through the REVA system, linked from the county Provider Information and Training page; provider enrollment and support at (916) 787-8859, registry support at (916) 787-8836.
resources.notes: Offices: 11434 B Avenue, Auburn CA 95603 and 101 Cirby Hills Dr, Roseville CA 95678. Registry available only to authorized IHSS recipients. IHSS Advisory Committee accepts applications at (530) 886-3683. United Domestic Workers Union: (916) 751-2450.

resources.name: Placer County Office of Economic Development (Placer Business Resource Center)
resources.mission: The Placer Business Resource Center is your hub for free, confidential support to help local businesses launch, grow and succeed, offering expert guidance in business planning, funding, marketing, permitting and more, in person, online or through on-demand webinars.
resources.services: County government gateway for small business help: free workshops and classes, free confidential one-on-one advising delivered in partnership with the Sierra Small Business Development Center, help with hiring, permitting, licensing and regulatory compliance, referrals to lenders and technical assistance programs. Open to future and current small business owners countywide. Contact by phone, email or the online contact form to schedule advising.
resources.notes: Located at 1000 Sunset Blvd., Suite 105, Rocklin, CA 95765. Serves all of Placer County including Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln and Auburn. Advising is free and confidential, delivered in partnership with the Sierra SBDC; schedule by email, phone or the online contact form. Gateway entry: start here for referrals to all other Placer business programs.

resources.name: Placer County Probation Department (Placer Re-Entry Program, PREP)
resources.mission: The Placer Re-Entry Program is based on best practice research advocating for individualized service planning according to a client's unique reentry needs, providing both in custody and out of custody services structured around three phases.
resources.services: Day reporting center style reentry program for men and women residing in Placer County, in custody and out of custody. All clients receive risk, needs, educational and employment assessments and an Individualized Service Plan with a dedicated case manager. Program menu includes life skills (Courage to Change, parenting, money management, anger management), high school diploma/GED, computer education, job development and referrals to Golden Sierra, NCCT and Caltrans, substance abuse programming, 52-week batterer treatment, 12-step meetings, benefit screening and PC 1000. Access is by referral through Probation or the courts.
resources.notes: PREP Center, 10810 Justice Center Drive, Roseville, CA 95678 (back side of the Probation building). Hours Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Mailing: Placer County Probation, 2929 Richardson Drive, Suite B, Auburn, CA 95603. Listed as the county Probation program; day-to-day center operations may be delivered by a contracted provider (historically BI Inc., a for-profit contractor, which is why the county program rather than the contractor is listed). Cross-reference: Employment (Golden Sierra, NCCT referrals), Substance Abuse tab for treatment components.
resources.contactPerson: PREP Center staff, Placer County Probation Department

resources.name: Placer County Public Defender (Koukol and Associates, contracted)
resources.address: 3785 Placer Corporate Drive, Suite 550, Rocklin, CA 95765
resources.mission: The Public Defender's Office defends people charged with crimes who cannot afford to hire an attorney; Placer County provides this service through a private contract overseen by the Board of Supervisors.
resources.services: Court-appointed criminal defense for indigent adults and juveniles in Placer County: felonies, misdemeanors, juvenile delinquency, probation violations, and related proceedings. Appointment is made by the court at arraignment after a financial eligibility screening; there is no walk-in intake, but the office answers questions from current clients and families. No cost or low cost depending on ability to pay as determined by the court.
resources.notes: 3785 Placer Corporate Drive, Suite 550, Rocklin, CA 95765 (per placer.ca.gov, July 2026). Primary public defender contract held by Koukol and Associates Inc. through June 30, 2028; the county also maintains separate first and second level conflict defense contracts. Contractor site placerpublicdefender.com loads unreliably; use the county page. For record clearance see the Placer Clean Slate Clinic row.
resources.contactPerson: Dan Koukol, Public Defender (Koukol and Associates Inc.)

resources.name: Placer County Superior Court (Self-Help Center and Family Law Facilitator)
resources.mission: The Placer County Superior Court Self-Help Center provides free legal information and assistance to people representing themselves in court, including family law matters through the Family Law Facilitator.
resources.services: Free help for self-represented litigants: family law (divorce, custody, child and spousal support), child support calculations through the Family Law Facilitator, restraining orders, eviction response, name changes, small claims, guardianships, conservatorships, and limited probate. Telephone or video appointments Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 8:00 am to 12:00 pm and Wednesday 8:00 am to 3:00 pm; in-person appointments Tuesday and Thursday 8:00 am to 12:00 pm. Schedule via the court's online appointment system. Free to all court users; staff give legal information and form help, not representation.
resources.notes: Located at the Santucci Justice Center, 10820 Justice Center Drive, Roseville, CA 95678. Recorded information line; services by appointment. Staff cannot give legal advice or represent you. Quarterly probate workshops offered with the Placer County Probate Bar Section. For eviction defense attorneys see Housing tab (Legal Services of Northern California).

resources.name: Placer County Superior Court Self-Help Center
resources.mission: The Self-Help Center provides legal and procedural information and assistance with court forms to self-represented litigants with cases in or who reside in Placer County. All services of the Self-Help Center are free of charge.
resources.services: Free assistance with domestic violence restraining orders (obtaining, responding, renewing) and related family law matters for self-represented litigants. Telephone and video appointments Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday 8 a.m.-12 p.m. and Tuesday 8 a.m.-4 p.m.; limited walk-in appointments Monday, Tuesday, Thursday 8-10 a.m. (4 per day, first come first served) at the clerk's window, first floor, Hon. Howard G. Gibson Courthouse at the Santucci Justice Center in Roseville; prescheduled in-person appointments also available. Live chat for some case types. Online form preparation via Odyssey Guide & File. Not confidential and not legal representation; staff assist both sides equally.
resources.notes: Address: 10820 Justice Center Drive, Roseville, CA 95678. Phone is a recorded information line; email with ATTN: Self-Help in the subject line, response within about 2 days. Appointments via the court's online reservation system. Emergency (ex parte) protective order filings should be discussed with the clerk or a DV advocate (Stand Up Placer).

resources.name: Placer County Transit (fixed route, Dial-A-Ride, Placer Commuter Express)
resources.mission: Placer County Transit provides safe, reliable public transportation connecting Auburn, Lincoln, Rocklin, Loomis, Penryn, Newcastle, Roseville and surrounding communities: We're going your way.
resources.services: County-operated public bus system: fixed routes ($1.25 general one way, $0.60 discounted for seniors 60+, youth 6-12 and riders with disabilities, $2.50 24-hour pass, $1.25 discounted), Dial-A-Ride on-demand service ($2.50 general, $1.25 discounted) bookable via the GO South Placer app or by phone, and Placer Commuter Express weekday commuter buses from I-80 corridor Park-N-Ride lots to downtown Sacramento ($3.70 to $5.75 one way by zone). Medicare cardholders and Social Security recipients ride half fare. Dial-A-Ride hours vary by zone; check the website or call. Cash fares require exact change (no mobile passes accepted on board); 14-day and 30-day passes via Connect Card. Open to the general public; proof of age or disability for discount fares.
resources.notes: Operated by Placer County Public Works. PCT office: 3091 County Center Drive, 2nd Floor, Auburn, CA 95603, (530) 745-7570, TDD (530) 745-8732. Trip booking and rider info through the South Placer Transit Information call center, (916) 745-7560 or (530) 745-7560, and southplacertransitinfo.com. Taylor Road Shuttle became an on-demand Dial-A-Ride zone July 2025. $10 Summer Youth Bus Pass (June 1 to August 31) for students. Eastern Placer County (Tahoe area) is served separately by TART, also county operated. Serves western Placer County including unincorporated areas; connects to Sacramento via Placer Commuter Express and to SacRT at Watt/I-80.
resources.contactPerson: Transit Operations Manager, Placer County Department of Public Works

resources.name: Placer County Veterans Court (Placer County Superior Court Collaborative Courts)
resources.mission: Collaborative court for defendants who are veterans of the armed forces suffering from qualifying disorders related to their military service, offering treatment and supervision instead of traditional prosecution.
resources.services: Veteran-specific case supervision; court-ordered treatment for PTSD, traumatic brain injury, substance use and mental health conditions; coordination with VA and county Veterans Service Office benefits and care; probation case management; suitability assessment referrals through Probation and Adult System of Care; veteran mentor support.
resources.notes: Placer County Superior Court, 101 Maple St., Auburn, CA 95603. Referrals are made through defense counsel, Probation or the Adult System of Care; a suitability assessment is required.

resources.name: Placer County Veterans Service Office
resources.mission: The Placer County Veterans Service Office helps veterans and their dependents obtain the federal, state and local benefits they have earned, at no cost to the veteran.
resources.services: Free assistance filing VA disability, pension and survivor claims; appeals support; benefits counseling and eligibility screening; DD-214 and military records retrieval; referrals to VA health care, housing and employment services; veteran advocacy.
resources.notes: Administrative office at 11434 B Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603, with additional appointment locations around the county.

resources.name: Placer Independent Resource Services (Assistive Technology Services)
resources.mission: The mission of PIRS is to advocate, empower, educate and provide services for people with disabilities, enabling them to control their alternatives for independent living.
resources.services: Independent living center providing assistive technology information and referral, home accessibility modifications (installs adaptive equipment such as grab bars, threshold ramps, flashing doorbells, and CO/smoke detectors; no remodeling or major construction), independent living skills training, information and referral, peer support, personal assistant referrals, benefits counseling, housing information, and transition services. All services free and available to any person with a disability in Placer County. Call or use the website contact form to request services.
resources.notes: Main office: 11768 Atwood Rd. #129, Auburn, CA 95603. For free 30 day assistive device loans, see the Ability Tools entry (Both Counties). Cross-reference: Disability tab.

resources.name: Placer Independent Resource Services (Housing Accessibility & Advocacy)
resources.mission: PIRS is a non-profit independent living center. Our mission is to advocate, empower, educate the community and provide services for people with disabilities enabling them to control their alternatives for independent living.
resources.services: Housing information and advocacy: housing resource information, application assistance, search strategies, tenant and landlord rights. Minor Home Modifications for safety and accessibility (grab bars, threshold ramps, lever faucets, flashing doorbells, CO and smoke detectors, minor repairs). Transition and diversion services to obtain or maintain community-based living, including institutional transition. Assistive technology, independent living skills training, peer support, personal assistant registry. All services free to any person with a disability.
resources.notes: Main office: 11768 Atwood Rd. #129, Auburn, CA 95603. Founded 1993; serves Placer, El Dorado, and Alpine counties. Non-residential; does not provide housing itself. Go-to for accessibility modifications and disability housing advocacy.

resources.name: Placer Independent Resource Services (PIRS)
resources.mission: PIRS is a nonprofit independent living center whose mission is to advocate, empower, educate and provide services for people with disabilities enabling them to control their alternatives for independent living.
resources.services: Independent living center and Placer disability gateway: information and referral, independent living skills training, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology, housing assistance, transition services, and the Placer Aging and Disability Resource Connection (ADRC) with person-centered planning for seniors and people with disabilities. Any person with a disability of any age is eligible; call or walk in to start services. Also runs the Healthy Brain Project (Alzheimer's and dementia awareness).
resources.notes: Main office: 11768 Atwood Rd. #129, Auburn, CA 95603 (confirmed from pirs.org contact page, July 2026). Auburn based independent living center serving people with disabilities in Placer County. Website confirmed active July 2026 with current activities calendar. Cross-reference: Housing tab (housing assistance).

resources.name: Placer Independent Resource Services (PIRS)
resources.mission: PIRS is a non-profit independent living center. Our mission is to advocate, empower, educate and provide services for people with disabilities enabling them to control their alternatives for independent living.
resources.services: Independent living center serving people with disabilities of any age in Placer, El Dorado, and Alpine counties. Services include independent living skills training, information and referral, advocacy, assistive technology and device assistance, and the Placer ADRC (Aging and Disability Resource Connection) partnership providing person-centered planning, referral to long-term services and supports, and transition services for seniors and people with disabilities. Historically has offered minor home modification assistance (grab bars, ramps); call to confirm current availability. Any person with a disability is eligible.
resources.notes: Main office: 11768 Atwood Rd #129, Auburn CA 95603. Org operation verified on pirs.org (2026); minor home modification program specifics not detailed on current site, confirm by phone. Cross-reference: Disability tab.

resources.name: Placer School for Adults (Placer Union High School District)
resources.mission: Placer School for Adults provides lifelong learning opportunities including career technical education pathways to employment in multiple industry sectors, taught by credentialed teachers.
resources.services: Public adult school offering low-cost career technical education: clinical medical assistant training, computer and office skills, high school diploma and equivalency (GED/HiSET) completion, English as a Second Language, and a Career Center Lab where adults use computers to conduct job searches, prepare resumes, and submit applications with career counselors available by appointment. Open enrollment for adults 18 and over; fees vary by course with some free programs.
resources.notes: Main office: 3775 Richardson Dr., Auburn, CA 95602, open Monday-Friday 8:00am-4:00pm; Career Center at 1919 Grass Valley Hwy., Auburn. Call (530) 885-8585 to schedule a counselor appointment. Government provider (Placer Union High School District). Classes at multiple Placer County locations.

resources.name: Placer Sheriff's Activities League, Inc. (PSAL)
resources.mission: The mission of the Placer County Sheriff's Activities League is to unite the Sheriff's Office personnel, citizens, and youth of Placer County in the pursuit and implementation of initiatives that will reduce crime, better the lives of area residents, and enhance the community through action and collaboration with its partners.
resources.services: Free after school program Monday through Wednesday, 3:30-5:30pm, at Rock Creek Elementary School, 3050 Bell Rd, Auburn, for Placer County youth ages 8-17: mentoring by Sheriff's deputies and partner staff, leadership, sports, homework help (LEAP with KidsFirst), and drug and gang prevention. Also free Brazilian jiujitsu classes twice weekly during the after school program, outdoor adventure program for ages 13 and up, and Placer County Sheriff Explorers. All programs free; register via website.
resources.notes: 501(c)(3) nonprofit (EIN 80-0841816) founded 2012, run in partnership with the Placer County Sheriff's Office. Own websites: mypsal.com (programs) and placersal.com (events). Program site moved from Parkside Church to Rock Creek Elementary, Auburn, per mypsal.com; confirm current schedule and enrollment via Sheriff's Office main line, as no direct program phone is published. Also described on placer.ca.gov Youth Services page. KidsFirst co-facilitates LEAP mentoring at Rock Creek Elementary with this program.
resources.contactPerson: Youth and Community Outreach Deputy, Placer County Sheriff's Office

resources.name: Placer Veterans Stand Down
resources.mission: All-volunteer Placer County nonprofit dedicated to giving back to the local veteran community by providing free services to veterans and their families.
resources.services: Annual multi-day Stand Down offering free medical, dental, vision and hearing care; haircuts and hygiene supplies; clothing, boots and backpacks; hot meals; transportation to the event; employment and job-search services; transitional housing referrals; legal services; VA benefits counseling; pet care for veterans; year-round referrals to Placer County veteran programs.
resources.notes: Mailing address P.O. Box 582, Roseville, CA 95661. Spouses and children welcome; pre-registration recommended. Event is held at @the Grounds, 700 Event Center Dr., Roseville.

resources.name: Powerhouse Ministries
resources.mission: Powerhouse Ministries exists to inspire and empower people to rise above their circumstances, change their lives, and impact their community, helping break the cycles of addiction, abuse, and poverty.
resources.services: Faith based Christian nonprofit serving people leaving incarceration, homelessness and addiction. Men's Recovery Center and Women and Children's Center: no-cost residential recovery programs including relapse prevention, licensed therapy, case management, life skills, job readiness and family reunification. Crisis and Community Care Center in Folsom provides resources for people leaving cycles of incarceration, homelessness, addiction, abuse and sex trafficking, with immediate help plus long-term plans and referrals. Leadership College is a no-cost residential program for ages 18 to 24. Apply via the Get Help page on the website or call; office hours Sun 3 to 5 p.m., Mon to Wed 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Thu 9 a.m. to noon.
resources.notes: 11 Natoma Street, Folsom, CA 95630; mailing PO Box 1611, Folsom, CA 95763. Long term residential commitments with faith based programming. Cross-reference: Housing tab and Substance Abuse tab (recovery components); listed here for its reentry and family reunification services.

resources.name: Powerhouse Ministries (Folsom)
resources.mission: Powerhouse Ministries is a Christian non-profit which exists to inspire and empower people to rise above their circumstances, change their lives, and impact their community.
resources.services: No-cost residential recovery housing: Women and Children's Center and Men's Residential Recovery Center (relapse prevention, licensed therapy, case management, life skills, job readiness, family reunification). Crisis and Community Care Center: walk-in resource center for people leaving homelessness, addiction, abuse, sex trafficking, or incarceration; homeless prevention help, free medical clinic referrals, treatment referrals, job readiness, and connections to temporary and permanent housing. Care Center hours: Mon-Wed 9am-4pm, Thu 9am-12pm. General application on website.
resources.notes: Main office: 11 Natoma Street, Folsom, CA 95630. Serves eastern Sacramento County (Folsom/Rancho Cordova area). Confirm Crisis and Community Care Center street address directly. Cross-reference: Substance Abuse category.

resources.name: Powerhouse Ministries (Residential Recovery Centers)
resources.mission: Powerhouse Ministries is a Christian nonprofit which exists to inspire and empower people to rise above their circumstances, change their lives, and impact their community.
resources.services: No cost, faith based residential recovery: Men's Residential Recovery Center (two year program in Folsom) and Women and Children's Center for women with or without children, addressing addiction, depression, homelessness and incarceration; relapse prevention, licensed therapy, case management, life skills, job readiness, family reunification. Crisis and Community Care Center at 311 Market St, Folsom offers walk-in resources Monday to Wednesday 9 am to 4 pm and Thursday 9 am to noon.
resources.notes: 11 Natoma St, Folsom 95630 (ministry base); Crisis and Community Care Center at 311 Market St, Folsom. Christian program with religious participation expectations. Cross-reference: Housing category (Powerhouse Ministries).

resources.name: PRIDE Industries (Employment Services / I AM ABLE Helpline)
resources.mission: PRIDE Industries' mission is to create employment for people with disabilities, providing competitive business services that fuel that mission since 1966.
resources.services: Employment services for people with disabilities and other barriers to employment: I AM ABLE helpline (844) I-AM-ABLE connecting job seekers to services, vocational assessment, job coaching, supported and competitive placement in PRIDE's own manufacturing, logistics, and facilities operations and with outside employers, youth employment services, and Department of Rehabilitation vendor services. Serves people with intellectual, developmental, physical, and mental health disabilities; also veterans, foster youth, and others with employment barriers.
resources.notes: Headquarters: 10030 Foothills Blvd., Roseville, CA 95747; main line (800) 550-6005. Absorbed Sacramento nonprofit Crossroads Diversified Services in July 2020, adding mental health disability employment expertise; do not list Crossroads separately. Serves both counties and beyond.

resources.name: PRIDE Industries (Youth Employment and Transition Services)
resources.mission: PRIDE Industries' mission is to create employment for people with disabilities.
resources.services: Transition-to-work services for young adults with disabilities or barriers to employment: the Youth Employment Services (YES!) program serves opportunity youth ages 16-24 in Sacramento and Placer counties with soft skills and vocational training, job search guidance, paid internships, job placement, and on-the-job coaching. Job development services for former foster and at-risk youth ages 18-24 (income eligible, no longer in school, with a qualifying circumstance such as foster care experience, homelessness, or disability) include skills assessment, employment preparation, tutoring and mentoring, temp-to-hire paid internships, placement with a network of over 250 employer partners, and employee liaison support. Call the toll-free I AM ABLE helpline, Monday-Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., to start.
resources.notes: Headquarters: 10030 Foothills Blvd, Roseville (Placer County); Career Hub at 7011 Sylvan Road, Suite A, Citrus Heights (Sacramento County), (916) 676-2540. 501(c)(3) nonprofit social enterprise; referrals also come through DOR and Alta California Regional Center. Cross-reference: Employment and Disability tabs.

resources.name: PRO Youth & Families
resources.mission: PRO's mission is to inspire, educate, and mobilize young people to build a healthier future for themselves, their families, and their communities.
resources.services: Free school- and community-based youth development programs since 1981: youth leadership programs and youth advisory boards, mental wellness and relationship skills programs (MindOneSix initiative), substance use prevention education, paid youth stipend opportunities and the Youth & Family Collective. Served about 3,800 youth in a recent year. Contact via phone or email for program enrollment.
resources.notes: Programs offered at school and community sites across the Sacramento region. Cross-reference Mentorship tab. 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

resources.name: PRO Youth and Families, Inc.
resources.address: 3841 N Freeway Blvd Suite 210, Sacramento, CA 95834
resources.mission: PRO Youth's mission is to inspire, educate, and mobilize young people to build a healthier future for themselves, their families, and their communities.
resources.services: School and community-based youth development programs for youth roughly ages 12-26: mentoring that engages high school students as trained mentors to younger neighborhood youth, youth leadership and advisory boards, MindOneSix mental wellness initiative, life skills workshops, community service, and paid youth stipends through the Youth and Family Collective. Contact by phone or email to enroll; programs offered at partner school and community sites.
resources.notes: Office: 3841 N Freeway Blvd Suite 210, Sacramento, CA 95834; Mon-Fri 8:30am-5pm. Operating since 1981; served about 3,800 youth at 100 school and community sites in the most recent year reported, on track for 4,250. Website confirmed active 2026.

resources.name: Project GO, Inc. (Home Energy Assistance Program and Weatherization)
resources.mission: Project GO, Inc. operates the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) for Nevada and Placer County and has helped over 40,000 residents conserve energy as a means to lower utility costs and ensure a safe living environment.
resources.services: HEAP utility bill assistance for income-eligible Placer and Nevada County households: once-per-12-months payment toward gas, electric, propane, or firewood costs, ranging from $350 to $1,000 based on household income and energy costs; ECIP emergency utility assistance also available. Free Weatherization Assistance Program (attic insulation, weather-stripping, caulking, minor home repairs, carbon monoxide testing). Call the toll-free line and press 1 for Placer County; calls returned in order within 24 to 48 hours (the mailbox accepts up to 40 calls per day, try again after 9 a.m. the next day if full). Income documentation and copies of utility bills required.
resources.notes: Roseville-based nonprofit serving all of Placer County including Tahoe area. PG&E customers should also ask about the state-mandated CARE and FERA monthly discount rates (enroll directly with PG&E at pge.com/CARE, (866) 743-2273); Project GO HEAP payments can be applied on top of CARE discounts. Cross-reference: Housing tab (Project GO also listed for housing/energy services).

resources.name: Project GO, Inc. (Weatherization, Utility Assistance & Affordable Housing)
resources.mission: Project GO, Inc. is a non-profit community action organization that advocates for and enhances the quality of life of low to moderate income and at-risk families and seniors.
resources.services: Weatherization Assistance Program: free insulation, weather stripping, window and door work, water heater and heater repair or replacement, energy-efficient appliances (1,000+ homes annually across a five-county area including Placer). HEAP utility payment assistance: annual payment of roughly $287-$1,000 toward gas, electric, propane, or firewood; first-come first-served with priority to highest energy burden. Develops and manages affordable housing including Maidu Village I-III (senior, Roseville) and Colonial Village Auburn and Roseville (56 family units each).
resources.notes: Utility assistance once per 12 months per household, income-qualified with documentation. Weatherization line (888) 524-5705; HEAP line (800) 655-7705. Not an emergency shelter provider. Cross-reference: Financial category.

resources.name: Project Optimism, Inc.
resources.mission: Project Optimism is a 501(c)(3) organization based in both Sacramento and Los Angeles County that fosters optimism through personal and professional development services and community engagement.
resources.services: School-based Project Optimism Mentoring Sessions (POMS) for underserved students in grades 4-12: weekly culturally responsive workshops and mentorship focused on social-emotional learning, leadership, and academic growth, operating in about 12 schools and serving roughly 360 students annually; also scholarships, personal and professional development workshops, and community engagement events. Contact by email; volunteer mentors apply via website form.
resources.notes: Serves Sacramento and Los Angeles counties; Tax ID 82-1542836. No public phone listed on website, contact by email. Founded 2015 by counselors who mentored foster youth at the Children's Receiving Home of Sacramento.
resources.contactPerson: Armoni Easley and Ishmael Pruitt, Co-Chief Executive Officers

resources.name: RAINN (National Sexual Assault Hotline)
resources.mission: RAINN, the nation's largest anti-sexual violence organization, operates the National Sexual Assault Hotline in partnership with local sexual assault service providers, offering confidential 24/7 support.
resources.services: Call (800) 656-HOPE (4673) 24/7 to be routed automatically to a trained staff member from a local sexual assault service provider (WEAVE in Sacramento, Stand Up Placer in Placer). Online chat at rainn.org/hotline; text HOPE to 64673. Confidential support for survivors and loved ones: crisis support, information about medical and legal options, local referrals. Free; Spanish available.
resources.notes: Number (800) 656-4673, 24/7 phone, chat, and text options re-confirmed against rainn.org (July 2026). Local 24/7 equivalents: WEAVE (916) 920-2952 and Stand Up Placer (800) 575-5352.

resources.name: Rebuilding Together Sacramento
resources.mission: Rebuilding Together Sacramento's mission is to transform the lives of low income homeowners by improving the safety and health of their homes and revitalizing our communities.
resources.services: Free home repairs and safety modifications for low income homeowners, prioritizing seniors, veterans, and people with disabilities: Safe at Home falls-prevention program installs grab bars, handrails, transition ramps, smoke detectors and fire safety devices; essential repair program addresses health and safety issues so seniors can age in place. Must own and occupy the home in the Sacramento area and meet income guidelines; apply via website or phone. About 300 homes improved per year, over 8,500 since 1991.
resources.notes: 501(c)(3), EIN 68-0246355. Serves Sacramento area only (not Placer County; Placer seniors see Seniors First or Rebuilding Together affiliates elsewhere). Application required with proof of ownership and income. Cross-reference: Housing tab and Veterans tab.

resources.name: Rebuilding Together Sacramento
resources.mission: We envision safe homes and communities for everyone. To make this a reality, we repair homes, revitalize communities, and rebuild lives.
resources.services: Free home repair and home modification programs for eligible low income homeowners: Safe at Home (safety and accessibility modifications such as grab bars and ramps), Critical Repair, and Home Improvement Project programs in Sacramento County and the City of West Sacramento. Volunteer-driven repairs help seniors, people with disabilities, veterans, and families stay safely in their homes. Applications are open: apply online via the website homepage link or download the homeowner application (May 2026 version; Spanish available).
resources.notes: Mailing: PO Box 255584, Sacramento CA 95865. Fax (916) 731-7077. 501(c)(3), EIN 68-0246355, Contractors License 930688. Homeowners only (owner-occupied); income eligibility applies. Online application portal and downloadable application confirmed active July 2026. Media/partnerships: Bonnie Patterson, bpatterson@rebuildingtogethersacramento.org. Cross-reference: Housing tab.

resources.name: Resources for Independent Living (RIL)
resources.address: 420 I Street (Level B), Suite 3, Sacramento, CA 95814
resources.mission: Resources for Independent Living promotes the socio-economic independence of persons with disabilities by providing peer-supported, consumer-directed independent living services and advocacy.
resources.services: Sacramento's independent living center and disability gateway, serving people with disabilities since 1976: individual and systems advocacy, peer counseling, information and referral, independent living skills training, housing assistance, employment services, assistive technology services with an AT Device Lending Program, personal care assistance (caregiver/PCA registry), community living and institutional diversion, the Aging and Disability Resource Connection (ADRC), and the PEARLS program. Free; any person with a disability is eligible. Call or visit to begin services.
resources.notes: 420 I Street (Level B), Suite 3, Sacramento, CA 95814 (corner of 5th and I Street). Hours Mon-Fri 8:30-12:00 and 1:00-5:00 (closed Wed 11:30-2:00). Serves Sacramento and Yolo counties; celebrating 50 years in 2026. Cross-reference: Housing tab (housing assistance).

resources.name: Richard W. Townsend American Legion Post 84 (Auburn)
resources.mission: Auburn-area American Legion post dedicated to serving veterans, their families and the greater Placer County community.
resources.services: Veteran peer support and fellowship; assistance connecting with VA benefits and the county Veterans Service Office; military funeral honors and flag ceremonies; youth programs including Boys State and oratorical contests; community service projects; hall rental at the Auburn Veterans Memorial Hall.
resources.notes: Meets at Auburn Veterans Memorial Hall, 100 East St., Auburn, CA 95603. Mailing address P.O. Box 7004, Auburn, CA 95604.

resources.name: Ride to Walk, Inc.
resources.mission: Ride to Walk is a nonprofit organization providing life-changing therapeutic and recreational horseback riding for children and adults with special needs.
resources.services: Therapeutic horseback riding for children and adults with special needs; riders' challenges range from learning disabilities to quadriplegia, including cerebral palsy, autism, and recovery from injury. Riding sessions improve physical strength, mobility, balance, posture, socialization skills, and self-esteem. Each rider is accompanied by a trained leader, two side walkers, and a physical therapist when needed. Contact via website, phone, or email for enrollment; volunteer opportunities available.
resources.notes: Ranch located at 2460 Delmar Avenue, Penryn, CA 95663. Founded 1985 by Dr. Kristine Corn; twelve horses and dozens of clients as of 2026. Serves families from Placer County and the greater Sacramento region; ask about child sponsorships. All details confirmed from ridetowalk.org July 2026.
resources.contactPerson: Dr. Kristine Corn, Founder and Director

resources.name: River Oak Center for Children
resources.mission: River Oak Center for Children provides a comprehensive array of behavioral health services to children and youth throughout Sacramento County using a community based model.
resources.services: Outpatient and community-based mental health services for Sacramento County children and youth from birth up to age 21: assessment, individual and family therapy, medication support, wraparound, school-based services, and early intervention. Primarily serves Medi-Cal eligible children; referrals through the Sacramento County Access Team (888) 881-4881 or directly via the website referral page. Office hours M-F 8:00 am-5:00 pm.
resources.notes: County-contracted children's provider; access can also flow through Children's Access/BHS gateway listed above.

resources.name: Roberts Family Development Center (After School Program)
resources.mission: Roberts Family Development Center provides services to the Greater Sacramento area that meet the individual needs of each family member, with a holistic approach focusing on K-12 education and enrichment, parent education and empowerment, community advocacy and civic involvement.
resources.services: After-school academic program focused on building the skills and confidence of low-income K-12 students at risk of academic failure: academic support, tutoring, educational enrichment and parent engagement activities. Providing academic enrichment since 2001; now serves over 500 students and their families at about 7 sites in high-risk neighborhoods across the Greater Sacramento area, based in North Sacramento. Call to enroll.
resources.notes: Main center: 770 Darina Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95815; email info@robertsfdc.org. Cross-reference Mentorship tab (Freedom Schools and Food for Thought mentoring). 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

resources.name: Roberts Family Development Center (Food for Thought Mentoring)
resources.mission: RFDC's mentoring services provide high-risk students with one-on-one or small group supports that help them gain new skills, develop social-emotional resiliency, and build positive relationships.
resources.services: One-on-one and small group mentoring for high-risk students through the Food for Thought program, embedded in RFDC's after school Expanded Learning sites and summer CDF Freedom Schools; also Pacers Moving Forward college prep initiative and broader youth development programming. Serves North Sacramento children and families; contact center by phone, email, or website form to enroll.
resources.notes: 770 Darina Ave, Sacramento, CA 95815; Mon-Fri 9am-5pm. Founded 2001, serves 700+ children and families annually. Cross-reference: Youth Activities (after school and Freedom Schools) and Food tabs (Black Child Legacy Campaign partner site).
resources.contactPerson: Derrell Roberts, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: Root & Rebound (Reentry Legal Hotline)
resources.mission: Root & Rebound's mission is to support people navigating reentry and reduce the harms perpetuated by mass incarceration.
resources.services: Statewide Reentry Legal Hotline: currently and formerly incarcerated people, people with conviction histories, family members and service providers can speak with reentry legal staff for free. Hotline schedule per the current site: Monday to Thursday (800) 207-6992 ext 704; Friday hotline (800) 207-5047; the long-standing (510) 279-4662 line is also still listed. Record cleaning/expungement update lines: (510) 467-0917 and (510) 463-1969. Also answers confidential legal mail (Root and Rebound Project, P.O. Box 280680, San Francisco, CA 94128), publishes the Roadmap to Reentry legal guide, and holds workshops and trainings across California. Covers record cleaning, parole/probation, housing and employment rights, ID and benefits questions.
resources.notes: Serves Placer and Sacramento residents by phone, mail and statewide clinics (no local office). Website (rootandrebound.org, redirects to rootandreboundsc.org) posts a notice that its phone system is mid upgrade; urgent messages: (510) 279-4992. Former Friday-only 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. schedule and Oakland office address (1730 Franklin St.) are no longer published. Confirm current hotline number and hours before referral. Cross-reference: Legal tab.

resources.name: Roseville Home Start (VOA-NCNN Family Emergency Shelter & Affordable Housing)
resources.mission: Volunteers of America NCNN manages Home Start in collaboration with the City of Roseville to address homelessness among Placer County families; the campus provides emergency housing and affordable housing with access to needed services.
resources.services: Family Emergency Housing: 5 individual on-site units for families of 2-7, operating 24/7/365, with intensive case management, housing advocacy and placement, food as needed, after-hours support, life skills groups, and Ready to Rent training. No pets. Referral ONLY through Placer County Coordinated Entry, (833) 375-2237; placement by vulnerability score and unit availability. Also 21 affordable units on the Home Start campus (Riverside Avenue, downtown Roseville); currently referral waitlist.
resources.notes: Campus on Riverside Avenue, downtown Roseville. Formerly independent nonprofit Roseville Home Start Inc.; now managed by VOA-NCNN. Families cannot self-refer; must go through the Homeless Resource Helpline (833) 375-2237.

resources.name: Roseville Housing Authority (City of Roseville Affordable Housing Division)
resources.mission: The Roseville Housing Authority, established in 1974, provides tenant-based rental assistance to households earning 50% of area median income or less, ensuring households can afford safe and decent housing.
resources.services: Housing Choice Vouchers for roughly 850 low-income households (families, veterans, seniors, people with disabilities) usable in Roseville and Rocklin city limits; Project Based Vouchers; VASH vouchers for homeless veterans; Mainstream vouchers for disabled adults 18-61 who are homeless, at risk, or leaving institutions; landlord incentive program; publishes an Affordable Housing List of local income-restricted apartments. City also funds homeless prevention and rapid rehousing delivered through AMI Housing. Income limits (50% AMI): $46,000 (1 person) to $86,750 (8 persons).
resources.notes: City Hall: 311 Vernon St., Roseville, CA 95678. Office hours: Mon 9-12 and 1-3; Tue-Thu 9-12 and 1-5; Fri 8-12. Cross-reference AMI Housing for city-funded rapid rehousing and prevention funds.
resources.contactPerson: Housing Authority staff, City of Roseville

resources.name: RRUFF Healing Heroes
resources.mission: RRUFF Healing Heroes funds service dog training and healing programs for disabled veterans and first responders living with PTSD and other invisible disabilities.
resources.services: Sponsorship of service dog training costs for disabled veterans and first responders; peer support and healing programs; veteran resource referrals; RRUFF community dog park.
resources.notes: Program established in 2014; based at 4465 Granite Drive, Rocklin. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Sacramento Bicycle Kitchen
resources.mission: The Sacramento Bicycle Kitchen was formed to promote cycling as a low cost, alternative form of transportation, enable self-sufficiency through knowledge of bicycle maintenance, and promote bicycle safety through education and classes.
resources.services: Volunteer run nonprofit do-it-yourself bike shop: use of tools, work stands, donated parts, and volunteer mechanic help in exchange for a small daily membership donation (fee waivers informally available, donations of time accepted). Donated bikes are refurbished and sold at very low cost or given to youth in need. Free maintenance classes offered periodically. Donors can drop off used bikes and parts during shop hours. Hours vary with volunteer availability: typically Tue 6-9 pm, Wed 7-9 pm, Thu 6-9 pm, Fri 10 am-2 pm, Sun 10 am-1 pm.
resources.notes: 1915 I Street, Sacramento, CA 95811 (Midtown). Hours subject to closure if volunteers unavailable; check website or Instagram before visiting. All volunteer 501(c)(3), EIN 20-5009664.

resources.name: Sacramento Blue Star Moms (Chapter CA7, Rocklin)
resources.mission: Nonpartisan nonprofit of mothers and family members of service members that supports deployed troops, veterans and military families across the Sacramento and Placer region.
resources.services: Care packages for deployed service members; support and camaraderie for parents of active-duty troops; welcome-home and homecoming support; assistance and outreach to local veterans; participation in veteran memorial and holiday events; volunteer opportunities and donation drives.
resources.notes: Chapter CA7. Mailing address P.O. Box 1446, Rocklin, CA 95677. Based in Placer County but serves military families throughout the greater Sacramento region.

resources.name: Sacramento Central YMCA (YMCA of Superior California)
resources.mission: The YMCA is a nonprofit dedicated to strengthening community through youth development, healthy living and social responsibility, building healthy spirit, mind and body for all.
resources.services: Youth development programming including youth sports, swim lessons, aquatics, teen fitness (Safe & Fit for Teens), Summer at the Y day camps and family memberships at the Sacramento Central YMCA, 2021 W Street. Open Mon-Thu 5:30 am-9 pm, Fri 5:30 am-8 pm, Sat 7 am-6 pm, Sun 9 am-6 pm. Y-Assist financial assistance program helps with membership and program fees based on income and family size; apply online, by PDF or in person at the branch. Awards last two years, then reapply. Youth membership (ages 12-18) about $30 per month plus $25 joining fee.
resources.notes: Y-Assist applications at ymcasuperiorcal.org/membership; Summer at the Y and Bear Valley camp use separate Y-Assist scholarship applications. Note: no YMCA branch operates in Placer County (nearest branches are Sacramento, Capital, Rollingwood, Yolo, Gold Country).

resources.name: Sacramento Children's Home (Crisis Nursery Program)
resources.mission: The Sacramento Children's Home Crisis Nursery is a family-strengthening resource dedicated to preventing child abuse and neglect by supporting families in times of crisis.
resources.services: Sacramento County's only crisis nurseries: parents can voluntarily bring children ages 0-5 for free emergency daytime child care or overnight stays (up to 30 days) when facing overwhelming circumstances such as homelessness, hospitalization, mental health crisis, or job emergencies. Children receive beds, meals, clothing, diapers, and formula. Not affiliated with CPS; voluntary, confidential, and free. 24-hour emergency childcare available every day of the year. Two locations: North Crisis Nursery, 4533 Pasadena Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95821, (916) 679-3600; South Crisis Nursery, 6699 South Land Park Drive, Sacramento, CA 95831, (916) 394-2000. The Children's Home also operates a Birth & Beyond FRC and parenting education on its Sutterville Road campus.
resources.notes: Main campus: 2750 Sutterville Road, Sacramento, CA 95820; main line (916) 452-3981. Both site phones and addresses confirmed on kidshome.org July 2026. Call ahead for space availability. Cross-reference: Childcare and Foster tabs (agency also provides foster and mental health services).

resources.name: Sacramento City Unified School District (American Indian Education Program, Title VI)
resources.mission: The purpose of the Title VI Indian Education Formula Grant is to fulfill the federal government's unique and continuing trust relationship with and responsibility to American Indians and Alaska Natives for the educational needs of their students.
resources.services: Federal Title VI Indian Education Formula Grant program within SCUSD Youth Development Support Services. Academic assistance, cultural activities, summer programming for younger students, and the Native Youth of Sacramento (NYS) group for 7th to 12th grade Native students (a safe space with educational enrichment). Eligibility: student is an enrolled member of an American Indian tribe or Alaska Native group, or a child or grandchild of an enrolled member; families complete a Title VI Student Eligibility Certification Form (ED 506) through the district. Annual public hearing gathers parent input on the grant. Free to eligible SCUSD students.
resources.notes: Serves students enrolled in SCUSD schools only; families in other districts should ask their own district about Title VI Indian Education (Twin Rivers, San Juan, Elk Grove, and Washington Unified in West Sacramento also operate Native education services). Phone listed is the SCUSD main line; ask for the American Indian Education Program. Cross-reference: Education/Childcare categories.

resources.name: Sacramento County Adult Protective Services (24-Hour Abuse Hotline)
resources.mission: Sacramento County Adult Protective Services receives and investigates reports of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of elders and dependent adults, available 24 hours a day.
resources.services: 24/7 hotline to report physical, sexual, or financial abuse, neglect, self-neglect, isolation, or exploitation of adults 60+ and dependent adults 18-59 in Sacramento County. Urgent reports must be made by phone; a non-emergency online report form is processed weekdays 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. Reports may be anonymous. Call 911 for emergencies.
resources.notes: Operated by Sacramento County DCFAS, Senior and Adult Services. Cross-reference: Seniors category if built.
resources.contactPerson: Senior and Adult Services Division Manager, Sacramento County DCFAS

resources.name: Sacramento County Behavioral Health Services (24/7 Mental Health Access and Crisis Line)
resources.mission: Sacramento County Behavioral Health Services connects people of all ages to mental health and substance use services based on their needs, and provides 24-hour telephone response for mental health crises.
resources.services: Toll-free line answered 24 hours a day, 365 days a year for mental health crisis calls and for screening and referral into Sacramento County mental health and substance use treatment (Behavioral Health Services-Screening and Coordination is the main entry point). Local line (916) 875-1055 also answered 24/7. Serves all ages; Medi-Cal and uninsured residents prioritized for county services. Interpreter services available. Online Behavioral Health Request Form on website for non-urgent requests.
resources.notes: 7001-A East Parkway, Sacramento. County also funds mobile crisis support teams dispatched through 988 and this line. For immediate danger call 911. Cross-reference: Mental Health category.

resources.name: Sacramento County Child Protective Services (24-Hour Child Abuse Hotline, 875-KIDS)
resources.mission: Sacramento County Child Protective Services operates a 24-hour hotline that receives and investigates reports of child abuse or neglect to determine if a child's health or safety is at risk.
resources.services: 24/7 hotline (916-875-KIDS) for reporting suspected abuse or neglect of children in Sacramento County. Anyone may call; reports may be anonymous. Mandated reporters must make a verbal report then submit form SS8572 within 36 hours (online reporting available for mandated reporters, non-emergency only). Interpreter services available. Call 911 if a child is in immediate danger.
resources.notes: Operated by Sacramento County Department of Child, Family and Adult Services (DCFAS). Cross-reference: Foster tab (Sacramento child welfare).
resources.contactPerson: DCFAS Director, Sacramento County Department of Child, Family and Adult Services

resources.name: Sacramento County DCFAS (Senior Volunteer Services: RSVP, Foster Grandparent, Senior Companion)
resources.mission: Senior Volunteer Services engages Sacramento County adults age 55 and older in meaningful volunteer service that supports children, frail elders, and the community while promoting the volunteers' own health and social connection.
resources.services: Three federal AmeriCorps Seniors programs for adults 55+: RSVP (Retired and Senior Volunteer Program) places volunteers with nonprofits and public agencies; Foster Grandparent Program pairs income-eligible seniors with children needing mentoring and tutoring (modest tax-free stipend); Senior Companion Program pairs income-eligible seniors with frail, homebound adults for companionship and respite (stipend, mileage). Call (916) 875-3631 to enroll; background check required.
resources.notes: Program of Sacramento County DCFAS Senior and Adult Services. Volunteering itself combats senior isolation; Senior Companion clients receive free in-home companionship visits. Stipended roles require meeting income guidelines.

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Child, Family and Adult Services (Child Protective Services, CSEC Response)
resources.mission: The Department of Child, Family and Adult Services protects children from abuse and neglect; Sacramento County CPS operates a Commercially Sexually Exploited Children response as part of its child protective services.
resources.services: Government gateway for child sex trafficking victims: 24-hour Child Abuse Hotline (916) 875-5437 (875-KIDS) for reports of suspected commercial sexual exploitation of children; CPS investigates, determines temporary and permanent placement, and coordinates the county CSEC response with law enforcement, Probation, the DA's CSEC Court, and WEAVE, whose Anti-Trafficking Response Team advocate is assigned to each identified CSEC youth. Mandated reporters (teachers, medical and mental health professionals) must report suspected minor sex trafficking to CPS. Available 24/7; serves all of Sacramento County.
resources.notes: Verified July 2026: county CPS site loads at updated URL (old CPS-Home.aspx address redirects) and confirms 24-hour Child Abuse Hotline (916) 875-5437 (875-KIDS). CSEC response and WEAVE Anti-Trafficking Response Team advocate role confirmed on WEAVE's website. Sacramento DA also operates a CSEC Court. Cross-reference: Foster tab (CPS/DCFAS).

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Child, Family and Adult Services (In-Home Supportive Services, IHSS)
resources.mission: IHSS is a Medi-Cal based program funded by county, state and federal dollars, with the goal of allowing low income aged, blind, and disabled persons, including children, who are at risk for out-of-home placement, to remain safely at home by providing payment for care provider services.
resources.services: Pays a care provider so eligible residents can remain safely at home. Authorized services: housecleaning, meal preparation, laundry, grocery shopping, personal care services (bowel and bladder care, bathing, grooming, paramedical services), accompaniment to medical appointments, and protective supervision for the mentally impaired. Eligibility: low income aged, blind, or disabled (including children) with Medi-Cal. Apply by calling (916) 874-9471 Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 4:00 pm (application processed by phone) or mail an application to PO Box 269131, Sacramento CA 95826.
resources.notes: Mailing address: PO Box 269131, Sacramento CA 95826. Applications also by fax (916) 854-8828 or email IHSSApplications@saccounty.gov. Phone intake Monday to Friday 9 am to 4 pm. IHSS Payroll: (916) 874-9805. Requires Medi-Cal; a social worker conducts an in-home needs assessment. Cross-reference: Sacramento County IHSS Public Authority row for provider registry.

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Child, Family and Adult Services (Independent Living Program)
resources.address: 925 Del Paso Blvd, Suite 500, Sacramento, CA 95815
resources.mission: The Independent Living Program is a federally funded program which assists current and former foster youth between the ages of 16 and 21 achieve self-sufficiency prior to, and after, exiting the foster care system.
resources.services: Independent life skills classes, daily living skills, education resources, help with student aid applications, job search help, housing resources for emancipated youth, money management, decision making, self-esteem building, support and advocacy. Eligible: youth in foster care at any time between their 16th and 19th birthdays, served up to age 21. Referral by social workers, probation officers, foster parents, other county ILP coordinators, or self-referral; a Transitional Independent Living Plan is developed with the youth. Office hours Monday-Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
resources.notes: DCFAS also administers Extended Foster Care (AB 12) to age 21 and maintains a Housing for Emancipated Youth resource list. Cross-reference: Foster tab and Housing tab (THP-Plus providers).

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Health Services (Behavioral Health Services, Suicide Prevention and Crisis Services)
resources.mission: Sacramento County Department of Health Services is committed to ensuring residents have access to safe, trusted behavioral health resources, directing residents in crisis to the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline and county crisis programs.
resources.services: Behavioral Health Services Screening and Coordination (BHS-SAC) at (916) 875-1055 or toll free (888) 881-4881 for mental health screening and linkage; Mental Health Urgent Care Clinic at (916) 520-2460, walk-in, all ages, for mental health or co-occurring substance use crisis, 2130 Stockton Blvd, Building 300, Sacramento; Community Wellness Response Team (CWRT) responds 24/7 to 988 referrals with in-person crisis intervention, needs and risk assessment, and safety planning without law enforcement; Consumer-Operated Warm Line (916) 366-4668, Monday to Friday 9 am to 5 pm; Supporting Community Connections culturally responsive suicide prevention programs. Services available regardless of insurance.
resources.notes: Mental Health Urgent Care Clinic: 2130 Stockton Blvd, Building 300, Sacramento, CA 95817. Verified via saccounty.gov news release dated January 22, 2026, which also warns the former National Warm Line (855) 642-6222 is out of service; do not list that number. Gateway entry for Sacramento County. Cross-reference: Crisis Help Lines and Mental Health tabs.
resources.contactPerson: Behavioral Health Services Screening and Coordination staff

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Health Services (Mental Health Access Team)
resources.address: 3331 Power Inn Road, Suite 180, Sacramento, CA 95826
resources.mission: The Sacramento County Mental Health Access Team links Sacramento County residents of all ages to mental health services. Anyone may request mental health services for themselves or on behalf of others by phone, online form, or mail.
resources.services: 24/7/365 phone line at (916) 875-1055 or toll-free (888) 881-4881 providing over-the-phone screening, assessment, and linkage to county specialty mental health services for residents of all ages regardless of insurance. Anyone can call on someone else's behalf. Online Mental Health Service Request form at mentalhealthservicerequest.saccounty.net (non-urgent response within 3 business days). Substance use treatment access via the county Entry Point line. Free to access; services billed to Medi-Cal where applicable.
resources.notes: CA Relay 711. Not an emergency service: call 911 for life-threatening emergencies or 988 for suicidal crisis (cross-ref Crisis Help Lines tab; WellSpace Health operates the regional 988 center).

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Health Services (Sacramento County Health Center)
resources.mission: The Sacramento County Health Center is a Federally Qualified Health Center committed to providing accessible, high-quality primary care for Medi-Cal members and uninsured or under-insured residents of Sacramento County.
resources.services: County-run FQHC at 4600 Broadway: adult medicine with same-day appointment capacity, family medicine, pediatrics including the Circle Clinic for children and youth in foster care, Refugee Health Clinic, integrated behavioral health, on-site pharmacy, lab, and radiology. Accepts Medi-Cal, Medicare, and uninsured or under-insured county residents on a sliding fee scale. Also operates the Wellness Without Walls mobile medicine van for unhoused residents, drop-in care at Loaves and Fishes, and school-based health centers. Call (916) 874-9670 for appointments; arrive 30 minutes early to the first visit with ID and any benefit card. After-hours calls reach a health professional.
resources.notes: 4600 Broadway, Sacramento, CA 95820; Mon-Fri 8am-5pm. County immunization and maternal-child services run through the separate Public Health division at dhs.saccounty.gov; call to confirm walk-in immunization availability. Sacramento County WIC (cross-ref Food tab): (916) 876-5000, 4600 Broadway, plus Elk Grove satellite. CHDP program ended statewide July 2024; see Medi-Cal for Kids and Teens row.

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Health Services, Behavioral Health Services (Mental Health Access Team)
resources.mission: The Sacramento County Mental Health Access Team links Sacramento County residents of all ages to mental health services, conducting intake for adults and children and linking eligible individuals to culturally competent and linguistically proficient mental health service providers.
