resources.services: County gateway for public mental health: intake, screening, and referral to county-contracted outpatient providers (including River Oak, Pacific Clinics, Stanford Sierra, APCC Transcultural Wellness Center, and others). Services include prevention and early intervention, outpatient therapy, case management, crisis intervention and stabilization, and inpatient coordination. Anyone may request services for themselves or others by phone (24-hour toll free (888) 881-4881, local (916) 875-1055), online form, or mail. Primarily Medi-Cal and uninsured residents.
resources.notes: Mailing: Sacramento County Mental Health Access Team, 7000-A East Parkway, Suite 700, Sacramento, CA 95823. The 24-hour Access line also fields urgent mental health calls: cross-reference Crisis Help Lines tab.
resources.contactPerson: Ryan Quist, PhD, Behavioral Health Director

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Health Services, Behavioral Health Services (Substance Use Prevention and Treatment, System of Care)
resources.mission: Sacramento County Substance Use Prevention and Treatment Services provides access to treatment and recovery services for alcohol and drug use, contracting with community based providers throughout the county to support residents in recovery.
resources.services: County gateway (Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System) for adults 18 and older: phone screening and assessment, then referral to contracted prevention, outpatient, intensive outpatient, medication assisted treatment, withdrawal management (detox), residential treatment and recovery residences. Call (916) 874-9754 or toll free (888) 881-4881, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. Assessment offices at Granite Regional Park, 3321 Power Inn Rd, Suite 120, Sacramento 95826. Must be a Sacramento County resident; Medi-Cal accepted, sliding fees for uninsured.
resources.notes: 3321 Power Inn Rd, Suite 120, Sacramento 95826. Entry point for county funded providers (WellSpace, Bridges, Strategies for Change, VOA, Sacramento Recovery House and others). Youth access through the same system. Cross-reference: Mental Health.

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Homeless Services and Housing (DHSH)
resources.mission: DHSH leads Sacramento County's homeless response, funding and coordinating emergency shelter, outreach, and housing programs for county residents experiencing homelessness.
resources.services: Administers county-funded emergency shelters, the Homeless Engagement and Response Team (HEART, field- and shelter-based outreach), Full-Service Rehousing Shelters, and the Flexible Housing Pool (approved 2025; rental subsidies and housing navigation administered by Brilliant Corners in partnership with the Department of Health Services). Public guidance routes individuals to 211 for shelter assessment.
resources.notes: County site is JavaScript-rendered and could not be fully confirmed; phone and email from county listings. Residents seeking shelter should call 211 rather than the department line. How To Get Help page: schs.saccounty.gov/Pages/HowToGetHelp.aspx.

resources.name: Sacramento County Department of Human Assistance (CalWORKs and General Assistance)
resources.mission: The Department of Human Assistance helps Sacramento County residents who are in need become self-sufficient and independent by providing public benefits, employment assistance, and supportive services.
resources.services: County gateway for cash aid and benefits enrollment: CalWORKs cash aid and welfare-to-work services for families with children, General Assistance (county cash aid for indigent adults without dependent children), CalFresh, Medi-Cal, and CAPI. Apply online at BenefitsCal.com, by phone, by mail, by fax, or in person at DHA bureaus; form SOC 814 begins a cash aid application. Service Center phone hours Monday-Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
resources.notes: Multiple bureau locations countywide (see peoplesguidesac.org for the current list). General Assistance information lines: (916) 875-8908 and (916) 874-2599. GA is typically a loan repayable to the county and carries work requirements for employable adults. Cross-reference: Food tab (CalFresh) and Housing tab.

resources.name: Sacramento County Dept. of Child, Family and Adult Services (Senior and Adult Services / Adult Protective Services)
resources.mission: The Senior and Adult Services Division is committed to serving older adults and people living with disability by providing protection from abuse, neglect and exploitation while striving to preserve independence and self-determination.
resources.services: County gateway for seniors: Adult Protective Services hotline (916) 874-9377 for reporting abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or financial exploitation of adults 60+ and dependent adults; In-Home Supportive Services intake (916) 874-9471; Public Administrator/Public Guardian/Conservator (916) 875-4467; Age and Disability Friendly Sacramento County initiative; and referral to the Senior Safe House and community providers. Anyone may report suspected elder abuse; mandated reporter forms available online.
resources.notes: SAS Administration: (916) 874-9598. APS fax for mandated reporters: (916) 854-9341. Cross-reference: In-home Help tab (IHSS detail). Elder abuse emergencies in progress: call 911.
resources.contactPerson: Senior and Adult Services Division staff

resources.name: Sacramento County District Attorney (Victim/Witness Assistance Program)
resources.mission: The Sacramento County District Attorney's Office Victim Services Program provides services free of charge, with skilled and experienced victim advocates supporting victims of domestic violence throughout the court process.
resources.services: County government advocacy for DV victims whose cases are in the criminal justice system. The Domestic Violence Unit's victim advocates provide crisis and short-term counseling, court accompaniment and support, updated case status, safety planning, help preparing victim impact statements at sentencing, assistance obtaining emergency services (food, clothing, shelter), assistance completing temporary restraining orders, and help filing California Victim Compensation Board applications for crime-related expenses. Free of charge; contact (916) 874-6218.
resources.notes: Office address: 901 G Street, Sacramento, CA 95814; fax (916) 321-2201. Part of the Sacramento County DA's Victim Services program; works closely with the Sacramento Regional Family Justice Center (916-875-4673). Advocates can also help DV and stalking victims apply for the Secretary of State's Safe at Home confidential address program. Call to confirm eligibility.

resources.name: Sacramento County In-Home Supportive Services Public Authority (Provider Registry)
resources.mission: IHSS Public Authority assists recipients and providers within the IHSS program. Public Authority works closely with Sacramento County IHSS, but we are a separate entity.
resources.services: Services include provider enrollment (required for all new IHSS caregivers, with DOJ background check), a free Provider Registry that refers screened caregivers to IHSS recipients (Registry Specialists match consumer needs with provider skills, availability, and location), provider and recipient education classes, and the IHSS Advisory Committee. Recipients request a list of available providers by calling (916) 874-2888 or emailing IHSS-PA-RECIPIENT-REGISTRY@saccounty.gov; caregivers who want to join the registry call (916) 874-2888 option 2. Public counter hours 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM; forms drop-off 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday through Friday.
resources.notes: Office: 9300 Tech Center Drive, Suite 100, Sacramento CA 95826. Registry is free and available only to IHSS recipients. Registry applicants need three professional references, DOJ background check, an interview, Care Academy online training, and Registry Orientation. Provider registry email: ihss-provider-registry@saccounty.gov.

resources.name: Sacramento County Office of Education (WorkAbility I / Transition Partnership Program)
resources.mission: WorkAbility I is a nationally recognized school-to-world program that provides students receiving special education services with comprehensive pre-employment training, employment placement, and follow-up, facilitating a successful transition from school to work, independent living, and post-secondary education or training.
resources.services: Pre-employment training, paid work experience, job placement, and follow-up for middle and high school students with IEPs in SCOE special education programs and partner districts. The Transition Partnership Program links local education agencies with the Department of Rehabilitation to transition high school students with disabilities into employment or post-secondary education. Access through the student's IEP team or school transition specialist.
resources.notes: SCOE: 10474 Mather Blvd, Mather, CA 95655 (mail: P.O. Box 269003, Sacramento, CA 95826). No direct WorkAbility line published; ask the front office (916) 228-2500 for Special Education Services, or go through the student's IEP team. SCOE also supports Galt Joint Union High and River Delta Unified students ages 14-22 with IEPs. Placer students access WorkAbility I through their own school districts and Placer County Office of Education special education programs. Cross-reference: Disability and Employment categories.

resources.name: Sacramento County Probation (Certified Batterers' Treatment Programs)
resources.mission: Sacramento County Probation certifies the Batterers' Treatment Programs that satisfy the 52-week domestic violence offender treatment requirement imposed as a condition of probation under Penal Code 1203.097; the Superior Court and Probation Department publish the list of certified providers.
resources.services: Government gateway for court-ordered batterer intervention: people convicted of domestic violence offenses must complete 52 weekly consecutive sessions at a program certified by Sacramento County Probation. Enroll directly with a certified provider from the current list (July 2026): A Better You Services Inc. (916) 454-4242, Affordable Counseling (916) 630-9188, Man Alive Sacramento Inc. (877) 662-8465, A Path for Change (916) 251-9411, Enlighten (916) 369-5369. Fees follow the Probation Department's standardized fee policy. Sacramento County Probation does not accept Zoom/online BTP classes.
resources.notes: Provider list verified July 2026 on saccourt.ca.gov (cr-btp-programs.pdf) and the Probation Department's batterers-treatment-programs page. Always check the current list before enrolling; certification changes. Note: Terra Nova Counseling, previously listed in some directories as a BTP provider, is NOT on the current certified list and its website now advertises only DUI programs and general counseling, so it was removed from this tab.
resources.contactPerson: Sacramento County Probation, Adult Court Services

resources.name: Sacramento County Probation Department (Adult Community Corrections, Adult Day Reporting Centers)
resources.mission: The Adult Community Corrections Division provides community-based treatment and supervision as an alternative to incarceration through Adult Day Reporting Centers, collaborative courts, screening/intake/assessment units and community outreach.
resources.services: County gateway for adult reentry: Adult Day Reporting Centers (ADRC) provide intensive on-site supervision and therapeutic programming for justice-involved adults 18 and over assessed as moderate to high risk to reoffend; most individualized treatment plans run 9 to 12 months. Services include cognitive behavioral treatment, substance misuse treatment, self-help courses, educational programming (High School Equivalency/GED through Elk Grove Adult Education and SCOE), vocational assistance including NCCT construction pre-apprenticeship, connections to housing, and family support. Division partners with Health Services, Behavioral Health, Human Assistance and Correctional Health to connect clients to medical care, mental health treatment and benefits. Not self-referral: participants are screened and assigned by probation officers at intake.
resources.notes: Central Adult Day Reporting Center: 8745 Folsom Blvd, Sacramento, CA 95826, (916) 875-2372. South ADRC: 7300 Lincolnshire Drive, Sacramento, CA 95823, (916) 876-4041. North ADRC temporarily relocated to the Central ADRC per the county site. Participation is assigned through Probation supervision, not self-referral. Cross-reference: Employment and Substance Abuse tabs for partner programming.

resources.name: Sacramento County Public Defender (Clean Slate Program)
resources.mission: The Public Defender's Clean Slate Program helps people clear criminal records, including expungement under Penal Code 1203.4, juvenile record sealing, felony reduction and Proposition 64 relief.
resources.services: Free record clearance help for Sacramento County convictions: expungement (dismissal under PC 1203.4) for people who completed probation, felony reduction to misdemeanor, juvenile record sealing, Prop 64 marijuana conviction relief, and certificates of rehabilitation. Applicants must not be currently serving a sentence or on probation for another offense. To start, download the intake form from the website and email it to publicdefendere@saccounty.gov; applicants should also gather mitigation evidence (1 personal statement and at least 3 character letters). The office runs self-help expungement clinics announced on its Instagram and Facebook pages.
resources.notes: 700 H Street, Sacramento (county administration area); intake is by emailed form, clinic dates announced on social media. Sacramento County convictions only; for other counties contact that county's public defender. Capital Pro Bono, (916) 551-2102, is a companion referral for related civil legal help. Cross-reference: Legal tab.
resources.contactPerson: Clean Slate Program staff, Sacramento County Public Defender

resources.name: Sacramento County Public Defender (including Record Clearing and Expungement Unit)
resources.mission: The Sacramento County Public Defender provides quality legal representation and advice to any person financially unable to employ counsel in adult criminal, juvenile delinquency, and mental health conservatorship cases.
resources.services: Court-appointed defense for indigent clients: felonies, misdemeanors, juvenile delinquency, and conservatorship cases, appointed at arraignment after financial screening. The office also runs a free criminal record relief (expungement) program for Sacramento County convictions: conviction dismissal and reduction, arrest record sealing, and related Clean Slate remedies; call (916) 874-5732 or email PublicDefender-Expungement@saccounty.net. Office hours Monday through Friday 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.
resources.notes: 700 H Street, Suite 2701, Sacramento, CA 95814; main line (916) 874-6411, expungement line (916) 874-5732. Expungement help is for Sacramento County convictions; Placer convictions go to the Placer Clean Slate Clinic. Capital Pro Bono also assists with misdemeanor expungements (see Both Counties row).

resources.name: Sacramento County Public Health (Nurse-Family Partnership Home Visiting)
resources.mission: Sacramento County Public Health's Nurse-Family Partnership provides public health nurse home visitation for first-time pregnant women during pregnancy and the first two years of the child's life to improve pregnancy outcomes, child health, and development.
resources.services: Free, voluntary nurse home visiting for low-income, first-time mothers enrolled early in pregnancy (by 28 weeks gestation). A registered nurse visits regularly through the child's second birthday, covering prenatal health, newborn care, breastfeeding, safe sleep, child development, and goal setting for school or work. Self-referrals and provider referrals accepted by phone or by submitting the county's universal Public Health Nursing Programs referral form (email or fax). Medi-Cal eligible or low income; Sacramento County residents.
resources.notes: Main number (916) 875-2229 (916-875-BABY), fax (916) 875-0860, is the county's own current Community Nursing referral line covering NFP and other public health nurse home visiting. NFP-specific intake line (916) 875-0900 also appears in current 211 Sacramento records July 2026. CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (Healthy Families America model) is also available to eligible CalWORKs families through DHA: ask DHA worker or call (916) 874-3100. Cross-reference: Health category.

resources.name: Sacramento County Public Law Library (Civil Self Help at the Law Library, SH@LL)
resources.mission: The Sacramento County Public Law Library provides access to legal information for all members of the community, and its SH@LL program gives free guidance to self-represented parties in civil cases.
resources.services: Free civil self-help services for self-represented Sacramento County residents in limited civil case types: debt collection lawsuits (breach of contract complaints and answers), enforcement of judgment, claims of exemption from wage garnishment or bank levy, name and gender changes, guardianship and conservatorship of the person only, and small estate or limited probate matters (petition for succession, spousal property petition, small estate affidavits). All assistance is by telephone appointment: leave a detailed voicemail at (916) 476-2731 with name, callback number, and case type; staff return calls within five business days to screen eligibility. Cannot help people who have a lawyer or represent a business. Law library itself is open to all at no charge.
resources.notes: Law library at 609 9th Street, Sacramento, CA 95814. SH@LL cannot help with small claims (court Small Claims Advisory Clinic), evictions (court Unlawful Detainer Advisory Clinic), civil harassment restraining orders (court Civil Self Help Services), family law (Family Law Facilitator or Capital Pro Bono), or personal injury. Appointments by callback only; expect up to five business days for a return call. Details confirmed on saclaw.org July 2026.

resources.name: Sacramento County Veterans Service Office (Department of Human Assistance)
resources.address: 3075 Prospect Park Drive, Suite 170, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670
resources.mission: Sacramento County’s Veterans Service Office assists veterans, their dependents and survivors in accessing the federal and state veterans benefits they have earned.
resources.services: Free VA claims filing and appeals assistance; benefits eligibility screening; compensation, pension and dependency claims; military records retrieval; referrals to county and community services for housing, food and health care.
resources.notes: Open Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 4 PM.

resources.name: Sacramento Employment and Training Agency (SETA) / Sacramento Works America's Job Centers
resources.address: 925 Del Paso Blvd., Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95815
resources.mission: SETA, a joint powers agency of the City and County of Sacramento formed in 1978, is the local America's Job Center of California operator, connecting people to jobs, business services, training, child development, and other family services.
resources.services: Administers WIOA and operates the Sacramento Works network of neighborhood-based America's Job Centers across Sacramento County. Free services: job listings and referrals, resume and interview workshops, computer labs, career assessments, funded occupational training, on-the-job training, youth programs (ages 16-24), veteran priority of service, and specialized services for refugees, CalWORKs participants, and dislocated workers. Open to all; WIOA training enrollment requires eligibility documentation. Most centers open weekdays during business hours.
resources.notes: Main office: 925 Del Paso Blvd., Suite 100, Sacramento, CA 95815. Gateway agency for federally funded job training in Sacramento County; job centers hosted by partners including Greater Sacramento Urban League, La Familia, Asian Resources, and Folsom Cordova Community Partnership (see those entries). Also administers Head Start (cross-reference Childcare).

resources.name: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services
resources.mission: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services believes every child, adult and senior should have access to familiar, nutritious and sufficient food, and provides daily essentials and additional services so neighbors do not have to make impossible tradeoffs between food and other necessities.
resources.services: Official diaper bank for Sacramento County (National Diaper Bank Network member): free diapers distributed through 52 partner agencies countywide; download the public diaper distribution list from the website or call partner agencies first to confirm sizes in stock. Also provides free food through neighborhood distributions at over 200 sites, food for seniors 60 plus, and CalFresh application help. The former Oak Park clothing program has closed; for free clothing see other entries in the Clothing tab.
resources.notes: Main campus: 1951 Bell Ave., Sacramento, CA 95838. The Oak Park campus (3333 3rd Ave.) closed and clothing distribution ended; all operations now at Bell Ave. Diapers accessed via partner agency list on website, not at the main campus. Cross-reference: Food tab (food distribution).

resources.name: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services (Diaper Bank)
resources.mission: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services believes every child, adult and senior should have access to familiar, nutritious and sufficient food, and provides daily essentials and additional services so neighbors do not have to make impossible tradeoffs between food and other necessities.
resources.services: Official diaper bank for Sacramento County (National Diaper Bank Network member): free diapers distributed through 52 partner agencies countywide; download the public diaper distribution list from the website or call partner agencies first to confirm sizes in stock. Also provides free food through neighborhood distributions at over 200 sites, food for seniors 60 plus, and CalFresh application help. The former Oak Park clothing program has closed; for free clothing see other entries in the Clothing tab.
resources.notes: Main campus: 1951 Bell Ave., Sacramento, CA 95838. The Oak Park campus (3333 3rd Ave.) closed and clothing distribution ended; all operations now at Bell Ave. Diapers accessed via partner agency list on website, not at the main campus. Cross-reference: Food tab (food distribution).

resources.name: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services (Immigration Legal Services)
resources.mission: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services is dedicated to assisting those in need by alleviating their immediate pain and problems and moving them toward self-sufficiency and financial independence; its Immigration Legal Services program, operated under the auspices of Catholic Charities of Sacramento, provides no-cost and low-cost help navigating the process of obtaining legal status.
resources.services: No-cost and low-cost immigration legal services by a managing attorney and DOJ accredited representatives: consultations, DACA renewals, green card replacement, employment authorization, naturalization, certificate of citizenship, family petitions, adjustment of status, U visas, VAWA, TPS, SIJS, I-601A provisional waivers, and representation in immigration court for children (not adults). Expedited consultations for adjustment of status and for green cards or DACA work permits near expiration. Consultations cannot be scheduled in person: use the online request form or call (916) 313-7604 and leave a voicemail; low-income, no status requirement.
resources.notes: Program is the Catholic Charities of Sacramento immigration legal program operating through SFBFS (listed in DOJ/Immigration Advocates directory as Catholic Charities of Sacramento, Inc. - Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services), so no separate Catholic Charities row is needed. Spanish page available (sacramentofoodbank.org/inmigracion). Cross-reference: Food tab (SFBFS food programs at same campus).

resources.name: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services (Sacramento Diaper Bank)
resources.mission: Sacramento Food Bank & Family Services serves individuals and families in Sacramento County with a bounty of resources including food, clothing, and education programs.
resources.services: Official diaper bank for Sacramento County: free diapers distributed through roughly 52 partner agencies countywide (family resource centers, WIC-adjacent sites, clinics, nonprofits). Families download the public distribution list from the website or call 211 to find the nearest partner site; contact the partner agency to confirm sizes and hours before visiting. SFBFS also offers parent education, mother-baby university style classes, food, and clothing programs at its Oak Park campus.
resources.notes: Diapers are distributed via partner agencies, not typically direct from the warehouse; check current distribution list. Cross-reference: Food and Clothing tabs (org appears there).

resources.name: Sacramento FUEL Network (Sacramento Rapid Response Network)
resources.mission: The Sacramento Family Unity, Education, and Legal Network for Immigrants is a coalition of over 80 local nonprofits, religious organizations, law school immigration clinics, pro bono attorneys, and community partners dedicated to serving the legal, information, and health needs of the region's immigrant and refugee population.
resources.services: Rapid response hotline, call or text (916) 382-0256, to report ICE activity or get help for someone detained in the past 24 hours; covers Sacramento, Placer, El Dorado, Yolo, Sutter, Nevada, Butte, and Colusa counties. Trained Moral and Legal Observers dispatched to verify and document ICE activity; the FUEL legal team gathers case information and refers detained people's families to attorneys for consultation; the network dispels false raid rumors. Spanish and English capacity, usually one dispatcher at a time. Also lists legal services and know your rights resources (ACLU cards, ILRC red cards) on its website. Free, anonymous, regardless of status.
resources.notes: Hotline is the direct service (coalition otherwise; included per direct-service rule because the hotline serves individuals). The hotline is operated by NorCal Resist; number (916) 382-0256 confirmed July 2026 on both sacfuelnetwork.org and norcalresist.org. Use only to report ICE activity or seek help for someone detained in the past 24 hours. Highly relevant in July 2026 given increased ICE arrests in the region.

resources.name: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency (SHRA)
resources.mission: SHRA, acting as the Housing Authority of the City and County of Sacramento, provides assistance to very low-income individuals and families to enable them to afford decent, safe, and sanitary housing in the private rental housing market.
resources.services: Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) tenant-based and project-based vouchers for all of Sacramento County including incorporated cities; public housing; 12 waitlists managed at sacwaitlist.com (apply online free; preference points for county residents and workers, disabled, rent-burdened, veterans, homeless). Also homeless housing resources: Emergency Bridge Housing for transitional-age youth, Meadowview Navigation Center (women), X Street Navigation Center, VASH vouchers, Shelter Plus Care, and the SERA emergency rental assistance program. Office by appointment only; documents by mail, fax, or drop box.
resources.notes: Income limit example (2024): $41,300 (1 person) to $58,950 (4 persons). Waitlist openings announced at sacwaitlist.com and on social media. Applying is always free.

resources.name: Sacramento LGBT Community Center (Mental Health Services)
resources.mission: The Sacramento LGBT Community Center works to create a region where LGBTQ+ people thrive, supporting health and wellness through counseling, support groups, and community resource navigation.
resources.services: Free individualized counseling by appointment for anyone age 13 and older, with counseling services available Monday through Friday, 10 am-6 pm. Drop-in mental health respite helps de-escalate urgent stressors that could lead to suicide, hospitalization, or incarceration; also crisis intervention and counseling for victims of crime, support groups, and community resource advocates who connect clients to affirming providers, housing, social services, and legal aid. Funded in part by Sacramento County Behavioral Health, so services are free.
resources.notes: 1015 20th Street, Sacramento, CA 95811; Q-Spot youth center at 2031 K St, Sacramento, CA 95811. Website blocked automated verification again in July 2026 (JavaScript wall); counseling for ages 13+ and M-F 10-6 hours summarized from the Center's own mental health page via search. Adult respite reported relocated to partner sites during main building renovations. Confirm current waitlist and respite location by phone.

resources.name: Sacramento LGBT Community Center (STEP Shelter & Transitional Living Program)
resources.mission: The Sacramento LGBT Community Center works to create a region where LGBTQ+ people thrive, supporting health and wellness, advocating for equality and justice, and building a culturally rich LGBTQ+ community.
resources.services: Short-Term Transitional Emergency Placement (STEP): community shelter with average 90-day stay for youth 18-24 who have been victims of crime; meals, clothing, transportation assistance, case management, mental health clinicians, help obtaining ID documents, and navigation to permanent housing. Transitional Living Program (TLP): up to 24 months of stable housing for ages 18-24 (victims of crime) with intensive case management, counseling, education and employment services, and life skills. All housing services free; access through the Q-Spot drop-in center or via 211 for STEP placement.
resources.notes: Eligibility for STEP/TLP includes crime-victim criteria (federal VOCA funding); screen before referral.

resources.name: Sacramento Metropolitan Air Quality Management District (Clean Cars 4 All)
resources.mission: Sacramento's Clean Cars 4 All is an incentive program offered to income-qualified Sacramento residents that provides grants to help residents retire their old vehicles and replace them with zero or near-zero emission vehicles or electric bikes.
resources.services: Vehicle replacement grants for income-qualified Sacramento County residents: retire an operational vehicle 15 model years or older (in 2026, model year 2011 or older) that has been registered in California for the past two years, and receive up to $12,000 toward purchase or lease of an eligible new or used clean vehicle, or opt for an electric bike package instead. Household income must be at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level (for example, $46,950 for a household of one, based on 2024 tax filing); one grant per household; valid California driver's license required; higher grant amounts for residents of disadvantaged communities. Eligibility quiz and application on the program website; case management at (855) 201-5626 or cc4a@energycenter.org.
resources.notes: Sac Metro Air District office: 777 12th Street, Suite 300, Sacramento, CA 95814; district line (279) 207-1122, toll free (800) 880-9025 (old 916 numbers no longer listed). Sacramento County residents only; Placer residents are not eligible for this district's program. CAUTION: as of July 2026 the program website still posts a notice that new applications were paused June 7, 2024 to expand the program countywide and increase grant amounts, while the 2026 eligibility quiz is live; call (855) 201-5626 to confirm applications are open before referring. EVgo prepaid charging option currently on hold.
resources.contactPerson: CC4A Case Management (Center for Sustainable Energy, program administrator)

resources.name: Sacramento Municipal Utility District (Energy Assistance Program Rate and EnergyHELP)
resources.mission: SMUD is Sacramento's community-owned, not-for-profit electric service provider, offering income-eligible assistance programs to help customers manage and reduce their energy bills.
resources.services: Energy Assistance Program Rate (EAPR): monthly discount on electric bills based on household size and income for income-eligible customers. Apply online through SMUD My Account, by mail-in application, or by phone. EnergyHELP: donation-funded emergency bill assistance up to $200 per year toward unpaid SMUD balances for customers with a shut-off notice, distributed through four charities (The Salvation Army, Sacramento Food Bank and Family Services, Travelers Aid, Folsom Cordova Community Partnership). Medical Equipment Discount rate ($15/month) also available, plus payment arrangements, installment plans, and payment extensions through My Account.
resources.notes: SMUD is a municipal (government) utility serving most of Sacramento County. PG&E gas customers in the region should also enroll in the state-mandated CARE (20%+ discount) or FERA programs directly with PG&E, (866) 743-2273; PG&E itself is for-profit and is noted here rather than listed separately.

resources.name: Sacramento Native American Health Center
resources.mission: SNAHC is committed to enhancing quality of life by providing a culturally competent, holistic, and patient-centered continuum of care. SNAHC is committed to serving the Native community and welcomes everyone to receive high-quality healthcare.
resources.services: Nonprofit FQHC open to everyone: there are no tribal or ethnic requirements to receive care. Adult medicine, pediatrics, comprehensive dental for children and adults, optometry, mental health and substance use counseling combined with traditional healing practices (Healing Ways), specialty services including acupuncture, chiropractic, and gender-affirming care, nutrition and diabetes care, Enhanced Care Management, and Covered California enrollment help. Appointments at (916) 341-0575. Two health centers: Midtown (2020 J Street) and South Sacramento (3800 Florin Road), plus a school-based clinic at Grant Union High School.
resources.notes: 2020 J Street, Sacramento, CA 95811 and 3800 Florin Road, Sacramento, CA 95823. FQHC since 2007, roots to 1974. Community HealthWorks outstations enrollment staff at the Florin Road site (see Community HealthWorks row).

resources.name: Sacramento Native American Health Center (SNAHC)
resources.mission: SNAHC is committed to continuing and sharing the legacy of a healthy American Indian and Alaska Native community based on cultural values, delivered through a traditional, innovative, and accessible patient-centered health home.
resources.services: Nonprofit urban Indian health program and Federally Qualified Health Center serving Sacramento since 2006. Medical, dental, optometry, podiatry, chiropractic, and behavioral health care. Behavioral health combines counseling with traditional healing: individual, child, adolescent, and family counseling, psychiatry, White Bison 12-step recovery groups, culturally informed outpatient substance use treatment, talking circles, traditional healing, culturally informed parenting groups, domestic violence prevention and anger management groups, case management. No tribal or ethnic requirement: open to all, with Medi-Cal, Medicare, private insurance, and sliding scale accepted. Call to register and make an appointment; after-hours on-call staff available 24/7 at the main number. J Street clinic open Monday to Friday 8:00am to 5:00pm; Florin Road clinic open Monday to Friday 8:30am to 5:30pm; both open at 10:00am the first Wednesday of each month.
resources.notes: Main clinic: 2020 J St, Sacramento, CA 95811. Second clinic: 3800 Florin Rd, Sacramento, CA 95823 (South Sacramento), now open. One phone number for all locations: (916) 341-0575. Serves anyone regardless of tribal status; Native patients receive culturally centered care and IHS-funded services. Cross-reference: Health category (medical/dental) and this category for cultural and behavioral health programs.

resources.name: Sacramento Recovery House, Inc. (Gateway House for Women)
resources.mission: Gateway House for Women, established in 1968, is a licensed and certified facility dedicated to helping women in their recovery from substance abuse, operated by Sacramento Recovery House, Inc. with gender responsive, trauma informed care.
resources.services: Residential social model recovery program for adult women: structured live-in treatment, 12 step orientation, substance use education, individual and group counseling, trauma informed and gender responsive programming, life skills and peer support. Program operates 24 hours, seven days a week; office information Monday to Friday 7 am to 5 pm. Access by phone intake or county access line (916) 874-9754; Medi-Cal and self pay.
resources.notes: 4049 Miller Way, Sacramento 95817. Same 501(c)(3) as Sacramento Recovery House men's program; listed separately because intake and facility are distinct.

resources.name: Sacramento Recovery House, Inc. (Men's Program)
resources.mission: Sacramento Recovery House, Inc. is dedicated to providing gender responsive, trauma informed residential services to adult persons seeking recovery from substance use and co-occurring disorders, and their related issues.
resources.services: Nonprofit (founded 1964) 17 bed social model residential recovery program for adult men, licensed by DHCS: structured 30, 60 and 90 day live-in programs in a residential neighborhood, 12 step oriented (at least one meeting per day), substance misuse education classes, individual and group meetings, peer accountability and life skills. Access by phone intake or via county access line (916) 874-9754; Medi-Cal and self pay.
resources.notes: Corporate office: 1914 22nd St, Sacramento 95816. Sister program: Gateway House for Women (separate row). 501(c)(3) per GuideStar (EIN 94-1582683).

resources.name: Sacramento Regional Family Justice Center
resources.address: 3701 Power Inn Road, Suite 3100 (third floor), Sacramento, CA 95826
resources.mission: The Sacramento Regional Family Justice Center brings advocates, law enforcement, legal help and community services together under one roof so that survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, elder abuse, human trafficking and stalking can find safety, hope and healing in a single location.
resources.services: One-stop, co-located multi-agency center: survivors can meet with victim advocates, get help filing police reports, receive restraining order assistance, safety planning, connections to emergency shelter, counseling referrals, legal aid, and support for children, all in one visit at no cost. Walk-in and phone intake Monday-Friday 8:30 a.m.-5 p.m.; phone (916) 875-HOPE (4673). Operated in partnership with the Sacramento County District Attorney's Office and community partners. No documentation required; interpreters available.
resources.notes: Location: 3701 Power Inn Road, Suite 3100 (third floor), Sacramento, CA 95826. Hours Monday-Friday 8:30-5, closed weekends. Co-located near the Family Relations Courthouse (3341 Power Inn Rd), convenient for same-day restraining order filing. Partnership includes DA victim advocates and nonprofit partners.

resources.name: Sacramento Regional Transit District (Reduced Fares and RydeFreeRT)
resources.mission: The Sacramento Regional Transit District provides bus, light rail and on-demand public transit connecting the Sacramento region.
resources.services: Regional bus and light rail with discount fares for seniors 62 and over (proof of age), persons with disabilities (SacRT disabled ID, Medicare card or other agency ID) and students; Super Senior sticker for riders 75 and over; children 5 and under free (up to two per fare-paying adult). Veterans, seniors 65+ and Medicare cardholders can also get discount fares through the Tap2Ride program (pre-registration required). RydeFreeRT lets all TK-12 grade youth who live or attend school in the service area ride free with a RydeFreeRT card: 2026-27 school year cards (valid June 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027) are distributed at school offices, the Customer Service Center (1225 R Street) and Sacramento County public libraries. Attendants of riders with an attendant notation on their SacRT disabled ID ride at discount fare. Pay by cash, Connect Card, ZipPass app or Tap2Ride.
resources.notes: Customer Service and Sales Center: 1225 R Street, Sacramento, CA 95811 (adjacent to 13th Street Station); call center Mon-Fri 6:30am-6pm, weekends 7am-4pm. District offices: 1102 Q Street, Suite 3000. Service area covers most of urbanized Sacramento County including Citrus Heights, Rancho Cordova, Folsom and Elk Grove (e-tran services annexed into SacRT 2021). Proof of age or disability required for discount fare ID. RydeFreeRT confirmed active for the 2026-27 school year.

resources.name: Sacramento Regional Transit District (SacRT GO Paratransit and SacRT Flex)
resources.mission: SacRT GO offers door-to-door, shared-ride transportation for individuals who are unable to use SacRT's bus and light rail system.
resources.services: Two demand-response programs: SacRT GO ADA paratransit provides door-to-door shared rides for people whose physical, cognitive or visual disability prevents independent use of fixed-route transit; requires an ADA eligibility application (download online, submit by mail, or call to request), with rides reserved in advance; serves locations within 3/4 mile of bus routes and light rail. SacRT Flex (replaced SmaRT Ride January 2025; operated by Via) is $2.50 per ride curb-to-curb shared-ride service for approved riders: seniors 62+, SacRT disabled ID cardholders, low-income riders (CalFresh, CalWORKs, TANF, Medi-Cal or DHA pass) and minors 13-17 in low-income households. Flex hours effective July 1, 2026: Mon-Fri 6am-7pm and Sat 9am-5pm, in nine zones: Elk Grove, Florin-Gerber, Franklin-South Sacramento, Downtown-Midtown, Natomas-North Sacramento, Arden-Carmichael, Rancho Cordova, Citrus Heights-Antelope-Orangevale and Folsom. Book via the SacRT Flex app or reservation line (916) 915-0972, on demand 30 minutes ahead or up to two days in advance.
resources.notes: SacRT GO applications and eligibility: (916) 557-4685 or paratransit@sacrt.com. SacRT Flex requires advance approval: apply at sacrt.com/applyflex; $2.50 flat fare, no passes or Connect Card accepted, cash or card in app; children ride free with parents. SmaRT Ride microtransit was discontinued December 31, 2024. Flex received Access for All funding to expand wheelchair accessible on-demand service.

resources.name: Sacramento Steps Forward (Continuum of Care Lead / Coordinated Access System)
resources.address: 2150 River Plaza Drive, Suite 385, Sacramento, CA 95833
resources.mission: Sacramento Steps Forward coordinates the data, dollars, and daily work of the region's efforts to prevent and resolve homelessness for our community. Our vision is a Sacramento where everyone has a safe place to call home.
resources.services: County gateway for housing crisis. Lead agency for the Sacramento Continuum of Care since 2011. Operates the Coordinated Access System (CAS), the front door to shelter, housing navigation, homelessness prevention, and permanent supportive housing referrals countywide; also HMIS administration, Survivor CAS for domestic violence survivors, and CoC/HHAP funding administration. Not a direct shelter provider: individuals access help by dialing 2-1-1 (press 8) or (844) 546-1464 for a shelter and housing assessment.
resources.notes: EIN 27-4907397. Clients should NOT call the office for shelter; access is exclusively via 211 (press 8) or the CAS line. Access page: sacramentostepsforward.org/access-support/.

resources.name: Sacramento Superior Court (Family Law Facilitator's Office / Self-Help Center)
resources.mission: The Family Law Facilitator's Office Self-Help Center provides assistance with obtaining, responding to, modifying, and renewing domestic violence and elder abuse restraining orders for self-represented litigants.
resources.services: Free court-based help preparing domestic violence restraining order (DVRO) paperwork. Family Law and Probate Self-Help Center, Room 314 (third floor), William R. Ridgeway Family Relations Courthouse, 3341 Power Inn Road, Sacramento; open Monday-Thursday 8:30 a.m.-4 p.m. and Friday 8:30 a.m.-12 p.m. Help available in person (first come, first served or by appointment), through Zoom and in-person workshops, the Virtual Front Counter, and e-correspondence; no attorney-client relationship. DVRO requests filed at the Ridgeway courthouse or via the court's e-delivery portal by 1 p.m. Monday-Friday receive a same-day response; forms submitted after 1 p.m. are ready the next court day.
resources.notes: Located at the William R. Ridgeway Family Relations Courthouse, 3341 Power Inn Road, Sacramento, CA 95826, Room 314 (near the Family Justice Center at 3701 Power Inn Rd). No public direct phone published for restraining order help; use in-person visit, workshops, the Virtual Front Counter, or e-correspondence via the court website (responses within about 3 business days). A 211 Sacramento resource specialist staffs the Community Resource Room off the Self-Help Center lobby. The DA's office and WEAVE Legal also assist with restraining orders.

resources.name: Sacramento Superior Court (Self-Help Center and Family Law Facilitator)
resources.mission: The Sacramento Superior Court Self-Help Center and Family Law Facilitator provide free assistance and legal information to self-represented litigants in family law and other case types.
resources.services: Free help for self-represented litigants: divorce and legal separation, parentage, child custody and visitation forms, child and spousal support (Family Law Facilitator), domestic violence restraining orders, and referrals for civil matters. Walk-in and workshop formats; hours 8:30 am to 12:00 pm Monday through Friday and 1:30 pm to 4:00 pm Monday through Thursday. Free to all Sacramento County court users; staff provide information and form preparation help, not legal advice or representation.
resources.notes: Located in the William R. Ridgeway Family Relations Courthouse, 3341 Power Inn Road, Sacramento, CA 95826. For non-family civil matters (small claims, some civil cases) see also the court's Civil Self Help Services and the SH@LL row (Sacramento County Public Law Library). Eviction help: cross-reference Housing tab.

resources.name: Sacramento Valley Small Business Development Center (hosted by California Capital FDC)
resources.mission: Whether you are just starting or looking to grow, SBDC can help you navigate every turn at every stage of your business; SBDC advising is confidential and 100 percent pro-bono.
resources.services: Free confidential one-on-one business advising at every stage (startup, growth, transition and sale), help getting funded including SBA loan packaging, free webinars and trainings, restaurant program, technology and import/export specialty advising, and The Shop beauty and barber program. Serves Sacramento, Sutter, Yolo and Yuba counties. Sign up online at sacramentovalleysbdc.org/join; advising by appointment.
resources.notes: 1792 Tribute Road, Suite 455, Sacramento, CA 95815; open Mon-Fri by appointment. Part of the Northern California SBDC network (Cal Poly Humboldt Sponsored Programs Foundation), funded by SBA and CalOSBA. Hosted by California Capital FDC. This center replaced the former Capital Region SBDC branding for the area; Placer County is covered by Sierra SBDC, not this center. Email listed in the NorCal SBDC network directory.

resources.name: Sacramento Vet Center (VA Readjustment Counseling Service)
resources.mission: Vet Centers provide confidential readjustment counseling to combat veterans, service members and their families, supporting the transition from military to civilian life.
resources.services: Individual, group, family and couples counseling; PTSD and military sexual trauma counseling; bereavement counseling; substance use screening and referral; community outreach and mobile Vet Center services.
resources.notes: Nationwide Vet Center call center available 24/7 at 1-877-927-8387.

resources.name: Sacramento Youth Symphony & Academy of Music (Tuition Assistance)
resources.mission: The Sacramento Youth Symphony & Academy of Music's mission is to educate and advance the musical skills of the youth in our communities in ways that engage, challenge and inspire them to reach their highest potential.
resources.services: Orchestral and music education programs for school-age youth with need-based tuition assistance: partial or full assistance up to 90 percent of tuition granted by financial need (indicate on the registration form and complete the financial questions; tax documentation may be requested). All registrants including assistance applicants pay a $100 deposit plus small registration fee; 2026 aid deadline is July 28. Limited merit scholarships for new members on oboe, bassoon, string bass and brass. Auditions required for orchestras; summer workshops available.
resources.notes: Office: 3443 Ramona Avenue, Suite 22, Sacramento, CA 95826. Rehearsals held at 601 N. 10th Street and other Sacramento venues. Assistance is limited and granted to greatest financial need first; apply early in the registration cycle. 501(c)(3) nonprofit (Tax ID 68-0233148).

resources.name: Safer Alternatives thru Networking and Education (SANE)
resources.mission: SANE's mission is to provide services and education for people who inject drugs which help them enhance their health and wellness and improve their quality of life. All services are provided free of charge.
resources.services: Nonprofit harm reduction agency: needs based syringe exchange program, safer use and safer sex supplies, naloxone and overdose prevention education, HIV and hepatitis C testing, education and referral, street outreach to people experiencing homelessness, and a low barrier medication assisted treatment (MAT) program. Also packs and ships naloxone and supplies for NEXT Distro requests in California. Open Tuesday through Saturday, 3 pm to 6 pm; no documentation required.
resources.notes: 2211 Del Paso Blvd, Sacramento 95815. Needs based model (no one for one exchange requirement). NEXT Distro mail based naloxone partner for California.

resources.name: Saint John's Program for Real Change
resources.mission: Saint John's Program for Real Change's mission is to end the generational cycle of trauma and homelessness by providing a safe space for women and children to heal and develop the skills necessary to transform their lives.
resources.services: Residential program (up to 18 months) for homeless women and their children in Sacramento County; more than 70 percent of clients are survivors of domestic violence. Provides safe housing, behavioral health and mental health services, counseling, case management, on-site childcare (First Steps Child Development Center), career education, and paid job training through the Plates Catering and Red Door Desserts social enterprises. Admissions by application and interview; call (916) 453-1482. This is a structured recovery and workforce program, not a walk-in emergency DV shelter.
resources.notes: Mailing address 2443 Fair Oaks Blvd #369, Sacramento, CA 95825; Tax ID 68-0132934. One of the largest shelter programs for women and children in Sacramento County; 569 women and children housed on its campuses in the most recent reported year. Structured program with participation requirements. Cross-reference: Housing tab. For immediate DV shelter use WEAVE (916) 920-2952 instead.

resources.name: Saint John's Program for Real Change
resources.mission: Saint John's Program for Real Change empowers women and children experiencing homelessness to overcome drug addiction, trauma, and mental health concerns through a comprehensive residential program.
resources.services: 12-18 month residential program for homeless mothers and their children including hands-on parenting education, family services, mental health and substance use treatment, First Steps Child Development Center for children on campus, children's therapeutic and education services, career training through Plates Cafe and Catering, and transitional housing. Mothers must enroll in the residential program; call for admissions.
resources.notes: Program campus: 4410 Power Inn Road, Sacramento, CA 95826; mailing 2443 Fair Oaks Blvd #369, Sacramento, CA 95825. Primary listing in Housing tab; included here for parenting education and children's programming for enrolled mothers.

resources.name: Saint John's Program for Real Change
resources.mission: Saint John's Program for Real Change empowers homeless women and their children to overcome drug addiction, trauma and mental health concerns. Since 1985, Saint John's has equipped 35,000 women and children with the tools to transform their lives.
resources.services: Residential program (up to 12 to 18 months) for homeless women and their children with required sobriety: safe sober campus with 24/7 staffing, substance use disorder counseling, individual, group and family therapy, mental health care, life skills classes, high school diploma/GED support, job training and employment coaching, on-site childcare, transitional housing, plus a 7 day emergency stay option. Intake by phone; women with children prioritized.
resources.notes: Campus at 4410 Power Inn Rd, Sacramento 95826 (mailing: 2443 Fair Oaks Blvd #369, Sacramento 95825). Sobriety required for all programs except housing assistance. Cross-reference: Housing category.

resources.name: Saint John's Program for Real Change (Employment Readiness)
resources.mission: Saint John's Residential Program is a 12-month, on-campus program designed for women and children seeking stability, independence, and real change, with hands-on job training, childcare, therapy, and housing support to help women break the cycle of poverty and homelessness.
resources.services: Employment readiness within the 12-month Residential Program for women 18 and over (with or without children): job training through Saint John's social enterprises Plates Catering and Red Door Desserts, resume building, interview preparation, GED support, financial literacy, and case management; sobriety required. A separate Professional Development Program provides up to 12 months of housing plus employment coaching for women already working 20-24 hours per week or enrolled in school. Apply online or call (916) 453-1482.
resources.notes: Mailing address: 2443 Fair Oaks Blvd., #369, Sacramento, CA 95825. Employment training is embedded in the residential program; entry is through Saint John's intake, not open enrollment. Also runs a Female Community ReEntry Program for incarcerated women. Cross-reference Housing (residential and transitional housing for women and children).
resources.contactPerson: Scott B. Richards, Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: Saint John's Program for Real Change (Female Community Reentry Program)
resources.mission: Saint John's Female Community Reentry Program provides currently incarcerated women the opportunity to serve the remainder of their sentence in a structured, supportive environment, giving them the tools they need to successfully transition back into the community.
resources.services: CDCR pre-release community program: eligible women incarcerated at CCWF or CIW, approved by CDCR, serve the remainder of their sentence in a 50-bed, 24/7 staffed secure residential facility in Sacramento. Services include a six week vocational training and employment program (resume, cover letters, mock interviews), mental health and substance use counseling, individualized therapy, case management, education and life skills (financial literacy, parenting, self-sufficiency) and family reunification support. Application is made through CDCR while incarcerated, not by walk-in.
resources.notes: Program operated by Saint John's under contract with CDCR; enrollment only via CDCR approval from CCWF or CIW. Saint John's mailing address: 2443 Fair Oaks Blvd, #369, Sacramento, CA 95825. See CDCR FCRP page for statewide eligibility details. Cross-reference: Housing tab (Saint John's residential programs for women and children).

resources.name: Saint John's Program for Real Change (Women and Children)
resources.mission: Saint John's Program for Real Change offers a safe place for women and children to break free from the cycles of homelessness and poverty. Through comprehensive services, we foster resilience, growth, and lasting transformation for women and children experiencing trauma, addiction, incarceration, and homelessness.
resources.services: Residential Program: structured shelter and transitional program for women with or without children (housing, classes, mental health, sobriety support). Professional Development Program for women working or in school. Saint John's Square Housing for women with stable income. Housing Assistance Program (eviction-avoidance help). Female Community ReEntry Program for justice-involved women. Hands-on employment training via Plates Catering and Red Door Desserts. Shelter placement starts via 211 assessment; program-finder questionnaire on website.
resources.notes: Mailing: 2443 Fair Oaks Blvd #369, Sacramento, CA 95825. Serving since 1985; 569 women and children stayed on campuses last year, 62% transitioned to stable housing. Entry to residential shelter through 211 coordinated entry.

resources.name: SCORE Capital Corridor (Chapter 0044)
resources.mission: SCORE mentors help small businesses get off the ground, grow and achieve their goals through free, confidential business mentoring and low-cost workshops, as a resource partner of the U.S. Small Business Administration.
resources.services: Free confidential one-on-one business mentoring from experienced volunteer business leaders, by in-person appointment, video, phone or email; free and low-cost workshops, webinars and seminars on business planning, marketing, finance and operations, including small-group Sounding Board workshops in Citrus Heights. Serves anyone starting or running a small business in Sacramento, Capital Corridor and Sierra foothill communities including Auburn, Roseville, Placerville, Grass Valley, Chico and Redding. Request a mentor online at score.org/capitalcorridor.
resources.notes: Office at 6501 Sylvan Road, Citrus Heights, CA 95610; in-person sessions by appointment only. Part of the SCORE Northern California District. No public chapter email on the current chapter page, use the Send Us a Message form at score.org/capitalcorridor or call. Mentoring requests submitted online are routed by zip code. Serves both Sacramento and Placer counties from one chapter.

resources.name: Seniors First (Housing Placement & Senior Stability Services)
resources.mission: Seniors First is Placer County's leading provider of senior services, delivering over 125,000 essential services each year, dedicated to helping older adults thrive.
resources.services: Housing-relevant programs: Information and Assistance line (800) 878-9222 connecting seniors to housing resources and benefits; Living Placement, a free personalized assisted-living placement consultation. Also Meals on Wheels and senior nutrition, transportation, telephone reassurance, Lincoln Senior Center, and AniMEALS pet food. Core partner in the Placer County Aging and Disability Resource Connection. Serves seniors in Western Placer County: Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln, Colfax, Auburn, Granite Bay.
resources.notes: Office: 2543 Warren Drive, Rocklin, CA 95677 (relocated from Auburn; update older records). Tax ID 68-0430154. Website no longer lists home modification and safety repair program; refer home-repair needs to PIRS. Cross-reference: Eldercare category.

resources.name: Seniors First (Meals on Wheels Placer County)
resources.mission: Seniors First is Placer County's leading provider of senior services, dedicated to helping older adults thrive. Meals on Wheels Placer County is its flagship nutrition program, designed to help older adults age in place.
resources.services: Home-delivered meals (Meals on Wheels Placer County) for homebound Placer County seniors age 60 and over who have difficulty preparing meals, plus congregate Senior Cafe lunch sites and the AniMEALS pet food program delivered alongside meals. Meals are delivered three times per week (a combination of fresh and frozen meals) by screened volunteers; short-term service available after a hospital stay or illness. Service area is the western slope of Placer County (Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln, Auburn, Colfax, Foresthill, I-80 corridor communities); the Tahoe-Truckee area is not served. Call (530) 889-9500 or the Information and Assistance line (800) 878-9222 to enroll; suggested voluntary contribution is $6 per meal, but no senior is denied for inability to pay.
resources.notes: Office: 2543 Warren Drive, Rocklin CA 95677. Meals on Wheels America member. Senior Cafes serve lunch Mon, Wed, Fri at Auburn, Rocklin, and Roseville sites and Monday through Friday at Lincoln Senior Center; reservations required. Cross-reference: Food tab for full senior nutrition details; listed here because home delivery by volunteers supports aging in place.

resources.name: Seniors First (Placer Rides Transportation Assistance)
resources.mission: Seniors First administers two transportation programs, Placer Rides and non-emergency medical transportation, to help Placer County older adults maintain their independence.
resources.services: Placer Rides, run by Seniors First with the Western Placer Consolidated Transportation Services Agency (WPCTSA): eligible riders recruit their own private drivers (neighbors, friends, caregivers) and the program reimburses the driver's gas expenses for essential trips; if a rider cannot find a driver, Placer Rides may arrange and fund up to two last resort rides per month through a commercial carrier. Eligibility: Placer County residents who are seniors 60+, individuals with disabilities, or low income, and who have no other means to take essential trips. Application on the website or call (530) 889-9500 or email placerrides@seniorsfirst.org. Seniors First also runs a separate non-emergency medical transportation program (funded by Agency on Aging Area 4 and Sutter Health) providing rides to medical appointments such as dialysis, chemotherapy and physical therapy for seniors with chronic health conditions. Placer Rides replaced the former My Rides volunteer driver and Health Express medical shuttle programs.
resources.notes: Seniors First is Placer County's leading senior services nonprofit (Meals on Wheels Placer County), 501(c)(3) EIN 68-0430154. Office: 2543 Warren Drive, Rocklin, CA 95677; toll free (800) 878-9222. Serves Placer County including Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln, Auburn, Colfax, Granite Bay and rural areas. Note: My Rides and Health Express were consolidated into Placer Rides; old program names still circulate in directories. Verified from seniorsfirst.org July 2026. Cross-reference: Eldercare category for Seniors First meals, care management and senior center programs.
resources.contactPerson: Placer Rides Program Staff, Seniors First

resources.name: Seniors First (Telephone Reassurance)
resources.mission: Seniors First is Placer County's leading provider of senior services, delivering over 125,000 essential services each year. From health and safety to well-being and quality of life, we are dedicated to helping older adults thrive.
resources.services: Free Telephone Reassurance program provides homebound seniors with weekly social calls from screened and trained volunteers to relieve loneliness and isolation; volunteers also connect clients to community services that help them stay independent at home. Eligibility: age 60 and over, homebound (no longer driving), able to interact socially. Call (530) 889-9500 to request calls. Agency also runs an Information and Assistance line at (800) 878-9222 covering all senior needs.
resources.notes: Office: 2543 Warren Drive, Rocklin CA 95677. 501(c)(3), Tax ID 68-0430154. Also operates senior transportation, living placement consultation, and Lincoln Senior Center. Cross-references: Food tab (Senior Nutrition, Meals on Wheels), Transportation.

resources.name: Seniors First, Inc.
resources.mission: Seniors First is Placer County's leading provider of senior services, delivering over 125,000 essential services each year. From health and safety to well-being and quality of life, we are dedicated to helping older adults thrive.
resources.services: Placer County senior services gateway nonprofit: Information and Assistance line (800) 878-9222 connecting seniors and families to resources; Meals on Wheels Placer County home delivered meals and Senior Cafes (143,180 hot meals served last year); AniMEALS pet food delivered with meals; Lincoln Senior Center weekday lunches and activities; door-to-door senior transportation (10,248 rides last year); telephone reassurance calls to homebound seniors; and free assisted living placement consultation. Generally serves Placer County residents age 60+; call the assistance line to start services.
resources.notes: Office: 2543 Warren Drive, Rocklin, CA 95677. 501(c)(3), Tax ID 68-0430154. Operates the ADRC of Placer County in partnership with Agency on Aging Area 4 and PIRS. Cross-reference: Food tab (Meals on Wheels Placer), Transportation tab (rides), Housing tab (living placement).

resources.name: SHELTER, Inc. (Sacramento County Program)
resources.mission: SHELTER, Inc.'s mission is to prevent and end homelessness for low-income, homeless and disadvantaged families and individuals by providing housing, services, support and resources that lead to self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Operates a year-round emergency shelter in Sacramento's River District for individuals, with case management, employment services, health and wellness checks, benefits connection, and individualized success plans toward permanent housing. Agency-wide, SHELTER Inc. served 5,824 people last year and provided homelessness-prevention financial assistance averaging $5,179 per household. Sacramento shelter beds assigned via 211/Coordinated Access referral.
resources.notes: Headquartered in Concord, CA; Sacramento-specific program page confirms local shelter operation. Local phone and site address not published; confirm via shelterinc.org before referral.

resources.name: Shifa Community Clinic (UC Davis student-run free clinic)
resources.address: 419 V Street, Suite A, Sacramento, CA 95818
resources.mission: To deliver high quality and free multilingual, multicultural healthcare, and to integrate socially and medically disenfranchised communities into the mainstream healthcare system.
resources.services: Free care for the uninsured, by appointment only, Sundays 8am-12pm: primary care, dental (extractions and fillings), vaccine clinics (COVID-19, flu), women's health (exams, Pap smears, pregnancy tests), diabetic retinopathy screening, mental health (Mind clinic), dermatology, podiatry, and a legal clinic. Primarily serves South Asian and Muslim communities but open to all uninsured patients. Multilingual staff; culturally tailored resources including halal medication guidance.
resources.notes: By appointment only; own site lists Sundays 8am-12pm (UC Davis directory differs), so call to confirm current hours. 501(c)(3).

resources.name: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians (Shingle Springs Health and Wellness Center)
resources.mission: Shingle Springs Health and Wellness Center is the tribal health program of the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians, providing medical, dental, and behavioral health care to Native and non-Native patients of all income levels.
resources.services: Tribal FQHC on the Shingle Springs Rancheria (El Dorado County, just east of Sacramento County line off Highway 50). Medical and pediatrics, dental and orthodontics, behavioral health and medication-assisted treatment, children's behavioral health, acupuncture, chiropractic, physical therapy, podiatry, and pharmacy. Accepts all patients, Native and non-Native, all income levels: self-pay, private insurance, Medi-Cal, Medicare. Native Services / Purchased Referred Care (PRC) covers referred specialty care for eligible Native patients (requires active patient status, provider referral, tribal enrollment proof, residency proof, and insurance information); PRC service area is El Dorado County. Call for new patient registration; open Monday to Friday 8:00am to 5:00pm. NOTE: as of August 2025 the Dental Department is not accepting new patients (restriction does not apply to Indian Health Service beneficiaries).
resources.notes: Location: 5168 Honpie Rd, Placerville, CA 95667 (on the Rancheria near Shingle Springs/Cameron Park). Physically in El Dorado County but a practical option for Native families in eastern Sacramento County and south Placer; open to all. PRC (no-cost referred care) is limited to eligible Natives residing in El Dorado County; Sacramento and Placer Natives should use SNAHC or Chapa-De for IHS-funded care. Patient benefits coordinator: (530) 387-8037. Cross-reference: Health category.

resources.name: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians (Shingle Springs Tribal TANF Program)
resources.mission: Promoting a culturally rich Native community that enhances traditional values, education, employability, and wellness.
resources.services: Tribal TANF cash aid and supportive services for eligible needy Native American families in Sacramento, Placer, El Dorado, and Yolo Counties. Monthly cash assistance plus diversion (short-term crisis) assistance, culturally based case management, education and job training support, employment services, child care assistance, transportation assistance, parenting and life skills classes, prevention and cultural programming, and referrals to domestic violence, behavioral health, and substance abuse services. Eligibility: low-income families with a child under 18 (or pregnant member) where at least one household member is a member or descendant of a federally recognized tribe or eligible California Native; income limits apply, similar to CalWORKs. Apply at the county office serving your county.
resources.notes: Sacramento office: 2033 Howe Ave, Ste 100, Sacramento, CA 95825, (916) 760-1660, toll free (888) 688-6816. Placer office: 1919 Grass Valley Hwy, Ste 110, Auburn, CA 95603, (530) 820-0141. Families receiving Tribal TANF cannot receive CalWORKs at the same time; county CalWORKs offices can transfer eligible Native families. Note: the separate California Tribal TANF Partnership (cttp.net) does NOT serve Placer or Sacramento Counties.

resources.name: Sierra Business Council (Sierra Small Business Development Center)
resources.mission: Sierra SBDC provides no-cost, confidential advising and training to help entrepreneurs start, grow and transition their businesses as part of the Northern California SBDC network, funded by the U.S. Small Business Administration and the State of California.
resources.services: Free one-on-one business advising (strategic planning, cash flow, marketing, operations, HR, site selection, feasibility), free and low-cost trainings and webinars, help accessing capital including SBA loans and disaster loans, restaurant and technology specialty programs. Serves startups and existing small businesses in Placer, Nevada, El Dorado, Sierra, Plumas, Modoc and Lassen counties. Sign up online at sierrasbdc.com/join; advising delivered locally through the Placer Business Resource Center in Rocklin.
resources.notes: Hosted by Sierra Business Council, 10183 Truckee Airport Road, Suite 202, Truckee, CA 96161. NorCal SBDC network directory also lists (530) 582-4800. Covers all of Placer County including North Lake Tahoe; in-person advising available through the Placer Business Resource Center, 1000 Sunset Blvd., Suite 105, Rocklin. Advising is 100 percent free; register online first. Sacramento County residents should use Sacramento Valley SBDC instead.

resources.name: Sierra College (Career and Technical Education & Workforce Development)
resources.mission: Sierra College Career and Technical Education programs prepare students for entry into professional level employment, and its Workforce Development division delivers training solutions for Placer and Nevada County employers and workers.
resources.services: Community college offering more than 20 career technical education programs (advanced manufacturing, mechatronics, IT, nursing and allied health, construction, business), short-term certificates, community education career classes, and a Career and Transfer Connections center on the Rocklin campus with job boards, resume help, and employer events. Open enrollment; California residents pay standard community college fees with financial aid and California College Promise Grant available.
resources.notes: Government provider (Sierra Joint Community College District). Kept for direct-to-student CTE and career center services; employer-contracted training also offered. Additional campuses in Grass Valley and Truckee.

resources.name: Sierra College (Guardian Scholars and NextUp)
resources.mission: The Guardian Scholars Program and the NextUp Program provide services to current or former foster youth attending Sierra College, equipping and empowering students to do well academically and to navigate the life and financial challenges that are barriers to their success.
resources.services: Campus support for current and former foster youth: counseling, priority financial aid processing, funds for meals, transportation and textbooks, on-campus housing support and housing essentials, care packs with school supplies and hygiene products, peer advisors, transfer assistance. NextUp eligibility: current or former foster youth whose dependency was established or continued on or after age 13, and no older than 25 at the start of the academic year. Enroll through the Guardian Scholars office on the Rocklin campus.
resources.notes: Rocklin campus, 5100 Sierra College Blvd, Rocklin, CA 95677; office in Building L, Room 141. Office hours fall/spring: Monday-Thursday 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday 8 a.m. to noon. Apply via the Special Programs Common Application (covers EOPS, Guardian Scholars, NextUp, TRiO). Sierra College also serves students from western Placer and Nevada counties.

resources.name: Sierra College Veterans Success Center
resources.mission: Supports student veterans, active service members and their dependents in using their education benefits and succeeding in college.
resources.services: GI Bill and VA education benefit certification; CalVet College Fee Waiver assistance; academic counseling and priority registration; dedicated veteran study and computer space; tutoring referrals; veteran peer support and Student Veterans of America chapter; connections to county Veterans Service Office and VA health care.
resources.notes: Rocklin campus, Building LR Room 424, 5100 Sierra College Blvd., Rocklin, CA 95677. Nevada County campus line (530) 274-5303.

resources.name: Sierra Mental Wellness Group
resources.mission: The mission of Sierra Mental Wellness Group is to provide professional and affordable individual, couple and family counseling, crisis services, child and adolescent programs, and substance abuse treatment and prevention.
resources.services: Affordable outpatient mental health counseling for children, adolescents, and adults in individual, group, family, and couple modalities at clinical offices in Roseville, Auburn, and Tahoe City. Outpatient mental health therapy offered in partnership with Placer County Behavioral Health, including bilingual therapy at the Tahoe City location. Also provides 24/7 crisis evaluations and mobile crisis services for Placer County. Access via office phone or through Placer County screening line (888) 886-5401.
resources.notes: Roseville office: 406 Sunrise Avenue, Suite 300, Roseville, CA 95661; additional offices in Auburn and Tahoe City. 501(c)(3) confirmed, EIN 23-7249387. Incorporated 1970 (formerly Roseville Area Youth Services / Sierra Family Services). Crisis role: cross-reference Crisis Help Lines tab.

resources.name: Sierra Native Alliance
resources.mission: Sierra Native Alliance is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to preserving the health of Native families, cultures, and environments, working to strengthen leadership skills and resources for youth, families, and communities in the Sierra Nevada Foothills.
resources.services: Native American family resource center in Auburn. Family Wellness programs: family advocacy for families involved with child welfare and the justice system (including rights under the Indian Child Welfare Act), Positive Indian Parenting classes (NICWA curriculum), Families of Tradition family activity nights, anger management classes, 52-week court-approved domestic violence groups for men and for women, perinatal and early childhood developmental assessments, home visitation (Parents as Teachers model), and case management. Behavioral health: DHCS-certified outpatient and intensive outpatient substance use treatment and recovery support (White Bison, Native Matrix, family, and relapse prevention groups meet weekday evenings), plus individual, group, family, and child mental health counseling and Traditional Indian Health services. Youth programs and cultural education. Call for intake; services focus on Native families, call to confirm eligibility.
resources.notes: Mailing: PO Box 6346, Auburn, CA 95603 (website lists PO Box only; office at 610 Auburn Ravine Rd, Ste G, Auburn per 211 directory, confirm when calling). DHCS outpatient SUD license 310020AN current through 7/31/2026. Home visitation and early childhood contact: Jessica Ornalez, (530) 888-8767. Cross-reference: Foster (family advocacy) and Health (recovery) categories.

resources.name: Sierra Sacramento Valley Medical Society (SPIRIT Program)
resources.mission: Since 1995, the SPIRIT program of the Sierra Sacramento Valley Medical Society has worked to increase access to specialty healthcare for underserved residents of our region, addressing the healthcare needs of the community's most vulnerable patients.
resources.services: Free specialty consults and outpatient surgeries donated by volunteer physicians at area hospitals (Kaiser, Mercy General, Mercy San Juan, Sutter, UC Davis Health), plus colonoscopies and optometry consults with free glasses. Eligibility: uninsured with income at or below 300 percent of the Federal Poverty Level; full-scope Medi-Cal, Medicare, or private insurance disqualifies (emergency-only Medi-Cal qualifies). REFERRAL ONLY: patients cannot self-refer; ask your primary care clinic or free clinic to submit a SPIRIT referral. SPIRIT provides case management and care coordination.
resources.notes: SSVMS office: 5380 Elvas Avenue, Suite 101, Sacramento, CA 95819. Serves Sacramento and surrounding counties including Placer. Over 12 million dollars in donated care and 54,000 patients since 1995. Patients must be referred by a medical home; direct readers to their clinic.

resources.name: Sleep in Heavenly Peace (CA-Sacramento Chapter)
resources.mission: Sleep in Heavenly Peace is a group of volunteers dedicated to building, assembling and delivering top-notch bunk beds to children and families in need. No kid sleeps on the floor in our town!
