resources.services: Builds and delivers free twin beds (frame, mattress, bedding) to children ages 3 to 17 who lack a bed of their own, such as kids sleeping on floors, sofas, or air mattresses. Families apply online through the chapter application page; service limited to zip codes covered by the chapter and to bed availability. Donors can fund beds, donate new bedding, or volunteer at build days.
resources.notes: Volunteer chapter, no walk-in office; apply at shpbeds.org/apply and email via the contact form at shpbeds.org/contact-us. Phone (844) 432-2337 ext 5139 for the Sacramento chapter. New twin bedding donations accepted via the chapter's Walmart wishlist. Placer County families should check the chapter finder for coverage of their zip code; no separate Placer chapter confirmed as of July 2026. Cross-reference: Parenting tab.

resources.name: SMART Recovery (Sacramento and Placer area meetings)
resources.mission: SMART Recovery empowers people to achieve independence from addiction problems through science based, secular mutual support meetings and its 4-Point Program of tools for recovery.
resources.services: Free, secular, science based mutual support meetings for any addictive behavior (substances and behavioral addictions): local in person meetings in the Sacramento region (including Sunday morning and Saturday evening Sacramento meetings) plus daily online meetings; trained volunteer facilitators; open to people at any stage, including those who have not yet stopped using. Meetings typically 60 to 90 minutes; donations optional. Find current meetings at meetings.smartrecovery.org.
resources.notes: National 501(c)(3); local meeting locations change, so check the online meeting finder for current sites and times in Sacramento and Placer counties.

resources.name: Snowline Health (Snowline Hospice and Grief Support)
resources.address: 6520 Pleasant Valley Rd, Diamond Springs, CA 95619
resources.mission: Snowline's mission is to bring peace and dignity through life's transitions by providing comfort, care, and support to people in need.
resources.services: Community nonprofit founded 1979 (46+ years). Medicare-certified hospice and palliative care for patients on the western slope of El Dorado County, in Sacramento County (Sacramento, Folsom, Rancho Cordova, Fair Oaks, Carmichael), and in south Placer County (Roseville, Granite Bay). Grief support services (individual support, groups, children's grief programs) are free and open to community members regardless of whether the loss involved Snowline hospice; grief line (916) 817-2338 or (530) 621-7820. Dementia and caregiver support programs. Snowline Thrift stores in El Dorado County fund services beyond what Medicare covers. To start care call (530) 621-7820, 24/7 intake.
resources.notes: Headquarters: 6520 Pleasant Valley Rd, Diamond Springs, CA 95619; Sacramento area office in Gold River. Own site states it serves the Sacramento, South Placer, and El Dorado regions (confirm specific Placer zip at intake). Grief line (916) 817-2338 confirmed on Snowline grief pages July 2026. Nonprofit: do not confuse with for-profit hospices in the region. Thrift stores are in El Dorado County but revenue supports tri-county care.

resources.name: Society for the Blind
resources.mission: Society for the Blind's mission is to empower individuals living with low vision or blindness to discover, develop and achieve their full potential.
resources.services: Comprehensive blindness and low vision services: Low Vision Clinic evaluations, orientation and mobility (cane travel) training, Braille instruction, independent living skills classes, access technology and computer training, Senior IMPACT Project retreats for adults 55+, youth programs, career and employment services, and a store with adaptive aids. Open to people of all ages with vision loss; call to schedule an assessment. Hours Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30.
resources.notes: Services delivered from the Sacramento center to a 27 county Northern California region including Placer County; some travel training and senior programs offered in outlying counties. Cross-reference: Health tab (low vision clinic).

resources.name: Society for the Blind
resources.mission: Our mission is to empower individuals living with low vision or blindness to discover, develop and achieve their full potential.
resources.services: Low Vision Clinic with evaluations by low-vision optometrists and demonstrations of assistive devices (appointment request and provider referral forms online); classes in independent living skills, orientation and mobility (white cane), braille, and assistive technology; Senior IMPACT Project for adults 55 and older; youth programs; CareersPLUS employment program; Access News audio reading service; and a retail store for low-vision aids. Serves a 27-county Northern California region including Placer and Sacramento counties; the only comprehensive rehabilitative teaching center for the region. Some services grant-funded; costs vary, ask at intake.
resources.notes: 1238 S Street, Sacramento, CA 95811; Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm. Low Vision Clinic appointments: (916) 889-7545, by appointment only. Rehabilitation and low-vision services, not free eye surgery (see Lions Eye Foundation row for surgery). 2026 note: state funding cut of 60 percent to the Senior IMPACT Project; services continuing but flagged.

resources.name: Society for the Blind (Senior IMPACT Project)
resources.mission: The Senior IMPACT Project provides services and classes geared toward individuals 55 and older with visual impairments, focusing on alternative, non-visual techniques and skills that enable them to perform day-to-day tasks and activities.
resources.services: Free program for adults 55+ experiencing vision loss: multi-day immersion retreats and ongoing classes teaching independent living skills (cooking, cleaning, shopping, personal finance, organization), orientation and mobility (safe travel with a white cane), assistive technology training, braille support, low vision support groups, and peer mentoring. Funded by grants and donations so there is no cost to eligible participants, including transportation to and from select activities. Call to enroll; no doctor referral required.
resources.notes: Headquarters: 1238 S Street, Sacramento, CA 95811. Society for the Blind serves 27 Northern California counties; Senior IMPACT enrolls residents of both Placer and Sacramento counties. Cross-reference: Disability tab (full Society for the Blind services).

resources.name: Society for the Blind (Senior IMPACT Project)
resources.mission: Society for the Blind continues to create innovative ways to empower individuals living with low vision or blindness to discover, develop and achieve their full potential, serving a 27-county region of northern California since 1954.
resources.services: Senior IMPACT Project for adults 55 and older with vision loss: training in orientation and mobility, independent living skills (cooking, cleaning, shopping, home maintenance, organization, personal finance), assistive technology, and braille. Includes on-site IMPACT Retreats, monthly peer support groups (English and Spanish), and Bring IMPACT Home in-home instruction for those unable to attend the retreat. No cost to eligible participants, including transportation to select activities. Contact (916) 889-7516 for the Senior IMPACT Project.
resources.notes: 1238 S Street, Sacramento CA 95811. Open Monday to Friday 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Serves 27 northern California counties; Sacramento and Placer are among the primary counties served. Cross-reference: Disability tab.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul, Sacramento (Direct Assistance and Thrift Store)
resources.mission: A network of friends, inspired by Gospel values, growing in holiness and building a more just world through personal relationships with and service to people in need. No act of charity is foreign to the Society.
resources.services: Parish based conferences provide direct assistance with furniture, mattresses and frames, clothing, food, rent, utilities, and transportation for neighbors in need, typically through home visits; call the Helpline at (916) 572-7553 to be connected with help in your area. Thrift store at 2275 Watt Ave. sells low cost furniture, new mattresses and bed frames, household goods, clothing, and books; open 10:00 am to 6:00 pm, donation drop-off behind the store 10:00 am to 4:00 pm. Free donation pickup of most furniture and household goods (average wait about 5 days, email photos first); not accepted: used mattresses or box springs, tube TVs, computers, worn or damaged furniture, paint or toxic materials; large appliances only if 5 to 7 years old and testable on site.
resources.notes: Main phone (916) 972-1212 is the thrift store at 2275 Watt Ave., Sacramento, CA 95825 (customer service ext 0, transportation ext 1); assistance Helpline (916) 572-7553; council office (279) 345-2362. Parish conferences operate throughout the Diocese of Sacramento, including some Placer County parishes (Auburn, Roseville). Cross-reference: Food, Clothing, and Housing tabs (rent and utility assistance).

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul, Sacramento Diocesan Council
resources.mission: The Society of St. Vincent de Paul is a nonprofit organization that provides direct assistance to a community's most vulnerable residents, helping them meet basic needs, build self-sufficiency, and ultimately break the cycle of poverty.
resources.services: Direct financial assistance through parish-based conferences, subject to available resources: rent assistance (typically requires an eviction or 3-day notice, one time only), utility assistance (requires a shut-off notice from PG&E, SMUD, or water utility, one time only), plus food, clothing, beds and furniture, transportation help, and consultation, referral, and intervention services. Assistance is delivered through home visits by volunteer teams; call the Helpline to be routed to the conference serving your zip code. Serves anyone in need regardless of religion.
resources.notes: Mailing address: P.O. Box 162487, Sacramento, CA 95816; office line (279) 345-2362 (office matters only, not assistance requests). Helpline number confirmed on the org's own site (July 2026). The Diocese of Sacramento includes Placer County; conference coverage and funds vary by parish and zip code, so availability differs across Roseville, Auburn, Lincoln, and Sacramento neighborhoods. Each assistance type is generally one time only. Cross-reference: Housing, Food, and Clothing tabs.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul, Sacramento Diocesan Council
resources.mission: In the spirit of love and justice, the Society of St. Vincent de Paul, Sacramento Diocesan Council, provides help to neighbors in need through person-to-person service; through a network of charity, members meet face to face with neighbors in need, and no act of charity is foreign to the Society.
resources.services: Person-to-person emergency assistance through parish-based conferences: rent and mortgage assistance, utility assistance, food, clothing, furniture, and homelessness-prevention help. Transition to Permanent Housing Solutions program (Holy Spirit conference) assists people in temporary financial distress facing eviction or needing help obtaining housing. Communities served include Auburn, Lincoln, and Roseville (Placer) and Greater Sacramento, Carmichael, Elk Grove, Fair Oaks, Folsom, Rancho Cordova (Sacramento). Call the Helpline (916) 572-7553 to be routed to the conference serving your address; typically requires ID and proof of the bill or rent owed.
resources.notes: Mail: PO Box 162487, Sacramento, CA 95816. Office (279) 345-2362. Council network spans 21 counties of the Diocese of Sacramento. The Auburn and Roseville conferences have their own intake lines and are listed separately under Placer County; use this Helpline for Sacramento County addresses or when unsure. Funds limited per household.

resources.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul, St. Teresa of Avila Conference (Auburn)
resources.mission: The Society of St. Vincent de Paul is an international Catholic organization of lay persons whose purpose is to sanctify its members in the exercise of charity and help the poor in their corporal and spiritual needs.
resources.services: Direct financial assistance for rent and utility bills (eviction and shutoff prevention), plus help with other essentials and referrals. Serves single mothers with children, disabled and seriously ill people, the homeless, and others in need throughout all of Placer County. Access: call (530) 305-1904, leave a message, and a volunteer returns the call.
resources.notes: Established 2011. Message-based intake; callers must leave voicemail. Funding from parishioner donations, so assistance is modest and availability varies. Distinct from the Roseville SVdP conference. See also the SVdP Sacramento Diocesan Council entry (Both Counties).

resources.name: Special Olympics Northern California (Sacramento and Placer County Programs)
resources.address: 3480 Buskirk Ave, Suite 340, Pleasant Hill, CA 94523
resources.mission: Special Olympics Northern California provides year-round sports training and athletic competition for children and adults with intellectual disabilities, giving them continuing opportunities to develop fitness, demonstrate courage, and share their skills and friendship with the community.
resources.services: Free year-round sports training and competition for children and adults with intellectual disabilities: local county programs in both Sacramento and Placer offer seasons in sports such as basketball, bocce, bowling, soccer, softball, track and field, and volleyball, with about eight weeks of training per sport plus competitions. Athletes must complete application, medical form, and registration each season; all programs free to athletes and families.
resources.notes: Regional HQ: 3480 Buskirk Ave, Suite 340, Pleasant Hill, CA 94523; hours Mon-Fri 8:30-5:00. Sacramento and Placer county pages on sonc.org list current seasons and registration; no local office, programs run at community venues.
resources.contactPerson: Local Program staff via main office

resources.name: St. James Episcopal Church, Lincoln
resources.mission: St. James Episcopal Church in Lincoln serves neighbors facing food insecurity and other hardship through its weekly food pantry, community garden and outreach ministries.
resources.services: Weekly food pantry every Friday 9-11 AM at 490 K Street; community garden produce; clothing and basic-needs assistance; ESL classes; referrals to other Lincoln-area services. Everyone is welcome.
resources.notes: Pantry at 490 K Street; church office at 479 L Street, Lincoln, CA 95648. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul – Lincoln Conference
resources.mission: To provide assistance to those in need in the Lincoln area through charitable food, household goods, and emergency aid.
resources.services: Emergency food assistance; clothing and household goods; rent and utility assistance; in-home visits and personal support for homebound and elderly neighbors; referrals to other local resources.
resources.notes: Serves Lincoln, Wheatland, and Nicolaus, CA. Saint Vincent de Paul (SVdP), 280 Oak Tree Ln., Lincoln, CA 95648; hosted at St. Joseph Catholic Church, Lincoln. Also listed locally as the St. Joseph Conference. Distinct from the Roseville Area Conference and Sacramento Diocesan Council entries in this directory.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul – Lincoln Conference
resources.mission: To provide assistance to those in need in the Lincoln area through charitable food, household goods, and emergency aid.
resources.services: Food pantry Tues–Fri 8am–12pm; emergency food assistance; clothing and household goods; referrals to additional resources.
resources.notes: Serves Lincoln, Wheatland, and Nicolaus, CA. Saint Vincent de Paul (SVdP) 280 Oak Tree Ln., Lincoln, CA 95648

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul Roseville
resources.mission: St. Vincent de Paul Roseville provides food, clothing, and material assistance to neighbors in need in south Placer County.
resources.services: Families with small children can receive formula, baby food, and diapers for children up to 3 years of age, as well as feminine hygiene products on request, alongside the Food Locker supplemental grocery program. Food Locker distribution: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 9:00 am to 11:00 am at 503 Giuseppe Court, Suite 8, Roseville. Serves south Placer County residents (Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln area). Also offers rent and utility assistance (grant dependent), hygiene kits, school backpacks, and holiday programs. Lighthouse (Lincoln) also runs a Placer diaper bank; Salvation Army Auburn and church closets provide diapers intermittently.
resources.notes: Phone (916) 781-3303, baby supplies offering, and Monday/Wednesday/Friday 9-11 am hours confirmed on placersvdp.com July 2026. Tax ID 68-0205405. Cross-reference: Food and Clothing tabs (org appears there). Diapers limited to children under 3.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul Roseville (Baby Supplies and Diapers)
resources.mission: St. Vincent de Paul Roseville provides food, clothing, and material assistance to neighbors in need in south Placer County.
resources.services: Families with small children can receive formula, baby food, and diapers for children up to 3 years of age, as well as feminine hygiene products on request, alongside the Food Locker supplemental grocery program. Food Locker distribution: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 9:00 am to 11:00 am at 503 Giuseppe Court, Suite 8, Roseville. Serves south Placer County residents (Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln area). Also offers rent and utility assistance (grant dependent), hygiene kits, school backpacks, and holiday programs. Lighthouse (Lincoln) also runs a Placer diaper bank; Salvation Army Auburn and church closets provide diapers intermittently.
resources.notes: Phone (916) 781-3303, baby supplies offering, and Monday/Wednesday/Friday 9-11 am hours confirmed on placersvdp.com July 2026. Tax ID 68-0205405. Cross-reference: Food and Clothing tabs (org appears there). Diapers limited to children under 3.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul Society, Roseville Area Conference
resources.mission: Providing basic human services and programs to prevent hunger and homelessness.
resources.services: Rent and utility assistance: since 2018 has helped Placer County residents remain in their homes; funding depends on current grants, so call (916) 781-3303 for eligibility and application. Also Food Locker (503 Giuseppe Ct., Suite 8, Roseville; Mon/Wed/Fri 9-11am); St. Vincent Dining Room free meals (105 Bonita St., Roseville; Tue-Thu 12-1:30pm, Sat-Sun 2:30-4pm, no ID required); BAGS home grocery delivery for homebound seniors and disabled adults in Roseville and Rocklin; hygiene kits.
resources.notes: Tax ID 68-0205405. Rent and utility funds are grant-dependent and can be exhausted; always call first. Serves South Placer primarily. See also the SVdP Sacramento Diocesan Council entry (Both Counties). Cross-reference: Food category.

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul Society, Roseville Area Conference (Rent & Utility Assistance)
resources.mission: Providing basic human services and programs to prevent hunger and homelessness.
resources.services: Rent and utility assistance: since 2018 has helped Placer County residents remain in their homes; funding depends on current grants, so call (916) 781-3303 for eligibility and application. Also Food Locker (503 Giuseppe Ct., Suite 8, Roseville; Mon/Wed/Fri 9-11am); St. Vincent Dining Room free meals (105 Bonita St., Roseville; Tue-Thu 12-1:30pm, Sat-Sun 2:30-4pm, no ID required); BAGS home grocery delivery for homebound seniors and disabled adults in Roseville and Rocklin; hygiene kits.
resources.notes: Tax ID 68-0205405. Rent and utility funds are grant-dependent and can be exhausted; always call first. Serves South Placer primarily. See also the SVdP Sacramento Diocesan Council entry (Both Counties). Cross-reference: Food category.

resources.name: Stand Up Placer
resources.mission: Saving lives by empowering survivors and educating communities to stand up to domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking.
resources.services: Placer County's designated domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking agency. 24/7 crisis helpline at (800) 575-5352 staffed by certified advocates, plus 24/7 confidential webchat (resourceconnect.com/standup/chat) and an online confidential support request form. Services are free and confidential: safety planning, Domestic Violence Emergency Response Team (DVERT) with law enforcement, individual and group therapy for adults and children (including an 8-week kids group for ages 5-10), legal assistance including restraining order help, emergency safe housing, and prevention education including teen dating violence outreach. No documentation required to call; eligibility screening by phone at (916) 773-7273.
resources.notes: Serves all of Placer County including Auburn, Roseville, Rocklin, Lincoln, and Tahoe area. Roseville advocacy office: 300 Derek Place, Roseville, CA 95678, (916) 773-7273. Admin office (530) 823-6224; 24-hour SMS/text line (530) 385-0755. Formerly PEACE for Families. Federal Tax ID 94-2578871. Website has quick-escape button. Cross-reference: Housing tab for Stand Up Placer safe house and housing programs; also serves trafficking survivors.

resources.name: Stand Up Placer (24-Hour Crisis Line)
resources.mission: Stand Up Placer saves lives by empowering survivors and educating communities to stand up to domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking.
resources.services: 24/7 confidential crisis line answered by trained advocates for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking in Placer County. Access point for emergency safe housing, Domestic Violence Emergency Response Team (DVERT), hospital accompaniment for sexual assault exams, counseling, legal assistance, and safety planning. Free, no documentation required. Office line (916) 773-7273 during business hours. Online chat available via website.
resources.notes: Confidential office locations in Auburn and Roseville. Serves all genders and orientations. Placer County's designated DV and rape crisis provider. Cross-reference: Housing tab (safe house and housing programs).

resources.name: Stand Up Placer (Human Trafficking Programs and Safe House)
resources.mission: Stand Up Placer empowers survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking to escape from abuse and to create new lives of strength and self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Placer County's primary trafficking service provider: 24/7 crisis helpline (800) 575-5352 and 24/7 webchat with certified advocates; confidential Safe House emergency shelter for trafficking, DV, and sexual assault survivors and their children; walk-in crisis intervention at Roseville and Auburn offices during business hours; counseling and therapy; legal assistance including restraining orders; Sexual Assault Response Team (SART) accompaniment; safety planning; case management; support groups. Free and confidential; serves all genders; no documentation required. Online confidential support request form available.
resources.notes: Administrative office: PO Box 5462, Auburn, CA 95604; business line (530) 823-6224. Safe House location confidential. Webchat at resourceconnect.com/standup/chat. Serves Placer County; Placer County DA and 211 Connecting Point both refer here. Cross-reference: Domestic Violence and Housing tabs (same org, DV services and safe housing).

resources.name: Stand Up Placer (Legal Services Department)
resources.mission: Stand Up Placer is saving lives by empowering survivors and educating communities to stand up to domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking.
resources.services: Free legal assistance and advocacy for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking in Placer County: Legal Assistance is a core service of the domestic violence program, including help with domestic violence restraining orders, court accompaniment, and guidance through the court process. Access through the 24-hour helpline (800) 575-5352, 24/7 webchat at standupplacer.org, or the confidential online support request form; call (916) 773-7273 to check service eligibility. Serves survivors of any gender or gender identity; no documents required.
resources.notes: Legal Assistance confirmed as a current domestic violence program service on standupplacer.org (July 2026). Whether help is advocate support or staff attorney representation varies by case; confirm at intake. Office line (916) 773-7273. Office at 11985 Heritage Oaks Place, Suite 200, Auburn, CA 95603. Cross-reference: Housing tab (Stand Up Placer DV shelter and housing programs).

resources.name: Stand Up Placer (Safe House & Housing Programs)
resources.mission: Saving lives by empowering survivors and educating communities to stand up to domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking.
resources.services: Confidential emergency safe house for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking and their children fleeing abuse, plus longer-term housing programs to help survivors stabilize. Access is through the 24/7 crisis line (800) 575-5352; advocates screen for eligibility and safety. The agency reported 33,194 safe bed nights provided in 2024 across residential programs. Free of charge; no documentation required to seek shelter.
resources.notes: Safe house location is confidential; all access via 24/7 crisis line. Cross-reference: Housing tab (Stand Up Placer housing programs are also listed there); this row covers the DV-specific emergency shelter function.

resources.name: Stand Up Placer (Safe House & Housing Programs)
resources.mission: Stand Up Placer is dedicated to empowering Placer County survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking, providing programs and resources that help individuals and their families heal from trauma and create new lives of strength and self-sufficiency.
resources.services: Confidential emergency safe house for survivors fleeing life-threatening domestic violence, sexual assault, or sex trafficking; serves all genders, pet-friendly, accepts minor and adult dependents. Scattered-site rapid rehousing: survivors choose their own units and receive short- and medium-term rental assistance plus supportive services. Limited community-based safe housing units for 12-24 month stays. Also legal advocacy, counseling, case management. Access: 24/7 helpline (800) 575-5352 or webchat at resourceconnect.com/standup/chat.
resources.notes: Safe house location confidential. Service office (916) 773-7273. Housing program capacity fluctuates with grant funding. Cross-reference: Domestic Violence category.

resources.name: Stanford Settlement Neighborhood Center (Senior Center)
resources.mission: The goal of the Senior Center program is to provide support to participants, ages 50 and over, allowing them to continue to live a healthy, independent life.
resources.services: Senior Center supporting aging in place for adults 50 and over in Sacramento's north area (most participants are 70 to 90): drop-in center and supportive services, nutritious daily lunch (Senior Nutrition Services site), door-to-door transportation for lunch and activities, case management, home visits, counseling, crisis intervention, help with forms, and health and wellness activities. Also a Senior Companion Program host site, and the agency connects volunteer drivers with seniors for rides to medical appointments. Call (916) 927-1303 to enroll.
resources.notes: 450 West El Camino Ave, Sacramento CA 95833. Fax (916) 922-1694. Primarily serves the north Sacramento area. Home visits and Senior Companion host site confirmed on agency site (2026); call for current Senior Center hours. Supported by Agency on Aging Area 4 and Sacramento County DCFAS. Cross-references: Food (daily lunch), Transportation.

resources.name: Stanford Settlement Neighborhood Center (Senior Transportation)
resources.address: 450 W. El Camino Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95833
resources.mission: Stanford Settlement is a neighborhood center serving north Sacramento; its Sister Jeanne Felion Senior Center helps the community recognize seniors as a vital part of the community and enables seniors to remain in their homes with as much independence as possible.
resources.services: Senior transportation in the north Sacramento area: door-to-door rides to the Sister Jeanne Felion Senior Center for lunch (senior nutrition site) and activities for seniors who cannot drive or use fixed-route transit, plus volunteer drivers connected with seniors for rides to medical appointments. Senior center services also include counseling, crisis intervention, help with forms, home visits and monthly Breakfast Bags. Call (916) 927-1303 to register and confirm current schedule.
resources.notes: Address: 450 W. El Camino Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95833; fax (916) 922-1694. Door-to-door senior transportation confirmed on stanfordsettlement.org July 2026. Service area: Gardenland/Northgate, North Sacramento, Del Paso Heights and Natomas. Senior center supported by Agency on Aging Area 4 and Sacramento County DCFAS. Cross-reference: Eldercare category for senior center programs.
resources.contactPerson: Executive Director, Stanford Settlement Neighborhood Center

resources.name: Stanford Sierra Youth & Families
resources.mission: Stanford Sierra Youth & Families empowers youth and families to solve serious challenges that threaten their ability to stay together, providing a continuum of care in mental health, juvenile justice, substance use treatment, foster care and adoption, and family support.
resources.services: Specialized mental and behavioral health services for children and youth ages 0-21 who are struggling at home, school, or in the community: Flexible Integrated Treatment (FIT) using evidence-based modalities (TF-CBT, FFT, PCIT, Cue Centered Treatment), community-based family services, therapeutic behavioral services, wraparound, and free parent-to-parent support groups. Services provided in home, school, community, or counseling center. Sacramento County services requested through the Access Team at (888) 881-4881; most services Medi-Cal funded at no cost to families.
resources.notes: 8912 Volunteer Lane, Sacramento, CA 95826 and 8421 Auburn Blvd, Suite 3, Citrus Heights, CA 95610. Hours M-Th 8:30-5:30, F 8:30-5:00. Tax ID 68-0065690. Cross-reference Suicide and Foster tabs.

resources.name: Stanford Sierra Youth & Families (Parent Partner Services and Support Groups)
resources.mission: Stanford Sierra Youth & Families connects, inspires, and empowers youth and families, helping parents and caregivers become advocates for their children and leaders in their communities.
resources.services: Free monthly parent-to-parent support groups open to any parent or caregiver, even families not receiving agency services. Parent Partner Services pair caregivers with trained parent partners with lived experience navigating child welfare, juvenile justice, and behavioral health systems. Also provides wraparound, adoption and permanency, and youth mental health services. Contact the Family and Youth Partnership team to join.
resources.notes: Cross-reference: Foster tab (adoption and permanency programs) and Mental Health tab.

resources.name: Stanford Sierra Youth & Families (Youth Suicide Prevention Program)
resources.mission: Every young person deserves support, hope, and a future filled with possibility. Our Youth Suicide Prevention Program is dedicated to reducing youth suicide through compassionate outreach, early intervention, and community education.
resources.services: Youth suicide prevention outreach, early intervention, and community education for Sacramento County youth, families, schools, and community partners; youth listening sessions centering BIPOC and LGBTQ+ youth voice; vetted youth mental health resource hub including The Source Sacramento (call or text 916-SUPPORT / (916) 787-7678 for 24/7 crisis support for youth up to age 26 and their caregivers, with in-person support available) and California Youth Crisis Line (800) 843-5200; suicide prevention resource guides for providers and families. No fee; access via website or main office.
resources.notes: Main office: 8912 Volunteer Lane, Sacramento, CA 95826; TDD 711. Nonprofit (Tax ID 68-0065690). Suicide prevention program page updated June 2025. Cross-reference: Foster tab (foster care and adoption programs) and Mental Health tab. Youth in crisis: call or text 916-SUPPORT any time.

resources.name: Stanford Sierra Youth and Families (Wonder Mentoring Program)
resources.mission: Stanford Sierra Youth and Families empowers youth and families to solve serious challenges that threaten their ability to stay together, with a commitment to permanency and the empowerment of youth and families.
resources.services: Wonder Mentoring matches children and youth impacted by foster care one-to-one with trained, screened volunteer adult mentors who commit to roughly 8-10 hours per month for at least a year of consistent, healing relationships and age-appropriate activities. No cost to families. Agency also provides foster care and adoption, kinship support, wraparound, and mental health services. Referrals and volunteer applications via website or phone.
resources.notes: 8912 Volunteer Lane, Sacramento, CA 95826; TDD 711. Formed by merger of Stanford Youth Solutions and Sierra Forever Families; services-by-county pages list both Sacramento and Placer. Cross-reference: Foster tab (foster care, adoption, kinship programs).
resources.contactPerson: Dr. Laura Heintz, Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: Strategies for Change (now part of WellSpace Health)
resources.mission: Strategies for Change, founded in 1978 to provide evidence based substance abuse treatment and co-occurring mental health services for adults, youth and families, now operates as part of WellSpace Health, a nonprofit community health system committed to achieving regional health through high quality comprehensive care.
resources.services: Outpatient and intensive outpatient SUD treatment, women's and perinatal services, mental health and co-occurring treatment, family therapy and court related programs at two Sacramento behavioral health centers formerly run by Strategies for Change and now operated by WellSpace Health: South Behavioral Health Center, 4343 Williamsbourgh Dr, (916) 395-3552, and the outpatient center at 4441 Auburn Blvd. Access directly, via WellSpace's main line (916) 737-5555, or through the county access line (916) 874-9754. Medi-Cal, Medicare, insurance, sliding scale.
resources.notes: Sites: 4343 Williamsbourgh Dr, Sacramento 95823 (South Behavioral Health Center) and 4441 Auburn Blvd, Sacramento 95841. The formerly independent nonprofit merged into WellSpace Health; NPI records list the sites as WellSpace Health Strategies for Change South and North, and strategies4change.org is no longer a reliable source. Address and phone confirmed on wellspacehealth.org July 2026. Cross-reference: WellSpace Health row (same 501(c)(3)).

resources.name: Sutter Health (Sutter Care at Home Hospice and Grief Support)
resources.mission: Sutter Care at Home's Hospice and Bereavement Program provides compassionate end-of-life care and offers free individual and group grief support to hospice families and community members alike.
resources.services: Hospice program of Sutter Health, a nonprofit health system, serving the greater Sacramento region including Placer County (Roseville office). Interdisciplinary home hospice covered by Medicare, Medi-Cal, and most insurance. Bereavement program is free and open to the whole community: eight-week grief groups for loss of spouse/partner and loss of a parent (Sacramento and Davis), and a Children's Bereavement Art Group for ages 4-17 led by an art therapist, offered in Sacramento (916) 887-5275 and Roseville (916) 797-7850, with children grouped by age and type of loss. Bereavement enrollment: (916) 388-6215; general information (866) 652-9178.
resources.notes: Sacramento hospice office: 8334 Ferguson Ave, Sacramento, CA 95828; grief programs also run in Roseville (Placer County). Grief services free to community members, no Sutter affiliation required. Not open only to Sutter patients for hospice either, though physician referral needed for hospice admission.
resources.contactPerson: Bereavement Program Coordinator, Sutter Care at Home

resources.name: The Arc of Placer County (Placer ARC)
resources.mission: The Arc of Placer County is a nonprofit dedicated to empowering individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, supporting their independence, social engagement, and personal growth.
resources.services: Five programs for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) covering personal care, healthy lifestyles, finances, visual and performing arts, volunteerism, vocational guidance, and higher education. The Adult Achievement Center in Auburn offers a life skills curriculum with vocational training, daily living practices, health and fitness, cognitive growth, and mobility training; the Roseville Adult Center offers day program services in downtown Roseville. Most participants access services through Alta California Regional Center funding; contact the office for intake.
resources.notes: Roseville Adult Center: 531 Vernon Street, Roseville, CA 95678, (916) 783-5700. Adult Achievement Center: 3217 Professional Drive, Auburn, CA 95602, (530) 537-2647. Chapter of The Arc national network; website confirmed active July 2026 (current fundraiser for Studio 700 window repair). Referrals commonly come through Alta California Regional Center service coordinators.

resources.name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Lincoln)
resources.mission: The Lincoln-area congregations of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints organize humanitarian and welfare service for neighbors in need, in partnership with local nonprofits and service groups.
resources.services: Humanitarian donation drives; sewing, knitting and blanket-making projects; volunteer labor for local service projects; welfare and food assistance referrals; sponsorship of projects listed on JustServe.
resources.notes: Listed in the source file as Latter Day Saints. Lincoln Stake humanitarian center at 252 O Street, Lincoln. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: The Foundry (Lincoln Youth Center)
resources.mission: The Foundry seeks to build character and compassion in Lincoln's youth through mentorship and community service, providing a safe and positive place for students in grades 6 through 12 to go after school.
resources.services: Free drop-in after-school youth center programming for middle and high school students in Lincoln. All services free. On-campus sites in partnership with Western Placer Unified School District: GEMS site at Glen Edwards Middle School, Classroom P1 (Mon-Fri after school to 6 pm, grades 6-8) and LHS site at Lincoln High School, Classroom 23b (LHS lunchtimes Mon-Thu; after school Tue-Thu to 6 pm; PHS and ATLAS students welcome Tue-Thu 1-6 pm). Homework help, enrichment, gardening and culinary skills, games, leadership program, internships, community service and junior high summer camps.
resources.notes: Mailing address: PO Box 67, Lincoln, CA 95648. Operates as a DBA of Emmaus Church Community (faith-based nonprofit); programming is free and open to all students. No public phone; contact by email or Instagram/Facebook @thefoundry_lincoln for schedule changes on irregular school days.

resources.name: The Gathering Inn (Clothing Closet and In-Kind Donations)
resources.address: 4020 Sierra College Blvd., Suite 100, Rocklin, CA 95677
resources.mission: The Gathering Inn uses in-kind donations to support individuals and families experiencing homelessness with clean, safe, and quality essentials, from clothing and hygiene products to household items and move-in supplies.
resources.services: Clothing Closet open twice weekly (Wednesdays and Saturdays) to program guests and neighbors in need: free donated clothing, shoes, and accessories. Donors may give in-season clothing (13 gallon bags or smaller, labeled, limit 3 bags), shoes, towels, blankets, luggage, and working bikes; hygiene items, socks, undergarments, and household essentials must be new. Furniture, beds, TVs, appliances, medical equipment, and other large items require pre-approval by email before drop-off.
resources.notes: Headquarters: 4020 Sierra College Blvd., Suite 100, Rocklin, CA 95677. Donation drop-off Tue-Sat 10:00 am-3:00 pm at South Placer Campus, 201 Berkeley Ave., Roseville, CA 95678 and Mid Placer Campus, 11442 E Avenue, Auburn, CA 95603. Clothing Closet open Wed and Sat; call for current hours. Primarily serves people experiencing homelessness in Placer County. Cross-reference: Housing tab (The Gathering Inn shelter programs) and Clothing tab.

resources.name: The Gathering Inn (Emergency Shelter, Permanent Supportive Housing & Medical Respite)
resources.address: 4020 Sierra College Blvd., Suite 100, Rocklin, CA 95677
resources.mission: Reaching out to end homelessness. The Gathering Inn provides emergency shelter, permanent supportive housing, and medical respite care, along with supportive services, so people can move from homelessness to sustainable housing.
resources.services: Operates Placer County's three main emergency shelters: South Placer Emergency Shelter (Roseville, church-partnership model, ~60 beds nightly, adults and families, meals, weekly medical and dental clinics); Mid Placer Emergency Shelter (Auburn DeWitt campus, 100 beds, 24/7 staffed, adults 18+, 4 full-time case managers); Mobile Temporary Shelter (Auburn, low-barrier safe-camping model with behavioral health support). Also permanent supportive housing (7 homes countywide with case management), medical respite after hospitalization, housing navigation with Ready to Rent certification, mental health clinicians, life skills and recovery classes, clothing closet. Access via Coordinated Entry: call 211 or (833) 375-2237.
resources.notes: Admin office: 4020 Sierra College Blvd., Suite 100, Rocklin, CA 95677. No walk-in placement; entry through Coordinated Entry/211. Also operates Sacramento-area shelters under separate contracts.

resources.name: The HUB: WPUSD Family Resource Center
resources.mission: The HUB is Western Placer Unified School District’s family resource center, connecting students and families to academic support, health and wellness services, and local community resources.
resources.services: Food pantry and food storage; clothing closet; school supplies; work permits; academic support and referrals; health and wellness programs; annual back-to-school resource fair; connections to local housing, counseling and youth services.
resources.notes: Located at 790 and 870 J Street, Lincoln, on the north side of the Lincoln High School parking lot. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: The Lazarus Project, Inc.
resources.mission: To meet the needs of the impoverished in Placer County by providing housing and comprehensive support services.
resources.services: Operates approximately 4 residential homes in the Roseville area combining affordable housing with supportive services for homeless and at-risk single adults; has assisted 700+ formerly homeless men and women since 1998. Eligibility per application materials: homeless or precariously housed, extremely low income, over 21, single man or woman, living or working in Placer County or with immediate family in the county. Waitlist application required.
resources.notes: Mail: P.O. Box 1241, Roseville, CA 95678. Website not loading as of July 2026; organization shows recent third-party activity (GuideStar EIN 94-3312292) but current program status, phone, and intake should be confirmed by phone before referral.

resources.name: The Salt Mine
resources.mission: The Salt Mine is a faith-based public charity that has offered food assistance and emergency support to residents of Lincoln, Sheridan and surrounding communities since 1985.
resources.services: Food closet and emergency food distribution; thrift store providing low-cost clothing and household goods; emergency assistance; volunteer opportunities.
resources.notes: Operates as Vine Life Ministries, Inc. dba The Salt Mine. Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: The Salvation Army Auburn Corps (Emergency Financial Assistance)
resources.mission: The Salvation Army, an international movement, is an evangelical part of the universal Christian Church. Its mission is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and to meet human needs in His name without discrimination.
resources.services: Housing and utility assistance for individuals and families who need support meeting basic living needs (availability based on funding and service area). Also operates a food pantry (Monday, Wednesday, Friday 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.; Tuesday and Thursday by appointment) and ready-to-eat lunch bags for people experiencing homelessness all week. Social services office hours Monday-Friday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Call to schedule an appointment; bring valid ID, proof of residency, and the bill or notice for which help is requested.
resources.notes: 286 Sutter Street, Auburn, CA 95603; mailing address P.O. Box 4088, Auburn, CA 95604. Phone confirmed on the org's own site (July 2026). Assistance is funding-dependent and limited to the Auburn corps service area; call before visiting. Cross-reference: Food tab and Housing tab (Salvation Army multi-category org).

resources.name: The Salvation Army Auburn Corps (Social Services)
resources.mission: The Salvation Army, an international movement, is an evangelical part of the universal Christian Church. Its mission is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and to meet human needs in His name without discrimination.
resources.services: Housing and utility assistance: emergency financial help with rent and utilities for Placer County residents, based on available funding and zip code. Food pantry (Mon/Wed/Fri 10am-2pm; Tue/Thu by appointment); homeless ready-made lunch bags all week; intermittent adult and family case management; senior services. Social Services office hours Mon-Fri 10am-4pm. First visit requires valid ID, proof of residency, and children's birth certificates or guardianship papers.
resources.notes: 286 Sutter Street, Auburn, CA 95603; mail: P.O. Box 4088, Auburn, CA 95604. Rental and utility funds are limited and zip-code restricted; call first. Separate Roseville Corps partners on daily meals with SVdP Roseville. Cross-reference: Food category.
resources.contactPerson: Lieutenants Stephen & Faith Hartt, Corps Officers

resources.name: The Salvation Army of Sacramento Metro
resources.address: 3213 Orange Grove Avenue, North Highlands, CA 95660
resources.mission: The Salvation Army in Sacramento is committed to serving the local community by providing a breadth of social service assistance; assistance programs are based on residence, income qualifications, and availability of funding.
resources.services: SMUD EnergyHELP assistance: up to $200 per year toward unpaid SMUD balances for customers with a shut-off notice (grey envelope); the Salvation Army is one of four charities distributing EnergyHELP funds. Limited rental and other emergency assistance depending on funding; confirm amounts at intake. Also distributes food boxes and fresh produce (Tuesday-Thursday 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.) and senior food for ages 60+. Call (916) 678-4010, prompt 2, Monday-Thursday 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. for assistance intake; bring shut-off notice, ID, and proof of income.
resources.notes: North Highlands Family Services: 3213 Orange Grove Avenue, North Highlands, CA 95660; also Alhambra Community Center, 2500 Alhambra Blvd, Sacramento. Phone, address, and intake hours confirmed on the org's own site (July 2026). Dollar amounts for rental help vary with funding; note that PG&E REACH bill credits are now administered through Dollar Energy Fund via PG&E, not the Salvation Army. Cross-reference: Housing, Food, and Clothing tabs (Salvation Army multi-category org).

resources.name: The Salvation Army of Sacramento Metro (Utility and Rental Assistance)
resources.address: 3213 Orange Grove Avenue, North Highlands, CA 95660
resources.mission: The Salvation Army in Sacramento is committed to serving the local community by providing a breadth of social service assistance; assistance programs are based on residence, income qualifications, and availability of funding.
resources.services: SMUD EnergyHELP assistance: up to $200 per year toward unpaid SMUD balances for customers with a shut-off notice (grey envelope); the Salvation Army is one of four charities distributing EnergyHELP funds. Limited rental and other emergency assistance depending on funding; confirm amounts at intake. Also distributes food boxes and fresh produce (Tuesday-Thursday 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.) and senior food for ages 60+. Call (916) 678-4010, prompt 2, Monday-Thursday 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. for assistance intake; bring shut-off notice, ID, and proof of income.
resources.notes: North Highlands Family Services: 3213 Orange Grove Avenue, North Highlands, CA 95660; also Alhambra Community Center, 2500 Alhambra Blvd, Sacramento. Phone, address, and intake hours confirmed on the org's own site (July 2026). Dollar amounts for rental help vary with funding; note that PG&E REACH bill credits are now administered through Dollar Energy Fund via PG&E, not the Salvation Army. Cross-reference: Housing, Food, and Clothing tabs (Salvation Army multi-category org).

resources.name: The Salvation Army Sacramento Metro (Center of Hope Emergency Shelter)
resources.mission: The Salvation Army meets human needs in His name without discrimination, providing emergency shelter and a path out of homelessness for men, women, and veterans in Sacramento.
resources.services: Center of Hope Emergency Shelter: approximately 130 beds, the largest shelter in Sacramento County; 30-90 day stays for adults 18+ (men, women, veterans). Three meals a day, showers, laundry, case management, spiritual and emotional counseling, employment referrals, legal-issue referrals, family reconnection, and housing referral services. Also the E. Claire Raley Transitional Living Center (34-unit family transitional housing, 6-24 months). Access: adults via 211 shelter assessment; veterans via the VA Mather homeless walk-in clinic (Building 800) for direct referral. TB clearance required.
resources.notes: Not walk-in; beds assigned through 211/Coordinated Access. Phone confirmed July 2026. Salvation Army corps in Placer County listed separately under Placer.

resources.name: The Trevor Project
resources.mission: The Trevor Project is the leading suicide prevention and crisis intervention nonprofit for LGBTQ+ young people, working to end suicide among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and questioning young people.
resources.services: Free, confidential 24/7/365 crisis counseling for LGBTQ+ young people under 25: call (866) 488-7386, text START to 678-678, or chat at thetrevorproject.org; trained counselors help with suicidal thoughts, coming out, identity, and depression; no documentation or fee; nationwide service available to youth in Placer and Sacramento counties.
resources.notes: National nonprofit, no local office; services delivered by phone, text, and chat. LGBTQ+ youth can also reach specialized counselors through 988. Cross-reference: Crisis Help Lines and LGBTQ+ tabs.

resources.name: The Trevor Project (Crisis Services for LGBTQ+ Young People)
resources.mission: The Trevor Project is the leading suicide prevention and crisis intervention organization for LGBTQ+ young people, providing free, confidential support 24/7.
resources.services: Call (866) 488-7386, text START to 678-678, or chat at TheTrevorProject.org, 24/7/365. Serves LGBTQ+ young people under 25 in crisis, feeling suicidal, or needing a safe, judgment-free person to talk to. Counselors are trained on LGBTQ+ issues; anonymous and free. Note: the 988 Lifeline's specialized LGBTQI+ youth press 3 option was discontinued in July 2025, making Trevor the primary specialized line.
resources.notes: National nonprofit. Local LGBTQ community centers (Sacramento LGBT Community Center) offer non-crisis support; see other categories.
resources.contactPerson: Crisis Services Team, The Trevor Project

resources.name: Turning Point Community Programs (Community Outreach Recovery Empowerment, CORE)
resources.mission: Turning Point Community Programs provides integrated, cost-effective mental health services, employment and housing tailored to the needs of persons with mental illness, offering caring, hope, respect, and support on the path to recovery since 1976.
resources.services: Outpatient behavioral health for adults 18+ with a qualifying diagnosis plus a Community Wellness Center open to all community members 18+: short-term therapy, coping skills building, medication support, case management, psychosocial rehabilitation and therapeutic groups, SOAR benefits assistance, and support for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. No one denied access to services due to inability to pay. Access directly or via the county Access Team (888) 881-4881.
resources.notes: CORE locations: 3810 Rosin Court, Suite 170, Sacramento 95834; 3628 Madison Ave, North Highlands 95660 (916) 388-3231; 9340 E. Stockton Blvd, Elk Grove 95624 (916) 509-8198. Cross-reference Housing tab and Crisis Help Lines tab (Turning Point also runs the Mental Health Urgent Care Clinic).

resources.name: Turning Point Community Programs (Sacramento Housing & Homelessness Programs)
resources.mission: Turning Point Community Programs began in 1976 with the unique vision to offer caring, hope, respect, and support on the path to recovery and mental health. Everyone has a path to mental health.
resources.services: Sacramento County programs relevant to housing: Pathways to Success After Homelessness (housing and intensive services for people who are homeless with serious mental illness), Transitional Support Services, Abiding Hope Respite House, Crisis Residential Program, CORE outreach, Mental Health Urgent Care Clinic, plus flexible integrated treatment teams. Supported housing linked to mental health treatment; access primarily via Sacramento County Behavioral Health referral.
resources.notes: Housing tied to behavioral health services; not general-population shelter. CARF accredited. Also runs TAY housing partnership with AMI Housing in Placer (see AMI Housing entry).

resources.name: Turning Point Community Programs (Sacramento Mental Health Urgent Care Clinic)
resources.mission: The Mental Health Urgent Care Clinic provides voluntary, walk-in services to Sacramento County residents of all ages experiencing a mental health and/or co-occurring substance use crisis, regardless of ability to pay.
resources.services: Walk-in crisis alternative to the emergency room: same-day crisis counseling, psychiatric evaluation, medication support, peer support, and linkage to ongoing care. Open Monday-Friday 8:00 am to midnight (last walk-in 10:00 pm), weekends and holidays 8:00 am to 8:00 pm (last walk-in 6:00 pm). All ages, no appointment, no insurance required. Phone answered during clinic hours for guidance before arrival.
resources.notes: County-funded, operated by nonprofit Turning Point Community Programs. Not a phone hotline: for 24/7 phone crisis support use 988 or the county line (888) 881-4881. Cross-reference: Mental Health category.
resources.contactPerson: Al Rowlett, CEO, Turning Point Community Programs

resources.name: UC Davis CAARE Diagnostic and Treatment Center
resources.mission: The CAARE (Child and Adolescent Abuse Resource and Evaluation) Diagnostic and Treatment Center is recognized nationally as a model program for the evaluation and treatment of child maltreatment and the training of mental health providers in empirically based treatments.
resources.services: Mental health services for children who have experienced abuse, neglect, exposure to violence, or other crimes: evidence-based therapies including PCIT, PC-CARE, and trauma-focused treatment to reduce emotional and behavioral symptoms following trauma. Serves Sacramento County children, largely at no cost through Medi-Cal, Victims of Crime funding, and county contracts. Referrals through the Sacramento County BHS Screening and Coordination/Access Team at (916) 875-1055; expedited and walk-in appointment coordination available.
resources.notes: Public university (government) provider. Referral-based: EPSDT Medi-Cal referrals go through the county Access Team, but families can call Gloria Sisneros directly for expedited and walk-in appointments, and (916) 734-8396 reaches Cal OES-funded Trauma Recovery Services. Cross-reference Foster and Trafficking tabs for related child victim services.

resources.name: UC Davis Health (UC Davis Hospice Program and Bereavement Services)
resources.mission: UC Davis Hospice provides comprehensive, compassionate end-of-life care that honors the medical, emotional, and spiritual needs of patients and families facing life-limiting illness.
resources.services: University (public) hospice program under UC Davis Health Home Care Services. Interdisciplinary hospice care in the home for patients with a prognosis of six months or less; covered by Medicare, Medi-Cal, and most insurance. Bereavement program provides support groups throughout the year free of charge to the entire community, not only hospice families, including a Young Adult Bereavement Art Group (ages roughly 17-24) and general grief groups; register with the bereavement team at (916) 946-1404. Office hours 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday; hospice on call 24/7.
resources.notes: Government/university provider (University of California). Bereavement groups free and open to community members; typically invited to next available group about three months after a loss. Hospice service area is greater Sacramento; confirm coverage for specific Placer addresses at intake.

resources.name: UC Davis School of Law Immigration Law Clinic
resources.mission: The UC Davis Immigration Law Clinic, one of the first of its kind in the nation, serves Northern California's immigrant communities with education and legal services and provides legal representation to indigent non-citizens in removal proceedings before immigration courts, the Board of Immigration Appeals, and federal courts.
resources.services: Free representation for indigent non-citizens, with law students working under clinic attorneys: removal defense (detained and non-detained) including Ninth Circuit appeals, asylum, naturalization problems, immigration consequences of criminal convictions, and help for people in ICE detention; community naturalization workshops and know your rights presentations in detention centers. Service area includes Placer, Sacramento, El Dorado, Nevada, Sutter, Yolo, and Yuba counties. Cases mostly selected via referrals from other legal organizations; call for intake.
resources.notes: UC Davis School of Law, King Hall, 400 Mrak Hall Drive, Davis, CA 95616. Public university (government) provider. Limited capacity, referral-driven intake; attorneys advise clients only, not general public. UC students should use the separate UC Immigrant Legal Services Center (ucimm.law.ucdavis.edu, ucimmhelp@law.ucdavis.edu).

resources.name: UCP of Sacramento and Northern California
resources.mission: The mission of UCP of Sacramento and Northern California is to provide programs and services that improve the independence, productivity, and quality of life for people with developmental disabilities and their families.
resources.services: Programs for children and adults with a wide range of developmental disabilities (autism, cerebral palsy, epilepsy, intellectual disability, Down syndrome, and more): Adult Day Programs with community based instruction, CLASP independent living support, Family Respite Services giving caregivers a break, accessible transportation, and recreation and therapy programs including UCP Camps and the Saddle Pals horsemanship program. Most services accessed via Alta California Regional Center referral; respite intake direct. Current program directory posted on the website.
resources.notes: Program lineup confirmed from ucpsacto.org July 2026 (Adult Day Programs, CLASP, Family Respite, Transportation, Recreation and Therapy). Serves Sacramento and surrounding Northern California counties including Placer.

resources.name: Union Gospel Mission Sacramento
resources.mission: Union Gospel Mission Sacramento is a Christian ministry helping the homeless of Sacramento with shelter, meals, clothing, and a residential Christ-centered rehabilitation program.
resources.services: Men's overnight shelter: sign-ups nightly at 5:30pm, 7 days/week (photo ID and current negative TB card required); includes 7:30pm chapel service (required), dinner, shower, clean clothing and bedding, bed, and breakfast. Free hot evening meals for men, women, and children 365 days/year. Women's Clothes Closet and showers Tue and Thu 9:30-11:30am (sign-ups 9:00-9:30am). Winter Warming Center in dining room during cold months. 18-month men's residential rehabilitation program.
resources.notes: Office Mon-Thu 8am-4pm, Fri 9am-12pm. Religious participation (chapel) required for shelter. One of the few walk-in (no coordinated entry) shelter options. Cross-reference: Clothing category.

resources.name: United Auburn Indian Community (Community Services Department)
resources.mission: The United Auburn Indian Community is invested in enriching the community through economic development, education services, and a commitment to aid philanthropic programs.
resources.services: Federally recognized tribe (Miwok and Nisenan) headquartered at the Auburn Rancheria in Placer County. Community Services Department provides family support services: ICWA advocacy and intervention, foster care support, mental health support, substance abuse counseling and treatment referrals, and support for adults with disabilities. Education Department runs a Pre-K to 8th grade tribal school, tutoring, cultural and extracurricular activities, homeschool support, and college tuition assistance. Most direct services are for UAIC tribal members and their families; ICWA intervention occurs in county courts where UAIC children are involved. Call the tribal office to be directed to the appropriate department.
resources.notes: Tribal office: 10720 Indian Hill Rd, Auburn, CA 95603. IMPORTANT: most programs (school, tuition assistance, elder and disability grants) are for enrolled UAIC members only; the tribe is not a walk-in service agency for the general Native public. Non-members needing Indian health care should contact Chapa-De, which UAIC supports. Cross-reference: Foster (ICWA) category.

resources.name: United Way California Capital Region (Free Tax Prep / VITA)
resources.mission: In partnership with the California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC), United Way's Free Tax Preparation program helps families get cash back from state and federal credits, helping thousands of families every year save more than $1 million in tax fees and receive close to $10 million in refunds.
resources.services: Free tax preparation (IRS VITA program) for households earning less than $68,000 per year with IRS-certified preparers; also offers a free self-preparation option online. Preparers screen for CalEITC, federal EITC, and Child Tax Credit to maximize refunds; average savings of $200 in preparer fees. Serves Sacramento, Placer, Yolo, Amador, El Dorado, Yuba-Sutter, and Colusa counties. For the most recent season no standing in-person appointment sites were offered: filing runs through the MyFreeTaxes online platform (self-file or virtual assisted filing), plus occasional in-person DIY tax events (register by dialing 211 or (916) 498-1000). Virtual program can also prepare prior-year returns.
resources.notes: Headquarters: 10389 Old Placerville Road, Sacramento, CA 95827, (916) 368-3000, Monday-Friday 8 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Income cap, service counties, and intake process confirmed on the org's own site (updated June 2026). Delivery model changes each tax season; check the website each January. Households over the cap can self-file free at MyFreeTaxes.com.

resources.name: VA Northern California Health Care System (Homeless Veteran Care / HUD-VASH)
resources.mission: VA Northern California health care helps Veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless due to financial hardship, unemployment, addiction, depression, or transition from jail, connecting them with housing, health care, and supportive services.
resources.services: Homeless services care coordination for veterans: immediate food and shelter, transitional and permanent housing placement, HUD-VASH (HUD Housing Choice Voucher plus VA case management for permanent supportive housing), financial support to prevent homelessness, job training and life skills, justice re-entry support, addiction and mental health treatment. Serves veterans throughout the VA NorCal catchment covering both counties (clinics in Sacramento, Mather, McClellan, and the Roseville area). HUD-VASH vouchers administered locally with housing authorities (SHRA in Sacramento, Placer County and Roseville housing authorities); VA refers applicants. Sacramento VA Medical Center homeless coordinator: (916) 843-7271.
resources.notes: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans (877) 424-3838 is 24/7 and routes to local staff. Veteran must generally be VA health care-eligible for HUD-VASH. Cross-reference: Veterans + Military category (VA NorCal also listed there).
resources.contactPerson: Homeless Services Care Coordinator, Sacramento VA Medical Center

resources.name: Veterans Crisis Line (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs)
resources.mission: The Veterans Crisis Line provides 24/7, confidential crisis support for Veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and those who support them.
resources.services: Free, confidential 24/7 crisis support: dial 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat at veteranscrisisline.net; caring, qualified responders (many Veterans themselves) provide suicide crisis intervention and connect callers to local VA and community resources; available to all Veterans and their loved ones regardless of VA enrollment or discharge status; no documentation required.
resources.notes: Primary access is 988 press 1 (legacy number (800) 273-8255 press 1 still works), so main phone column is N/A by design. Serves both counties; VA enrollment not required. Cross-reference: Veterans tab and Crisis Help Lines tab.

resources.name: Veterans Crisis Line (US Department of Veterans Affairs)
resources.mission: The Veterans Crisis Line connects veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve, and their families with caring, qualified responders through a confidential toll-free hotline, online chat, and text, 24/7/365.
resources.services: Dial 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat at VeteransCrisisLine.net/Chat, 24/7. Responders are trained in military culture; many are veterans themselves. Available even if not enrolled in VA benefits or health care. Support for suicidal crisis, emotional distress, and concerned family and friends. Legacy number (800) 273-8255 press 1 still works.
resources.notes: Federal program. Cross-reference: Veterans tab for local VA and county veterans services offices.
resources.contactPerson: Veterans Crisis Line Program Office, US Department of Veterans Affairs

resources.name: Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 1487 (Roseville)
resources.mission: Chartered in 1929, the Roseville VFW post works as a team assisting veterans, their families and the surrounding community.
resources.services: Peer support for combat and overseas veterans; guidance on VA benefits and claims; referrals to the Placer County Veterans Service Office and VA health care; military funeral honors; community service and youth programs; veteran gatherings and meeting space at the Roseville Veterans Memorial Hall.
resources.notes: Roseville Veterans Memorial Hall, 110 Park Dr., Roseville, CA 95678.

resources.name: Volunteers of America NCNN (Sacramento Senior Safe House)
resources.mission: The Sacramento Senior Safe House is an emergency shelter for abused, neglected, and exploited seniors age 62 and older, operated by Volunteers of America Northern California and Northern Nevada in partnership with Sacramento County.
resources.services: Elder abuse emergency shelter: about 30 days of shelter for up to 6 seniors age 62+ in six private bedrooms, three nutritious meals and snacks daily, 24-hour staffing with volunteer support, and case management connecting residents to community resources and a permanent, safe living situation. Serves seniors experiencing abuse, neglect, exploitation, or homelessness. Access by referral: call 211 or the Adult Protective Services hotline (916) 874-9377; no walk-ins (confidential location).
resources.notes: Confidential location; entry only through APS or 211 referral. Operated by Volunteers of America NCNN (multi-category org, see Housing tab). Cross-reference: Housing tab (senior homelessness) and this tab's APS entries for reporting abuse.

resources.name: Volunteers of America Northern California & Northern Nevada (Sacramento Shelters & Housing)
resources.mission: Established in the Greater Sacramento Area in 1911, Volunteers of America's mission to reach and uplift all people includes families with children, seniors, the homeless, former foster youth, and people with substance abuse issues, with the goal of ending homelessness.
resources.services: Operates 40+ locally managed programs in the Sacramento region: emergency shelters and interim housing for families, single adults, and veterans; transitional housing for former foster youth; senior housing; substance abuse treatment and rehabilitation; counseling; independent living and parenting skills; job development. VOA provides shelter or housing to over 3,500 people every night regionally. Shelter placements generally via 211/Coordinated Access referral.
resources.notes: Office Mon-Fri 8am-5pm. Specific shelter sites change with county contracts; confirm current programs via office or 211. Placer-specific Home Start program listed separately under Placer. Cross-reference: Veterans category.

resources.name: Volunteers of America Northern California and Northern Nevada (Recovery Services, Options for Recovery)
resources.mission: Volunteers of America's mission is to reach and uplift all people, going wherever we are needed and doing whatever comes to hand. The NCNN affiliate has served the region since 1911 with more than 40 housing, employment and recovery programs.
resources.services: Recovery services centered on Options for Recovery, a long term (about 90 day) residential treatment program for pregnant, postpartum and parenting women at 1001 Grand Ave, Sacramento, with beds that allow young children (under 5) to stay with their mothers: counseling, dual diagnosis support, life skills, employment readiness and housing linkage. Program line (916) 929-1951. Placement for county funded beds is through the county access line (916) 874-9754; Medi-Cal accepted.
resources.notes: Options for Recovery: 1001 Grand Ave, Sacramento 95838; main office 3434 Marconi Ave, Sacramento 95821, (916) 265-3400 (both numbers current as of July 2026). 501(c)(3), Tax ID 94-6001984 per voa-ncnn.org. Program details confirmed via directories and VOA claimed findhelp listings; VOA's own site uses a searchable service finder, so confirm intake by phone before referral. Cross-reference: Housing, Veterans (VOA NCNN appears in multiple categories).

resources.name: Waking the Village (Tubman House)
resources.mission: Waking the Village provides creativity, community, and shelter for youth facing homelessness. Tubman House provides 18 to 24 months of housing and support so that Sacramento's homeless, parenting youth and their children can get busy living rather than surviving.
resources.services: Transitional housing community for pregnant or parenting youth ages 18-24 and their children across three shared housing sites (5-8 families each): free housing, groceries and essentials, free licensed preschool for children, youth development, physical and mental health support, educational attainment, career development, financial management. Residents commit 3 hours weekly to Youth Corps community projects. Also operates the Creation District outreach and youth leadership hub with daily arts, wellness, and leadership workshops.
resources.notes: Three shared housing sites in Sacramento; 18-24 month program. Call or text (916) 601-2979 or use the online form to join the housing wait list, which also covers Audre's Emporium of New Tomorrows, the agency's second transitional living program. Also operates The Village shelter and a licensed preschool (Art Beast, (916) 896-6195). Outcomes reported: 77 percent secure income-based housing, 77 percent attend college. Cross-reference: Housing tab.

resources.name: Waking the Village (Tubman House)
resources.mission: Waking the Village leads programs blending creativity and community for youth and children experiencing homelessness so parenting youth can get busy living rather than surviving.
resources.services: Tubman House provides 18-24 months of shared housing and wraparound support for homeless parenting youth (roughly 18-24) and their children across three housing sites (5-8 families each). Single parents and couples welcome. Program includes parenting development, free licensed on-site preschool and childcare, mental and physical health support, education and career development, and financial management. Call to join the waitlist. Also operates the Village Shelter, Creation District drop-in arts space, and prevention programs.
resources.notes: Mailing: PO Box 160085, Sacramento, CA 95816. Primary listing is in Housing tab; included here for its parenting-youth family programming and on-site childcare. Executive director name, housing waitlist phone (call or text (916) 601-2979), and program details confirmed on wakingthevillage.org July 2026. Second transitional living program, Audre's Emporium of New Tomorrows, also serves parenting youth; Art Beast Child Development Center line (916) 896-6195.
resources.contactPerson: Bridget Alexander, Co-Founder and Executive Director

resources.name: Waking the Village (Tubman House)
resources.mission: Waking the Village creates communities where youth facing homelessness thrive; Tubman House provides 18 to 24 months of housing and support so Sacramento's homeless, parenting youth and their children can get busy living rather than surviving.
resources.services: Tubman House transitional housing (18-24 months) for parenting youth roughly ages 18-24 and their children across three shared housing sites (5-8 families each); parenting and leadership workshops, support groups, education and career development, financial management, free licensed on-site preschool; staff on site daily 8am-4pm. Intake: complete the online form to join the waitlist; Outreach Director calls within 2 days. Outcomes: 77% secure income-based housing, 77% attend college. Also operates Creation District arts drop-in for youth.
resources.notes: Mail: PO Box 160085, Sacramento, CA 95816. Typically has a waitlist; intake via website form. Contact info confirmed July 2026.

resources.name: WarmLine Family Resource Center
resources.mission: WarmLine's mission is to provide information, education and support to promote and strengthen the foundation of families and children with special needs so they can face the challenges of the present and create new dreams for the future.
resources.services: Parent to parent support for families of children with disabilities and special health care needs ages 0-26: free information and referral, help navigating Alta California Regional Center, special education (IEP) coaching and Family Empowerment Center services, Early Start family support, a Community Navigator Program, workshops and trainings, and peer parent matching. Staffed by parents of children with disabilities; no charge; call or email, appointments preferred.
resources.notes: 3336 Bradshaw Road, Suite 255, Sacramento, CA 95827; hours 9:00-5:00 by appointment. Spanish line (916) 922-1490. Serves six counties: Sacramento, Yolo, Placer, El Dorado, Nevada, Alpine. Cross-reference: Childcare tab (special needs parenting support).

resources.name: WarmLine Family Resource Center (Transition Support)
resources.mission: WarmLine Family Resource Center was founded by and is staffed by parents who share the common experience of parenting a child with developmental delays or disabilities, providing parent-to-parent support, information, and referral to community resources.
resources.services: Free help for families of children and young adults with disabilities navigating transition to adulthood: information and referral, parent-to-parent support, help understanding IEP transition plans, regional center adult services, conservatorship alternatives, and benefits. Community Navigator Program (DDS-funded) matches families of children birth to 22, and individuals with disabilities 22 and older, with trained navigators who have lived experience; serves Sacramento, Placer, El Dorado, Nevada, Yolo, and Alpine counties, referral form online. Call to schedule office meetings; Spanish line available.
resources.notes: 3336 Bradshaw Rd, Suite 255, Sacramento, CA 95827; Spanish line (916) 922-1490. Serves families across the Alta California Regional Center 10-county catchment including Placer. Cross-reference: Disability tab.

resources.name: Wayfinder Family Services (Kinship Support Services Program, formerly Lilliput Families)
resources.mission: Wayfinder Family Services ensures that children, youth, and adults facing challenges always have a place to turn.
resources.services: Free Kinship Support Services Program (KSSP, also called Kinnections) for grandparents, relatives, and close family friends raising kinship children, whether informal or CPS court-dependent, including post-permanency through legal guardianship: service and systems navigation, in-home support, support groups, respite resources, trainings, advocacy, legal referrals, guardianship workshops and adoption assistance, family activities and events, mentoring, and assistance with basic emergency needs. No time limit on how long the child has lived with the caregiver. Enroll by phone, email, or walk-in. Sacramento County office: 910 Florin Road, Suite 112, Sacramento, (916) 688-4750. Placer County office: 1540 Eureka Road, Suite 100, Roseville, (530) 722-2233.
resources.notes: Lilliput Families merged into Wayfinder Family Services (programs now under Children and Family Services). Historic Lilliput line (916) 923-5444 no longer listed; current office numbers and addresses confirmed on wayfinderfamily.org July 2026. Placer referral email: placerkssp@wayfinderfamily.org. Cross-reference: Foster tab (primary listing for foster care and adoption services).

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc.
