resources.mission: WEAVE's mission is to promote safe and healthy relationships and support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence and sex trafficking. WEAVE is the primary provider of crisis intervention services for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault in Sacramento County.
resources.services: Sacramento County's primary DV/SA crisis agency. 24-hour Support and Information Line at (916) 920-2952 plus online chat. Services for all genders and ages: safety planning, crisis intervention, therapeutic counseling for adults and children, support groups, WEAVE Legal (restraining order assistance, family law help for survivors), confidential Emergency Safehouse, sexual assault response including Sacramento's rape crisis services, sex trafficking services, stalking support, LGBTQ+ inclusive services, Spanish-language services (En Espanol), and WEAVE on Campus plus teen dating violence education. Services are free and confidential; access starts with the 24-hour line.
resources.notes: Business line (916) 448-2321; 24/7 support line (916) 920-2952. Midtown Sacramento offices at 1900 K Street. Website has quick-exit feature. Cross-reference: Clothing tab (WEAVE Thrift, Wear It. Share It.), Housing tab (Safehouse and transitional housing). Serves all of Sacramento County including Elk Grove, Rancho Cordova, Citrus Heights.

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc. (24-Hour Support and Information Line)
resources.mission: WEAVE serves adult and child survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking; programs are available to any survivor regardless of gender, gender identity, or sexual orientation.
resources.services: 24/7 Support and Information Line staffed by trained peer counselors offering immediate crisis intervention, safety planning, and entry to all WEAVE services (safe shelter, counseling intake, legal services, sexual assault response). Help available in over 23 languages. Free and confidential; no documentation, proof of address, or police report required. Call any time, even if the incident happened months or years ago. WEAVE is Sacramento County's rape crisis center: advocates respond 24/7 for sexual assault exams.
resources.notes: Midtown Services Center, 1900 K St, Sacramento, CA 95811. Business line (916) 448-2321. Online chat via weaveinc.org. Cross-reference: Clothing tab (WEAVE Thrift) and Housing tab (safe shelter).

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc. (DV Safehouse & Survivor Housing)
resources.mission: WEAVE's mission is to promote safe and healthy relationships and support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, and sex trafficking. When Everyone Acts, Violence Ends.
resources.services: Confidential emergency Safehouse shelter for adult and child survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking (any gender, gender identity, or orientation); safety planning; 24/7 support line with help in 23+ languages; individual and group counseling; WEAVE Legal (protective orders, family law); Rent TRUE housing program; Survivor Coordinated Access System partner for DV-specific housing. No documentation, proof of address, or police report required. Access all services via the 24-hour line (916) 920-2952.
resources.notes: Midtown Services Center, 1900 K Street, Sacramento, CA 95811. Safehouse location confidential. Business line (916) 448-2321. Call 911 if in immediate danger. Cross-reference: Domestic Violence and Clothing categories.

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc. (Emergency Safehouse & Transitional Housing)
resources.mission: WEAVE operates an Emergency Safehouse Program for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, sex trafficking and their children. Survivors can find safe and confidential temporary shelter.
resources.services: Confidential emergency safehouse for survivors of domestic violence (recent violence between intimate partners), sexual assault, and sex trafficking, and their children. Access is exclusively through the 24-hour support line (916) 920-2952 with a safety and eligibility screening. WEAVE's Transitional Housing Program is available only to individuals and families who complete the Emergency Safehouse Program; it always operates at full capacity and direct entry is not possible. Free of charge.
resources.notes: Safehouse location is confidential; call the 24-hour line to request shelter. Cross-reference: Housing tab for WEAVE transitional housing; this row covers DV-specific emergency shelter. Domestic violence is defined for program purposes as recent intimate partner violence.

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc. (Sex Trafficking Services and Anti-Trafficking Response Team)
resources.mission: WEAVE's mission is to promote safe and healthy relationships and support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, and sex trafficking. When Everyone Acts, Violence Ends.
resources.services: 24/7 Support Line (916) 920-2952 used by victims, CPS, and law enforcement to request an advocate; operates Sacramento County's only 24/7 Anti-Trafficking Response Team (ART) for child victims of sex trafficking, with a consistent advocate assigned to each CSEC youth; for adult sex trafficking victims: confidential emergency shelter, transitional housing up to 24 months, crisis intervention, trauma-informed counseling by MFTs and MSWs, legal assistance and advocacy, and case management. Free and confidential; access via 24/7 Support Line.
resources.notes: Business line (916) 448-2321; shelter locations confidential. Serves Sacramento County. WEAVE is the county's designated advocate agency for CSEC youth identified by CPS. Cross-reference: Domestic Violence and Clothing tabs (WEAVE DV services, WEAVE Thrift).

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc. (WEAVE Legal)
resources.mission: WEAVE's mission is to promote safe and healthy relationships and support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, and sex trafficking; WEAVE Legal provides legal assistance to those survivors.
resources.services: Free legal help for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking in Sacramento County: consultation, representation, or forms assistance (case by case) for domestic violence restraining orders and related family law matters, civil harassment restraining orders for sexual assault victims, and vacatur petitions for trafficking survivors. Call the confidential legal line (916) 319-4944 and leave a safe callback number; 24-hour support line (916) 920-2952.
resources.notes: Confidential legal line; leave a message with a safe number and whether voicemail is okay. Services are case by case and capacity limited. Cross-reference: Clothing tab (WEAVE), Housing tab (DV shelter); Placer survivors see Stand Up Placer row.

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc. (WEAVE Thrift)
resources.mission: WEAVE's mission is to promote safe and healthy relationships and support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence and sex trafficking. 100 percent of WEAVE Thrift proceeds are invested in WEAVE's survivor services.
resources.services: Nonprofit thrift store selling low cost clothing, housewares, home items, shoes, purses, and jewelry to the public; survivors in WEAVE programs receive goods free through internal vouchers. Store open Monday through Saturday, 10:00 am to 5:30 pm. Donations accepted Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, 10:30 am to 1:30 pm (limit six bags or boxes, 13 gallon max size); pickups for large donations can be scheduled by phone. Greatest needs: housewares and home items.
resources.notes: WEAVE 24/7 Support Line: (916) 920-2952 for survivor services. Cross-reference: Clothing tab and Domestic Violence resources.

resources.name: WEAVE, Inc. (WEAVE to Work)
resources.mission: WEAVE is the primary provider of crisis intervention services for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking in Sacramento County; WEAVE to Work helps survivors attain financial independence through employment.
resources.services: Employment support for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and trafficking: free professional clothing and styling from a dedicated 2,500 square foot boutique, makeup consultation, interview preparation, and connection to WEAVE case management, counseling, and safety services. No program fees; all clothing free to participants. Access through WEAVE services or the 24/7 support line.
resources.notes: WEAVE to Work boutique: 2401 Arden Way, Sacramento, CA 95825. 24/7 Support and Information Line: (916) 920-2952. Cross-reference Clothing and Domestic Violence categories.

resources.name: WellSpace Health
resources.mission: WellSpace Health's mission is achieving regional health through high quality comprehensive care. It is a nonprofit community health system providing comprehensive medical, dental, behavioral health, and supportive services to underserved people and neighborhoods in the greater Sacramento region.
resources.services: FQHC with sites in more than 30 neighborhoods across the Sacramento region, including the Placer Community Health Center in Roseville: adult and pediatric primary care, women's health and OB/GYN, adult and children's dental (birth to age 20), full behavioral health continuum including substance use disorder treatment and medication-assisted treatment, Immediate Care centers with extended 7-day hours, in-house pharmacy with same-day delivery, and Birth and Beyond family resource centers. Welcomes Medi-Cal, Medicare, and uninsured patients. Appointments at (916) 737-5555 or online; telehealth Immediate Care evenings and weekends.
resources.notes: Operates the regional 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline center; 24-hour local crisis lines include Sacramento (916) 368-3111, Auburn (530) 885-2300, Roseville (916) 773-3111, Lincoln (916) 645-8866 (cross-ref Crisis Help Lines tab). Walk-in Immediate Care at Arden Arcade, Mon-Fri 8am-4pm. Centers directory at wellspacehealth.org/providers-and-centers/centers/.
resources.contactPerson: Jonathan Porteus, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: WellSpace Health (988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, 988 Sacramento)
resources.mission: 988 is a suicide prevention and mental health crisis center providing confidential support via talk, text, and chat 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, across the Greater Sacramento Region.
resources.services: WellSpace Health operates the accredited 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline center answering 988 calls, texts, and chats for the Greater Sacramento region, including Sacramento and Placer counties; free, confidential, 24/7/365 for anyone in emotional distress, suicidal crisis, or worried about someone else. Legacy local 24-hour lines: Sacramento (916) 368-3111, Auburn (530) 885-2300, Roseville (916) 773-3111, Lincoln (916) 645-8866. Also operates Crisis Receiving for Behavioral Health (CRBH), a voluntary 4 to 12 hour crisis stabilization program with wraparound services, and a 24-hour Maternal Support Line (916) 681-2907. No insurance, documentation, or referral needed.
resources.notes: Call or text 9-8-8, or chat via 988lifeline.org. WellSpace Health is a nonprofit FQHC headquartered in Sacramento; its 988 center answers for Sacramento, Placer, and 30+ Northern and Central California counties and is a member of 988 California. Main appointments line (916) 737-5555. Cross-reference: Crisis Help Lines tab (988 belongs in both tabs) and Mental Health tab.

resources.name: WellSpace Health (Behavioral Health and Counseling)
resources.mission: WellSpace Health is a nonprofit community health system providing comprehensive medical, dental, behavioral health, substance use disorder treatment, and supportive services to underserved people and neighborhoods in the greater Sacramento region.
resources.services: Full range of mental health treatment at community health centers: individual counseling/psychotherapy for children, adolescents, adults, couples and families, group counseling, child and adult psychiatry and medication management, mental health evaluations, and co-occurring addiction treatment. Federally Qualified Health Center: accepts Medi-Cal and Medicare and offers sliding fee discounts for uninsured/low-income patients; no one turned away for inability to pay. Appointment line for Sacramento and Placer county residents: (916) 313-8433.
resources.notes: Multiple health center locations across Sacramento County (Midtown, South Valley, Oak Park, and others). Also operates crisis programs and the regional 988 suicide line: cross-reference Crisis Help Lines and Suicide tabs.
resources.contactPerson: Jonathan Porteus, PhD, Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: WellSpace Health (Behavioral Health Co-Occurring Continuum of Care)
resources.mission: WellSpace Health is a nonprofit community health system committed to achieving regional health through high quality comprehensive care, including medical, dental, behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment and supportive services.
resources.services: Full SUD continuum for adults: withdrawal management (medically managed residential detox at 1550 Juliesse Ave, Sacramento), residential rehabilitation, outpatient treatment, medication assisted treatment (buprenorphine, naltrexone) for alcohol, opioids, methamphetamine and other drugs, co-occurring mental health care, criminal justice and reentry services. Access via main line (916) 737-5555 or through the county access line (916) 874-9754. Accepts Medi-Cal, Medicare, sliding scale for uninsured. Federally Qualified Health Center, Joint Commission accredited.
resources.notes: Detox/residential campus: 1550 Juliesse Ave, Sacramento 95815; clinics throughout Sacramento County. Also operates the 988/suicide crisis line regionally. Cross-reference: Health category.
resources.contactPerson: Dr. Jonathan Porteus, Chief Executive Officer

resources.name: Wellspring Women's Center
resources.mission: Wellspring Women's Center nurtures the innate goodness and personal self-esteem of women and their children, providing hospitality with dignity and love in Oak Park.
resources.services: Daytime safety-net center for women and children, many homeless or housing-insecure: Nutritious Meal Program (weekday breakfast and lunch), Safety Net Services (case management, referrals to housing and shelter, help with documents and benefits), Women's Wellness Program (free counseling, art therapy, wellness classes), Children's Corner. Drop-in weekday mornings 8:30-11:30am; afternoons by appointment. Closed weekends. Not an overnight shelter; a stabilization and referral resource.
resources.notes: Hours drawn partly from third-party directories; confirm current schedule with the center before referral.

resources.name: Western Placer Unified School District
resources.mission: Western Placer Unified School District serves Lincoln and surrounding communities, fostering a love of learning, developing essential skills and preparing students to confidently explore the complexities of the world.
resources.services: TK-12 public education; The HUB family resource center; student work permits; student and family support services; community partnerships; career and college pathways; district employment opportunities.
resources.notes: Source: Lincoln Serves Info roster.

resources.name: Western Sierra Medical Clinic (Auburn and Kings Beach sites)
resources.mission: Providing accessible, quality medical, dental and behavioral health services through innovative, patient-centered care in our communities. Vision: to promote the health and wellness of Nevada, Placer, Sierra, and Yuba counties through patient-centered care.
resources.services: FQHC with Placer County sites: Auburn Education clinic (11720 Education St., Suite 3, Auburn) offering medical care, medication-assisted treatment, pediatrics, and podiatry, Mon-Fri 8-5 (closed 12-1), (530) 537-3000; Auburn Greenlee clinic (3720 Grass Valley Hwy) for chiropractic, Tue/Thu 8-5; and Kings Beach clinics in North Lake Tahoe (8665 Salmon Ave., (530) 584-9762). Accepts Medicare, Medi-Cal, private insurance, and uninsured patients on a sliding fee scale. New patient coordinator (530) 273-5469. Designated by Placer County to accept former county clinic patients. After-hours on-call coverage.
resources.notes: Headquartered in Grass Valley (Nevada County) with additional sites in Nevada, Sierra, and Yuba counties, including urgent care in Grass Valley. Sierra Family Health Center merged into Western Sierra in 2025 (sierraclinic.org now redirects to wsmcmed.org); Sierra Family had no Placer or Sacramento sites. Closed first Tuesday monthly 12:30-1:30pm.

resources.name: Whole Person Learning (HOPE, Housing Opportunities Providing Experience)
resources.mission: HOPE offers transitional housing along with intensive life skills support for young adults who have emancipated from court-ordered foster or group home care; Whole Person Learning empowers youth and young adults to thrive in their communities using a collaborative, individually tailored positive youth development approach.
resources.services: THP-Plus transitional housing plus intensive independent living skills coaching for young adults who emancipated from foster care or group home care: housing, case management, education and employment support, financial management. Typical THP-Plus eligibility is former foster or probation youth ages 18-24 (up to 25 in some cases) for up to 24-36 months. Call for intake; capacity is limited.
resources.notes: 11816 Kemper Road, Auburn. Placer County Children's System of Care page currently lists Whole Person Learning THP-Plus at (530) 823-6903 as a county ILP/transition partner (checked July 2026), confirming the contract is active; still confirm capacity and intake before referral. HOPE is operated with Youth Empowerment Support (YES!), youthempowermentsupport.com, YES! line (530) 886-5461; that site did not load when checked, so the 211 record is listed instead. Also partners with Golden Sierra Job Training Agency and AMI Housing on housing for youth 16-24 enrolled in school, job training, or employment. Cross-reference: Housing tab and Foster tab.

resources.name: Whole Person Learning, Inc. (HOPE Transitional Housing for Youth)
resources.mission: Whole Person Learning empowers youth and young adults to thrive in their communities using a collaborative, individually tailored positive youth development approach.
resources.services: HOPE program: transitional housing plus intensive life skills support for young adults who have emancipated from court-ordered foster care or group home care. Operates Placer County's THP-Plus (Transitional Housing Placement-Plus) under county contract. Partner in the TAY Housing Collaborative with AMI Housing and Golden Sierra Job Training Agency, providing housing assistance for ages 16-24 who are homeless or at risk and enrolled in education, job training, or employment.
resources.notes: Organization website not loading as of July 2026; program confirmed via 211 Connecting Point and Placer County contract documents. Call to confirm current intake before referral. Cross-reference: Foster category.

resources.name: Widowed Persons Association of California, Sacramento Chapter
resources.address: 2628 El Camino Avenue, Suite D-18, Sacramento, CA 95821
resources.mission: WPAC is a nonprofit, non-denominational community service organization dedicated to helping widowed people overcome grief and learn to live and laugh again; its philosophy is that a grief shared is a grief diminished.
resources.services: Grief support for widowed men and women of all ages (membership is largely older adults): Sunday Support Group every week 3:00-5:00 pm at the WPAC meeting room (doors open 2:30; virtual Zoom group discontinued), four-week Grief Recovery Workshops held four times per year, telephone support, monthly newsletter, and an extensive social activities calendar (luncheons, outings, clubs) to rebuild social connection. Open to any widowed person; attend a Sunday meeting or call the office to start. Modest annual membership dues; initial support open to non-members.
resources.notes: Office: 2628 El Camino Avenue, Suite D-18, Sacramento, CA 95821; office hours Mon, Wed, Fri 10am-1pm (leave a message after hours). Website confirmed current July 2026 (July 2026 activity calendar posted). Cross-reference: Crisis tab (grief support resources).

resources.name: Wilton Rancheria
resources.mission: Wilton Rancheria is committed to promoting health, wellness, economic success, and education for our tribal community and for generations to come.
resources.services: Sacramento County's only federally recognized tribe (Miwok), headquartered in Elk Grove. Tribal government departments include Cultural Preservation, Education, Enrollment, Health, Housing, Social Services (which handles Indian Child Welfare / ICWA matters), and Member Services, plus a Tribal Court. Education Department offers language, culture, and other classes, some open to the wider Native community. ICWA department participates in child welfare cases involving Wilton Rancheria children in Sacramento County and other courts. Call the tribal office to reach a specific department.
resources.notes: Tribal office: 9728 Kent St, Elk Grove, CA 95624. Most benefit programs (housing, education assistance, health coverage support) are for enrolled Wilton Rancheria citizens; some cultural and language classes are open to the community. Not a walk-in agency for the general Native public. Cross-reference: Foster (ICWA) category.

resources.name: Wind Youth Services (24-Hour Adolescent Shelter Hotline)
resources.mission: Wind Youth Services provides youth experiencing homelessness and at-risk youth ages 12-24 in the Sacramento area with basic safety net services, a safe place to stay, and pathways to housing.
resources.services: 24-hour hotline for youth ages 12-17 (or their parents/guardians) needing emergency overnight shelter; Wind runs the only low-barrier adolescent emergency shelter in the greater Sacramento area. Youth 18-24 seeking emergency housing dial 211 for intake. Drop-in center for ages 18-24 at 815 S Street open daily from 8:30 am (closing times vary by day, with shorter hours Tuesdays and weekends; call to confirm) with meals, showers, case management, and ID help.
resources.notes: Drop-in center and administrative offices: 815 S Street, Sacramento, CA 95811. Main phone (916) 504-3313. Cross-reference: Housing tab (youth shelter and housing programs).

resources.name: Wind Youth Services (Drop-In Center)
resources.mission: Wind Youth Services provides youth experiencing homelessness and housing insecurity in the Sacramento area with basic safety net and survival services and a safe place to stay.
resources.services: Free drop-in center for young adults ages 18-24 at 815 S Street: breakfast (9-10 am) and lunch (1-2 pm), showers, laundry, hygiene supplies, essential needs closet, mail services, Rejuvenation Haven six-bed daytime respite room, case management, life skills workshops, anti-human trafficking services and an on-site health clinic (Thursdays 1-5 pm with One Community Health). Hours: Mon 8:30 am-4 pm, Tue 8:30 am-2:30 pm, Wed-Fri 8:30 am-4 pm; Sat-Sun 8:30 am-4:30 pm respite center only. Intakes Mon 9-11 am and Thu 2-4 pm, no appointment needed; ID required to verify age 18-24.
resources.notes: Drop-In Center: 815 S Street, Sacramento, CA 95811. Cross-reference Housing/Crisis tab (Wind also runs an emergency shelter and housing programs, including for minors). 501(c)(3), EIN 23-7348227. Drop-in now serves ages 18-24 only; younger youth should be referred to Wind's shelter line.

resources.name: Wind Youth Services (Transition Age Youth Programs)
resources.mission: Wind Youth Services provides homeless and at-risk youth between the ages of 12 and 24 in the Sacramento area with basic safety net and survival services and a safe place to stay.
resources.services: Drop-in center at 815 S Street for ages 18-24: full services Monday-Friday including case management, breakfast (9-10 a.m.) and lunch (1-2 p.m.), showers, laundry, hygiene supplies, essential needs closet, mail service, life skills workshops, anti-trafficking team; weekends the six-bed Rejuvenation Haven respite room only, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Drop-in intakes Mondays 9-11 a.m. and Thursdays 2-4 p.m., ID required. On-site partners: One Community Health clinic (Thursdays 1-5 p.m.), Juma YouthConnect employment (ages 16-24), WEAVE, Legal Services of Northern California. Shelters: Common Ground low-barrier co-ed TAY shelter, ages 18-24, up to 120 days, referral by calling 211; adolescent shelter ages 12-17, hotline (916) 628-1492; TAY House 90-day step-up by internal referral.
resources.notes: Drop-in center: 815 S Street, Sacramento, CA 95811; full services weekdays, weekend respite only. Common Ground TAY shelter access is via 211, not the drop-in center. 501(c)(3), EIN 23-7348227. Cross-reference: Housing tab (shelters) and Foster tab; many clients are former foster youth.

resources.name: Wind Youth Services (Youth 12-24)
resources.mission: Wind Youth Services provides supportive services and opportunities to youth experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity in Sacramento so they may pursue self-determined lives.
resources.services: Drop-In Center at 815 S Street, Sacramento for ages 18-24: meals, showers, laundry, peer support, CA IDs and birth certificates, employment and education assistance, case management, crisis intervention, counseling, mental health respite. Emergency Youth Shelter (ages 12-17): low-barrier overnight shelter 365 days/year, hot meals, counseling, life skills, trans-affirming and LGBTQ-friendly, pet friendly; self-referral accepted, no parent required. TAY Shelter (18-24): low-barrier emergency shelter, pet friendly. Street outreach. Access: 24-hour hotline (916) 628-1492 or walk in to drop-in center.
resources.notes: Drop-In: 815 S Street, Sacramento, CA 95811. Use windyouthservices.org (old domain windyouth.org shows outdated content). Cross-reference: Foster and Youth categories.

resources.name: Women's Empowerment
resources.mission: Women's Empowerment educates and empowers women who are experiencing homelessness with the skills and confidence necessary to get a job, maintain a healthy lifestyle, and regain a home for themselves and their children.
resources.services: Nine-week Job Readiness and Empowerment program for women 18 and over experiencing or at risk of homelessness (staying with family, in a motel, shelter, car, or outside, couch surfing, transitioning out of prison, or facing eviction): job seeking skills, resume building, mock interviews, computer literacy, one-on-one support, on-site Child Development Center child care during class, paid job training program, Trellis Gardens housing program, and graduate services. Enrollment requires attending a free 2.5 hour orientation held several times before each session; walk-in orientations at 1590 North A St. Non-binary people welcome.
resources.notes: 1590 North A St., Sacramento, CA 95811 (Loaves & Fishes campus area). Office hours Monday-Friday 8:30am-3:30pm. Orientation is required for acceptance; call (916) 669-2307 or check womens-empowerment.org for the next orientation dates (new session cohorts run several times per year). Cross-reference Housing (Trellis Gardens, serves homeless women).

resources.name: Work for Warriors (California Military Department)
resources.mission: Work for Warriors is a state and federally funded free job placement program for veterans of all eras, active National Guard and Reserve members, spouses, and Gold Star families, assisting them in finding civilian employment in California.
resources.services: Free direct job placement: employment specialists match veterans' skill sets to civilian employers in a network of over 350 business partners, resume development, interview coaching, and referrals to apprenticeships and training. Register online at workforwarriors.org; serves veterans, National Guard, Reserve, military spouses, and Gold Star family members statewide from its Sacramento-area headquarters.
resources.notes: Run by the California Military Department at 10601 Bear Hollow Dr., Rancho Cordova, CA 95670; serves all of California including both counties. Cross-reference Veterans category.

resources.name: Working Solutions CDFI
resources.mission: Working Solutions is a certified nonprofit Community Development Financial Institution that makes affordable loans of $5,000 to $100,000 accessible to start-up and early-stage entrepreneurs in California, and provides free business consulting in conjunction with every loan.
resources.services: Small business loans from $5,000 to $100,000 (3 or 5 year terms, fixed rate) with no minimum revenue, no minimum credit score and no collateral required, paired with free one-on-one business consulting; small application and closing fees apply. Business must be located in California; at least one owner must live in California and have one year of same-industry experience (startups also need a secondary income source). ITIN applicants accepted regardless of immigration status. Expanded statewide in 2024, now lends across California including the Sacramento region. Apply online.
resources.notes: Headquartered at 870 Market Street, Suite 677, San Francisco, CA 94102; services delivered remotely statewide. Sacramento and Placer counties covered under the 2024 statewide expansion. Nonprofits, cannabis, gambling and passive real estate businesses ineligible. Eligibility details and current loan terms at workingsolutions.org/terms.

resources.name: World Relief Sacramento (Immigration Legal Services)
resources.mission: World Relief is a global Christian humanitarian organization; its Immigration Legal Services program partners with local churches and the wider community to provide low-cost, high-quality legal services to immigrants throughout the Sacramento area.
resources.services: DOJ recognized program with attorney and accredited caseworkers: consultations, adjustment of status, green card replacement and renewal, refugee/asylee green cards, family petitions, naturalization, DACA renewals and DACA advance parole, T visas, U visas, VAWA, TPS, travel documents, certificate of citizenship, fiance petitions, and document translation. By appointment only; initial consultations by Zoom or phone. Fees sliding by service type and income, some services free under grants. Interpretation in Spanish, Pashto, Dari, Russian, and Ukrainian. Does NOT serve people in detention or removal proceedings, and does not do affirmative asylum or employment/student/visitor visas.
resources.notes: Current address per World Relief's own site (July 2026): 2233 Watt Avenue, Suite 360, Sacramento, CA 95825; the older 4616 Roseville Road, North Highlands address in some directories is outdated. Main office (916) 978-2650; ILS appointments (916) 707-5038 or online scheduler (wrsils.as.me). Serves the greater Sacramento area including nearby Placer residents willing to travel; appointments required, initial consultations by Zoom or phone. For removal defense, see Opening Doors, UC Davis clinic, or NorCal Resist referrals.

resources.name: YoloCares (formerly Yolo Hospice, Center for Loss & Hope)
resources.address: 1909 Galileo Ct, Suite A, Davis, CA 95618
resources.mission: Our mission is to serve our community, providing the highest quality of care to every patient, every family, every time.
resources.services: Nonprofit founded as Yolo Hospice, the first established independent hospice in the Sacramento Valley; renamed YoloCares in 2021. Joint Commission accredited hospice and palliative care serving Sacramento, Yolo, Colusa, Sutter, Placer, and Solano counties. Center for Loss & Hope provides grief counseling and support groups open to the community, including YoloCares for Kids (formerly Stepping Stones) for children, teens, and families coping with terminal illness or loss. Also operates Galileo Place adult day program and Joshua's House homeless hospice. Referrals 24/7: (800) 491-7711 or fax (530) 758-9017; care covered by Medicare, Medi-Cal, and private insurance.
resources.notes: Serves six counties including Sacramento and Placer; confirm coverage for specific address at referral. Grief services open to public, not just hospice families. Cross-reference: Joshua's House row (Sacramento County).
